# 22. ADC Engagement Module (Session Bookmarks)

**What this group covers.** Engagement is the ADC bounded context that holds everything an attendee *does* at the conference beyond browsing the catalog. Five capability families live here, and they are worth naming up front because the chapter title only mentions the oldest one: the **session-bookmark aggregate** (the personal schedule), the **QR badge check-in surface** (badges, organizer scanning, the manual fallback, attendee self-service from printed room and sponsor codes, and the attendance rollup), the **points economy** (an append-only ledger plus an opt-in public leaderboard), the **ticket roster** (an organizer-uploaded TicketLeap roster, the invites it sends, the linking of tickets to accounts, the attendee's barcode claim, and the organizer insights reports), and the **attendee-facing pages** the module contributes to the Blazor UI (feedback forms, the badge, the points screens, and the now-next surface). Around those sit the shared module plumbing: use cases, EF persistence, the REST API, the cross-service gRPC contracts and adapters, and the extracted service host. The module also hosts the conference-day live layer (LivePolls and SessionQuestions), a surface large enough that its aggregates, use cases, controllers, wire payloads and pages are documented on their own in [Group 23](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md). What stays in this chapter is everything the rest of the module shares with that layer: the flags in [EngagementFeatures](#engagementfeatures), the capabilities in [EngagementPermissions](#engagementpermissions) with the role map in [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants), the outbound publish queue behind [ILiveChannelPublishQueue](#ilivechannelpublishqueue), the two UI helpers the conference-day pages share ([LiveChannelSubscription](#livechannelsubscription) and [LiveBroadcastPatch](#livebroadcastpatch)), the browser-side client layer those pages call ([ILiveEventUIService](#iliveeventuiservice), [ILivePollUIService](#ilivepolluiservice) and [ISessionQuestionUIService](#isessionquestionuiservice) with their implementations), the session catalog lookup behind [ISessionLookupService](#isessionlookupservice), and the LivePolls table shapes ([LivePollConfiguration](#livepollconfiguration), [LivePollOptionConfiguration](#livepolloptionconfiguration) and [LivePollVoteConfiguration](#livepollvoteconfiguration)), which sit beside the other EF configurations of the one database this module owns. One live-layer controller is documented here as well: [LivePollVotingController](#livepollvotingcontroller) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/LivePollVotingController.cs:37`) is the attendee-facing half of the poll surface (open polls with live tallies, one poll's results, and casting a vote), split out of [LivePollsController](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollscontroller) only so that controller stays within the repo's constructor-dependency ceiling. It keeps the same `LivePolls` route prefix, the same `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.LivePolls)]` and the same plain `[Authorize]`, so no URL, verb or authorization posture moved with the split, and it binds the caller from the token, never from the request (`:20-34`); the vote action carries [IdempotentAttribute](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#idempotentattribute) because the request names the option explicitly (set my vote to X, not toggle), so a retry over flaky conference wifi is safe to replay (`:97-103`). Read [Group 02](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md) for the entity primitives and [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to) for the styles before you go deep here.

**Five small aggregates, one shape.** Every write in this module lands on an [AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype) with private setters, private constructors, and a static `Create` factory returning `Result<T>` after a `Result.Combine` over a matching invariants helper. (A sixth aggregate root, [ErasedUser](#eraseduser), is not a capability of its own but the erasure record taught under Persistence below.) [UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmark.cs:16`) carries two scalar foreign keys, `UserId` and `SessionId` (`:19`, `:22`), and raises one [UserSessionBookmarkChanged](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) event with a [DomainEntityState](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate) discriminator instead of separate Created and Deleted events (`:57`, `:73`, `:88`, documented in-code as BR-60); its `Reactivate()` (`:68-76`) undeletes a soft-deleted row and re-raises the Added variant, which is the domain half of the re-bookmarking rule BR-135. The comment at `:55-56` is worth reading before you copy the event: the bookmark's identity is generated by the INSERT, so the event captures a zero id by value and consumers correlate on the user and the session instead. [CheckIn](#checkin) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/CheckIns/CheckIn.cs:28`) is one aggregate for all three scopes of the [CheckInScope](#checkinscope) enum, because the row, the idempotency rule, and the attendance query have the same shape for each and only the required target differs (`:13-15`); its `CheckedInByUserId` (`:49`) is what keeps a self-recorded scan distinguishable from an organizer's, and it is the one aggregate here that raises an integration event straight from its factory (`:112`). [AttendeeBadge](#attendeebadge) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Badges/AttendeeBadge.cs:18`) holds one opaque `Guid` credential per user (`:24`) and raises no domain event at all, since a badge existing is not a fact any other module reacts to (`:12-15`); `Regenerate()` (`:59`) revokes every printed or screenshotted copy, and the credential is minted with `Guid.NewGuid()` rather than `Guid.CreateVersion7()` precisely because a v7 value embeds a timestamp and orders monotonically, which is the one property a bearer credential must not have (`:65-68`). [PointsEntry](#pointsentry) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/PointsEntry.cs:31`) is an append-only ledger row with no mutators, so a total is always the sum of its entries (`:12-13`), and it snapshots the configured award at earn time (`:39-40`) so retuning the economy never rewrites history. [LeaderboardOptIn](#leaderboardoptin) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/LeaderboardOptIn.cs:19`) stores the display name the attendee explicitly published (`:35`), which is why serving the board needs no call into Identity, and it keeps `EraseDisplayName()` (`:130`) deliberately separate from `Delete()` (`:109`): leaving the board and erasing the name you published there are two different promises, and only the second is irreversible. `CheckIn` and `PointsEntry` additionally declare [IAuditedEntity](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#iauditedentity) (`CheckIn.cs:28`, `PointsEntry.cs:31`), so their field-level change history is written by the audit-trail interceptor ([ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html)): an attendance assertion about a named person and a prize-bearing ledger are both things you want to be able to prove rather than merely assert.

**The bookmark slice, end to end.** [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:37`) is the thin REST edge: each action injects a handler and delegates, mapping [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) failures to RFC 9457 Problem Details through [ApiControllerBase](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#apicontrollerbase). The POST does its own ownership bind first, because the owner arrives in the request body rather than in a query argument: a caller without the Organizer role may only create a bookmark whose `UserId` equals their user-identifier claim, otherwise the action returns `Error.Forbidden` (`:63-70`, [ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)). It also carries [IdempotentAttribute](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#idempotentattribute) (`:50`), which is safe here for the reason stated in the doc comment: the request names the (user, session) pair explicitly and a duplicate already answers 409, so replaying a retried star is what the attendee meant ([ADR-017](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/017-request-idempotency.html)). It then routes into [CreateBookmarkHandler](#createbookmarkhandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/Create/CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:18`), still the most instructive slice in the module: it first refuses an erased account through [ErasedUserGuard](#eraseduserguard) (`:30-34`), then asks Conference's [ISessionBookmarkValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#isessionbookmarkvalidationservice) whether the session may be bookmarked at all (`:37`, BR-49 and BR-91 across the service boundary), returns `Error.Conflict` on an existing active bookmark (`:43-54`, BR-21), loads any soft-deleted row through the repository's `FindIncludingDeletedAsync` (`:57-61`) and hands the create-or-reactivate decision to the pure, static [BookmarkManagementDomainService](#bookmarkmanagementdomainservice) (`:64`), so BR-135 lives in the domain instead of being smeared across the handler. The domain service is a `static class` with one `CreateOrReactivate` method over the pre-fetched row (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/BookmarkManagementDomainService.cs:11`, `:20-35`): it has no dependencies and no state, so there is no interface and no DI registration, and the handler calls it directly. Only a genuinely new entity is added to the repository (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:61-64`), and the save is wrapped in a `catch` filtered by the framework's injected [IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector) (`:70`), so a request that loses the insert race against the filtered unique index sees the same 409 the pre-check would have produced rather than a raw 500 (`:70-82`). That detector is the module's shared answer to "the database is the rule, the pre-check is only a courtesy": [PointsAwarder](#pointsawarder), [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) and [SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler](#setleaderboardparticipationhandler) inject the identical abstraction. On the read side, [GetUserBookmarksHandler](#getuserbookmarkshandler) (`.../GetUserBookmarks/GetUserBookmarksHandler.cs:17`) returns a paged, `CreatedOn`-descending [PagedCollectionResult<T>](group-01-result-error-handling.md#pagedcollectionresultt) of DTOs, with the page size clamped by [PagingMath](group-03-querying-specifications.md#pagingmath) before anything touches the database (`:31`) and ordering plus OFFSET/FETCH pushed into SQL through [IQueryableExecutor](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iqueryableexecutor), the `Id` tie-break after `CreatedOn` making the ORDER BY total so bookmarks created in the same instant neither repeat nor vanish across pages (`:60-70`); [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler](#getbookmarkedsessionidshandler) (`.../GetBookmarkedSessionIds/GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:12`) is the lightweight sibling the unified Sessions page turns into per-row filled or empty bookmark icons. Both list endpoints are scoped by the shared [OwnerOrAdminFilter](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilter) applied as a `[ServiceFilter]` (`BookmarksController.cs:84`, `:105`), configured for ADC through [OwnerOrAdminFilterOptions](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilteroptions) in `AddModuleEngagementAPI` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:45-56`): `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier` as the owner claim, the `userId` query argument, and the Organizer bypass role. The DELETE keeps a separate inline, database-backed ownership check that returns 404 rather than 403 so it never leaks whether a bookmark exists (`BookmarksController.cs:131-148`), then runs the generic [DeleteEntityCommand<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#deleteentitycommandtentity-tidentifiertype) (`:151`), which soft-deletes.

**Check-in: four ways in, one row out.** [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:42`) exposes the whole surface behind `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.CheckIn)]` and a plain `[Authorize]` (`:37-38`). An attendee fetches their own badge at `GET my-badge` with no permission at all (`:50`), because [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) (`.../GetOrCreateMyBadge/GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler.cs:19`) reads the identity from the token, refuses an erased account so a still-valid token cannot mint a fresh badge after erasure deleted the old one (`:38-42`), and mints on first use (`:44-79`), returning a [MyBadgeDTO](#mybadgedto) carrying nothing but the credential (`:81-83`). The QR itself is formatted by [BadgePayload](#badgepayload) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/Badges/BadgePayload.cs:12`), one place that owns both the `mmca-adc:badge:` prefix (`:15`) and the parser (`:30`), so the display side and the check-in handler cannot drift. The organizer paths are gated by `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage)]` (`CheckInsController.cs:79`, `:103`, `:187`): [CheckInAttendeeHandler](#checkinattendeehandler) (`.../CheckInAttendee/CheckInAttendeeHandler.cs:19`) resolves the scanned credential to a badge row and answers a malformed payload and an unknown-but-well-formed credential with the *same* error, since a scanner that could tell them apart would be an oracle for guessing credentials (`:41-56`), and [ManualCheckInHandler](#manualcheckinhandler) covers the dead-phone fallback. Both then run the shared [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:23`), a static helper rather than an injected service so neither handler gains a dependency it does not own (`:11-14`). The processor is split in two halves on purpose: `ExecuteAsync` (`:130`) is the organizer path, which validates the target through Conference and lets the *server's* answer for the owning event win over the value the scanning client sent (`:145-149`), while `RecordAsync` (`:60`) is the write half every entry point shares, short-circuiting a repeat scan into a success carrying the original timestamp rather than a conflict (`:74`) and otherwise recording exactly one row via the [RecordedCheckIn](#recordedcheckin) outcome struct (`:38`). The two self-service flows are separate handlers that reuse only that write half. [RecordSponsorVisitHandler](#recordsponsorvisithandler) (`.../RecordSponsorVisit/RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:37`) and [RecordRoomCheckInHandler](#recordroomcheckinhandler) (`.../RecordRoomCheckIn/RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:43`) take the attendee from the token, never the request, run the same [ErasedUserGuard](#eraseduserguard) check before anything else (`RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:58`, `RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:65-68`), and each carries its own feature flag (`CheckInsController.cs:134`, `:169`) so a printed sponsor code and a printed room code can be retired independently. The room flow is the sharpest piece of design here: only the room travels in the request, and the server resolves which session that room is hosting at the request instant plus a grace window this module owns and sends along (`RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:70-75`), so a shared link records nothing outside a session's window and nobody can name a session they are not standing in; an unknown room and an idle room answer identically so the response never confirms which room ids exist, while a transport failure still propagates so a Conference outage is not reported as an empty schedule (`:76-86`). Room switching needs no staff, because an attendee already checked in to an overlapping session is still checked in here, and the points question is settled by [SessionTimeSlotPoints](#sessiontimeslotpoints) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:29`), the one statement of "session points once per time slot": a session check-in earns nothing when the attendee holds an earlier check-in for a different, overlapping session of the same event, and attendance itself is never affected (`:10-14`). "Earlier" is decided from the committed rows (an earlier `CheckedInOn`, or the same instant with a smaller id), never from handling order, so concurrent or out-of-order handling still lets exactly the slot's first check-in earn (`:16-21`, `:71-76`). Two callers ask it: the room handler asks before it writes and fails closed, reporting the answer as `EarnsPoints` and skipping the question entirely when session points are switched off (`RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:94-113`), and [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler) asks for every session check-in, door scans included, letting a Conference NotFound stand the award and throwing on any other failure so the delivery is retried rather than awarded in breach of the rule (`.../IntegrationEventHandlers/AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler.cs:62-67`, `:87-111`). [GetAttendanceStatsHandler](#getattendancestatshandler) (`.../GetAttendanceStats/GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:15`) closes the loop for organizers, and both of its figures are computed in SQL: a `CountAsync` for the event scope and a `CountByAsync` grouped per session, so what crosses the wire is one row per session rather than one per check-in (`:27-34`). All of this is [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html); the camera half of the scanner is [ADR-071](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/071-barcode-scanning-and-qr-display.html).

**Points: one write path, several adapters.** Everything that earns goes through [IPointsAwarder](#ipointsawarder) / [PointsAwarder](#pointsawarder) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/Services/PointsAwarder.cs:30`), which takes an `(activity, subjectKey)` pair and knows nothing about events, sessions or sponsors. It reads the configured value from [PointsSettings](#pointssettings) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/PointsSettings.cs:13`) and treats a configured or missing `0` as a per-rule kill switch, writing nothing rather than a zero-value ledger row (`PointsAwarder.cs:43-51`); it pre-checks for an existing award purely to make the common duplicate path a clean no-op (`:55-64`); and it reads the unique-index violation as *already awarded*, not as a failure to retry (`:75-82`). The rule that matters is the index, not the code: the unique `(UserId, ActivityType, SubjectKey)` index in [PointsEntryConfiguration](#pointsentryconfiguration) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/Points/PointsEntryConfiguration.cs:45-48`) is simultaneously the idempotency guarantee and the anti-farming rule, because [PointsSubjectKeys](#pointssubjectkeys) collapses N questions or N answers in one session onto one subject key. Four adapters feed it. Three are integration-event handlers built on [ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent): [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler) (`.../IntegrationEventHandlers/AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler.cs:31`) maps the wire scope string onto an earn rule and logs-and-skips a scope this build has never heard of rather than dead-lettering a message no retry could fix (`:42-46`, `:65-99`), while [SessionFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler](#sessionfeedbacksubmittedpointshandler) and [EventFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler](#eventfeedbacksubmittedpointshandler) consume events Conference publishes. The fourth, [SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler](#sessionquestionsubmittedpointshandler) (`.../DomainEventHandlers/SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:54`), rides an in-process domain event instead, an explicit at-most-once trade-off documented in the type: a crash between the commit and the dispatch loses one small award and nothing else, and promoting it to an integration event later is a one-file change on each side (`:31-40`). Its doc comment is also the best worked example in the module of the id-by-value trap described above, and of why every field it needs now comes off the event rather than from a read-back (`:22-30`). A fifth handler earns nothing at all: [UserDeletedPointsHandler](#userdeletedpointshandler) (`.../IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedPointsHandler.cs:37`) consumes Identity's `UserDeleted` and erases the published leaderboard name, reading with `ignoreQueryFilters: true` precisely because an attendee who already left the board still has a soft-deleted row carrying the name that must be erased (`:53-61`). It is not the only consumer of that event in this module, because the Identity-side erasure cannot reach across the database boundary: [UserDeletedBookmarksHandler](#userdeletedbookmarkshandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedBookmarksHandler.cs:22`) deletes the account's session bookmarks, the promise PRIVACY.md section 5 makes (`:10-13`), and [UserDeletedBadgeHandler](#userdeletedbadgehandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedBadgeHandler.cs:22`) deletes the attendee badge that carries the per-user credential while deliberately keeping the check-in records themselves (`:10-13`); the live layer's [UserDeletedSessionQuestionsHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#userdeletedsessionquestionshandler) and [UserDeletedVotesHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#userdeletedvoteshandler) do the same for questions and votes. The two new handlers are the same shape line for line: each extends `ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<UserDeleted>` (`:25` in each), reads only active rows with tracking on, calls `Delete()` on each, skips the save entirely when nothing was deleted, and lets exceptions propagate (`:33-58`), so a redelivery under at-least-once delivery finds nothing and writes nothing, and a failed erasure is retried rather than acked away (`:15-17`).

**Reading the points back.** [PointsController](#pointscontroller) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/PointsController.cs:37`) is a good study in designing an ownership problem out of existence: nothing on the surface takes a user id, so the three attendee endpoints resolve the caller from the token inside their handlers and there is no ownership check to get wrong (`:25-29`). [GetMyPointsHandler](#getmypointshandler) serves the caller's own total and a page of the entries behind it; [SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler](#setleaderboardparticipationhandler) (`.../SetLeaderboardParticipation/SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler.cs:32`) takes the published display name from the caller's token claims server-side, which is why [SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest](#setleaderboardparticipationrequest) carries only a boolean (`:16-19`), and rejoining reactivates the soft-deleted opt-in rather than accumulating dead rows (`:22-24`). [GetLeaderboardHandler](#getleaderboardhandler) (`.../GetLeaderboard/GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:28`) builds the board from the opt-in list and the ledger with no call into Identity (`:12-17`), projecting the opt-ins to the two columns it needs through the private [OptInRow](#optinrow) record (`:40-43`, `:85`) and summing the ledger with one grouped `SumByAsync` in the database rather than pulling every row back to fold in memory (`:50-59`). Ranks are distinct and sequential with an ordinal name tie-break, so repeated reads return the same order (`:18-24`, `:65-77`). Only the organizer rollup carries a permission, `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.PointsViewOverview)]` (`PointsController.cs:121`), and even that view returns activity, points and timestamps without attendee identity (`:114-119`).

**Tickets: a TicketLeap roster, from upload to account.** [Ticket](#ticket) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/Ticket.cs:30`) is one row of an organizer-uploaded TicketLeap roster: it keeps the whitelisted columns only and exists to invite the ticket holder and to link the ticket to an account, while door admission stays with TicketLeap (`:12-15`, BR-268, BR-248). It is the module's third [IAuditedEntity](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#iauditedentity), because a disputed link (a barcode claimed by the wrong attendee) needs a record of the row before, and it implements `IAnonymizable` so the `[Pii]` holder fields (attendee name, order email, barcode) are stored redacted in the audit trail and overwritten when the linked account is erased, soft-deleted rows included (`:16-27`, `:56-73`, [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)). The REST surface is two controllers under one `Tickets` prefix, each behind `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.Tickets)]` and `[Authorize]`. [TicketRosterImportController](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketRosterImportController.cs:36`) owns the upload: a dry run answers 200 with the counts, a commit answers 202 with a queued import run whose progress a GET reports, and a second commit while the event's run is active answers 409 (`:24-45`). [TicketsController](#ticketscontroller) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:42`) owns the organizer's invites, link-existing-accounts run, summary, insights and delete, gated on `EngagementPermissions.TicketsManage`, plus the attendee's barcode claim and own tickets, which take the attendee from the token and need no permission (`:26-41`). A committed upload is not applied inside the request. [ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler](#processticketrosterimporthandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ProcessRosterImport/ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:29`) runs as an internal command and applies the run in batches of 100 (`:37`) through the same [TicketRosterApplier](#ticketrosterapplier) rules as the dry run; each batch commits together with the progress on [TicketImportRun](#ticketimportrun), so any replica can read it and a retried attempt resumes where the last one stopped, the per-ticket upsert making a twice-applied batch a no-op. After the last batch the run voids what the file no longer contains, links the holders who already have an account, and completes, which clears the staged roster; any failure ends the run as failed in a fresh scope and still answers success, so the queue does not retry a run that already ended (`:13-27`). Linking has one rule in one place: [TicketLinker](#ticketlinker) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/TicketLinker.cs:32`), a static helper behind [UserRegisteredTicketLinkHandler](#userregisteredticketlinkhandler), [UserEmailVerifiedTicketLinkHandler](#useremailverifiedticketlinkhandler) and [ExistingAccountLinker](#existingaccountlinker), links per event the Live tickets whose attendee name matches the account, otherwise the address's only ticket for that event, otherwise nothing, leaving the tickets for a barcode claim (`:9-18`); it is idempotent under at-least-once delivery, never takes over a ticket linked to another account, and links nothing for an erased account (`:25-30`). The claim, [ClaimTicketHandler](#claimtickethandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ClaimTicket/ClaimTicketHandler.cs:32`), is built not to be an existence oracle: an unknown barcode, a ticket linked to another account and a voided ticket all get the same NotFound, and each account has an attempt budget from [TicketSettings](#ticketsettings) counted in the shared cache before the lookup (`:17-30`). Across the process boundary, [PendingTicketInvitationService](#pendingticketinvitationservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/PendingTicketInvitationService.cs:35`) tells Identity whether an address still holds a standing invitation, so an invite link that expired before the invitee had an account can be re-issued, and its answer never carries the ticket id, the barcode or the order (`:11-31`). The organizer pages [TicketRosterUpload](#ticketrosterupload), [TicketRoster](#ticketroster) and [TicketInsights](#ticketinsights) and the attendee's [MyTicketsPanel](#myticketspanel) call the API through [ITicketUIService](#iticketuiservice) and [TicketService](#ticketservice). The slice is [Rubric §11, Security] (the non-oracle claim and the redacted holder fields), [Rubric §29, Resilience] (the resumable batched import) and [Rubric §30, Compliance and Privacy] (anonymize on erasure).

**Persistence.** Engagement declares no context class of its own. The module contributes only its `IEntityTypeConfiguration` classes, and the framework's one sealed per-engine context over the common [ApplicationDbContext](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#applicationdbcontext) (`SQLServerDbContext` today) builds the model from them and supplies auditing, soft-delete query filters and domain-event dispatch, one instance per physical database ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)). Those configurations cover bookmarks, badges, check-ins, the three live-poll sets, the two question sets, the points ledger, the opt-ins, the erased-account records, and the ticket roster with its import runs ([TicketConfiguration](#ticketconfiguration), [TicketImportRunConfiguration](#ticketimportrunconfiguration)). The newest set closes a gap the erasure handlers cannot: they only reach rows that exist when `UserDeleted` is handled, and an access token stays valid for its whole lifetime after the account is gone, so a late bookmark, badge, check-in, vote, upvote or question would otherwise carry an erased user id no erasure revisits (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/ErasedUsers/ErasedUser.cs:9-14`). [ErasedUser](#eraseduser) (`ErasedUser.cs:20`) is the record of that erasure, holding only `UserId` and `ErasedOn` and no other personal data (`:16`, `:23`, `:26`); the live layer's [UserDeletedSessionQuestionsHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#userdeletedsessionquestionshandler) writes it (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/SessionQuestions/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedSessionQuestionsHandler.cs:108`). [ErasedUserConfiguration](#eraseduserconfiguration) (`.../ErasedUsers/ErasedUserConfiguration.cs:15`) puts a unique index on `UserId` (`:29-30`), so a redelivered `UserDeleted` that raced the existence check fails rather than duplicates, and the same index serves the lookup every guarded write runs (`:11-13`). That lookup is [ErasedUserGuard](#eraseduserguard) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/ErasedUsers/ErasedUserGuard.cs:15`), a static helper with one `EnsureNotErasedAsync` (`:26`) that runs an `ExistsAsync` over the read repository and answers `Error.Forbidden` with the one `Engagement.AccountErased` code (`:18`, `:32-41`); the bookmark, badge, sponsor-visit and room check-in handlers here call it first, as do the live layer's vote, upvote and question-submit handlers. The table shapes are where the module's business rules become enforceable, and every configuration derives from [EntityTypeConfigurationSQLServer<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#entitytypeconfigurationsqlservertentity-tidentifiertype). [UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration](#usersessionbookmarkconfiguration) (`.../UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration.cs:17`) makes BR-21 a filtered unique index over `(UserId, SessionId)` restricted to non-deleted rows (`:31-34`) and adds a `SessionId`-leading index the composite cannot serve (`:36-39`). [CheckInConfiguration](#checkinconfiguration) (`.../CheckInConfiguration.cs:19`) carries three filtered unique indexes, one per scope, with the scope literals kept side by side as named constants because an index filter is SQL and cannot read the enum (`:22-26`, `:48-62`); the sponsor one is the once-per-sponsor cap that makes a shared booth link worth nothing past the first scan (`:58-62`), and two more indexes serve the attendance rollup (`:64-69`). [PointsEntryConfiguration](#pointsentryconfiguration) adds the `UserId`-leading index that makes "my points" a seek (`:50-52`). The live-poll tables follow the same discipline even though their aggregates are taught in [Group 23](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md): [LivePollVoteConfiguration](#livepollvoteconfiguration) (`.../LivePolls/LivePollVoteConfiguration.cs:17`) makes BR-225, one active vote per `(LivePollId, UserId)`, a filtered unique index through the shared `HasSoftDeleteFilter()` helper (`:34-37`), which is the database-level guarantee behind the vote handler's create-or-reactivate dance (`:12-15`), and adds the `(LivePollId, OptionId)` index the tallies group by (`:39-40`). [LivePollConfiguration](#livepollconfiguration) (`.../LivePolls/LivePollConfiguration.cs:16`) indexes `EventId` for the Happening Now and organizer manage views (`:34-35`) and `(SessionId, Status)` for the session Live page and presenter view, the conference-day hot path that previously scanned (`:37-41`), and pins the `Options` navigation to `PropertyAccessMode.Field` so the encapsulated collection cannot silently stop materializing if the property changes shape (`:43-50`). [LivePollOptionConfiguration](#livepolloptionconfiguration) (`.../LivePolls/LivePollOptionConfiguration.cs:10`) is the plain child-entity case: a required text column bounded by the domain's own `LivePollInvariants.OptionTextMaxLength` and the required FK back to its poll (`:18-25`). Cross-module identifiers (`UserId`, `EventId`, `SessionId`, `SponsorId`) are scalar columns throughout, never cross-database foreign keys (`CheckInConfiguration.cs:16-17`). The module owns `ADC_Engagement` and is its sole migrator, applying EF migrations idempotently at startup (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:242-248`, [ADR-030](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/030-startup-sole-migrator.html); the one run that skips the schema step is design-time OpenAPI generation, and only in Development, which a production host can never be talked into, [ADR-122](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/122-dev-only-relaxations-fail-closed.html)), so events serialized into its own outbox during `SaveChangesAsync` never race another service's rows ([ADR-003](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/003-outbox-dual-dispatch.html)).

**How Engagement talks to its neighbors.** Engagement is both a client and a server on the gRPC mesh ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html), [ADR-008](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/008-service-extraction-topology.html)). As a **server**, its in-process [BookmarkCountService](#bookmarkcountservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/Services/BookmarkCountService.cs:11`) answers "how many people bookmarked this session" for Conference's speaker pages, including a batched variant that replaces the caller's per-session fan-out with one grouped COUNT and back-fills a zero for every requested session that has none (`:37-46`). It goes on the wire through [BookmarkCountsGrpcService](#bookmarkcountsgrpcservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Grpc/BookmarkCountsGrpcService.cs:30`) and is consumed through the client-side [BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter.cs:14`), which re-implements the same C# interface so calling code never knows it crossed a process. Read the trust-boundary note before copying the pattern: that endpoint is mapped deliberately **without** `RequireAuthorization()`, because the Conference callers serve `[AllowAnonymous]` output-cached endpoints and a cache-miss request from an anonymous visitor carries no bearer to forward; the exposure is bounded by the payload (aggregate counts, no PII, no user ids) and by an internal-only container ingress. The omission is now stated rather than implied with `.AllowAnonymous()`, because the framework's fallback authorization policy gates every endpoint that declares nothing and would otherwise turn the deliberate omission into a 401 on the public speaker pages (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:250-262`). The identical bridge carries the privacy export, and there the choice flips. [UserEngagementExportService](#userengagementexportservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Exports/UserEngagementExportService.cs:21`) projects a user's bookmarks, submitted questions, points ledger, check-in history, live-poll votes, session-question upvotes and leaderboard participation server-side into a [UserEngagementExportDTO](#userengagementexportdto) of ids and dates (`:22-99`), with soft-deleted rows excluded by the global query filter; check-ins are exported independently of the ledger, because a switched-off rule or a deduped repeat scan means the ledger is no proxy for the attendance record a data subject is entitled to (`:50-52`). The two live-layer rows ride the same projection: a [UserEngagementPollVoteExportDTO](#userengagementpollvoteexportdto) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Exports/UserEngagementPollVoteExportDTO.cs:7`) carries the poll, the chosen option and when, and a [UserEngagementQuestionUpvoteExportDTO](#userengagementquestionupvoteexportdto) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Exports/UserEngagementQuestionUpvoteExportDTO.cs:7`) carries the upvoted question and when, both ids and a date only; a retracted vote or a removed upvote is soft-deleted, so the filter keeps it out like every other kind (`UserEngagementExportService.cs:66-78`). It is served by [UserEngagementExportGrpcService](#userengagementexportgrpcservice) and consumed by Identity through [UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapter](#userengagementexportservicegrpcadapter), and *that* endpoint does carry `RequireAuthorization()` because it returns personal data keyed by a raw user id (`Program.cs:264-271`, PRIVACY.md §7, [ADR-076](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/076-data-subject-export.html), [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)). The Contracts-layer `DependencyInjection` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/DependencyInjection.cs:19`) is what swaps in-process for remote: each helper registers the typed client and then `Replace`s (never `TryAdd`s) the existing registration, so it overwrites both the real service and the disabled stub (`:45-51`), and it must run after `ModuleLoader.DiscoverAndRegister` (`:36-39`).

**The outbound live-channel path.** Engagement never blocks a command on Notification. Handlers enqueue a post-commit broadcast as a [LiveChannelPublishWorkItem](#livechannelpublishworkitem) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Live/ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:10`) through [ILiveChannelPublishQueue](#ilivechannelpublishqueue) (`:21`), a three-string record (channel key, event name, pre-serialized payload) carrying no entity and no per-user data. [LiveChannelPublishQueue](#livechannelpublishqueue) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Live/LiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:14`) is the single concrete channel, registered once as a singleton and exposed to handlers via the interface (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:59-60`). Read its backpressure contract carefully: the channel is bounded at 1024 items (`:18`) with `BoundedChannelFullMode.DropOldest` and `SingleReader` (`:33-40`), so `Enqueue` returns `void` and never rejects an item while the host runs (it evicts the oldest rather than refusing the write; only a write after shutdown has completed the queue is refused, silently, `:50-60`), and a discarded broadcast is observable only through `DroppedCount` (`:47`), the `itemDropped` callback, and a warning log. [LiveChannelPublishProcessor](#livechannelpublishprocessor) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Live/LiveChannelPublishProcessor.cs:41`) is the single-reader `BackgroundService` drain, one of the module's two hosted services (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:26-27`), forwarding items to [ILiveChannelPublisher](group-10-notifications.md#ilivechannelpublisher) in FIFO order: one reader preserves per-session ordering, and the swallow is [BestEffort](group-03-querying-specifications.md#besteffort)'s rather than a hand-rolled catch, so a peer that has quietly stopped accepting broadcasts is countable on the `besteffort.dispatch.failed` meter instead of being a warning nobody alerts on (`:21-28`, `:125`). Shutdown drains rather than drops: `StopAsync` completes the queue first, then publishes whatever is still queued in FIFO order on a token of its own, the whole stop sharing one five-second budget well inside the 30-second Container Apps grace so a hung Notification peer cannot hold the host; the in-flight publish is cancelled and lost, and anything left when the budget runs out is logged and abandoned (`:29-39`, `:50`, `:53-57`). What actually gets published is taught in [Group 23](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md).

**Keeping Conference's bookmark counts fresh.** Bookmark counts are owned here but served by Conference, from an output cache in another process that this side has no handle on, so a count change reaches it as a broker message. [UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler](#usersessionbookmarkcacheevictionhandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/DomainEventHandlers/UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler.cs:38`) subscribes to the aggregate's own [UserSessionBookmarkChanged](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) rather than to a command handler, because the delete path runs on the framework's generic `DeleteEntityCommand` with no ADC handler to hook, and the domain event covers create, reactivate and delete in one class; deferred post-commit dispatch also means no eviction is ever requested for a bookmark that did not persist (`:27-34`). It does not publish anything itself, it only raises a flag (`:54-57`). [BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal](#bookmarkcacheevictionsignal) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/Services/BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:25`) is a capacity-one channel with `BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite` (`:27-33`), registered as a singleton per replica (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:64`), so any number of requests made while one is pending collapse into it and `Request()` never blocks or fails a bookmark command (`:38-42`). The reason is load, stated in the type: every eviction drops the whole `conference:sessions` tag (the session list, the session reads and the batched counts together), and at a session changeover hundreds of stars in the same minute would otherwise keep that cache permanently cold (`:11-19`). [BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor](#bookmarkcacheevictionprocessor) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Caching/BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor.cs:35`), the module's second hosted service, is the single reader: an idle processor broadcasts at once, so an isolated star still reaches a speaker's dashboard in about a broker round trip, and after each broadcast it waits a ten-second `PacingWindow` (`:46`) during which every further request folds into one trailing broadcast (`:17-23`, `:56-79`). The message is an `OutputCacheEvictionRequested` for the tag constant `SessionsCacheTag` (`UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler.cs:45`), published through a scoped `IEventBus` inside `BestEffort.ExecuteAsync`, so a failed publish costs one warning and one metric and never stops the drain; Conference's 60-second TTL stays as the backstop for a dropped message or a request still pending at shutdown (`BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor.cs:25-29`, `:62-77`, `:82-85`).

**Module wiring, feature gating, and the extracted host.** [EngagementModule](#engagementmodule) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:15`) is the [IModule](group-14-module-system-composition.md#imodule) entry point discovered by [ModuleLoader](group-14-module-system-composition.md#moduleloader) and registered in topological order; it declares a dependency on Conference with `RequiresDependencies => true` (`:20`, `:23`), and `Register` is a one-liner into `AddEngagementModule` (`:26-27`), which chains the Application, Infrastructure and API registrations in dependency order (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:26-28`). The Application registration is where the module's own services land: the bookmark aggregate's navigation populator, entity query service and generic delete handler (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:40-42`; the bookmark domain service is static and needs no registration), the two cross-module services scoped (`:43`, `:47`), the awarder scoped and registered by hand because it is a plain service the convention scan does not see (`:78-85`), and everything conventional (handlers, mappers, validators, event handlers) discovered by `ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>()` (`:89`), which is where the per-layer [ClassReference](#classreference) marker earns its keep. Each of the four layers declares its own [AssemblyReference](#assemblyreference) / `ClassReference` pair, and the design-time migrations factory reaches for the *Infrastructure* one, because the `IEntityTypeConfiguration` classes live in Infrastructure rather than Application. When the module is disabled in a host, `RegisterDisabledStubs` swaps in [DisabledBookmarkCountService](#disabledbookmarkcountservice) and [DisabledUserEngagementExportService](#disableduserengagementexportservice) (`EngagementModule.cs:30-34`) so a Conference-only or Identity-only host still resolves those interfaces. Every capability has its own kill switch in [EngagementFeatures](#engagementfeatures) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/EngagementFeatures.cs:10`): `SessionBookmarks`, `LivePolls`, `CheckIn`, `SponsorVisits`, `RoomCheckIn`, `Points`, `SessionQA` and `Tickets` (`:22`, `:34`, `:46`, `:59`, `:71`, `:83`, `:95`, `:108`), each turning its controller or route into a 404 without a deploy. All eight are declared `[FeatureFlag(FeatureFlagLifetime.Permanent, Owner = "ADC Engagement")]` (`:21` and the same attribute above each of the other seven), and an organizer flips one without a new revision through the stored overrides that `AddReloadableFeatureFlags` layers over configuration, served by [AdminFeatureFlagsController](#adminfeatureflagscontroller) at `Admin/Engagement/FeatureFlags` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:124-130`), which is how the flag inventory is told these are shipped capability switches a conference chooses to run with or without, not rollout toggles waiting on a removal date ([ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html)); the two printed-QR switches say so explicitly, `SponsorVisits` naming the softer alternative of setting `Points:SponsorVisit` to 0 to keep the visit but stop the award (`:48-57`) and `RoomCheckIn` recording why it is separate at all, since the two printed surfaces are retired on their own schedules (`:61-70`). Authorization above authentication is capability-based, not role-based: [EngagementPermissions](#engagementpermissions) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Authorization/EngagementPermissions.cs:9`) declares three capabilities, `engagement:live:manage`, `engagement:checkin:manage` and `engagement:points:view-overview` (`:16`, `:23`, `:30`), plus an `All` list so the whole set can be granted in one call (`:33-38`). The grant map itself is a separate named type, [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Authorization/EngagementPermissionGrants.cs:24`), whose static `Apply` grants every Engagement capability to the Organizer role and to no other (`:33-38`); attendee-facing endpoints need no grant because they carry a plain `[Authorize]` with no capability, and a speaker's session-scoped rights come from the speaker-assignment check inside the handlers (BR-236) rather than from any permission declared here (`:26-31`). `AddModuleEngagementAPI` applies that map through `services.AddPermissions(EngagementPermissionGrants.Apply)` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:61`, [ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html)). The reason it is a named map in the Shared contracts project rather than a lambda inside the registration is that two hosts apply the same binding: this module's own host, to gate its `[HasPermission(...)]` endpoints, and the token-minting Identity host, so an issued access token carries a `permission` claim for every Engagement capability the caller's role holds and not only for the modules the minting host happens to boot (`EngagementPermissionGrants.cs:6-22`). `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service` boots exactly this one module and is worth reading top to bottom as the reference shape for an extracted host. Kestrel is configured in one line, `builder.ConfigureEndpointsWithHealthProbe(HttpProtocols.Http2)` (`Program.cs:69`), the shared helper from [KestrelEndpointExtensions](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#kestrelendpointextensions): Http2-only on cleartext so cross-service gRPC clients negotiate h2c by prior knowledge, plus the optional HTTP/1.1-only health-probe listener ([ADR-012](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/012-grpc-host-transport.html)). [PointsSettings](#pointssettings) and [CheckInSettings](#checkinsettings) are bound here rather than in the module, because the module registration takes no `IConfiguration`, and both are deliberately **not** `ValidateOnStart`: a missing section binds working defaults and an explicit `0` is the documented kill switch, so no value an organizer sets should stop this host from booting mid-conference (`:125-136`, a considered divergence from [ADR-070](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/070-fail-fast-configuration-contract.html)). The scheduler and audit trail are wired next (`:198`, `:202`, [ADR-074](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/074-recurring-job-scheduler.html), [ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html)), and [EngagementErrorResources](#engagementerrorresources) contributes the module's error-code translations (`:221`, [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)). Composition itself runs through `AddMmcaApplicationPipeline`, a single ordered chain that registers the modules first and then, because Conference is disabled in this process, re-points Engagement's two Conference dependencies at gRPC clients, swaps the framework's no-op live-channel publisher for the Notification adapter, and finally wires broker messaging (`:218-224`, [ADR-014](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/014-cqrs-decorator-pipeline.html) closes and seals the decorator pipeline at the end of it). This host is not publisher-only: it consumes six integration events (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:24-31`, `Program.cs:185-201`): `AttendeeCheckedIn`, `SessionFeedbackSubmitted` and `EventFeedbackSubmitted` earn points-game points, `UserDeleted` erases the deleted account's Engagement rows, and `UserRegistered` and `UserEmailVerified` link pending tickets to the new account. The one `UserDeleted` registration runs every handler for that type, so it reaches the points, bookmark, badge and ticket erasure handlers here and the session-question and vote erasure handlers of the live layer alike (`Program.cs:193-205`). [AttendeeCheckedIn](#attendeecheckedin) is the novel one: it is published by *this same service* (the [CheckIn](#checkin) factory raises it and the outbox captures it in the check-in transaction), so this is ADC's first broker self-consumption, and MMCA.Common's native broker transport handles it with no special casing: `EngagementBrokerConsumers.Register` subscribes the event to this host's one queue (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:24-26`), each `RegisterIntegrationEventConsumer<TEvent>` call binding the event's topic to that queue (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Messaging/Broker/IBrokerConsumerBuilder.cs:5-8`, `:26`), so the publish goes to the event's topic (or exchange), the queue named by `MessageBus:QueueName` (`mmca-adc-engagement`) receives it, and the message leaves through the broker and comes back to this process; under the InProcess transport the `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` integration tests run on, it is delivered in process instead (`Program.cs:178-183`, `:207-214`). [SelfHttpWarmupTask](#selfhttpwarmuptask) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/SelfHttpWarmupTask.cs:23`) extends [SelfHttpWarmupTaskBase](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#selfhttpwarmuptaskbase) and holds `/health/ready` not-ready until the routing, auth and middleware pipeline has been JITted (`Program.cs:156-160`, [ADR-025](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/025-startup-warmup-readiness.html)); the three gRPC endpoints are mapped last (`:262`, `:271`, `:278`).

**The UI surfaces.** [EngagementUIModule](#engagementuimodule) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementUIModule.cs:22`) implements [IUIModule](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iuimodule) to contribute the module's Blazor assembly (`:33`), the invisible [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener) layout component (`:31`), and six nav items declared as resource keys with the organizer ones carrying a `RequiredRole` so the shared NavMenu hides them from attendees (`:21-29`, [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)); their targets live in [EngagementRoutePaths](#engagementroutepaths) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementRoutePaths.cs:8`), which also holds the two deep-link-only self-service routes that deliberately contribute no nav item at all (`:29-32`). The pages divide by actor. Attendees get [MyBadge](#mybadge) (`Pages/CheckIns/MyBadge.razor.cs:15`), which renders the opaque payload beside the account name as plain text so a human can confirm the badge belongs to its holder (`:11-13`), [MyPoints](#mypoints), and the two QR landing pages [SponsorVisit](#sponsorvisit) (`Pages/CheckIns/Sponsors/SponsorVisit.razor.cs:22`) and [RoomCheckIn](#roomcheckin), which post the write themselves so the whole interaction is one scan with nothing to press; both keep the write off the prerender pass and behind a once-per-instance guard (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:16-19`, `:55-57`) and branch their on-screen state off the server's stable error code carried back by [SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>](#selfcheckinoutcometresult) (`Services/CheckIns/SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:20`) and named in [CheckInErrorCodes](#checkinerrorcodes) (`Services/CheckIns/CheckInErrorCodes.cs:8`), because two of the three refusals share the same 404 status. Organizers get [CheckInScan](#checkinscan) (`Pages/CheckIns/CheckInScan.razor.cs:21`), which loops the shared scanner where a camera exists and falls back to the [AttendeeSearchPanel](#attendeesearchpanel) name and email search everywhere else (`:16-19`, `:46`), [OrganizerAttendance](#organizerattendance) and [OrganizerPointsOverview](#organizerpointsoverview). The two feedback pages, [EventFeedback](#eventfeedback) (`Pages/Feedback/EventFeedback.razor.cs:20`) and [SessionFeedback](#sessionfeedback) (`Pages/Feedback/SessionFeedback.razor.cs:19`), render a dynamic question form whose definitions and answers belong to Conference, with per-question values held in a [FeedbackAnswerModel](#feedbackanswermodel) (`Pages/Feedback/FeedbackAnswerModel.cs:24`) whose DataAnnotations are the single declaration of the 4000-character free-text rule (`:31-35`). Both submit the same way. Before anything is sent, the page flags every required question left unanswered, for every question type, because MudForm already blocks an empty required text field but not an unset rating (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:188-203`, `:217-221`, `SessionFeedback.razor.cs:217-232`, `:246-250`). It then collects every answered question and posts the whole form as one POST-as-upsert the server applies atomically, so a refusal wrote nothing, there is no partially saved state to report, and the form stays dirty for the same Submit button to retry; a form with nothing answered that passes the required check stays a local no-op rather than a request the batch endpoint would refuse as empty (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:229-248`, `SessionFeedback.razor.cs:258-277`, BR-107). The contracts say so on the batch member of [IEventFeedbackUIService](#ieventfeedbackuiservice) and its session sibling (`Services/Feedback/IFeedbackUIService.cs:32-36`, `:66-70`), and [EventFeedbackService](#eventfeedbackservice) mints the idempotency key once, outside its retry pipeline, so a timed-out submit that retries is recognized by the server rather than re-applying the form (`Services/Feedback/EventFeedbackService.cs:54-58`). Behind the pages sit ordinary authenticated HTTP clients built on [AuthenticatedServiceBase](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#authenticatedservicebase): the cross-module [SessionBookmarkUIService](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) (whose three bookmark HTTP calls sit in [BookmarkApiClient](#bookmarkapiclient), `Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkApiClient.cs:21`, shared with [BookmarkCreateReplayHandler](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler) and [BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler](#bookmarkdeletereplayhandler), which replay a toggle queued offline under the versioned write kinds and the per-user, per-session coalesce key of [BookmarkOfflineWrites](#bookmarkofflinewrites), `Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkOfflineWrites.cs:5-23`; each constructs the client rather than resolving it, because a shared registration would close a DI circle through the offline write queue, `BookmarkApiClient.cs:10-14`; the toggle service also feeds [SessionReminderCoordinator](#sessionremindercoordinator) and the pure [SessionReminderPlanner](#sessionreminderplanner), whose [SessionReminder](#sessionreminder) records carry a stable notification id so rescheduling replaces rather than duplicates, `Services/HappeningNow/SessionReminderPlanner.cs:15`, `:39`, `:41-48`, [ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html)), [CheckInService](#checkinservice), [PointsService](#pointsservice), [AttendeeLookupService](#attendeelookupservice) (whose by-identifier lookup is answered from a roster snapshot because the Identity users endpoint filters by name and email but cannot be queried by identifier, `Services/Lookups/AttendeeLookupService.cs:11-15`), and [NowNextService](#nownextservice) behind [INowNextService](#inownextservice), which mirrors the Conference API's now-next wire shape locally rather than referencing `Conference.Shared` for one payload (`Services/HappeningNow/INowNextService.cs:6-9`). The conference-day pages taught in [Group 23](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md) get their client layer from here too, and it is the same shape. [LivePollUIService](#livepolluiservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LivePollUIService.cs:14`) and [SessionQuestionUIService](#sessionquestionuiservice) (`Services/SessionLive/SessionQuestionUIService.cs:15`) are `AuthenticatedServiceBase` clients over the Gateway's `livepolls` and `sessionquestions` routes (`:19` in each), and their contracts [ILivePollUIService](#ilivepolluiservice) (`Services/SessionLive/ILivePollUIService.cs:15`) and [ISessionQuestionUIService](#isessionquestionuiservice) (`Services/SessionLive/ISessionQuestionUIService.cs:15`) both open with the rule that keeps a live page calm: every member answers with a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), so a server refusal is data the page renders rather than an exception, and only the caller's own cancellation still propagates (`ILivePollUIService.cs:10-13`, `ISessionQuestionUIService.cs:10-13`). Both also say in the contract that the API enforces the manage and moderation rights regardless of what the UI chooses to render (`ILivePollUIService.cs:7-9`, `ISessionQuestionUIService.cs:7-9`), which is the only safe way to write a doc comment about a permission a browser can be told to ignore. [LiveEventService](#liveeventservice) behind [ILiveEventUIService](#iliveeventuiservice) (`Services/SessionLive/LiveEventService.cs:17`, `Services/SessionLive/ILiveEventUIService.cs:7`) resolves the currently-live-or-next published event from the Conference API and computes its window with the same math the backend enforces, then degrades to `null` on any API failure so the live layer simply stays dormant instead of erroring a page (`LiveEventService.cs:9-16`, `:38-42`); the [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext) record it returns (`Services/SessionLive/LiveEventContext.cs:13`) answers `IsLiveAt` and `ToEventLocal` for the pages, and its zone id always resolves because the Conference write path guards it (`:20-31`). [SessionLiveUIService](#sessionliveuiservice) (`Services/SessionLive/SessionLiveUIService.cs:10`) is the smallest type in the chapter and the clearest one about module boundaries: it implements the [ISessionLiveUIService](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#isessionliveuiservice) extension point with a single line returning Engagement's own route (`:13-14`), so a Conference session page lights up its Live button only when this module is present. [SessionLookupService](#sessionlookupservice) behind [ISessionLookupService](#isessionlookupservice) (`Services/Lookups/SessionLookupService.cs:13`, `Services/Lookups/ISessionLookupService.cs:19`) is the enrichment client that turns session ids into the titles and times the bookmark surfaces display, projecting the Conference page into a session-keyed dictionary of the small [SessionInfo](#sessioninfo) record (`ISessionLookupService.cs:9`, `SessionLookupService.cs:25-41`); its contract carries the usage rule as well as the signature, because the catalog call is cheap to misuse: `GetAllAsync` is for a page that genuinely needs every session (the reminder planner, which schedules against every bookmarked one), and a single-session page must call `GetByIdAsync` rather than transfer the catalog to label one row (`ISessionLookupService.cs:21-28`). The comment above the fetch is worth keeping when you copy it: the base `sessions` endpoint serves one page capped at the framework's 500-row maximum over every edition's catalog sorted by start time, so a single page would silently drop the current event's sessions once the catalog passes 500; the lookup therefore walks the Id-sorted lookup URL with `PagedReadAll` until the reported total, as the Conference speaker and event lookups do (`SessionLookupService.cs:20-25`). One more UI type is easy to miss and easy to get wrong: [CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider](#currenteventnotificationscopeprovider) (`Services/Notifications/CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider.cs:30`) scopes ADC's notifications to `event:{EventId}`, caching a resolved key for five minutes because the bell polls every 30 seconds (`:41`), and it never answers `null`: on `INotificationScopeProvider` a null key means *unscoped*, which would widen an attendee's inbox to every event, so an instance that has never resolved an event answers with a well-formed key no row carries (`:20-24`, `:35-39`), failing to an empty inbox rather than to everyone's.

**Rubric lens.** This module is a compact end-to-end illustration of most of Part A. Five small aggregates whose rules live in factories and invariants are the [Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design] story; the controller-handler-domain-service split and the one-slice-per-folder layout are [Rubric §5, Vertical Slice] and [Rubric §6, CQRS and Event-Driven], with the points adapters showing both dispatch styles (broker integration events and an in-process domain event) side by side and stating the trade-off in code. The gRPC adapters, disabled stubs and `Replace`-based composition are [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness] and [Rubric §9, API and Contract Design]; the per-service database, the filtered unique indexes carrying idempotency, anti-farming and one-vote-per-poll, and the pushed-down grouped COUNT and SUM in the attendance and leaderboard reads are [Rubric §8, Data Architecture] and [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]. Security ([Rubric §11]) is the recurring theme rather than a bolt-on: identity taken from the token instead of the body on every self-service path, the 404-not-403 delete, indistinguishable answers for a bad payload and an unknown credential, server-resolved room sessions, a bearer credential minted from a non-monotonic Guid, and one documented unauthenticated-by-necessity gRPC endpoint. The drop-oldest publish queue with its dropped-count meter and draining shutdown, and the coalesced, paced bookmark cache eviction, are [Rubric §29, Resilience] and [Rubric §13, Observability and Operability], as is the live client layer's `Result`-only surface and its dormant-rather-than-broken answer when the event lookup fails; per-capability feature flags plus a retunable points economy with per-rule kill switches are [Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability] and [Rubric §17, DevOps]; the export projection and the leaderboard name erasure are [Rubric §30, Compliance and Privacy]. The pages extend the story into Part B ([Rubric §18, UI Architecture], [Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety] for the single-declaration answer model, and [Rubric §25, Navigation and IA] for the deep-link-only QR routes). Relevant ADRs, roughly in the order they surface above: [ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html) (audit trail), [ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html) (owner-or-admin filter), [ADR-017](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/017-request-idempotency.html) (request idempotency), [ADR-001](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/001-manual-dto-mapping.html) (Mapperly mapping), [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html) and [ADR-003](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/003-outbox-dual-dispatch.html) (outbox), [ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html) and ### AssemblyReference

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/AssemblyReference.cs:5` · Level 0 · class (static)
>
> *One byte-identical copy per Engagement layer.* This section covers the API and Application copies; the Domain, Infrastructure, Shared, and UI copies are the same type in another part of this chapter.

- **What it is**: a tiny static class that exposes the assembly it lives in (`Assembly`) plus that assembly's simple name (`AssemblyName`), so anything that needs to say "scan the assembly this type belongs to" has a compiled, refactor-safe anchor instead of a namespace string.

  | Type | File:Line | Notes (what differs) |
  |------|-----------|----------------------|
  | `AssemblyReference` (API) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/AssemblyReference.cs:5` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API` (`:3`) |
  | `AssemblyReference` (Application) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/AssemblyReference.cs:5` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application` (`:3`) |

  Nothing else differs: both files are eleven lines long and declare the same two fields at the same line numbers.
- **Depends on**: `System.Reflection.Assembly` (BCL) only, imported at line 1 of each file. No first-party dependencies, which is why both copies sit at Level 0.
- **Concept, assembly-marker types for convention scanning.** The framework-level explanation lives with the shared copy in [AssemblyReference](group-14-module-system-composition.md#assemblyreference); these are the Engagement-local instances of the same idiom. `[Rubric §2, Design Patterns]` assesses whether recurring problems are solved with a recognized idiom: handing an `Assembly` to a scanner through a purpose-built token, rather than through some incidental business class, is that idiom. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` (Dependency Inversion) applies too: registration and configuration code depends on this deliberate marker, not on `typeof(SomeHandler).Assembly`, so renaming or moving a real type never silently breaks a scan.
- **Walkthrough**: two `public static readonly` fields, resolved once at type initialization and identical in both copies. `Assembly` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/AssemblyReference.cs:7`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/AssemblyReference.cs:7`) captures `typeof(AssemblyReference).Assembly`. `AssemblyName` (line 8 of each file) reads `Assembly.GetName().Name ?? string.Empty`, the null-coalesce keeping the field non-null under nullable-reference-type analysis even if the runtime reports no simple name. There are no methods and no other state.
- **Why it's built this way**: each layer can be scanned from inside itself without a cross-layer reference, and a compiled `typeof` cannot go stale the way a hardcoded assembly-name string would. The Engagement module declares the pair once per scannable layer, which is why the same two type names recur across the chapter.
- **Where it's used**: the convention scan the Application layer runs takes the companion [ClassReference](#classreference) rather than the static class, because a static class cannot be a generic type argument (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`). The static handle is the shape used where an `Assembly` value is passed by hand, for example the design-time EF factories and the architecture-fitness map.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: neither of these two copies has a reader inside the Engagement API or Application projects themselves; they exist so that every layer carries the same anchor.

### ClassReference

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/AssemblyReference.cs:11` · Level 0 · class
>
> *One byte-identical copy per Engagement layer.* This section covers the API and Application copies.

- **What it is**: the non-static companion to [AssemblyReference](#assemblyreference), an empty instantiable class declared at the bottom of the same file. It supplies an assembly anchor for the APIs that need a *generic type argument*, which a static class can never satisfy.

  | Type | File:Line | Notes (what differs) |
  |------|-----------|----------------------|
  | `ClassReference` (API) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/AssemblyReference.cs:11` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API` |
  | `ClassReference` (Application) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/AssemblyReference.cs:11` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application` |

- **Depends on**: nothing first-party, and nothing from the BCL beyond `object`.
- **Concept**: the companion half of the marker pattern, introduced at framework level under [ClassReference](group-14-module-system-composition.md#classreference). C# forbids a static class as a generic type argument, and the registration helper the modules use takes its marker as a type parameter, so a second, non-static token fills that slot without weakening `AssemblyReference`'s static-ness. `[Rubric §33, Developer Experience]` assesses how much ceremony the inner loop costs: one conventional token per layer is the whole of it.
- **Walkthrough**: `public class ClassReference { }` at line 11 of both files. No members, no behavior; its only meaningful property is the assembly it belongs to, read as `typeof(ClassReference).Assembly` by a scanner.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the two forms separate sidesteps the static-class generic-argument restriction while leaving [AssemblyReference](#assemblyreference) impossible to instantiate by accident. Every layer declares its own copy so it scans itself with a local token.
- **Where it's used**: the Application-layer copy is the one with a call site: `services.ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>()` in the Application [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`), which registers domain event handlers, DTO and request mappers, command and query handlers, and validators by convention.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the API-layer copy has no reader in the repo; it exists to keep the per-layer convention uniform.

### EngagementErrorResources

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Resources` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Resources/EngagementErrorResources.cs:9` · Level 0 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: an empty sealed class that serves as the *resource anchor type* for the Engagement module's localized error-code translations. It carries no members; its job is to name the `.resx` family that sits beside it.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party in code. Its behavioral partners are the shared [ErrorLocalizer](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#errorlocalizer) infrastructure (through the [IErrorLocalizer](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#ierrorlocalizer) contract) and the `AddErrorResources<T>()` host registration helper, both named in the type's doc comment.
- **Concept, resource-anchor types for per-module error localization.** `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` assesses whether user-facing strings are externalized and culture-resolved rather than hard-coded. The doc comment (`EngagementErrorResources.cs:3-8`) states the mechanism: the type's `.resx` siblings (`EngagementErrorResources.resx` for the invariant culture, `EngagementErrorResources.es.resx` for Spanish) are keyed by a domain error's `Code`, and the shared `IErrorLocalizer` resolves a failing [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result)'s code to a translated message once the host registers this type via `AddErrorResources<EngagementErrorResources>()`. That is [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html) applied per module: the class is empty because a resource anchor only needs a stable full name from which the resource base name is computed.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed class EngagementErrorResources` with an empty body (`EngagementErrorResources.cs:9-11`), no members. `sealed` because it is never meant to be subclassed; it exists purely as a `typeof` handle for the resource manager.
- **Why it's built this way**: one anchor per module keeps error strings out of a single monolithic resource file, so each bounded context owns its own translation table ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)). The type lives in the API layer because that is where errors become HTTP responses.
- **Where it's used**: registered by the Engagement service host through `AddErrorResources<EngagementErrorResources>()`; read by the shared [ErrorLocalizer](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#errorlocalizer) when mapping a domain error code to a message. The codes it translates are the ones the handlers raise, for example `CheckIns.Forbidden` and `CheckIns.BadgeConflict` in [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) and `CheckIns.EventNotPublished` in [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the `.resx` files themselves and the host registration call live outside this `.cs` file; only the anchor type is verified here, the rest is quoted from its doc comment.

### GetAttendanceStatsQuery

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.GetAttendanceStats` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/GetAttendanceStats/GetAttendanceStatsQuery.cs:8` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the read request behind the organizer dashboard's attendance rollup for one event: how many people arrived at the event, plus a count for each session that has at least one session-scoped check-in.
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias only (an identifier type alias linked solution-wide, see [primer §4](00-primer.md#4-c-build-and-code-style-conventions)). Paired with [GetAttendanceStatsHandler](#getattendancestatshandler) through the query contract, and answered as an [AttendanceStatsDTO](#attendancestatsdto).
- **Concept, the CQRS query as an immutable record.** This is a vertical-slice read: the query type and its handler live in the same `UseCases/GetAttendanceStats/` folder. `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses whether reads and writes are modeled as distinct messages; this is a pure read, so the pipeline runs it without a transaction. `[Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]` assesses feature-folder cohesion, which the layout embodies. `record class` gives value equality and immutability for free, so the message is safe to pass and compare.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record class GetAttendanceStatsQuery(EventIdentifierType EventId)` (`GetAttendanceStatsQuery.cs:8`), one positional parameter and no body. The XML doc (`GetAttendanceStatsQuery.cs:3-7`) fixes the contract: an event-scoped arrival count plus a per-session count for every session that has at least one session-scoped check-in.
- **Why it's built this way**: the whole request is one event id, so the record is a one-line declaration; naming the message explicitly still lets the query pipeline decorate it uniformly and keeps the read intent greppable.
- **Where it's used**: constructed by [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) on `GET /api/checkins/stats` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:221`) from a `[FromQuery, Required] EventIdentifierType eventId` argument (`CheckInsController.cs:217`), on an endpoint gated by `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage)]` (`CheckInsController.cs:213`), and dispatched through the injected [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) (`CheckInsController.cs:47`).
