### GetMyBadgeQuery

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.GetMyBadge` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/GetMyBadge/GetMyBadgeQuery.cs:12` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the read request for the caller's own *existing* badge. The doc comment (`GetMyBadgeQuery.cs:3-6`) names it the read path of `GET /checkins/my-badge`, the path that never mints.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. Paired with [GetMyBadgeHandler](#getmybadgehandler) through [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) and answered as a [MyBadgeDTO](#mybadgedto).
- **Concept introduced, the deliberately empty query.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether a caller can reach data that is not theirs. The doc (`GetMyBadgeQuery.cs:7-10`) says the record is empty for the same reason as the mint command [GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand](#getorcreatemybadgecommand): the attendee is the caller, read from the token by the handler, never a client-supplied id. A message with no id field cannot be used to ask for someone else's badge. `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses whether reads and writes are distinct messages: splitting this read out of the mint command is what lets a read-only "View as" session, for which every command (the mint included) is refused, still read the attendee's badge (`GetMyBadgeQuery.cs:4-6`).
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record class GetMyBadgeQuery;` (`GetMyBadgeQuery.cs:12`), no positional parameters and no body. `record class` keeps it consistent with the module's other request messages even though there is no state to compare.
- **Why it's built this way**: the endpoint reads first and mints only on a miss, so the read needs its own message rather than a flag on the command; keeping it parameterless means the identity rule lives in exactly one place, the handler.
- **Where it's used**: constructed as `new GetMyBadgeQuery()` in `CheckInsController.GetMyBadgeAsync` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:68`) on `[HttpGet("my-badge")]` (`CheckInsController.cs:60`), dispatched through the injected `IQueryHandler<GetMyBadgeQuery, Result<MyBadgeDTO>>` (`CheckInsController.cs:43`); also built directly by the handler tests (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/CheckIns/UseCases/GetMyBadgeHandlerTests.cs:27`).

### RecordedCheckIn

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:38` · Level 0 · record struct (internal readonly)

- **What it is**: the two-field outcome of a check-in write, nested inside [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor): whether a check-in for the same target already existed, and the timestamp that applies (the original one when it did, the newly written one when it did not).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. Only `bool` and `DateTimeOffset` from the BCL. It is produced by `CheckInProcessor.RecordAsync` and consumed by the three writers that call it.
- **Concept introduced, the small internal result type that keeps a shared helper honest.** A `RecordAsync` that returned only a timestamp would force each caller to re-derive "was this a repeat", and one that returned a full DTO would force every caller into the same response shape even though the room path, the sponsor path, and the organizer path each answer with a different DTO. This record struct is the middle ground: it carries exactly the two facts the shared write half knows, and each caller maps them into its own contract. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether a contract carries what it means and nothing more, which is what two named components buy here (`AlreadyRecorded`, `RecordedOn`) over a `bool`/`DateTimeOffset` tuple. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` is the reason it is a `readonly record struct` rather than a class: the value is created on every check-in, has no identity, and is never mutated, so it stays on the stack. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`: `internal` keeps it a module-private detail, so no API-layer contract can accidentally start depending on it.
- **Walkthrough**: one declaration, `internal readonly record struct RecordedCheckIn(bool AlreadyRecorded, DateTimeOffset RecordedOn)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:38`), with the per-parameter docs directly above it (`CheckInProcessor.cs:35-37`): `AlreadyRecorded` is true when a prior check-in for the same target was found, and `RecordedOn` is that prior check-in's timestamp, or the timestamp of the one just written. Both construction sites are inside `RecordAsync`: the short-circuit path builds `new RecordedCheckIn(AlreadyRecorded: true, existing.CheckedInOn)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:76`) and the write path builds `new RecordedCheckIn(AlreadyRecorded: false, checkIn.CheckedInOn)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:112`). Both use named arguments, so the boolean at the call site says what it means.
- **Why it's built this way**: idempotency is the whole point of the check-in write (a repeat scan must not double count), so the outcome type has to make "this was a repeat" a first-class fact rather than something a caller infers. Returning the *original* timestamp on a repeat is what lets a UI show the attendee when they actually checked in rather than when they rescanned.
- **Where it's used**: returned as `Result<RecordedCheckIn>` from `CheckInProcessor.RecordAsync` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:60`). Three call sites unwrap it: [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor)'s own `ExecuteAsync` maps it onto a [CheckInResultDTO](#checkinresultdto) (`CheckInProcessor.cs:163-169`), [RecordRoomCheckInHandler](#recordroomcheckinhandler) maps it onto a `RoomCheckInResultDTO` and suppresses its log line when `AlreadyRecorded` is true (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/RecordRoomCheckIn/RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:121-133`), and [RecordSponsorVisitHandler](#recordsponsorvisithandler) does the same into a `SponsorVisitResultDTO` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/RecordSponsorVisit/RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:90-100`).

### EngagementModule

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:15` · Level 5 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the [IModule](group-14-module-system-composition.md#imodule) implementation for the Engagement bounded context, the type [ModuleLoader](group-14-module-system-composition.md#moduleloader) discovers by reflection and uses to slot Engagement into the application in dependency order.
- **Depends on**: [IModule](group-14-module-system-composition.md#imodule) (the contract), [ApplicationSettings](group-14-module-system-composition.md#applicationsettings), the API-layer [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection) extension (`AddEngagementModule`), and the three disabled-stub pairs it registers when Engagement is not co-hosted: [IBookmarkCountService](#ibookmarkcountservice) / [DisabledBookmarkCountService](#disabledbookmarkcountservice), [IUserEngagementExportService](#iuserengagementexportservice) / [DisabledUserEngagementExportService](#disableduserengagementexportservice), and [IPendingTicketInvitationService](#ipendingticketinvitationservice) / [DisabledPendingTicketInvitationService](#disabledpendingticketinvitationservice) (imported from the Shared project's `Tickets.Invitations` namespace, `EngagementModule.cs:4`).
- **Concept, the module descriptor and its declared dependency on Conference.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses whether a modular monolith can be split into services without a rewrite; a module that declares its dependencies *and* can register disabled stubs for modules that are not co-hosted is exactly that boundary. Engagement names `Conference` as a dependency (`EngagementModule.cs:21`) and sets `RequiresDependencies => true` (`EngagementModule.cs:24`), so the loader orders Conference before Engagement in its topological (Kahn) sort. When Engagement runs as its own service, Conference is not in-process and the cross-module contracts are satisfied by gRPC clients instead ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html) / [ADR-008](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/008-service-extraction-topology.html)); conversely, in a host where Engagement is off, `RegisterDisabledStubs` supplies no-op implementations so a dependent module's calls into Engagement's bookmark count, data-subject export and pending ticket invitation lookup still resolve.
- **Walkthrough**: five members implementing [IModule](group-14-module-system-composition.md#imodule).
  - `Name => "Engagement"` (`EngagementModule.cs:18`): the module's identity in the loader's graph.
  - `Dependencies => ["Conference"]` (`EngagementModule.cs:21`): the modules that must register first.
  - `RequiresDependencies => true` (`EngagementModule.cs:24`): declares the Conference dependency mandatory, not optional.
  - `Register(...)` (`EngagementModule.cs:27-28`): an expression body delegating the whole wiring to `services.AddEngagementModule(applicationSettings)` in the API [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection). Note the signature also receives an `IConfigurationBuilder`, which this module does not use.
  - `RegisterDisabledStubs(...)` (`EngagementModule.cs:31-36`): registers three singletons for hosts where Engagement is off, `IBookmarkCountService` as [DisabledBookmarkCountService](#disabledbookmarkcountservice) (line 33), `IUserEngagementExportService` as [DisabledUserEngagementExportService](#disableduserengagementexportservice) (line 34), and `IPendingTicketInvitationService` as [DisabledPendingTicketInvitationService](#disabledpendingticketinvitationservice) (line 35). Each mirrors a cross-module service the Application-layer [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection-1) registers for real when Engagement is co-hosted.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the module's shape (name, dependencies, register, disabled stubs) behind one contract lets the loader treat every module uniformly, and lets a module run in-process or as an extracted service without changing its business code ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html) / [ADR-008](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/008-service-extraction-topology.html)). The doc comment (`EngagementModule.cs:11-14`) records that the module depends on Conference for session data.
- **Where it's used**: instantiated and invoked by [ModuleLoader](group-14-module-system-composition.md#moduleloader) during host startup; its `Register` routes into the API [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection).

### GetMyBadgeHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.GetMyBadge` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/GetMyBadge/GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:17` · Level 9 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the query handler for [GetMyBadgeQuery](#getmybadgequery). It returns the caller's existing badge credential without writing anything, or a `NotFound` failure when no badge has been issued yet (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:11-16`).
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) and [ICurrentUserService](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice) through its primary constructor (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:17-19`); the `RequireUserId` member of [CurrentUserServiceExtensions](group-06-validation.md#currentuserserviceextensions) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Extensions/CurrentUserServiceExtensions.cs:35`); the [AttendeeBadge](#attendeebadge) aggregate read through an [IReadRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ireadrepositorytentity-tidentifiertype); [MyBadgeDTO](#mybadgedto); and [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) / [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). It implements [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:19`).
- **Concept introduced, read first and mint only on a miss.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`, `[Rubric §11, Security]`. The class doc (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:11-16`) states the split: the controller tries this read first and falls back to the mint command only for a caller allowed to write, so a "View as" session shows the attendee's badge read-only, or the "no badge yet" state, instead of the command refusal. The identity comes from the token (`RequireUserId`, line 29), never from the request, so no caller can read another attendee's credential. The comment at `GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:43-44` adds the data-minimization rule: only the credential leaves the handler, exactly as from the mint command, so the QR code built from it stays opaque to anyone who scans it.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `BadgeNotIssuedCode = "CheckIns.BadgeNotIssued"` (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:22`): a public constant so the tests (and any caller) can match the "no badge yet" outcome by code rather than by message.
  - `HandleAsync` (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:25-27`) resolves the caller with `currentUserService.RequireUserId("CheckIns.Forbidden")` (line 29) and returns its errors unchanged when there is no authenticated user (lines 30-33).
  - It reads the badge through `GetReadRepository<AttendeeBadge, AttendeeBadgeIdentifierType>()` with `FirstOrDefaultAsync(b => b.UserId == userId, asTracking: false, ...)` (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:36-41`): an untracked read, so nothing enters the change tracker.
  - A miss returns `Error.NotFoundError` with code `BadgeNotIssuedCode`, message "No badge has been issued for this account yet.", source `nameof(GetMyBadgeHandler)` and target `nameof(MyBadgeDTO.Credential)` (`GetMyBadgeHandler.cs:45-50`); a hit returns `new MyBadgeDTO { Credential = badge.Credential }` (line 51).
- **Why it's built this way**: the badge endpoint must behave for both a real attendee (who gets a badge minted on first use) and a support session viewing as that attendee (who must never cause a write). Making the read a separate query with a typed `NotFound` gives the controller one clean signal to branch on, and leaves the mint command untouched.
- **Where it's used**: injected into [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:43`). `GetMyBadgeAsync` returns the badge on success (`CheckInsController.cs:71-74`); on a `NotFound` for a caller who is not a "View as" session it falls through to the [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) mint (`CheckInsController.cs:82-87`), and otherwise surfaces the failure (`CheckInsController.cs:76-80`), which the badge page renders as its "no badge yet" state. Registered by the convention scan in the Application-layer [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection-1) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`). Covered by `GetMyBadgeHandlerTests` (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/CheckIns/UseCases/GetMyBadgeHandlerTests.cs:17`), including the cases that a caller never reads another attendee's badge (line 50) and that a missing user is refused (line 62).

### CheckInProcessor

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:23` · Level 11 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: the check-in core every check-in entry point runs: validate the target, short-circuit a repeat check-in, otherwise record one. It is split into a write half (`RecordAsync`, shared by all four writers) and an organizer-path half (`ExecuteAsync`, which resolves the target through Conference first), plus one shared error factory.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), Conference's [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice), the [CheckIn](#checkin) aggregate and its [CheckInScope](#checkinscope) discriminator, [CheckInResultDTO](#checkinresultdto), [CheckInErrorCodes](#checkinerrorcodes) for the shared error code, the read surface [IEntityQuerier<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ientityqueriertentity-tidentifiertype) obtained through `GetRepository`, and [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) / [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). Externals: `System.Linq.Expressions` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:1`) and `TimeProvider`.
- **Concept introduced, the static collaborator-passing helper.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]`, `[Rubric §14, Testability]`. The class doc (`CheckInProcessor.cs:10-22`) explains the shape: it is a static helper rather than an injected service so no handler gains a dependency it does not own. Each caller passes the collaborators it already holds ([IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), the validation service, a `TimeProvider`), which keeps the rule in one place without adding an interface, a registration, and a mock to every test. The cost is that it cannot be substituted in a unit test: a test of [CheckInAttendeeHandler](#checkinattendeehandler) exercises this code too, so the handler tests are where its branches are covered.
- **Concept, idempotency as an application rule with a database backstop.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`, `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`. The `RecordAsync` remarks (`CheckInProcessor.cs:43-50`) state the full model: a repeat scan reports the original check-in instead of writing a second row or publishing a second integration event; the filtered unique indexes from [CheckInConfiguration](#checkinconfiguration) are the race backstop for two concurrent scans of the same badge, room or booth: the losing save is refused rather than duplicating, and the loser then reports the winner's row exactly as a repeat does. The unit of work classifies the refusal because it implements [IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector) (`unitOfWork is IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector detector`, `CheckInProcessor.cs:95-96`), and any other save failure propagates. Those indexes are one per scope: `(UserId, EventId)` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/CheckIns/CheckInConfiguration.cs:50-52`), `(UserId, SessionId)` (`:54-56`), and `(UserId, SponsorId)` (`:60-62`), each `IsUnique()` with a soft-delete filter plus a scope filter, which is exactly the three-way split `FindExistingAsync` mirrors in LINQ.
- **Concept, the caller's event id is not trusted for a session check-in.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`. `ExecuteAsync` takes the resolved event from the validation result, not from the request (`CheckInProcessor.cs:148`), and the comment above it (`CheckInProcessor.cs:144-147`) gives the failure mode it prevents: a stale event context on the organizer's screen would file the attendance under the wrong event, where the rollup [GetAttendanceStatsHandler](#getattendancestatshandler) runs would never find it again.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `EventNotPublished(string source)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:29-33`): the shared "the owning event is not published" failure, `Error.Validation` with code `CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:30`) and target `nameof(CheckIn.EventId)`. The code is a constant on [CheckInErrorCodes](#checkinerrorcodes), whose value is `"CheckIns.EventNotPublished"` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInErrorCodes.cs:10`), so a client can match the code against the Shared constant instead of repeating the string. The architecture error catalog lists it as a code deliberately shared by this class, the room check-in handler and the sponsor visit handler (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.ADC.Architecture.Tests/Contracts/ErrorCatalogTests.cs:75`). `source` is a parameter (documented at `:26-28`) so the error still names the entry point the caller used, which is why the two attendee-path handlers can raise the identical error from their own code.
  - `RecordedCheckIn` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:38`): the nested outcome type, covered in its own section above.
  - `RecordAsync(...)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:60-113`): nine parameters, no state. It resolves the writable repository (line 71), looks for an existing check-in for the same target (line 73) and returns `AlreadyRecorded: true` with the *original* timestamp when it finds one (`CheckInProcessor.cs:74-77`); otherwise it calls `CheckIn.Create(...)` with `timeProvider.GetUtcNow()` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:79-86`), unwraps the factory result with `createResult.TryGetValue(out var checkIn)` and returns the factory's errors on failure (lines 87-88), and adds and saves inside a `try` (lines 90-94). The `catch` filter (lines 95-96) is the lost-race path: the comment (lines 98-104) explains that the attendee IS checked in, so the caller gets the same answer a sequential repeat gets rather than a raw 409. It re-reads the row untracked through `FindExistingAsync` (line 105); if the re-read finds nothing the violation is not this race and `throw` rethrows it unchanged (lines 106-107), otherwise it returns `AlreadyRecorded: true` with the winner's timestamp (line 109). `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`. A clean insert returns `AlreadyRecorded: false` (line 112). Note it takes both `sessionId` and `sponsorId` as nullable parameters, so all three scopes go through this one write.
  - `ExecuteAsync(...)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:129-170`): the organizer path. It validates the target first (lines 140-142), takes `resolvedEventId` from the validation result (line 148), delegates the write to `RecordAsync` with `sponsorId: null` (lines 150-159), propagates a write failure (lines 160-161), and maps the outcome onto a [CheckInResultDTO](#checkinresultdto) carrying `UserId`, `AlreadyCheckedIn`, and `CheckedInOn` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:164-169`).
  - `ValidateTargetAsync(...)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:181-208`): for a session scope it calls `GetSessionLiveInfoAsync` and returns the session's own `EventId` (lines 188-198); otherwise `GetEventLiveInfoAsync` and returns the requested event id (lines 200-207). Each path unwraps the Conference answer with `TryGetValue` (`sessionLive` at line 191, `eventLive` at line 201), returns the lookup errors unchanged on failure, and then runs the published check. The doc comment (`CheckInProcessor.cs:172-180`) records a deliberate v1 omission: the live window is **not** enforced, because an organizer scanning badges at the door or in the room works ahead of and behind the published clock, so a window check would reject legitimate check-ins; only the published and eligible facts gate the write.
  - `EnsureEventIsPublished(bool isPublished)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:210-213`): success, or `EventNotPublished(nameof(CheckInProcessor))`.
  - `FindExistingAsync(...)` (`CheckInProcessor.cs:221-237`, a non-`async` method returning the repository's `Task` directly): a `switch` expression picks the scope-specific predicate (lines 230-235) and hands it to `FirstOrDefaultAsync` with `asTracking: false` (line 236), correct here because the existing row is only inspected, never mutated (which is also why the race path's re-read reports only the stored winner). The three predicate builders are `SameSession` (line 239), `SameSponsor` (line 242), and `SameEvent` (line 245); each pins `c.Scope` as well as the target id, so a read can never cross scopes. The doc (`CheckInProcessor.cs:215-220`) ties them back to the filtered unique indexes they mirror.
- **Why it's built this way**: pulling the flow out of the handlers means the organizer scan path, the manual fallback, the room QR path, and the sponsor booth path cannot drift apart in their idempotency, timestamp, or event-resolution behavior, which for an attendance record is the difference between a defensible number and a guess. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`. Splitting `RecordAsync` out of `ExecuteAsync` is what lets the two attendee-driven paths share the write while doing their own target lookup, since each asks Conference a different question (`CheckInProcessor.cs:15-21`).
- **Where it's used**: `ExecuteAsync` by [CheckInAttendeeHandler](#checkinattendeehandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/CheckInAttendee/CheckInAttendeeHandler.cs:60`) and [ManualCheckInHandler](#manualcheckinhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/ManualCheckIn/ManualCheckInHandler.cs:50`). `RecordAsync` and `EventNotPublished` directly by [RecordRoomCheckInHandler](#recordroomcheckinhandler) (`RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:108` and `:67`) and [RecordSponsorVisitHandler](#recordsponsorvisithandler) (`RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:77` and `:64`), which resolve their own target first and then share this write half.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `ExecuteAsync` takes no `sponsorId` and `ValidateTargetAsync` has only a session branch and an event branch, so a sponsor visit cannot be recorded through the organizer path even though `CheckInScope` admits it; the sponsor scope reaches `RecordAsync` only through [RecordSponsorVisitHandler](#recordsponsorvisithandler), whose own comment cites the once-per-sponsor filtered index as its race backstop (`RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:73-75`). The `sessionId!.Value` dereference at `CheckInProcessor.cs:190` is guarded only by the caller passing a session id together with a session scope, not by anything in this file.

### GetAttendanceStatsHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.GetAttendanceStats` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/GetAttendanceStats/GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:16` · Level 11 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the query handler for [GetAttendanceStatsQuery](#getattendancestatsquery). It answers the organizer dashboard with one event-scoped arrival count plus one row per session that has check-ins, as an [AttendanceStatsDTO](#attendancestatsdto).
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) through its primary constructor (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:16`). It reads the [CheckIn](#checkin) aggregate through an [IReadRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ireadrepositorytentity-tidentifiertype), filters on [CheckInScope](#checkinscope), and builds [SessionAttendanceDTO](#sessionattendancedto) rows inside an [AttendanceStatsDTO](#attendancestatsdto). It implements [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:17`).
- **Concept introduced, the persistence-neutral grouped count.** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether a read pulls only what it needs. The class doc (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:10-15`) is explicit: both figures are read through the focused repository surface and both are computed in SQL, a `COUNT` for the event scope and a grouped `COUNT` per session, so what crosses the wire is one row per session rather than one per check-in. The member that makes this possible is `CountByAsync`, declared on the shared querier contract (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Persistence/IRepository.cs:169-174`); its remarks (`IRepository.cs:158-163`) name the problem it removes, that the Application layer references no EF Core and therefore has no `IQueryable` to group, which would otherwise force a handler to project every matching row out of the database and fold it in memory. `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` is the reason the fix took that shape: the aggregate is expressed as a persistence-neutral member rather than by letting the handler see the provider. `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` shows in how the two scopes are distinguished: a single `CheckIn` table holds both event arrivals and session attendance, separated by the `Scope` discriminator rather than by two tables, and [CheckInConfiguration](#checkinconfiguration) indexes `EventId` and `SessionId` for exactly this read (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/CheckIns/CheckInConfiguration.cs:65-70`). `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`: this is a pure read, resolved through `GetReadRepository` (line 25) rather than the writable repository, so nothing enters the change tracker.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleAsync` (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:20-22`) null-guards the query with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(query)` (line 23).
  - It resolves the read repository for [CheckIn](#checkin) (line 25).
  - The event figure is a server-side count: `CountAsync(c => c.EventId == query.EventId && c.Scope == CheckInScope.Event, cancellationToken)` (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:28-30`), which translates to a SQL `COUNT` and never materializes a row.
  - The session figures are a server-side `GROUP BY`: `CountByAsync(c => c.SessionId!.Value, c => c.EventId == query.EventId && c.Scope == CheckInScope.Session && c.SessionId != null, cancellationToken)` (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:32-35`) returns an `IReadOnlyDictionary<SessionIdentifierType, int>` holding one entry per session that has at least one session-scoped check-in of this event. The `!= null` filter is what makes the `SessionId!.Value` key selector safe.
  - The rollup is built with a collection expression (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:37-42`): `OrderBy(pair => pair.Key)` (line 39) makes the output order deterministic (a dictionary has none), and each pair becomes a `SessionAttendanceDTO { SessionId = pair.Key, Count = pair.Value }` (line 40).
  - It returns `Result.Success(new AttendanceStatsDTO { EventId = ..., EventAttendance = ..., SessionAttendance = ... })` (`GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:44-49`). There is no failure branch: with a valid event id the query always succeeds, and an event with no check-ins simply yields zero and an empty list.
- **Why it's built this way**: pushing both aggregates into SQL keeps the response size proportional to the number of sessions rather than to the number of attendees, which is the difference that matters on a conference day; sorting by key in memory afterwards costs nothing and means two calls with the same data return rows in the same order, which matters for a dashboard and for snapshot-style tests.
- **Where it's used**: dispatched from `CheckInsController.GetAttendanceStatsAsync` on `GET /api/checkins/stats?eventId=` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:212-224`), an endpoint gated by `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage)]` (`CheckInsController.cs:213`); registered by the convention scan in the Application-layer [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection-1) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`).

### SessionTimeSlotPoints

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:29` · Level 11 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: the one statement of the "session points once per time slot" rule. Its single method, `HasEarlierOverlappingCheckInAsync`, answers whether an attendee's session check-in is preceded by a check-in to a different session of the same event whose scheduled window overlaps this one (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:9-14`, `:52`). Attendance is never affected; every check-in row is still written, and only the points award depends on the answer.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), Conference's [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) (for `GetOverlappingSessionIdsAsync`), the [CheckIn](#checkin) aggregate and its [CheckInScope](#checkinscope) discriminator, and [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). It reads through `GetReadRepository` and `GetProjectedAsync` (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:61-67`).
- **Concept introduced, one rule asked from two places, with "earlier" decided from committed rows.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`, `[Rubric §14, Testability]`. The class doc (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:9-27`) says both the points award (every session check-in, door scans included) and the room-QR response, which tells the attendee, ask this one question, so they cannot drift. It is a static helper for the same reason as [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor): each caller passes the collaborators it already holds, and what a lookup failure means is the caller's policy, so failures are returned unchanged. "Earlier" never depends on the order events happen to be handled in: a row is earlier when its `CheckedInOn` is strictly earlier, or equal with a smaller id (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:71-76`), which keeps the outcome deterministic when two events are handled concurrently or out of order. The earliest check-in of a slot earns the points and every later overlapping one earns none.
- **Walkthrough**
  - It projects only `Id`, `SessionId` and `CheckedInOn` for the attendee's session-scoped rows in this event (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:62-67`), so no full entity is materialized.
  - The reference row is the attendee's committed row for `sessionId` when one exists (line 69). When it does not, because the room-QR path asks before it writes, the reference is a row about to be written at `pendingCheckedInOn`: an insert not yet made takes the largest id, so every other row at or before that instant counts as earlier (remarks at lines 35-40, local function `IsEarlier` at lines 73-76).
  - Candidates are the distinct other session ids whose rows are earlier (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:78-84`). With none, the method returns `Result.Success(false)` and Conference is not called at all (lines 85-86).
  - Otherwise it asks Conference which candidates overlap `sessionId` (`GetOverlappingSessionIdsAsync`, lines 88-90), unwraps the answer with `overlapping.TryGetValue(out var overlappingIds)`, and returns `true` when any id comes back, or the Conference failure unchanged (lines 92-94). `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]`: Conference answers only the schedule question, and the check-in history stays in Engagement.
- **Why it's built this way**: a rule that two code paths evaluate separately will eventually disagree, and here a disagreement would tell an attendee one thing while the ledger records another. Deciding "earlier" from stored rows rather than from handling order makes the answer replay-safe under broker redelivery.
- **Where it's used**: [RecordRoomCheckInHandler](#recordroomcheckinhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/RecordRoomCheckIn/RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:92`) and [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler.cs:92`).

### DependencyInjection

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:15` · Level 12 · class (static, extension block)

- **What it is**: the Engagement module's API-layer composition root. It exposes two extension methods on `IServiceCollection`: `AddEngagementModule(...)` chains the three layer registrations into one call, and `AddModuleEngagementAPI()` configures the shared ownership-authorization filter with ADC's vocabulary and declares the module's role-to-permission grants.
- **Depends on**: [ApplicationSettings](group-14-module-system-composition.md#applicationsettings) (passed straight through), the Application and Infrastructure registration extensions (`AddModuleEngagementApplication` on the Application-layer [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection-1) and `AddModuleEngagementInfrastructure`), the shared [OwnerOrAdminFilterOptions](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilteroptions) / [OwnerOrAdminFilter](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilter), the auth vocabulary [RoleNames](group-24-identity-module.md#rolenames), and [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants) (whose `Apply` method is handed straight to `AddPermissions`, and which in turn wraps [EngagementPermissions](#engagementpermissions) fed into the [IPermissionRegistry](group-08-auth.md#ipermissionregistry)), and `System.Security.Claims.ClaimTypes` from the BCL (`DependencyInjection.cs:1`).
- **Concept, C# `extension(T)` DI blocks composing a module top-down.** The class body is an `extension(IServiceCollection services)` block (`DependencyInjection.cs:17`), the codebase-wide registration idiom (introduced in the [primer](00-primer.md#c-extensiont-types-read-this-once)): the members inside read as instance methods on any `IServiceCollection`. `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` assesses whether layering is honored at composition time; `AddEngagementModule` registers Application, then Infrastructure, then API in dependency order (`DependencyInjection.cs:26-28`), so nothing binds before its dependencies exist. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether authorization is centralized and declarative: rather than hand-roll an ownership check, `AddModuleEngagementAPI` reuses MMCA.Common's [OwnerOrAdminFilter](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilter) and supplies only ADC's field names ([ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)), then wires the module's permission grants through the shared registry ([ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html)) so the `[HasPermission(...)]`-gated endpoints resolve.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `AddEngagementModule(ApplicationSettings applicationSettings)` (`DependencyInjection.cs:24`) calls `AddModuleEngagementApplication(applicationSettings)` (line 26), `AddModuleEngagementInfrastructure()` (line 27), then `AddModuleEngagementAPI()` (line 28), and returns `services` for chaining (line 30). This is the single method [EngagementModule](#engagementmodule)`.Register` invokes.
  - `AddModuleEngagementAPI()` (`DependencyInjection.cs:43`) does two things.
    - Configures [OwnerOrAdminFilterOptions](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilteroptions) (`DependencyInjection.cs:45-56`) with `OwnerClaimType = ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier` (line 53), `BypassRole = RoleNames.Organizer` (line 54, the role that skips the ownership check), and `OwnerParameterName = "userId"` (line 55, the query argument the Bookmarks list endpoints bind). The comment above those three lines (`DependencyInjection.cs:47-52`) is the part worth reading twice: the token carries the user id in `sub` only, but the JWT bearer handler maps inbound `sub` onto `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier`, so `NameIdentifier` is the claim type the principal actually carries by the time this filter runs; the raw `sub` form survives only where an identity is built straight from a token's claims (the Blazor client-side state provider), and those readers go through the claims-principal extensions instead of this filter. The filter itself is registered upstream by Common's `AddAPI`; this call injects only the module's vocabulary.
    - Calls `AddPermissions(EngagementPermissionGrants.Apply)` (`DependencyInjection.cs:61`), delegating the actual role-to-permission map to [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants) rather than inlining `Grant` calls here. The comment above the call (`DependencyInjection.cs:58-60`) explains why: the map lives in a shared static class because the token-minting Identity host applies the same binding, since a token must carry the permission claims of every module, not only of the module the minting host boots. The doc comment (`DependencyInjection.cs:33-41`) lists what those grants back, the module's `[HasPermission(...)]`-gated endpoints across the live layer, check-in, the points overview and tickets, and records the complement: organizers hold every Engagement capability, while attendee-facing endpoints stay on a plain `[Authorize]` that carries no capability rather than on a permission gate. That is the split you see on [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller), where the organizer stats endpoint carries `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage)]` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:213`) while the attendee's own-badge endpoint (`CheckInsController.cs:60`) carries no permission attribute and relies on the class-level `[Authorize]` (`CheckInsController.cs:40`).
- **Why it's built this way**: one `AddEngagementModule` entry point keeps the module's wiring in a single call the module loader can invoke; delegating ownership enforcement to a configured shared filter means that logic is written and tested once in Common ([ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)); and centralizing the role grants in [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants) rather than inlining them keeps the permission model auditable and reusable by the token-minting host ([ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html)). The doc comment (`DependencyInjection.cs:33-41`) is the authoritative note on which ADC value maps to which option.
- **Where it's used**: `AddEngagementModule` is called by [EngagementModule](#engagementmodule)`.Register`; `AddModuleEngagementAPI` runs inside it. The configured [OwnerOrAdminFilter](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilter) guards the list endpoints on [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller); the granted permissions gate the `[HasPermission(...)]` endpoints on [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller), [PointsController](#pointscontroller), [TicketsController](#ticketscontroller), [TicketRosterImportController](#ticketrosterimportcontroller), and the live-layer controllers covered in [group-23](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `AddModuleEngagementInfrastructure` lives in the Infrastructure project and is covered by that layer's section, not here.

TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult)), the live-layer types it also wires ([LivePoll](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepoll), [LivePollVote](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollvote), [LivePollOption](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolloption), [ClassReference](#classreference) marker.
- **Concept, explicit registration plus convention scanning, with idempotent `TryAdd`.** `[Rubric §2, Design Patterns]` assesses recognized composition idioms: this method mixes hand-written registrations (for services that need a specific lifetime or a closed generic the scanner cannot infer) with one convention scan for the many uniform types. `[Rubric §33, Developer Experience]` shows in `ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>()` (`DependencyInjection.cs:94`): a new use case is picked up as soon as its handler exists, with no registration edit, which is why none of [GetMyBadgeHandler](#getmybadgehandler), [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) or [GetAttendanceStatsHandler](#getattendancestatshandler) appears by name here. Every explicit line uses `TryAdd*` rather than `Add*`, so a registration is a no-op when the same service was already contributed elsewhere, which keeps module wiring composable across hosts. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`: the comments in this file carry the reasoning that the call sites cannot, notably why the queue is registered twice and why two aggregates deliberately get no populator.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `AddModuleEngagementApplication(ApplicationSettings applicationSettings)` (`DependencyInjection.cs:35`, inside the `extension(IServiceCollection services)` block at line 33) opens with `_ = applicationSettings;` and the comment "Reserved for future use" (line 37), acknowledging the parameter is part of the uniform module signature but unused today.
  - Per-aggregate services for [UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark): a `NullNavigationPopulator` (line 40, the bookmark aggregate needs no navigation loading), an `EntityQueryService` over [UserSessionBookmarkDTO](#usersessionbookmarkdto) for its read surface (line 41), and a `DeleteEntityHandler` bound to `ICommandHandler<DeleteEntityCommand<UserSessionBookmark, ...>, Result>` (line 42), so delete reuses the framework's generic handler.
  - Cross-module services, each consumed by another module through a contract in the Engagement Shared project:
    - `TryAddScoped<IBookmarkCountService, BookmarkCountService>()` (line 45), the count Conference consumes.
    - `TryAddScoped<IUserEngagementExportService, UserEngagementExportService>()` (line 49), the Engagement half of the data-subject export that Identity aggregates across services (the comment at lines 47-48 cites PRIVACY.md section 12, `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]`).
    - `TryAddScoped<IPendingTicketInvitationService, PendingTicketInvitationService>()` (line 53), which per the comment at lines 51-52 answers which ticket invitation still stands for an address (BR-271), for the Identity module's re-issue of an expired invitation.
  - Live-channel publish queue (`DependencyInjection.cs:55-60`): the concrete [LiveChannelPublishQueue](#livechannelpublishqueue) is registered as a singleton (line 59) and [ILiveChannelPublishQueue](#ilivechannelpublishqueue) is registered as a factory resolving that same instance (line 60). The double registration is deliberate and the comment above it (lines 55-58) explains why: handlers enqueue post-commit broadcasts (BR-229) instead of awaiting the gRPC publish inline, and the Infrastructure-hosted drain ([LiveChannelPublishProcessor](#livechannelpublishprocessor)) needs the concrete type while handlers only need the interface, so both must share one instance.
  - Bookmark cache-eviction signal (`DependencyInjection.cs:62-64`): [BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal](#bookmarkcacheevictionsignal) is registered as a singleton (line 64). Per the comment at lines 62-63 it is the coalescing flag between the bookmark domain-event handler and the Infrastructure-hosted [BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor](#bookmarkcacheevictionprocessor), which paces the Conference cache-eviction broadcasts.
  - Live-layer [LivePoll](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepoll) aggregate (`DependencyInjection.cs:66-75`): a real [LivePollNavigationPopulator](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollnavigationpopulator) (line 67, unlike the bookmark aggregate this one has navigations to load), a `NullNavigationPopulator` for [LivePollVote](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollvote) (line 68), a [LivePollOptionNavigationPopulator](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolloptionnavigationpopulator) for [LivePollOption](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolloption) (line 72, whose comment at lines 70-71 notes options are normally hydrated through the poll's own child descriptor and that this covers the option's back-reference on the manual path), an `EntityQueryService` over [LivePollDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolldto) (line 74), and the [LivePollResultsBuilder](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollresultsbuilder) projection helper (line 75). No delete-handler registration is made by hand for the poll aggregate here.
  - Live-layer [SessionQuestion](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestion) aggregate (`DependencyInjection.cs:77-80`): `NullNavigationPopulator`s for `SessionQuestion` (line 78) and [SessionQuestionUpvote](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionupvote) (line 79), plus the [SessionQuestionViewBuilder](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionviewbuilder) (line 80).
  - Points (gamification): `TryAddScoped<IPointsAwarder, PointsAwarder>()` (line 90). The comment above it (lines 82-89) records two things worth reading: there is one write path into the ledger, so the check-in and feedback integration-event handlers and the session-question domain-event handler all resolve this from their own scope and hand it an activity plus subject-key pair; and it is registered by hand because it is a plain service rather than a handler, so the convention scan below does not see it. The same comment states that [PointsEntry](#pointsentry) and [LeaderboardOptIn](#leaderboardoptin) deliberately get NO `INavigationPopulator`, since neither has a navigation to populate, exactly like the [CheckIn](#checkin) and [AttendeeBadge](#attendeebadge) aggregates this module already queries through the repository without one.
  - `services.ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>()` (line 94): convention-scans this assembly for domain-event handlers, DTO and request mappers, command and query handlers, and validators (comment at `DependencyInjection.cs:92-93`), then the method returns `services` for chaining (line 96).
- **Why it's built this way**: explicit `TryAdd` registrations pin the lifetimes and closed generics the scanner cannot infer, while the single scan removes the per-handler registration ceremony; together they keep module wiring short and additive. Passing the assembly marker [ClassReference](#classreference) rather than a business type keeps the scan decoupled from any specific handler. The live-layer aggregates are registered here even though their behavior is taught in [group-23](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md), because a module registers all of its aggregates from one Application-layer entry point.
- **Where it's used**: called by `AddEngagementModule` in the API [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection-1) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:26`), which is in turn invoked by [EngagementModule](#engagementmodule)`.Register` during host startup.

### GetLeaderboardQuery

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.UseCases.GetLeaderboard` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/UseCases/GetLeaderboard/GetLeaderboardQuery.cs:12` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the read request for the public points leaderboard. It is a parameterless record: the board has no page, no filter, and no caller-chosen size.
- **Depends on**: nothing. It is paired with [GetLeaderboardHandler](#getleaderboardhandler) through the CQRS query contract, and the board length it implies comes from [PointsSettings](#pointssettings), not from the message.
- **Concept, the empty message as a security decision.** A query with no parameters looks like an oversight until you read why it has none: the doc comment (`GetLeaderboardQuery.cs:5-10`) records that the board is a single fixed-size list whose length comes from configuration (`Points:LeaderboardSize`), so "there is no parameter through which a caller could ask for more of the board than the organizer chose to publish". `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether inputs that widen a disclosure exist at all; the cheapest way to make a knob untamperable is not to expose it. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether a contract says what it means: an empty record is an honest statement that this read has exactly one shape. `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]` is in scope because what the board publishes is attendee display names, which is why the size question is a privacy question and not just a paging one.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record class GetLeaderboardQuery;` (`GetLeaderboardQuery.cs:12`), a declaration with no positional parameters and no body. Callers write `new GetLeaderboardQuery()`.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the size in configuration rather than in the message means an operator can shorten or lengthen the published board without a deploy and without a client being able to override it; keeping the type (rather than passing no message at all) keeps the read on the same [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) pipeline as every other query.
- **Where it's used**: constructed by [PointsController](#pointscontroller)'s `GET /api/points/leaderboard` action (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/PointsController.cs:83`), whose own doc restates the fixed-length rule (`PointsController.cs:67-75`), and handled by [GetLeaderboardHandler](#getleaderboardhandler). The controller test asserts the action takes no parameter other than the cancellation token (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Tests/Controllers/PointsControllerTests.cs:98`).

### GetMyPointsQuery

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.UseCases.GetMyPoints` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/UseCases/GetMyPoints/GetMyPointsQuery.cs:14` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the read request for the calling attendee's own points: their running total, their leaderboard status, and one page of the ledger entries behind the total. It carries paging arguments and nothing else.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. Paired with [GetMyPointsHandler](#getmypointshandler), which produces a [MyPointsDTO](#mypointsdto).
- **Concept, the deliberately absent user id.** The most instructive thing about this record is a parameter it does *not* have. The doc comment (`GetMyPointsQuery.cs:6-10`) states it plainly: the attendee is the caller, read from the token by the handler, because "a user id in the query would make 'whose points do I get' a client-supplied value, which is exactly the input an attendee could change to read someone else's ledger". `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether authorization decisions depend on trusted inputs: an identity that is never accepted from the client cannot be forged by the client, which is a stronger guarantee than any check placed after it. Contrast [GetUserBookmarksQuery](#getuserbookmarksquery), which *does* carry a `UserId` and therefore needs the `OwnerOrAdminFilter` at the API edge to compare it against the caller's claim; this query removes the need for that comparison by removing the parameter.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record class GetMyPointsQuery(int PageNumber = 1, int PageSize = 20)` (`GetMyPointsQuery.cs:14`). Two positional parameters, both defaulted, so `new GetMyPointsQuery()` is the common call. The per-parameter docs (`GetMyPointsQuery.cs:12-13`) record where the safety lives: page numbers below 1 are treated as page 1, and the page size is "clamped into 1 to 100 by the handler", not by the record.
- **Why it's built this way**: defaults keep the ordinary call trivial, and pushing the clamping into the handler means the ceiling holds for every caller including tests and any future in-process dispatcher, not only for requests that passed through the controller's `[Range]` attributes (`PointsController.cs:55-56`).
- **Where it's used**: constructed by [PointsController](#pointscontroller)'s `GET /api/points/me` action from the `pageNumber`/`pageSize` query arguments (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/PointsController.cs:60`); the controller test asserts the arguments arrive on the query unchanged and that no user id is passed (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Tests/Controllers/PointsControllerTests.cs:43`), and a separate reflection test asserts that no action on the controller takes a user id from the caller at all (`PointsControllerTests.cs:219`). Handled by [GetMyPointsHandler](#getmypointshandler).

### LiveChannelPublishWorkItem

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Live` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Live/ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:10` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: one pending best-effort live-channel broadcast, captured as an immutable three-field record. It is exactly the argument tuple a drain worker will later hand to `ILiveChannelPublisher.PublishAsync`.
- **Depends on**: nothing but `string`. It is deliberately primitive-only so the item can sit in a queue with no entity, no `DbContext`, and no scope attached. Consumed by [ILiveChannelPublishQueue](#ilivechannelpublishqueue) and, on the other side, [ILiveChannelPublisher](group-10-notifications.md#ilivechannelpublisher).
- **Concept, the deferred-work message.** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether slow out-of-process work is kept off the request path: representing a broadcast as data (rather than as an in-flight `await`) is what makes deferral possible at all. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses failure containment: because the payload is *pre-serialized* into `PayloadJson` before enqueueing, the drain never needs the originating scope, its entities, or its `DbContext`, so a slow publish cannot pin request-scoped resources. The doc comment (`ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:3-9`) ties the type to BR-229 and [ADR-039](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/039-live-channel-push.html).
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record LiveChannelPublishWorkItem(string ChannelKey, string EventName, string PayloadJson)` (`ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:10`). `ChannelKey` is the session or event channel key (the doc points at [LivePollChannel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollchannel), `ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:7`), `EventName` is the channel event name such as `poll.results-changed` (`ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:8`), and `PayloadJson` is the pre-serialized broadcast body, which the doc states never carries per-user data (`ILiveChannelPublishQueue.cs:9`).
- **Why it's built this way**: a broadcast fans out to every subscriber of a channel, so the payload must be user-agnostic; encoding that rule in the doc of a single-purpose record keeps it visible at every construction site. Serializing eagerly also means the queue holds a small, immutable string triple rather than a live object graph.
- **Where it's used**: constructed by the live-layer command handlers after their commit, notably [OpenLivePollHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#openlivepollhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/LivePolls/UseCases/Open/OpenLivePollHandler.cs:110`), [CloseLivePollHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#closelivepollhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/LivePolls/UseCases/Close/CloseLivePollHandler.cs:93`), [SubmitQuestionHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#submitquestionhandler) (`SubmitQuestionHandler.cs:219`, `:157`), and [ModerateQuestionHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#moderatequestionhandler) (`ModerateQuestionHandler.cs:148`, `:154`), plus the two post-commit domain-event handlers [LivePollVoteChangedHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollvotechangedhandler) (`LivePollVoteChangedHandler.cs:79`) and [SessionQuestionUpvoteChangedHandler](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionupvotechangedhandler) (`SessionQuestionUpvoteChangedHandler.cs:86`); drained by [LiveChannelPublishProcessor](#livechannelpublishprocessor).

### OptInRow

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.UseCases.GetLeaderboard` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/UseCases/GetLeaderboard/GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:85` · Level 0 · record (private sealed, nested)

- **What it is**: the projection shape for one opted-in attendee inside [GetLeaderboardHandler](#getleaderboardhandler): the attendee's id and the display name they published when they joined the board.
- **Depends on**: the `UserIdentifierType` alias; `string` (BCL). Nothing else, which is the point.
- **Concept, the private projection record.** A projection read needs a target type, and the choice of target is a design decision. Using an anonymous type (as [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler](#getbookmarkedsessionidshandler) does) is fine when the shape is consumed one line later; naming the shape pays off when it is threaded through several LINQ stages, because the name documents what the two columns mean. Declaring it `private` and nested keeps it invisible outside the handler, so it can never be mistaken for a contract: nothing about it is a promise to any caller. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses reading only the columns you need, which is what a projection record makes explicit at the call site. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`: the type sits inside the only file entitled to change it.
- **Walkthrough**: `private sealed record class OptInRow(UserIdentifierType UserId, string DisplayName)` (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:85`), two positional members, with per-parameter docs at `:83-84` naming them as the attendee who joined the board and the name they published at opt-in.
- **Why it's built this way**: `record` gives value semantics for free and `sealed` plus `private` keeps the shape local. The `DisplayName` carried here is the snapshot taken at opt-in, which is why the board can be rendered with no call into Identity at all.
- **Where it's used**: the `select` argument of the [LeaderboardOptIn](#leaderboardoptin) projection read (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:41`), then read again for the user-id list that scopes the ledger sum (`:48`), for the ordering (`:68-69`), and for the final DTO projection (`:71-76`). It is the only projection row in this handler: the points side is summed by the database rather than projected, see [GetLeaderboardHandler](#getleaderboardhandler).

### GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.GetOrCreateMyBadge` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/GetOrCreateMyBadge/GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand.cs:11` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the request for "give me my badge", a parameterless command. The attendee it applies to is never stated in the message: the handler reads the caller from the token.
- **Depends on**: nothing. It has no members at all. Paired with [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler), which answers with a [MyBadgeDTO](#mybadgedto).
- **Concept introduced, the deliberately empty message as a security property.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether authorization decisions are made from trusted inputs rather than from client-supplied ones. The doc comment says exactly why the record is empty (`GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand.cs:5-9`): the attendee is the caller, read from the token by the handler, and carrying a user id in the body would make "whose badge do I get" a client-supplied value, which is precisely the input an attendee could change to obtain someone else's credential. Removing the parameter removes the attack rather than validating it away. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` shows in the pairing with the route: the endpoint is `GET /api/checkins/my-badge` with no id segment and no body ([CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller), `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:60`), so the contract has nowhere to put an identity even if a caller wanted to.
- **Concept, a command that reads.** It is declared a *command*, not a query, because the first call for an attendee writes a new badge row; see the rationale under [GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler](#getorcreatemybadgehandler).
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record class GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand;` (`GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand.cs:11`). One line, no positional parameters, no body.
- **Why it's built this way**: an empty message still buys the uniform dispatch, decoration, and naming of the CQRS pipeline while carrying no attack surface. The alternative (a `UserId` parameter validated against the token) would give the same behavior with a check that can be forgotten.
- **Where it's used**: constructed by `CheckInsController.GetMyBadgeAsync` (`CheckInsController.cs:83`, method at `:49`) and dispatched through the injected [ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult) (`CheckInsController.cs:44`).
