### EventClock
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.GetTicketInsights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/EventClock.cs:21` · Level 4 · record (internal, sealed)

- **What it is**: the clock both insight reports bucket days and half hours in: a basis, a UTC offset in
  minutes, and the event's UTC window when known (`EventClock.cs:6-25`).
- **Depends on**: [`IEventLiveValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice)
  (Conference's live-info lookup, returning
  [`EventLiveInfo`](group-17-conference-domain.md#eventliveinfo)),
  [`InsightTimeBasis`](#insighttimebasis); the `EventIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept introduced, deriving a zone offset without a zone id.** The doc explains that Conference does
  not give Engagement the event's IANA zone id, but its live info carries the event's first day in the
  event's zone and the UTC instant that day starts; their difference is the event's offset on its first
  day, exact for event-day buckets and at most an hour off for a day across a daylight-saving change
  (`EventClock.cs:9-12`). `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether a
  dependency failure degrades rather than breaks; here a failed or empty lookup yields UTC buckets with
  the basis reported, instead of a failed report (`EventClock.cs:12-14,50-51`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **`MaxOffsetMinutes = 14 * 60`** (`EventClock.cs:28`): the widest real offset; a larger derived
    value is treated as bad data.
  - **`Utc`** (`EventClock.cs:31`): the fallback clock, offset 0, no window. `Offset` and `WindowKnown`
    are derived properties (`:34,37`).
  - **`ResolveAsync`** (`EventClock.cs:44-63`): calls `GetEventLiveInfoAsync`; failure or null returns
    `Utc` (`:49-51`). The window instants are re-stamped `DateTimeKind.Utc` (`:54-55`). A default
    `StartDate` keeps UTC but keeps the window (`:56-57`). Otherwise the offset is the first day at
    midnight minus the window start, rounded away from zero (`:59`), and falls back to UTC (still with
    the window) when its magnitude exceeds 14 hours (`:60-62`).
  - **`DayOf`** (`EventClock.cs:68`): the UTC instant shifted by the offset, as a `DateOnly`.
  - **`HalfHourOf`** (`EventClock.cs:73-78`): floors the shifted time to `:00` or `:30` and stamps it
    as a `DateTimeOffset` at the clock's offset.
  - **`IsWithinEvent`** (`EventClock.cs:83-84`): true when the window is unknown, otherwise a half-open
    `[start, end)` test.
- **Why it's built this way**: a fixed offset is enough for a conference that spans a few days, and the
  degradation is visible in the response rather than silent: both handlers copy `Basis` and
  `UtcOffsetMinutes` into their DTOs, and the engagement one also copies `WindowKnown`
  (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:69-70`, `GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:72-74`).
- **Where it's used**: [`GetRosterInsightsHandler`](#getrosterinsightshandler) (A2 day buckets, the
  offset applied inside the SQL grouping, `GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:130-137`) and
  [`GetEngagementInsightsHandler`](#getengagementinsightshandler) (B4 arrivals,
  `GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:330-331`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `DayOf` has no caller in the two handlers shown here; A2 computes its days
  in the SQL projection instead. Whether another caller exists is not determinable from the brief's
  usage list, which names only the two handlers.

### TicketInsightsCsv
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.GetTicketInsights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/TicketInsightsCsv.cs:22` · Level 4 · class (static)

- **What it is**: renders one table of the ticket insights (A1 to A6 or B1 to B4) as CSV, plus the file
  name and the byte encoding of the download (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:10-22`).
- **Depends on**: [`TicketInsightsReport`](#ticketinsightsreport),
  [`RosterInsightsDTO`](#rosterinsightsdto), [`EngagementInsightsDTO`](#engagementinsightsdto) and
  their nested DTOs, [`InsightCount`](#insightcount), [`CsvBuilder`](#csvbuilder); BCL
  `FrozenDictionary`, `CultureInfo`, `Encoding`.
- **Concept**: the export conventions of
  [ADR-078](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/078-csv-export-endpoint.html): RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF
  rows, invariant number formatting, a UTF-8 byte order mark so Excel reads accented text, and `#`
  comment rows for notes (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:10-19`). `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data
  Governance]` assesses whether privacy rules hold at every output; a suppressed cell is written as
  `InsightCount.SuppressedText` and the DTOs already carry no number for it, so the file cannot leak one
  (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:16-18,281-294`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **Constants** (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:25-33`): `ContentType = "text/csv"`, the total-row label
    `"All ticket types"`, the `"No linked ticket"` label, and the private `"\r\n"` line ending.
  - **Dispatch tables** (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:36-55`): two frozen dictionaries mapping each report to
    its writer, A1 to A6 over the roster DTO and B1 to B4 over the engagement DTO. `IsRosterReport`
    is a key lookup into the first (`:60`).
  - **`FileName`** (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:70-73`):
    `ticket-insights-{report}-event-{id}-{yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ}.csv`, with `ReportName` lowering the first
    letter of the enum member and throwing on an undefined value (`:264-271`).
  - **`ToUtf8WithByteOrderMark`** (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:78-82`): preamble plus UTF-8 bytes.
  - **`Render`** overloads (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:88-95,101-108`): null-check, look up the writer, and
    throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for a report from the other family.
  - **Table writers** (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:110-262`): one per report. A1 and B1 append the total row
    relabeled with `AllTicketTypes` (`:114,200`); A2 writes the median as a trailing `#` comment row,
    or `n/a` (`:131-134`); B4 stamps each bucket as `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmzzz` (`:250`).
  - **Formatters** (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:273-294`): invariant integers, `Dec` rounding away from zero
    to a fixed number of decimals, UTC timestamps, and `Count`/`Percent`/`Average` that print the
    suppression text for a suppressed cell and an empty field when a rate is absent (percent to one
    decimal, average to two).
- **Why it's built this way**: putting rendering in the Application layer keeps the controller to a
  report dispatch and a file result, and the dispatch dictionaries make "is this a roster report"
  answerable without a parallel switch.
- **Where it's used**: [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller)'s `GET insights/export`, which picks the
  handler with `IsRosterReport`, renders, and returns the BOM-prefixed bytes with `ContentType` and
  `FileName` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:242-285`);
  covered by `TicketInsightsCsvTests` in the Engagement Application test project.

### GetRosterInsightsHandler
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.GetTicketInsights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:33` · Level 8 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: builds the roster-only ticket insights of one event: A1 funnel by ticket type, A2
  adoption over time, A3 follow-up queue, A4 group orders, A5 roster health and A6 email domain mix
  (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:13-15`).
- **Depends on**: [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (for the
  [`IEntityQuerier<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ientityqueriertentity-tidentifiertype)
  read surface over [`Ticket`](#ticket)),
  [`IEventLiveValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) (through
  [`EventClock`](#eventclock)), [`NewestRosterTicketSpecification`](#newestrosterticketspecification),
  [`PersonalWebmailDomains`](#personalwebmaildomains), [`InsightCount`](#insightcount),
  [`TicketStatus`](#ticketstatus), [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod),
  [`RosterInsightsDTO`](#rosterinsightsdto) and its parts
  ([`TicketTypeFunnelDTO`](#tickettypefunneldto), [`AdoptionTrendDTO`](#adoptiontrenddto),
  [`FollowUpQueueDTO`](#followupqueuedto), [`GroupOrdersDTO`](#groupordersdto),
  [`RosterHealthDTO`](#rosterhealthdto), [`EmailDomainMixDTO`](#emaildomainmixdto)),
  [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result); BCL `TimeProvider`.
- **Concept introduced, aggregate-only reporting over grouped reads.** `[Rubric §30,
  Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]` assesses whether personal data is minimized at the boundary;
  the class doc states nothing leaving the handler names a holder or returns an email address or account
  id, and A6's small-number rule is applied on the server (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:16-20`).
  `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether reads scale with the data; every read is a
  SQL `GROUP BY`/`COUNT` through `CountByAsync`, so the database returns grouped rows rather than ticket
  rows (`:21-27`), in line with the narrow read contract of
  [ADR-055](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/055-repository-and-specification-contract.html).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **Constants** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:40-46`): `TopDomainCount = 10`, `ReminderDays = 3`,
    `LateReminderDays = 7`.
  - **`HandleAsync`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:49-79`): takes `now` from `TimeProvider`, gets the
    ticket querier with `GetReadRepository`, resolves the [`EventClock`](#eventclock), then runs the
    funnel, adoption, order and health reads in sequence and returns `Result.Success` with the DTO
    (`:55-78`).
  - **A1 `BuildFunnelAsync`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:82-102`): one `CountByAsync` keyed by
    (ticket type, invited, link method) over Live tickets, folded per type in ordinal order and once in
    total through `Funnel` (`:104-119`).
  - **A2 `BuildAdoptionAsync`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:123-178`): groups by invite day and link
    day with the clock's offset added inside the projection (`:130-138`), returns an empty DTO when no
    rows (`:143-144`), walks every day from the first to the last event and accumulates the linked count
    and share (`:153-165`), and computes `MedianDaysInviteToLink` with `WeightedMedian` over the
    invite-to-link gaps (`:167-176,346-367`).
  - **Orders `ReadOrdersAsync`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:182-218`): one grouping by (order email,
    linked, invited at least 3 days, invited at least 7 days); the inline comment notes a never-invited
    ticket compares false on both in SQL and in memory (`:196`). Rows are regrouped per email into
    [`OrderTally`](#ordertally) and wrapped in [`RosterOrders`](#rosterorders).
  - **A3 `BuildFollowUp`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:221-227`): unlinked, invited tickets split by
    single-ticket and multi-ticket orders at both thresholds.
  - **A4 `BuildGroupOrders`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:230-247`): group order totals plus a
    tickets-per-order histogram.
  - **A6 `BuildDomainMix`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:251-280`): per-domain ticket totals; personal
    webmail versus company; the top ten company domains among those at or above
    `InsightCount.SmallNumberThreshold` (3), the rest folded into `OtherCompanyDomains`; every cell built
    with `InsightCount.Of` (`:261-278`).
  - **A5 `BuildHealthAsync`** (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:284-333`): one grouping by (status, erased,
    nameless) over every ticket of the event, where erased means the barcode starts with
    `Ticket.AnonymizedBarcodePrefix` (`:289-297`); one grouping by (order email, first, last) over named
    Live tickets, regrouped by name with [`NameComparer`](#namecomparer) to count duplicate names
    (`:299-310`); two reads through [`NewestRosterTicketSpecification`](#newestrosterticketspecification)
    for the last added and last changed timestamps (`:312-319`).
  - **Helpers**: `Percent` rounds to one decimal and returns 0 for an empty whole
    (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:336-337`); `DomainOf` takes the text after the last `@` (`:370-374`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the doc notes a roster is at most a few thousand tickets and the
  email-keyed groupings track the number of orders (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:24-27`), so regrouping
  in memory is cheap while no individual row is ever returned to the caller.
- **Where it's used**: injected into [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller) as
  `IQueryHandler<GetRosterInsightsQuery, Result<RosterInsightsDTO>>` and called by `GET insights/roster`
  and the A-series export
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:49,200,265`);
  covered by `GetRosterInsightsHandlerTests`.

### GetEngagementInsightsHandler
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.GetTicketInsights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:48` · Level 11 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: builds the roster-plus-activity insights of one event over its linked holders: B1
  engagement, B2 ticketed versus present, B3 sponsor reach and B4 arrival curve
  (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:21-24`).
- **Depends on**: [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (read repositories over
  [`Ticket`](#ticket), [`CheckIn`](#checkin), [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark),
  [`PointsEntry`](#pointsentry), [`LivePoll`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepoll),
  [`LivePollVote`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollvote) and
  [`SessionQuestion`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestion)),
  [`IEventLiveValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice),
  [`ISessionBookmarkValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#isessionbookmarkvalidationservice),
  [`EventClock`](#eventclock), [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys),
  [`InsightCount`](#insightcount), [`SessionScopeSource`](#sessionscopesource),
  [`EngagementInsightsDTO`](#engagementinsightsdto) and its parts
  ([`TicketTypeEngagementDTO`](#tickettypeengagementdto),
  [`TicketedVsPresentDTO`](#ticketedvspresentdto), [`SponsorReachDTO`](#sponsorreachdto),
  [`ArrivalBucketDTO`](#arrivalbucketdto)); the private [`Holders`](#holders),
  [`Activity`](#activity) and [`EventCheckInRow`](#eventcheckinrow); BCL `TimeProvider`.
- **Concept**: the aggregate-only rule taught at
  [`GetRosterInsightsHandler`](#getrosterinsightshandler), here applied to every count cell through
  `InsightCount.Of`, so a count of 1 or 2 is withheld on the server (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:25-28`).
  What this handler adds is an **in-memory join without a join operator**: the roster and the activity
  tables share the Engagement database, but the read surface has no join, so each table is aggregated in
  SQL to one row per account and the per-ticket-type split is folded here (`:30-35`).
  `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: cross-service lookups degrade instead of failing the
  report, and the DTO says how (`:39-41`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **`HandleAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:56-83`): resolves the clock, reads holders, reads
    activity, builds sponsor reach, then assembles the DTO, including `EventWindowKnown`,
    `SessionScope` and `SponsorNamesResolved` (true only when every sponsor name resolved, `:76`).
  - **`ReadHoldersAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:86-107`): see [`Holders`](#holders).
  - **`ReadActivityAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:110-148`): projects event-scope check-ins
    as [`EventCheckInRow`](#eventcheckinrow) (`:114-117`); one grouping by (scope, sponsor, account) over
    session and sponsor check-ins yields session check-ins per account and visitors per sponsor
    (`:120-132`); then sessions, feedback, bookmarks, votes and questions.
  - **`ReadSessionIdsAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:152-185`): asks Conference for the
    event's session ids; on failure falls back to the distinct session ids Engagement has seen in
    check-ins, questions and polls, and reports `SessionScopeSource.LocalActivity` (`:156-158,164-184`).
  - **`ReadBookmarkersAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:187-201`): returns empty for no
    sessions, otherwise the distinct users bookmarking any of them.
  - **`ReadFeedbackAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:206-224`): reads feedback from the points
    ledger, one entry per feedback keyed to its subject through
    [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys), split into session and event feedback givers (`:203-205`).
  - **`ReadVotersAsync`** / **`ReadAskersAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:226-243,245-253`):
    the event's poll ids then the distinct voters, and the distinct question askers.
  - **B1 `Engagement`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:256-271`): one row per holder set, each measure
    a `CountIn` intersection with the holder count as denominator.
  - **B2 `BuildTicketedVsPresent`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:274-286`): holders never checked
    in, per type and in total, and checked-in accounts holding no linked ticket.
  - **B3 `BuildSponsorReachAsync`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:290-320`): one
    `GetSponsorLiveInfoAsync` per visited sponsor; a failed or blank name becomes `Sponsor {id}` with
    `NameResolved = false` (`:298-306`); rows are ordered by the exact visitor count, which a suppressed
    cell no longer carries (`:313-319`).
  - **B4 `BuildArrivals`** (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:323-346`): event check-ins inside the
    event window, bucketed per half hour on the clock and split by ticket type, dropping types with no
    arrivals in the bucket.
- **Why it's built this way**: splitting B1 to B4 from A1 to A6 keeps the slower activity reads off the
  roster request (`GetEngagementInsightsQuery.cs:4-5`), and folding sets in memory keeps raw activity
  rows in the database, the one stated exception being the event check-in times B4 needs
  (`GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:34-36`).
- **Where it's used**: injected into [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller) as
  `IQueryHandler<GetEngagementInsightsQuery, Result<EngagementInsightsDTO>>` and called by
  `GET insights/engagement` and the B-series export
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:50,224,274`);
  covered by `GetEngagementInsightsHandlerTests`.

### GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.UseCases.GetBookmarkedSessionIds` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetBookmarkedSessionIds/GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery.cs:5` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the read request for "which sessions has this user bookmarked", a single-parameter query carrying only the `UserId`. Its handler answers with a map from session id to bookmark id, so a listing page can render per-row bookmark state.
- **Depends on**: the `UserIdentifierType` alias (an identifier type alias linked solution-wide, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)); paired with [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler](#getbookmarkedsessionidshandler) through the CQRS query contract.
- **Concept, the CQRS query as an immutable record.** This is a vertical-slice read: the query type and its handler live in the same `UseCases/GetBookmarkedSessionIds/` folder. `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses whether reads and writes are modeled as distinct messages; this is a pure read, so it carries no validator and no transaction (the query pipeline skips both, see the decorator order in [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult)). `[Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]` assesses feature-folder cohesion, which this layout embodies. The record shape gives value equality and immutability for free, so the query is a safe, comparable message.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery(UserIdentifierType UserId)` (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery.cs:5`), one positional parameter and no body. The XML doc (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery.cs:3-4`) states the intent: the set of session ids the user has bookmarked, keyed by session id to bookmark id.
- **Why it's built this way**: a dedicated query type keeps the read intent explicit and lets the [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) pipeline decorate it uniformly; carrying just the `UserId` keeps the request minimal.
- **Where it's used**: constructed by [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller)'s `GET /api/bookmarks/session-ids` action from the `userId` query argument (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:154`) and dispatched to [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler](#getbookmarkedsessionidshandler); the resulting map drives the star indicator per row on the unified Sessions page. The record's property round-trip is pinned by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandlerTests.cs:39`.

### BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/Services/BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:25` · Level 0 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: a coalescing "Conference's bookmark-count cache is stale" flag, built on a capacity-one `Channel<bool>`. Any number of `Request()` calls made while one is pending collapse into that one pending request.
- **Depends on**: `System.Threading.Channels` only (`Channel`, `BoundedChannelOptions`, `BoundedChannelFullMode`, `ChannelReader<T>`; `BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:1`). No first-party types, which is why it is Level 0.
- **Concept introduced, a flag instead of a queue, so the consumer sets the rate.** Every eviction drops the whole `conference:sessions` tag (session list, session reads and batched counts together), and at a session changeover hundreds of attendees star sessions within the same minute, so one broadcast per star would keep that cache permanently cold and send every session read to Conference's database (`BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:11-18`). A bounded channel of capacity 1 with `BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite` (`:28-30`) makes a write against a full channel a no-op, so the processor's pacing, not the bookmark rate, sets the eviction rate. Contrast [LiveChannelPublishQueue](#livechannelpublishqueue), which uses `DropOldest` because every broadcast carries distinct content; here every request means the same thing, so dropping the new one loses nothing. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses protecting a downstream store from write-driven thundering herds, which the coalescing gives. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: a bookmark command can never be slowed or failed by the cache signal (`:21-22`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - The `_channel` field (`BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:27-33`) is `Channel.CreateBounded<bool>(new BoundedChannelOptions(1) { FullMode = DropWrite, SingleReader = true, SingleWriter = false })`: one hosted reader, many concurrent request-thread writers.
  - `public ChannelReader<bool> Reader => _channel.Reader` (`:36`) is the read side the hosted processor consumes; the writer stays private.
  - `public void Request() => _channel.Writer.TryWrite(true)` (`:42`) marks the cache stale. A request made while one is pending is absorbed into it, because the pending broadcast will cover it (`:38-41`). The result of `TryWrite` is deliberately ignored.
- **Why it's built this way**: the payload is a `bool` because the signal carries no information beyond "stale"; the channel is used for its wake-up semantics, not as a data pipe. Registered as a singleton, so there is one flag per replica (`:21`).
- **Where it's used**: writer side is [UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler](group-22-engagement-module.md#usersessionbookmarkcacheevictionhandler), which takes it by constructor (`UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler.cs:38`) and calls `Request()` on every bookmark change; reader side is [BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor](group-22-engagement-module.md#bookmarkcacheevictionprocessor) in Infrastructure, registered with `AddHostedService<BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor>()` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:27`). Registered as a singleton in `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:64`. The pattern is recorded in ADR-121 (ephemeral in-process work queue).

### AssemblyReference

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain, MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain`, `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/AssemblyReference.cs:5`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/AssemblyReference.cs:5` · Level 0 · class (static)
>
> *One byte-identical copy per Engagement layer.* This section covers the **Domain** and **Infrastructure** copies together; the API and Application copies are covered earlier in this chapter.

- **What it is**: a two-field static class whose only job is to hand out the `Assembly` it was compiled into, plus that assembly's simple name, so anything that needs to say "scan the assembly this type lives in" gets a compiled anchor instead of a hand-typed assembly-name string.

  | Type | File:Line | Notes (what differs) |
  |------|-----------|----------------------|
  | `AssemblyReference` (Domain) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/AssemblyReference.cs:5` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain` (`:3`); no consumer anywhere in the repo today |
  | `AssemblyReference` (Infrastructure) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/AssemblyReference.cs:5` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure` (`:3`); this is the copy the design-time migrations factory consumes |

  The Engagement module carries four copies of this file (API, Application, Domain, Infrastructure). Each is eleven lines long and declares the same two fields at lines 7 and 8; only the namespace on line 3 differs. What actually distinguishes them is which assembly `typeof(AssemblyReference).Assembly` resolves to, and therefore which call sites can use them.
- **Depends on**: `System.Reflection` (BCL), imported at line 1 of each file. Nothing first-party, which is why both copies sit at Level 0 even though one of them lives in the module's outermost non-presentation layer.
- **Concept**: the framework-level explanation of assembly-marker types lives with the shared copy in [AssemblyReference](group-14-module-system-composition.md#assemblyreference); these are the Engagement Domain and Infrastructure instances of that idiom. `[Rubric §2, Design Patterns]` assesses whether a recurring problem is solved with a recognized, uniform idiom rather than an ad-hoc one each time: every layer of every ADC module exposes the same pair of fields, so "point a scanner at this layer" has exactly one spelling across the repo. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` (Dependency Inversion) is the other half: the migrations host depends on a marker declared for that purpose, not on some real EF configuration class it happens to know about, so renaming or deleting an entity configuration can never silently empty a scan.
- **Walkthrough**: two `public static readonly` fields per copy, both resolved once at type initialization.
  - `Assembly` (`AssemblyReference.cs:7`) is `typeof(AssemblyReference).Assembly`. Because the marker is declared inside its own project, the Infrastructure copy resolves to the `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure` assembly, the one holding the ten `EntityConfiguration` classes under `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/`, and the Domain copy resolves to the assembly holding the module's aggregates.
  - `AssemblyName` (`AssemblyReference.cs:8`) is `Assembly.GetName().Name ?? string.Empty`. The null-coalesce is what keeps the field non-null under nullable-reference-type analysis, since `AssemblyName.Name` is declared nullable even though a loaded assembly always reports one.
- **Why it's built this way**: a `typeof` cannot go stale the way a string literal can, and because each layer declares its own copy, a scan can be aimed at one layer without that layer's consumers taking a reference to any other. The four-copy shape is deliberate duplication of a token, not duplicated logic: there is no behavior here to keep in sync, which is also why an unused copy costs nothing.
- **Where it's used**: the Infrastructure copy is the one the EF Core design-time factory points at when it tells the module's [SQLServerDbContext](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#sqlserverdbcontext) where to find entity configurations: `options.AddConfigurationAssembly(typeof(MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure.AssemblyReference).Assembly)` at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosting/MMCA.ADC.Migrations.SqlServer.Engagement/DesignTimeSQLServerDbContextFactory.cs:37`, the per-service migrations project that owns the `ADC_Engagement` database ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)). That call site names the type through its full namespace, which is why the Infrastructure copy specifically is load-bearing: swapping in the Domain copy would point the scan at an assembly with no configurations in it. There are four such per-service migrations projects under `MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosting/` (Conference, Engagement, Identity, Notification), one per database.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the Domain copy has no consumer at all. The architecture-fitness map does not use either marker: `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.ADC.Architecture.Tests/AdcArchitectureMap.cs:44` pins the Domain assembly with a real aggregate type (`typeof(Engagement.Domain.UserSessionBookmarks.`[UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark)`).Assembly`) and `:46` pins Infrastructure with `Assembly.Load("MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure")`, a name string. So the marker's only production consumer today is the one design-time factory line above.

### ClassReference

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain, MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain`, `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/AssemblyReference.cs:11`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/AssemblyReference.cs:11` · Level 0 · class
>
> *One byte-identical copy per Engagement layer.* This section covers the **Domain** and **Infrastructure** copies; the API and Application copies are covered earlier in this chapter.

- **What it is**: an empty, instantiable class declared at the bottom of the same file as the static marker above, existing purely so the assembly can be named in a generic type argument.

  | Type | File:Line | Notes (what differs) |
  |------|-----------|----------------------|
  | `ClassReference` (Domain) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/AssemblyReference.cs:11` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain` (`:3`); declared for symmetry, no call site today |
  | `ClassReference` (Infrastructure) | `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/AssemblyReference.cs:11` | namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure` (`:3`); declared for symmetry, no call site today |

- **Depends on**: nothing. `public class ClassReference { }` is the whole declaration in both files.
- **Concept**: the companion half of the marker pattern, introduced at framework level under [ClassReference](group-14-module-system-composition.md#classreference). C# forbids a static class as a generic type argument, so a registration helper shaped as `Scan<TAssemblyMarker>()` cannot accept `AssemblyReference`; the empty non-static class fills that slot without weakening the static one. `[Rubric §33, Developer Experience]` assesses how much ceremony the inner loop costs: because every layer of every module carries the identical pair, a developer adding a module writes the same two lines and gets both call shapes for free.
- **Walkthrough**: no members. The only meaningful property of either copy is the assembly it belongs to, which a scanner reads as `typeof(ClassReference).Assembly` inside the generic helper.
- **Why it's built this way**: co-locating both markers in one file makes the pair a single copy-paste unit when a new layer is created, and keeps the "which one do I pass?" answer purely mechanical (static handle for `typeof(...).Assembly`, empty class for `<TMarker>`).
- **Where it's used**: neither of these two copies is referenced anywhere in the repository. The generic-marker call site in the Engagement module is the *Application* copy, `services.ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>()` at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`, which is what discovers the module's domain-event handlers, mappers, command/query handlers, and validators by convention. The Domain layer has nothing to scan for, and the Infrastructure layer registers its one hosted service explicitly instead (see [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection) below).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: both copies are unreferenced. They exist so the marker file is identical in every layer, not because something consumes them; nothing in the build fails if either is deleted. Read nothing here as saying they are wired up.

### GetUserBookmarksQuery

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.UseCases.GetUserBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetUserBookmarks/GetUserBookmarksQuery.cs:8` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the read request for a user's bookmarked sessions as a paged list, with an optional event filter. Unlike [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery](#getbookmarkedsessionidsquery), which returns a lightweight id map, this query yields full bookmark DTOs plus pagination metadata.
- **Depends on**: the `UserIdentifierType` and `EventIdentifierType` aliases (see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)); paired with [GetUserBookmarksHandler](#getuserbookmarkshandler).
- **Concept, a paged query with defaulted parameters.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether list endpoints expose paging and filtering as first-class inputs; this query does, defaulting `PageNumber` to 1 and `PageSize` to 10 so a caller can omit both. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether list reads are bounded: the doc comment (`GetUserBookmarksQuery.cs:7`) records the 500-item ceiling from BR-11, and the handler, not the record, enforces it. The optional `EventIdentifierType?` filter (BR-58, `GetUserBookmarksQuery.cs:5`) is resolved through a Session lookup that lives in another module, which is why the handler reaches into Conference.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record GetUserBookmarksQuery(UserIdentifierType UserId, EventIdentifierType? EventId, int PageNumber = 1, int PageSize = 10)` (`GetUserBookmarksQuery.cs:8-12`). Four positional parameters: the required `UserId`, the nullable `EventId` filter, and the two paging knobs with defaults. The XML doc (`GetUserBookmarksQuery.cs:3-7`) ties each parameter to its business rule.
- **Why it's built this way**: defaulted paging parameters keep the common call simple while still allowing explicit paging; making `EventId` nullable models "all events" as the absence of a filter rather than as a magic value. The `UserId` is a real parameter here (unlike on [GetMyPointsQuery](#getmypointsquery)) because an Organizer is allowed to read another attendee's bookmark list, which is exactly why the endpoint needs an ownership filter at the edge.
- **Where it's used**: constructed by [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller)'s `GET /api/bookmarks` action (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:101`) behind `[ServiceFilter(typeof(OwnerOrAdminFilter))]` (`BookmarksController.cs:91`, [ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)); handled by [GetUserBookmarksHandler](#getuserbookmarkshandler), which returns a [PagedCollectionResult<T>](group-01-result-error-handling.md#pagedcollectionresultt) of [UserSessionBookmarkDTO](#usersessionbookmarkdto).

### ImportTicketRosterCommand

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.ImportTicketRoster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ImportTicketRoster/ImportTicketRosterCommand.cs:15` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the request to dry-run one TicketLeap roster export against an ADC event: report the counts a commit would produce, write nothing (`ImportTicketRosterCommand.cs:3-7`).
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias ([primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)) and the BCL `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`. Paired with [ImportTicketRosterHandler](#importticketrosterhandler) and [ImportTicketRosterCommandValidator](#importticketrostercommandvalidator).
- **Concept, a dry run as its own command.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses whether intent is modeled as distinct messages. The dry run and the commit share one upload endpoint but are two commands: this one answers synchronously with counts, while the commit is [StartTicketRosterImportCommand](#startticketrosterimportcommand), which queues a durable [TicketImportRun](#ticketimportrun) (`ImportTicketRosterCommand.cs:5-6`). Both apply the same [TicketRosterApplier](#ticketrosterapplier) rules, so the preview cannot drift from the result.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record ImportTicketRosterCommand(EventIdentifierType EventId, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> Content)` (`ImportTicketRosterCommand.cs:15-17`). `EventId` is the ADC event the roster is for; `Content` is the raw CSV bytes (`:13-14`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the content is a `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` following the session-asset upload precedent: the size is already capped at `TicketRosterLimits.MaxFileBytes` by the controller and the validator, so one buffer serves both the validator and the parser with no second copy (`ImportTicketRosterCommand.cs:8-12`).
- **Where it's used**: built by [TicketRosterImportController](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) when `POST /tickets/roster` arrives with `dryRun = true` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketRosterImportController.cs:102-106`); validated by [ImportTicketRosterCommandValidator](#importticketrostercommandvalidator) and handled by [ImportTicketRosterHandler](#importticketrosterhandler).

### TicketRosterEntry

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketRosterEntry.cs:15` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the whitelisted fields of one ticket row in a roster upload: everything a [Ticket](#ticket) keeps from the TicketLeap export, and nothing else (`TicketRosterEntry.cs:3-7`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; six string fields, the last nullable.
- **Concept introduced, the whitelist as a type.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]` assesses data minimization. A TicketLeap export carries far more columns than ADC needs; because the parser can only hand the domain this record, any column not named here never reaches the database. The parser also resolves the buyer-name and order-email fallbacks before it builds one, so the aggregate only sees the values it stores (`TicketRosterEntry.cs:5-7`).
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record TicketRosterEntry(string ExternalTicketId, string Barcode, string TicketTypeName, string AttendeeFirstName, string AttendeeLastName, string? OrderEmail)` (`TicketRosterEntry.cs:15-21`). The parameter docs (`:8-14`) record that the attendee names fall back to the buyer's when blank, and that `OrderEmail` comes from `(Order) Email Address`, else `Buyer Email`, else null.
- **Why it's built this way**: as a record it compares by value, which [Ticket](#ticket)`.ApplyRosterEntry` uses directly: it rebuilds an entry from its stored fields and compares it with the normalized incoming one, so "did anything change" is one ordinal record equality (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/Ticket.cs:155-156`).
- **Where it's used**: produced by [TicketLeapRosterParser](#ticketleaprosterparser); consumed by [Ticket](#ticket)`.Create` / `ApplyRosterEntry`, by [TicketInvariants](#ticketinvariants)`.EnsureEntryIsValid`, and by [TicketRosterApplier](#ticketrosterapplier) and [TicketRoster](#ticketroster) in Application. `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.ADC.Architecture.Tests/Privacy/PiiConventionTests.cs` references it as well.

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.ImportTicketRoster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ImportTicketRoster/ImportTicketRosterCommandValidator.cs:11` · Level 1 · class (sealed)

### TicketImportRun

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketImportRun.cs:26` · Level 5 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root for one committed roster import: the durable record the background processor applies the roster from in batches, and the progress every replica reads (`Processed` of `Total`). One run per event is active at a time (`TicketImportRun.cs:9-12`).
- **Depends on**: [AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype), [IAnonymizable](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#ianonymizable), [PiiAttribute](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#piiattribute), [TicketRosterImportStatus](#ticketrosterimportstatus), [TicketRosterImportErrorCodes](#ticketrosterimporterrorcodes), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error).
- **Concept introduced, a long-running job as an aggregate.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether long work survives a crash. The import is too large for one request, so the commit creates this row and an internal command carrying only the run id; the processor resumes at `Processed` after any restart (`:48`). `AbandonAfter` is 30 minutes (`:37`), far above a real run and the processor's 5-minute lease, so an expiry backstop can fail a run whose processor died for good without cutting off a slow one (`:31-36`). [ADR-086](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/086-process-manager-deferred.html) mentions this type.
- **Concept, holder data that lives only while the run does.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]`. The staged roster is the run's only holder data and carries `[Pii]` (`:79-80`). Every way a run ends (`Complete`, `Fail`, `Anonymize`) clears it, so a finished run keeps counts and an error code, never names (`:13-19`). The class is deliberately not `IAuditedEntity`: an audit row of the staged roster would be a second copy of the file the purge could not reach (`:20-23`, [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)).
- **Walkthrough**
  - State: `EventId`, `Status`, `Total`, `Processed`, the outcome counts `Added` / `Updated` / `Unchanged` / `Voided` / `Reinstated` / `LinkedExistingAccounts`, `ErrorCode`, `LastProgressOn` (`:40-73`), and `StagedRoster` (`:80`).
  - `IsActive` is true while `Queued` or `Running` (`:83`); `IsAbandonedAt(now)` is active and idle for at least `AbandonAfter` (`:88`).
  - `Create(eventId, total, stagedRoster, now)` (`:99-119`) refuses a default event, a negative total or a blank roster with `Ticket.Import.Invalid`, else returns a `Queued` run.
  - `RecordBatch(...)` (`:128-137`) moves to `Running`, advances `Processed` (capped at `Total`) and adds the batch's counts, so progress and counts move together.
  - `Complete(voided, linkedExistingAccounts, now)` (`:143-151`) sets `Succeeded`, `Processed = Total`, records the final counts and clears the roster.
  - `Fail(errorCode, now)` (`:157-169`) clears the roster first, then returns `false` for a run that is no longer active, so a finished run is left alone; otherwise it records `Failed` and the code.
  - `Anonymize()` (`:176-180`) clears the roster idempotently; counts and status stay because they name nobody.
- **Where it's used**: created by [StartTicketRosterImportHandler](#startticketrosterimporthandler), advanced by [ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler](#processticketrosterimporthandler), expired by [ExpireTicketRosterImportHandler](#expireticketrosterimporthandler); mapped by [TicketImportRunConfiguration](#ticketimportrunconfiguration) (migration `20261103150907_AddTicketImportRuns`); its `[Pii]` marking is checked by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.ADC.Architecture.Tests/Privacy/PiiConventionTests.cs`.

### Ticket

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/Ticket.cs:30` · Level 6 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root for one ticket of an organizer-uploaded TicketLeap roster. It keeps only the whitelisted columns, and exists to invite the ticket holder (BR-270) and to link the ticket to an account (BR-272, BR-273); door admission stays with TicketLeap (`Ticket.cs:12-15`).

BCL: `System.Globalization` (`:1`).
- **Concept, a rich aggregate with guarded transitions.** `[Rubric §4, DDD]` assesses whether invariants live in the aggregate. Every state change is a named method that refuses an illegal transition with a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) or reports a no-op as `false`, so a re-run never double-applies (the factory and invariant pattern of [ADR-129](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/129-tactical-aggregate-contract.html)).
- **Concept, erasure that survives a re-upload.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]`. The attendee names, the order email and the barcode carry `[Pii]` (`:57-73`), so the audit trail stores them redacted, and the class is `IAuditedEntity` because a disputed link needs a record of the row before (`:16-19`, [ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html)). `Anonymize` overwrites them when the linked account is erased ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)), and an erased ticket then ignores later roster uploads, so re-importing the same file never writes the holder back.

  - State: `EventId`, `SourceEventName`, `ExternalTicketId` (the upsert key), `Barcode` (the claim key), `TicketTypeName`, the attendee names, `OrderEmail` (`:48-73`); `IsAnonymized` is derived from the barcode prefix, not stored (`:79`); then `Status`, `InvitedOn`, `LinkedUserId`, `LinkedOn`, `LinkMethod` (`:82-94`).
  - `Create(eventId, sourceEventName, entry)` (`:114-128`) normalizes first (trim every field, lowercase a well-formed email, keep a malformed one trimmed so the invariant refuses it; `Normalize`, `:378-388`), then combines the event, source-name and entry invariants, and returns a `Live` ticket.
  - `ApplyRosterEntry(sourceEventName, entry)` (`:137-164`) returns `Success(false)` for an anonymized ticket (`:143-144`), validates the normalized entry, and compares by ordinal record equality (`:155-156`), so a casing change on a name counts as a change. It leaves `Status` alone.
  - `ParkBarcodeForImport()` (`:174-181`) moves the barcode to `import-parked-{Id}` so two tickets can swap barcodes across batches without the unique `(EventId, Barcode)` index ever seeing a value twice; never on an erased ticket.
  - `Void()` (`:185-192`) and `Reinstate()` (`:196-203`) flip `Live` / `Voided` and return whether anything moved.
  - `MarkInvited(invitedOn)` (`:212-225`) accepts only a `Live`, unlinked, not yet invited ticket with an order email, else `Ticket.NotEligibleForInvite`.
  - `AnnounceInvitation(eventName, eventStart)` (`:237-266`) raises [TicketHolderInvited](group-24-identity-module.md#ticketholderinvited) before the save so the outbox captures it in the same transaction as the `InvitedOn` stamp (ADR-003), substituting the fallback names for blanks (`:257-263`).
  - `LinkTo(userId, method, linkedOn)` (`:277-310`): relinking to the same account is a no-op success (`:285-286`); a ticket linked elsewhere is `Ticket.LinkedToAnotherAccount` (`:288-295`); a non-`Live` ticket is `Ticket.NotLive` (`:297-304`). `Unlink()` (`:314-323`) clears the link.
  - `Anonymize()` (`:337-344`) blanks the names, clears the email and sets the barcode to `deleted-{Id}`, keeping the ticket id and invite stamp so a later upload finds this row instead of creating a fresh ticket that would invite the erased holder again. `AttendeeNameMatches` (`:353-359`) and the static `NormalizeEmail` (`:367-374`) serve linking.

### GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.UseCases.GetBookmarkedSessionIds` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetBookmarkedSessionIds/GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:12` · Level 8 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the query handler that answers [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsQuery](#getbookmarkedsessionidsquery), returning a read-only dictionary mapping each of a user's bookmarked session ids to its bookmark id. This is the lightweight lookup a listing page uses to decide which rows render as bookmarked, and which bookmark id a delete would target.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (constructor-injected, `GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:12-13`), the [UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark) aggregate it reads, the [IReadRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ireadrepositorytentity-tidentifiertype) it obtains from it, and [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). It implements [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult).
- **Concept, a projection read that never materializes the entity.** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether reads pull only the columns they need; this handler projects, so the SQL selects two columns rather than whole rows. It resolves a *read* repository through `GetReadRepository` (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:20`) rather than the writable one, which signals intent and is also the DI-safe way to obtain a repository: injecting [IRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#irepositorytentity-tidentifiertype) directly into a handler is the trap the persistence chapter warns about. `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` and `[Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]`: the handler sits beside its query in the same use-case folder and returns a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) rather than throwing.
- **Walkthrough**
  - The primary constructor injects [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:12-13`); the class closes the query-handler interface over `Result<IReadOnlyDictionary<SessionIdentifierType, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>>` (`:13`).
  - `HandleAsync` (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:16-18`) obtains the read repository for [UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark) (line 20), then calls `GetProjectedAsync` with `select: b => new { b.SessionId, b.Id }` and `where: b => b.UserId == query.UserId` (`:22-25`), so only the two ids for that user come back. The projection target is an anonymous type here rather than a named record, because it is consumed on the very next line.
  - It materializes the pairs into a dictionary keyed by `SessionId` with value `Id` (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:27`) and wraps it in `Result.Success<IReadOnlyDictionary<...>>` (line 29). There is no failure branch: this read cannot fail, so the [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) is always a success.
- **Why it's built this way**: the caller only needs "is this session bookmarked, and under which bookmark id", so projecting to a two-field shape and returning a dictionary avoids loading full aggregates and gives O(1) per-row lookups while rendering. The doc comment (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler.cs:8-11`) names the consumer explicitly: the unified Sessions page's per-row star state. Soft-deleted bookmarks are excluded by the global query filter, so a removed bookmark simply stops appearing without a predicate here.
- **Where it's used**: dispatched from [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller)'s `GET /api/bookmarks/session-ids` action (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:153-155`) through the [IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) pipeline. Covered by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandlerTests.cs:13`, which asserts the *read* repository is the one requested.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the anonymous projection target is why that test verifies the repository call rather than the returned map; the test's own comment records that a mocked `GetProjectedAsync` cannot produce an anonymous type (`GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandlerTests.cs:20-21`).

### BookmarkCountService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/Services/BookmarkCountService.cs:11` · Level 8 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the in-process implementation of the cross-module [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice), answering "how many active bookmarks does this session have?" for the Conference module, one session at a time or a whole set at once.
- **Depends on**: [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark), [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice). Externals: LINQ and `System.Collections.Generic`.
- **Concept, the cross-module read boundary.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses whether modules talk through explicit, extractable contracts rather than direct references. Conference must show a per-session bookmark count but must not reference Engagement's domain; it depends only on [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice), which lives in `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared`. In process this class satisfies that contract; once Engagement runs as its own service, [`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter`](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter) satisfies it over the wire and no Conference call site changes. This is one direction of the bidirectional Conference/Engagement pair (Engagement in turn calls Conference's [`ISessionBookmarkValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#isessionbookmarkvalidationservice)).
- **Concept introduced, the batch method that keeps the caller from fanning out.** `[Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]` assesses whether read paths avoid N+1 round trips. The second method exists because the conference-day session list needs a count per session, and calling the single-session method in a loop would issue one `COUNT` per row. `GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync` pushes one grouped `COUNT` for the whole set, "so the caller never fans out per session" as the comment puts it (`BookmarkCountService.cs:37-41`), and then guarantees a complete result map, so the caller never has to distinguish "zero bookmarks" from "session missing from the response" (`:43-46`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - The primary constructor injects only [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:11`). Note that no repository is constructor-injected: repositories are resolved per call off the unit of work, which is the framework's rule.
  - `GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync(sessionId, cancellationToken)` (`:14-22`): resolves the typed repository via `unitOfWork.GetRepository<UserSessionBookmark, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>()` (`:18`) and returns the `Task<int>` from `bookmarkRepo.CountAsync(b => b.SessionId == sessionId, cancellationToken)` directly (`:19-21`). The method is not `async`: it has nothing to do after the count, so it skips the state machine and passes the repository's task straight through. The count is a `COUNT` pushed to the database with no rows materialized, and the soft-delete global query filter means only active bookmarks count.
  - `GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync(sessionIds, cancellationToken)` (`:25-47`): guards null with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` (`:29`), short-circuits an empty request to an empty dictionary without touching the database (`:30-33`), then takes the **read** repository (`:35`) and calls its `CountByAsync(b => b.SessionId, b => sessionIds.Contains(b.SessionId), cancellationToken)` (`:38-41`), which returns the grouped counts per session. The final projection walks the requested ids `Distinct()` and builds the dictionary, using `GetValueOrDefault` to fill a 0 for any session the grouped result omitted (`:44-46`).
  - The grouped count lives behind the repository's `CountByAsync`, so this Application-layer class composes no `IQueryable` and needs no EF Core dependency or executor abstraction of its own. `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]`.
- **Why it's built this way**: exposing purpose-built count methods (rather than letting Conference query bookmarks) keeps the read cheap and the coupling to two stable signatures, which is what makes the gRPC swap a thin adapter. The batch method is paired with a schema decision: [`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration`](#usersessionbookmarkconfiguration) adds a `SessionId`-leading index precisely because counting by `SessionId` alone cannot seek the `(UserId, SessionId)` composite (`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration.cs:35-38`).
- **Where it's used**: registered `TryAddScoped` by the Engagement Application DI (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:45`); wrapped for the wire by [`BookmarkCountsGrpcService`](#bookmarkcountsgrpcservice); consumed by Conference's [`GetSessionBookmarkCountHandler`](group-18-conference-application.md#getsessionbookmarkcounthandler) and [`GetSessionBookmarkCountsHandler`](group-18-conference-application.md#getsessionbookmarkcountshandler). When Engagement is disabled in a host, [`DisabledBookmarkCountService`](#disabledbookmarkcountservice) stands in until the gRPC adapter replaces the registration.

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.UseCases.GetUserBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetUserBookmarks/GetUserBookmarksHandler.cs:17` · Level 9 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the query handler for [GetUserBookmarksQuery](#getuserbookmarksquery). It returns a page of a user's bookmarked sessions as DTOs, newest first, with an optional event filter resolved across the module boundary.

Externals: `System.Linq.Expressions` (`:1`).
- **Concept, server-side paging plus a cross-module lookup instead of a join.** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether counting, ordering, and paging happen in the database rather than in memory; every step here does. `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses cross-service reads: the event filter cannot be a SQL join because sessions live in the *Conference* database ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)), so the handler fetches the event's session ids through [ISessionBookmarkValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#isessionbookmarkvalidationservice) (a gRPC client once extracted, [ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html)) and filters on that id set. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` shows in how a Conference outage is handled: the code comment (`GetUserBookmarksHandler.cs:40-42`) states that a failure across the gRPC boundary propagates as a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) failure "so the request degrades gracefully instead of a raw 500".
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleAsync` (`GetUserBookmarksHandler.cs:24-26`) first clamps the page: `PagingMath.Clamp(query.PageNumber, query.PageSize, 500)` (line 31) is the BR-11 cap mechanism, and the comment above it (`:28-30`) records that it also floors a non-positive page number or size and range-checks the offset in 64-bit.
  - It resolves the read repository via `GetReadRepository` (line 33) and declares an `Expression<Func<UserSessionBookmark, bool>> filter` (line 36) so the predicate is built once and used by both the count and the page query.
  - When `query.EventId.HasValue` (line 38) it calls `sessionValidationService.GetSessionIdsByEventAsync(...)` across the module boundary (`:43-44`), unwraps the result with `TryGetValue(out var sessionIds)` and returns `Result.Failure` with the propagated `sessionIdsResult.Errors` when there is no value (`:45-46`), materializes the unwrapped `sessionIds` into a list (line 48, no null-forgiving `Value!` access), and filters bookmarks to that user *and* that session-id set (line 50, BR-58). Otherwise the filter is just `b => b.UserId == query.UserId` (line 54).
  - It counts server-side with `bookmarkRepo.CountAsync(filter, cancellationToken)` (line 58, translated to SQL `COUNT`), then orders and pages server-side by pushing `TableNoTracking.Where(filter).OrderByDescending(b => b.CreatedOn).ThenByDescending(b => b.Id).Skip(skip).Take(take)` through [IQueryableExecutor](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iqueryableexecutor)`.ToListAsync` (`:63-70`, translated to SQL `ORDER BY` plus `OFFSET`/`FETCH`). The `Id` tie-break is load-bearing and commented as such (`:60-62`): `OFFSET`/`FETCH` needs a total row order, or bookmarks created in the same instant "would otherwise repeat or vanish across pages".
  - It maps the page with [UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper](#usersessionbookmarkdtomapper)`.MapToDTOs` (line 72), builds `new PaginationMetadata(totalCount, take, Math.Max(query.PageNumber, 1))` (line 73) using the *clamped* take and a floored page number so the metadata describes what was actually returned, and returns `Result.Success(new PagedCollectionResult<UserSessionBookmarkDTO>(dtos, metadata))` (line 75).
- **Why it's built this way**: pushing count, order, skip, and take into the database keeps the read bounded and cheap even for a user with many bookmarks; resolving the event filter through a service interface (never a cross-database foreign key) is what makes the module independently deployable ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html) and [ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html)). `TableNoTracking` keeps the paged read off the change tracker, and the whole read still honors the soft-delete query filter, so a deleted bookmark simply is not in the page or the count.
- **Where it's used**: dispatched from [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller)'s `GET /api/bookmarks` action (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:100-102`), whose ownership is guarded by the `OwnerOrAdminFilter` configured for the module (`BookmarksController.cs:91`, [ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)). Pinned by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/GetUserBookmarksHandlerTests.cs`, which covers the event-filter path (`:140`), the failure propagation when the session lookup fails (`:161`), the over-large page size (`:199`, `:310`), the page number beyond the reachable offset (`:230`), and the negative page number and page size (`:250`, `:269`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: whether [ISessionBookmarkValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#isessionbookmarkvalidationservice) resolves to an in-process implementation or a gRPC client depends on the host composition, not on this file. This handler now takes the read repository via `GetReadRepository` (`GetUserBookmarksHandler.cs:33`), matching [GetBookmarkedSessionIdsHandler](#getbookmarkedsessionidshandler); the read itself still goes through `TableNoTracking`.

### EngagementPermissions

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Authorization` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Authorization/EngagementPermissions.cs:9` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the module's capability vocabulary: four permission strings plus an `All` list. Endpoints are gated on these capabilities rather than on role names, so "who can do what" is decided in one grant map instead of being spelled out across controllers.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; only `IReadOnlyList<string>` and a collection expression from the BCL. The consumers are elsewhere: [HasPermissionAttribute](group-08-auth.md#haspermissionattribute) on the controllers, [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants) for the role binding, and [IPermissionRegistry](group-08-auth.md#ipermissionregistry) behind the grants.
- **Concept, permission-based authorization instead of role checks.** The framework machinery (the attribute, the registry, `Grant`) is taught under [PermissionRegistry](group-08-auth.md#permissionregistry) and decided in [ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html); the module-specific idea worth teaching here is the *shape of the vocabulary*. The class doc (`EngagementPermissions.cs:4-7`) makes two commitments: endpoints require capabilities, not roles, with the role-to-permission binding declared in [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants), and the values are stable string identifiers because they may end up in tokens or logs. That second point is why these are not an enum: the wire and the log are part of the contract. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether authorization is expressed as least-privilege capability rather than as an identity shortcut, and whether the grant surface is small enough to audit; four constants and one `Grant` call is that surface. `[Rubric §9, API and Contract Design]` applies to the naming: `engagement:tickets:manage` is `module:resource:action`, so a permission is self-describing wherever it surfaces. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` shows in `All`: adding a fifth capability grants it to organizers automatically, because the grant map spreads the list rather than enumerating members.
- **Walkthrough**: four constants and a derived list. Each constant's doc comment records not just what it grants but what deliberately does *not* need it, which is the more useful half.
  - `LiveManage = "engagement:live:manage"` (`EngagementPermissions.cs:17`): the narrowest of the four. It gates only reading the event-wide live poll manage list, every poll of an event in any status. The comment (`:11-16`) records what it deliberately does not gate: authoring, opening, closing and deleting polls and moderating session Q&A are granted by the handlers to the Organizer role and to a session's assigned speakers for that session (BR-236). The controller states the same boundary from the other side: the per-session manage list is "Deliberately NOT behind" this permission so assigned speakers get the real list rather than an organizer-only 403 (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/LivePollsController.cs:165-170`).
  - `CheckInManage = "engagement:checkin:manage"` (`:24`): scan an attendee badge, record a manual check-in, read the attendance rollup. The comment (`:19-23`) records why fetching your own badge is authenticated-only: an attendee needs no capability to see their own QR.
  - `PointsViewOverview = "engagement:points:view-overview"` (`:31`): read the organizer points rollup (participation, payouts per activity, recent activity). Again the comment (`:26-30`) states the boundary: an attendee's own points and the opt-in leaderboard are authenticated-only, and only the organizer rollup is gated.
  - `TicketsManage = "engagement:tickets:manage"` (`:38`): manage an event's ticket roster, meaning upload and delete the TicketLeap roster, send the ticket-holder invites, link existing accounts, and read the roster summary and insights (BR-269). The comment (`:33-37`) keeps the attendee side open: claiming a ticket by barcode and reading your own tickets are authenticated-only.
  - `All` (`:40-47`) is a `public static IReadOnlyList<string>` (`:41`) initialized from a collection expression listing the four constants. It is a get-only property over an immutable-facing interface, so a caller can enumerate it but not append to it.
- **Why it's built this way**: the four-capability split follows the same rule as the flag list, but along a different axis: a capability exists where an *organizer-only* action would otherwise have to be spelled as a role check inside a controller. Everything an attendee does to their own data stays on plain authenticated access plus the ownership filter, which is why there is no `engagement:bookmarks:*` capability at all: bookmark ownership is enforced by [OwnerOrAdminFilter](group-08-auth.md#owneroradminfilter) ([ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)), configured with ADC's ownership vocabulary in the module's own API registration (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:45-56`, Organizer as the bypass role at `:54`), not by a permission. Where speakers need rights, the rule lives in the handlers (BR-236), which is why `LiveManage` gates a single organizer read.
- **Where it's used**: granted by [EngagementPermissionGrants](#engagementpermissiongrants)`.Apply`, which `AddModuleEngagementAPI` registers with `services.AddPermissions(EngagementPermissionGrants.Apply)` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/DependencyInjection.cs:61`) and the Identity service's [TokenPermissionGrants](group-24-identity-module.md#tokenpermissiongrants) also calls (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Service/Authorization/TokenPermissionGrants.cs:57`). Consumed as attribute arguments at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/PointsController.cs:122` (`PointsViewOverview`), `LivePollsController.cs:152` (`LiveManage`), `CheckInsController.cs:105`, `:129`, `:213` (`CheckInManage`), and [TicketsController](#ticketscontroller)`.cs:65`, `:94`, `:170`, `:193`, `:217`, `:243`, `:294` plus [TicketRosterImportController](#ticketrosterimportcontroller)`.cs:60`, `:125` (`TicketsManage`). Outside the module, the Identity host's verified-user lookup refuses a caller that holds `TicketsManage` neither as a claim nor through its roles (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Service/Grpc/VerifiedUserLookupGrpcService.cs:46-47`). Pinned by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Tests/Authorization/EngagementPermissionGrantsTests.cs`, which builds the real registry from `AddModuleEngagementAPI()` (`:27`) and asserts that organizers hold every capability (`:32`), that `"Admin"` holds none because it is not an ADC role (`:49`), and that attendees (`:61`) and content editors (`:73`) hold none.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: whether a given caller actually presents the Organizer role depends on token issuance in the Identity module, not on anything in this file. The poll and Q&A moderation actions that `LiveManage` does not gate live on [SessionQuestionsController](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionscontroller) and the live-poll controllers, covered in the live-layer chapter.

### CheckInErrorCodes

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInErrorCodes.cs:7` · Level 0 · static class

- **What it is**: the three stable error codes the check-in handlers emit and the self-service QR landing pages branch on, declared once in the Shared project that both sides reference.
- **Depends on**: nothing (three `const string` fields). Consumed together with [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult), which carries the code back from the transport layer.
- **Concept introduced, the error code as a client-facing contract.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether failures are expressed in a form a client can branch on. HTTP status codes are not enough here: "nothing is scheduled in this room" is a not-found error ([RecordRoomCheckInHandler](#recordroomcheckinhandler)`.cs:164-165`), so a page choosing its state from the status alone cannot tell it apart from a feature that is off or a target that does not exist. A stable machine-readable code in the ProblemDetails body is the distinguishing signal, and it must never be a human-readable message, because that message is localized and would break the branch in any non-English locale. The placement is the second half of the contract. The type doc (`CheckInErrorCodes.cs:3-6`) says the codes are shared by the handlers that emit them and the pages that read them "so a rename on one side fails the build on the other": one declaration site means neither a handler nor a page spells a code out inline, so a typo is a compile error rather than a silently unreachable branch.
- **Walkthrough** (`CheckInErrorCodes.cs:7-23`):
  - `EventNotPublished = "CheckIns.EventNotPublished"` (`:10`): the owning event is not published yet, so nothing is being recorded for it.
  - `NoCurrentSession = "CheckIns.NoCurrentSession"` (`:16`): nothing is scheduled in the scanned room at this instant. The member comment (`:12-15`) records the security decision folded into it: an unknown room answers the same way by design, so the state never confirms which room identifiers exist.
  - `RoomCodeRejected = "CheckIns.RoomCodeRejected"` (`:22`): the scanned room code is missing or no longer current because an organizer issued a new one (`:18-21`), so the attendee is asked to scan the code posted at the room door.
- **Why it's built this way**: the deliberate absence is as informative as the presence. There is no constant for "feature disabled" or "unknown target": those fall through to the pages' generic unavailable state ([`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin)`.razor.cs:139`, [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit)`.razor.cs:123`). Refusing to name them is what keeps a printed code from confirming which sponsors or rooms exist ([ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html)).
- **Where it's used**: emitted by [`CheckInProcessor`](#checkinprocessor) for the shared not-published failure (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:30`) and by [`RecordRoomCheckInHandler`](#recordroomcheckinhandler) for a rejected room code and an empty room (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/RecordRoomCheckIn/RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:159`, `:165`). Read by [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin), which maps all three codes onto page states (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Rooms/RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:136-138`), and by [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit), which maps only `EventNotPublished` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Sponsors/SponsorVisit.razor.cs:122`), since a sponsor visit has no room code.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: a code shared at compile time still crosses the wire as a string, so a client built against an older Shared assembly sees a new code as unknown and falls into its generic state. That degradation is a consequence of the pattern-match fallback (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:139`), not something a test pins.

### CheckInResultDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInResultDTO.cs:8` · Level 0 · record class

- **What it is**: the response body of both organizer check-in endpoints, who the badge resolved to, whether this was a repeat, and when the check-in was recorded.
- **Depends on**: the `UserIdentifierType` alias (module-specific `global using`, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)). Externals: BCL `DateTimeOffset`.
- **Concept, a repeat is a success, not a conflict.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses how a write's idempotent semantics are expressed to clients. The obvious design answers 409 on a second scan; this one answers 200 with `AlreadyCheckedIn = true` (`CheckInResultDTO.cs:3-7`). The reason is operational: the organizer scanning a lanyard needs the attendee's identity on screen either way, and at a door a second scan is a normal event rather than a client error to correct. Encoding the repeat as **data on a success** means the calling UI has one code path, and the status code stops carrying business meaning. [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) states the same rule at its POST (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:90-96`).
- **Walkthrough** (`CheckInResultDTO.cs:8-18`): three `required` `init` members. `UserId` (line 11) is the attendee the credential resolved to, which is the whole point of the scan response, since the organizer scans an opaque code and needs a person back. `AlreadyCheckedIn` (line 14) is the repeat flag. `CheckedInOn` (line 17) is the recorded time and, on a repeat, deliberately the **original** time rather than "now", so the UI can say "already checked in at ...". [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor) fills it from the existing row on the repeat branch (`.../CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:62-67`) and from the new entity otherwise (`:78-83`).
- **Why it's built this way**: `required` + `init` makes every field non-optional at construction and the value immutable afterwards, so no handler can return a partially filled outcome. The type carries no session or event id because the caller supplied those; only the facts the server discovered travel back.
- **Where it's used**: returned by [CheckInAttendeeHandler](#checkinattendeehandler) and [ManualCheckInHandler](#manualcheckinhandler) through [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), surfaced by [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) on `POST` and `POST manual` (`CheckInsController.cs:99`, `:89`), and consumed client-side by [ICheckInUIService](#icheckinuiservice)/[CheckInService](#checkinservice) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/ICheckInUIService.cs:27`, `:33`) into [CheckInScan](#checkinscan)'s result list (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:212`).
