### SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest.cs:8` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the request body for joining or leaving the public leaderboard. One boolean, nothing else.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party.
- **Concept, the request shape as the security control.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether a surface can be misused by a caller who controls the payload, and `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses contracts that make the wrong call impossible to express. The published display name is resolved from the caller's token principal server-side by [`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler`](#setleaderboardparticipationhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/UseCases/SetLeaderboardParticipation/SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler.cs:76`) and is deliberately absent from this record (`SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest.cs:4-6`). A `DisplayName` property here would let any caller publish a name they do not own on the one surface whose purpose is showing names to other attendees. ### PointsEntryDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/PointsEntryDTO.cs:7` · Level 1 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: one awarded entry from the points ledger, as seen on the wire: id, activity, points, subject, and when it happened.
- **Depends on**: [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype), [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys) (for the meaning of `SubjectKey`), and the `PointsEntryIdentifierType` alias (`int`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.GlobalUsings.IdentifierType.cs:11`).
- **Concept, the append-only ledger row and its snapshot value.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` assesses whether history is preserved rather than recomputed. `Points` is what the rules said at award time, not what the current configuration would pay (`PointsEntryDTO.cs:4-5`, and the same statement on the writer, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/Services/PointsAwarder.cs:13-18`). Retuning the economy mid-conference therefore changes the next award and never rewrites an attendee's history, which is what makes a total explainable.
- **Concept, the DTO that deliberately omits the owner.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` and `[Rubric §11, Security]`. There is no `UserId` on this record, and that absence is load-bearing: the same type serves the caller's own ledger (where the owner is the caller by construction) and the organizer's recent-activity tail (where the owner must not be disclosed). [`GetPointsOverviewHandler`](#getpointsoverviewhandler) projects a private `OverviewRow` that does carry the user id, uses it only for the distinct participant count, and drops it before anything leaves the handler (`GetPointsOverviewHandler.cs:91-107`, `:72-80`, `:84`).
- **Walkthrough** (`PointsEntryDTO.cs:7-23`): `Id` (line 10), declared `required`, so a projection that forgets to copy the entry id fails to compile instead of shipping a default `0` that would break the id tie-break in the ledger sort (both producers set it explicitly, `GetMyPointsHandler.cs:58`, `GetPointsOverviewHandler.cs:74`); `ActivityType` (line 13); `Points` (line 16), the snapshot; `SubjectKey` (line 19), defaulted to `string.Empty`, holding the `event:` / `session:` / `sponsor:` key built by [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys); `OccurredOnUtc` (line 22), a UTC `DateTime`.
- **Why it's built this way**: `OccurredOnUtc` is separate from the row's audit `CreatedOn` because an award can be written by a handler reacting to an event that happened earlier; the ledger sorts on the earn instant, with the id as the tie-break so awards stamped in the same instant keep a stable order across pages (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/UseCases/GetMyPoints/GetMyPointsHandler.cs:79-88`).
- **Where it's used**: [`MyPointsDTO.Entries`](#mypointsdto) via [`GetMyPointsHandler`](#getmypointshandler) (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:55-66`) and [`PointsOverviewDTO.RecentEntries`](#pointsoverviewdto) via [`GetPointsOverviewHandler`](#getpointsoverviewhandler) (`GetPointsOverviewHandler.cs:66-80`).

### PointsSubjectKeys

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/PointsSubjectKeys.cs:11` · Level 1 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the one place that formats the subject key scoping an award to the thing it was earned on. Three factories (`event:`, `session:`, `sponsor:`) plus the column-length constant they must fit.
- **Depends on**: [`NotificationScopeKey`](group-10-notifications.md#notificationscopekey) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Notifications` (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:2`), and the module identifier aliases `EventIdentifierType`, `SessionIdentifierType`, `SponsorIdentifierType` (solution-wide `global using`, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)). Externals: `System.Globalization` and `string.Create` (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:1`, `:32`).
- **Concept introduced, the idempotency key built in one place.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` assesses whether the schema's guarantees have a single owner in code, and `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses single responsibility. An award is idempotent because of the unique index on `(UserId, ActivityType, SubjectKey)` (`PointsEntryConfiguration.cs:45-48`). That index only works if every producer of a subject key formats it identically: `session:42` and `Session: 42` are different rows and therefore two awards for one attendance. This class exists so no call site ever hand-formats the string (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:7-9`): one shape, one culture, one place to change it. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`.
- **Concept, the format is shared with the notification scope key rather than re-derived.** The event- and session-scoped keys are not formatted here at all: `ForEvent` and `ForSession` delegate to `NotificationScopeKey.ForEvent` / `NotificationScopeKey.ForSession` in MMCA.Common (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:20`, `:26`). That is deliberate, because the two subsystems already agreed on the same string. The framework type owns the format, the `event`/`session` prefixes, and the regex that guards it, `^(event|session):[0-9]+$`, which the notification hub enforces before a client may join a live group (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Notifications/NotificationScopeKey.cs:20-51`, `:32`). Delegating means a points key and a live-channel key for the same session are byte-identical and cannot drift apart. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` and `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven Design]`: the shared format lives in the framework, and the ADC-specific extension of it (the sponsor scope, which the notification pattern does not know about) stays in the module.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `MaxLength = 64` (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:14`): the ceiling the column accepts. Both halves of the system read this same constant, the EF configuration through `HasMaxLength(PointsSubjectKeys.MaxLength)` (`PointsEntryConfiguration.cs:38-40`) and the domain through [`PointsEntryInvariants`](#pointsentryinvariants)`.EnsureSubjectKeyIsValid`, which range-checks 1 to `MaxLength` through [`CommonInvariants`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants)`.EnsureStringLengthIsWithin` (`PointsEntryInvariants.cs:36-44`), so a truncating schema and a permissive validator cannot drift apart.
  - `ForEvent(eventId)` (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:19-20`) and `ForSession(sessionId)` (`:25-26`): thin forwards to `NotificationScopeKey`, so the `event:{id}` and `session:{id}` shapes have exactly one definition in the codebase.
  - `ForSponsor(sponsorId)` (`PointsSubjectKeys.cs:31-32`): the one key formatted locally, `string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"sponsor:{sponsorId}")`. There is no sponsor scope in the notification pattern, so this scope is Engagement's own. `string.Create` with an explicit `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` is the deliberate choice over plain interpolation: an id formatted under a culture with non-ASCII digits or different separators would produce a key that never matches the one written yesterday. The framework methods it forwards to make the same choice for the same reason (`NotificationScopeKey.cs:16-18`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the subject key is the half of the idempotency rule that varies per activity, so it has to be data rather than a column. Encoding the scope as a prefix (`event:`, `session:`, `sponsor:`) keeps one column serving three scopes without a discriminator column, and keeps the key human-readable in a support query.
- **Where it's used**: [`AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler`](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler) picks the scope per check-in (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler.cs:125`, `:81`, `:92`); [`SessionFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler`](#sessionfeedbacksubmittedpointshandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/SessionFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:42`), [`EventFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler`](#eventfeedbacksubmittedpointshandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/EventFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:40`), and [`SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler`](#sessionquestionsubmittedpointshandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/DomainEventHandlers/SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:94`) each build theirs the same way. The value ends up on [`PointsEntryDTO`](#pointsentrydto) and [`UserEngagementPointsEntryExportDTO`](#userengagementpointsentryexportdto).

### MyPointsDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/MyPointsDTO.cs:7` · Level 2 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the caller's own points view: the running total, their leaderboard status and published name, and a page of the entries behind the total.
- **Depends on**: [`PointsEntryDTO`](#pointsentrydto).
- **Concept, the always-caller-scoped read model.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether a read can be widened by a hostile caller. This DTO has no user id on it, and neither does the route that returns it: [`GetMyPointsHandler`](#getmypointshandler) resolves the attendee through [`ICurrentUserService`](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice)`.RequireUserId("Points.Forbidden")` and returns that failure verbatim when the token carries no user id (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:41-45`). The paging arguments select how much of the caller's own ledger comes back, never whose ledger it is (`PointsController.cs:45-49`), and they are clamped through [`PagingMath`](group-03-querying-specifications.md#pagingmath)`.Clamp` against a `MaxPageSize` of 100 rather than trusted (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:31-32`, `:48-51`).
- **Concept, total summed on read rather than materialized.** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether a read cost is proportionate to the workload. `Total` is the sum of every entry the caller owns, computed per request (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:90-94`), not a counter maintained on a user row. The handler documents the trade explicitly (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:16-23`): at conference scale (about 100 attendees, a few dozen entries each) the summed read is trivial and it removes the class of bug where a materialized total drifts from its ledger. The named scale lever, if the population ever grows, is a materialized total updated by the awarder, and it would change only that handler and [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder).
- **Walkthrough** (`MyPointsDTO.cs:7-20`): `Total` (line 10), summed over every entry and not just the returned page; `IsOnLeaderboard` (line 13); `LeaderboardDisplayName` (line 16), nullable, null when the caller is not on the board; `Entries` (line 19), an `IReadOnlyList<PointsEntryDTO>` defaulted to `[]` and returned newest first.
- **Why it's built this way**: carrying the leaderboard status on the same document the points page already fetches means the UI renders the join/leave toggle without a second round trip; the opt-in read relies on the soft-delete query filter, so an attendee who left the board correctly reports as not on it (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:68-77`). `IsOnLeaderboard` is derived from `displayName is not null` rather than carried as its own column, so the flag and the name can never disagree (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:95-96`).
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller)`.GetMyPointsAsync` from `GET /api/points/me` (`PointsController.cs:50-66`); fetched client-side by [`IPointsUIService`](#ipointsuiservice) / [`PointsService`](#pointsservice) (`PointsService.cs:21-39`) for the [`MyPoints`](#mypoints) page.

### PointsOverviewDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/PointsOverviewDTO.cs:12` · Level 2 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the organizer rollup of the points game: how many attendees are playing, what has been paid out, the per-activity breakdown, and a tail of recent activity.
- **Depends on**: [`PointsActivityTotalDTO`](#pointsactivitytotaldto), [`PointsEntryDTO`](#pointsentrydto).
- **Concept, the cross-attendee read that carries no attendee.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether a privileged view exposes more personal data than its purpose needs. This is the only points surface that reads across every attendee, and it is built so there is nothing to leak: `RecentEntries` carries entry ids, activity, points, and timestamps only (`PointsOverviewDTO.cs:6-10`), so an organizer sees THAT points were earned and for what, never by whom. Who earned what stays with the attendee and with the leaderboard names those attendees chose to publish. `[Rubric §11, Security]`: the endpoint is additionally gated by `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.PointsViewOverview)]` on top of the controller-level `[Authorize]` (`PointsController.cs:35`, `:120-121`), the permission model of [ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html).
- **Walkthrough** (`PointsOverviewDTO.cs:12-25`): `ParticipantCount` (line 15), distinct attendees with at least one entry; `TotalPointsAwarded` (line 18); `PerActivity` (line 21), the [`PointsActivityTotalDTO`](#pointsactivitytotaldto) breakdown, defaulted to `[]`; `RecentEntries` (line 24), newest first, defaulted to `[]`.
- **Why it's built this way**: [`GetPointsOverviewHandler`](#getpointsoverviewhandler) reads the ledger once and folds every figure in memory rather than issuing a query per number (`GetPointsOverviewHandler.cs:17-21`, `:41-50`): the Application layer has no EF Core reference, so a SQL `GROUP BY` is not available to it, and at conference scale one projected pass is cheaper than the round trips a per-figure query set would cost. The requested tail length is clamped with `Math.Clamp(query.RecentCount, 1, MaxRecentCount)` against a ceiling of 100 (`GetPointsOverviewHandler.cs:27-28`, `:38`). `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]`: the trade is documented along with the materialized-rollup lever that would replace it.
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller)`.GetPointsOverviewAsync` from `GET /api/points/overview` (`PointsController.cs:114-136`); rendered by [`OrganizerPointsOverview`](#organizerpointsoverview) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Points/OrganizerPointsOverview.razor.cs:40`).

### PointsSettings

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/PointsSettings.cs:13` · Level 9 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the configuration object for the points economy: what each earn rule pays and how long the public leaderboard is. Bound from the `Points` configuration section.
- **Depends on**: [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype). Externals: the options binder (`Microsoft.Extensions.Options`), through the host's `AddOptions<PointsSettings>().Bind(...)`.
- **Concept introduced, configuration as an operational control, not just a default.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]` assesses how configuration is bound and consumed, and `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]` assesses whether an operator can degrade a feature without a deploy. A value of 0, or a missing configuration entry (which binds to 0), is a deliberate per-rule kill switch: [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) reads `GetPointsFor(activity)` and returns success without writing anything when the value is not positive (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/Services/PointsAwarder.cs:43-51`), so one earn rule can be turned off mid-conference while the rest keep earning, and the ledger is not polluted with zero-value entries (`PointsSettings.cs:7-10`).
- **Concept, deliberately not `ValidateOnStart`.** The Engagement host binds these options without eager validation, and the inline comment states why (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:131-133`): a missing `Points` section binds every award to the defaults below, and an explicit 0 is the documented kill switch, so there is no value an organizer could set that should stop this host from booting mid-conference. The same comment also explains why the binding lives in the host rather than in `AddEngagementModule`: the module registration takes no `IConfiguration` (`Program.cs:127-130`). Contrast the pattern with [`CheckInSettings`](#checkinsettings), bound the same way immediately after for the same reason (`Program.cs:137-142`). `[Rubric §13, Observability & Operability]`: the failure mode chosen here is "boot and keep serving", not "refuse to start".
- **Walkthrough**
  - `SectionName = "Points"` (`PointsSettings.cs:16`): the constant the host binds against, so the section name is not duplicated as a literal at the call site (`Program.cs:134-135`).
  - Six `int` award properties with defaults: `EventCheckIn = 25` (line 18), `SessionCheckIn = 10` (line 21), `SessionFeedback = 15` (line 24), `EventFeedback = 15` (line 27), `QuestionAsked = 5` (line 30), `SponsorVisit = 20` (line 37). The deployed `appsettings.json` sets exactly these same values (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/appsettings.json:26-34`), so the checked-in defaults are the live economy.
  - `SponsorVisit` carries the longest doc comment of the six (`PointsSettings.cs:33-37`) and it is the interesting one: the deep link an attendee scans is shareable, so the once-per-sponsor cap enforced by the subject key plus a bounded value is what makes passing the URL around worthless.
  - `LeaderboardSize = 10` (line 40): how many rows the public board shows. [`GetLeaderboardHandler`](#getleaderboardhandler) reads it through `Math.Max(settings.Value.LeaderboardSize, 0)` before `Take(...)` (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:63`, `:70`), so a negative configured value yields an empty board rather than an exception.
  - `GetPointsFor(activity)` (`PointsSettings.cs:49-59`): a `switch` expression over [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) with a `_ => 0` arm (line 57), so an undefined activity is treated exactly like a configured 0 and awards nothing.
- **Why it's built this way**: `init`-only properties keep the bound options immutable after startup, and putting `GetPointsFor` on the settings object rather than in the awarder means the "what is this worth" lookup has one home; the awarder is left holding only the idempotency and persistence concerns. Keeping the type in `*.Shared` (not Application) is what lets the host bind it without referencing the Application layer.
- **Where it's used**: bound by the Engagement service host (`Program.cs:134-135`); injected as `IOptions<PointsSettings>` into [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) (`PointsAwarder.cs:32`, `:46`) and [`GetLeaderboardHandler`](#getleaderboardhandler) (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:30`, `:63`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: whether a live production deployment overrides any of these values through environment configuration is not determinable from source; the repository shows only the checked-in `appsettings.json` values, which match the class defaults.

### ClaimTicketRequest
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/ClaimTicketRequest.cs:7` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the body of an attendee's barcode claim (BR-273, UC-50): the event and the barcode printed on the TicketLeap ticket. The account is never part of the request; the handler takes it from the token (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:3-6`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party beyond the `EventIdentifierType` alias (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:20`).
- **Concept**: a Shared-layer contract that also owns a number. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether contracts are explicit and stable; here the request is a `record class` with `required`/`init` members (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:17,20`), and it carries the one declaration of the barcode length so every layer agrees on it. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether identity comes from a trusted source; leaving the user id out of the body means a caller cannot claim on someone else's behalf.
- **Walkthrough**: `BarcodeMaxLength = 100` (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:14`) is declared here because Shared is the lowest layer every consumer reaches (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:9-13`). `EventId` (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:17`) and `Barcode` (`ClaimTicketRequest.cs:20`) are both `required`.
- **Why it's built this way**: writing the limit once removes drift between the UI input cap, the validator and the domain. [`TicketInvariants`](#ticketinvariants) re-exports the same constant (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketInvariants.cs:21`), and [`ClaimTicketRequestValidator`](#claimticketrequestvalidator) enforces it through that alias (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ClaimTicket/ClaimTicketRequestValidator.cs:23-24`).
- **Where it's used**: bound from the body of `TicketsController.ClaimAsync` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:137-138`), handled by [`ClaimTicketHandler`](#claimtickethandler) as an `ICommandHandler<ClaimTicketRequest, Result<MyTicketDTO>>` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ClaimTicket/ClaimTicketHandler.cs:38,44-45`), and sent by the UI [`TicketService`](#ticketservice).

### SendTicketInvitesRequest
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/SendTicketInvitesRequest.cs:6` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the organizer's request to email one invite per eligible order email of an event's roster (BR-270, UC-49) (`SendTicketInvitesRequest.cs:3-5`).
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias only.
- **Concept**: same request-record shape as [`ClaimTicketRequest`](#claimticketrequest); the new element is a dry-run switch that turns a side-effecting command into a preview.
- **Walkthrough**: `EventId` is `required` (`SendTicketInvitesRequest.cs:9`); `DryRun` (`SendTicketInvitesRequest.cs:12`) is optional and defaults to `false`, and when set the run reports counts without sending anything (`SendTicketInvitesRequest.cs:11`).

### TicketAccountLinkResultDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:9` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the outcome of linking an event's roster to accounts that already exist with a confirmed address (BR-277, UC-55). Every Live, unlinked ticket carrying an order email lands in exactly one of the three counts (`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:3-8`).
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept**: a partitioning result DTO. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether a response explains itself; the three buckets add up to the population considered, so an organizer can see why a ticket was not linked rather than only how many were.
- **Walkthrough**: `EventId` (`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:12`); `Linked` (`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:15`), the tickets this run linked; `LeftForBarcode` (`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:22`), tickets whose order email belongs to an account but sit on a multi-ticket order where none (or not this one) carries the account's name, so they wait for a barcode claim (BR-273); `NoAccount` (`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:25`), tickets whose order email has no account with a confirmed address. All are `required`.
- **Why it's built this way**: the doc comment records the idempotency property: a re-run reports zero linked, because the rules that linked nothing the first time link nothing the second (`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO.cs:6-7`).
- **Where it's used**: produced by [`ExistingAccountLinker`](#existingaccountlinker) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/ExistingAccountLinker.cs:42`), returned by [`LinkExistingAccountsHandler`](#linkexistingaccountshandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/LinkExistingAccounts/LinkExistingAccountsHandler.cs:26,29`) and `TicketsController.LinkExistingAccountsAsync` (`TicketsController.cs:99`), and read by [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice) for the [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster) page.

### TicketInvitesResultDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketInvitesResultDTO.cs:6` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the counts an invite run reports back, for a real run or a dry run.
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept**: the response half of [`SendTicketInvitesRequest`](#sendticketinvitesrequest). `[Rubric §31, Cost/FinOps]` assesses whether consumption of metered resources is bounded; `Remaining` makes the per-run cap from [`TicketSettings`](#ticketsettings) visible instead of silently truncating the send.
- **Walkthrough**: `EventId` (`TicketInvitesResultDTO.cs:9`); `DryRun` (`TicketInvitesResultDTO.cs:12`) echoes the request flag; `Sent` (`TicketInvitesResultDTO.cs:15`) counts distinct order emails sent (or that would be); `TicketsCovered` (`TicketInvitesResultDTO.cs:18`) counts the tickets those invites cover, since one buyer may hold several; `Remaining` (`TicketInvitesResultDTO.cs:21`) counts eligible order emails left over by the cap for the next run.
- **Why it's built this way**: the cap is applied per distinct email (`SendTicketInvitesHandler.cs:16,54`), so the DTO separates emails from tickets to keep both numbers honest.
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`SendTicketInvitesHandler`](#sendticketinviteshandler) (`SendTicketInvitesHandler.cs:38,41`) and `TicketsController.SendInvitesAsync` (`TicketsController.cs:70`); shown on the [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster) page through [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice).

### TicketLinkMethod
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketLinkMethod.cs:9` · Level 0 · enum

- **What it is**: how a roster ticket came to be linked to an account: by a verified order email (BR-272) or by a barcode claim (BR-273) (`TicketLinkMethod.cs:3-7`).

### TicketRosterImportErrorCodes
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Imports` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Imports/TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.cs:7` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the machine-readable error codes of a roster import run (UC-48), shared by the API that sets them and the upload component that words them in the selected language. None carries holder data (`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.cs:3-6`).
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept**: error codes as a cross-tier contract. `[Rubric §27, i18n]` assesses whether user-facing text is localized rather than baked into server responses; the server sends a stable code and the UI maps it to a resource key, so the wording follows the user's language.
- **Walkthrough**: four `const string` codes: `AlreadyRunning = "Ticket.Import.AlreadyRunning"` (`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.cs:10`), `Failed` (`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.cs:13`), `Abandoned` (`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.cs:16`, the run stopped making progress and was ended by its backstop), and `NoRun` (`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.cs:19`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the server-side owners re-export the codes rather than restating the strings: [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun)`.AbandonedErrorCode` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketImportRun.cs:29`), `StartTicketRosterImportHandler.AlreadyRunningCode` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/StartRosterImport/StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:37`), `ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler.FailedCode` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ProcessRosterImport/ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:40`) and `GetTicketRosterImportHandler.NoRunCode` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetRosterImport/GetTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:18`).
- **Where it's used**: [`TicketImportRunGuard`](#ticketimportrunguard) raises `AlreadyRunning` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/TicketImportRunGuard.cs:21`); the UI maps codes to resource keys in [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Tickets/TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:42,261`) and [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Tickets/TicketRoster.razor.cs:38`).

### TicketRosterImportResultDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:8` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the outcome of a synchronous roster upload (BR-268, UC-48): what the upload did, or for a dry run what it would do. Every ticket in the file lands in exactly one of Added, Updated, Unchanged or Reinstated; Voided counts tickets of the same source event the file no longer contains (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:3-7`).
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept**: a reconciliation report. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`: the partition is stated in the contract itself, so a consumer can check `TotalInFile` against the four per-ticket buckets.
- **Walkthrough**: `EventId` (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:11`), `SourceEventName` (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:14`, the TicketLeap `Event Name` from the file), `DryRun` (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:17`), `TotalInFile` (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:20`), then `Added`, `Updated`, `Unchanged`, `Voided`, `Reinstated` (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:23-35`), all `required`. `LinkedExistingAccounts` (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:42`) is optional: the tickets a committed upload linked to accounts already holding a confirmed address (BR-277), zero for a dry run and zero when the account lookup was unavailable, in which case the organizer's "Link existing accounts" run retries it (`TicketRosterImportResultDTO.cs:37-41`).
- **Why it's built this way**: `LinkedExistingAccounts` is not `required` because the linking step is best-effort after the roster is written; the field defaulting to zero keeps the upload result valid when that step is skipped.
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`ImportTicketRosterHandler`](#importticketrosterhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ImportTicketRoster/ImportTicketRosterHandler.cs:22,25`) via [`TicketRosterImportReport`](#ticketrosterimportreport), exposed by [`TicketRosterImportController`](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketRosterImportController.cs:37`), and shown by [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload). The committed-run counterpart is [`TicketRosterImportRunDTO`](#ticketrosterimportrundto).

### TicketRosterImportStatus
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Imports` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Imports/TicketRosterImportStatus.cs:7` · Level 0 · enum

- **What it is**: the lifecycle states of a background roster import run.
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept**: a small state-machine enum. `[Rubric §4, DDD]` assesses whether aggregates guard their own transitions; [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun) is the only writer of these values, moving `Queued -> Running -> Succeeded` or to `Failed` (`TicketImportRun.cs:114,130,145,165`).
- **Walkthrough**: `Queued = 0` (`TicketRosterImportStatus.cs:10`, recorded and waiting for the background processor), `Running = 1` (`TicketRosterImportStatus.cs:13`, applying batches while the processed count moves), `Succeeded = 2` (`TicketRosterImportStatus.cs:16`, counts final), `Failed = 3` (`TicketRosterImportStatus.cs:19`, stopped early; the error code says why and a re-upload completes it).
- **Why it's built this way**: `Queued` is zero, so a defaulted run is the not-yet-started state. Queued and Running together define "active" both on the aggregate (`TicketImportRun.cs:83`) and on [`TicketRosterImportRunDTO`](#ticketrosterimportrundto).
- **Where it's used**: [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun), [`TicketImportRunGuard`](#ticketimportrunguard), [`StartTicketRosterImportHandler`](#startticketrosterimporthandler), and the polling loop in [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload) (`TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:217,246`).

### TicketRosterLimits
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketRosterLimits.cs:8` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the size bounds for a roster upload (BR-268), shared by the endpoint, the command validators and the upload page so all three refuse the same file (`TicketRosterLimits.cs:3-7`).
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept**: one constant enforced at every tier. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses input bounding at the edge; `[Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety]` assesses whether the client refuses what the server would. The same number drives Kestrel's request cap, the stream read, the validator and the client pre-check.
- **Walkthrough**: `MaxFileBytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (2 MB, `TicketRosterLimits.cs:11`); `MaxRequestBytes = MaxFileBytes + 65536` (`TicketRosterLimits.cs:14`), the file plus headroom for the multipart form fields.
- **Why it's built this way**: a TicketLeap export of a few thousand tickets is well under a megabyte, so the cap only stops a wrong file, never a real roster (`TicketRosterLimits.cs:5-6`). The request headroom keeps a file at exactly the limit from being rejected by the request-size cap before the controller can answer with a clear message. The Conference module's `SessionAssetLimits` follows the same two-constant shape (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/SessionAssets/SessionAssetLimits.cs:11,20`).
- **Where it's used**: `[RequestSizeLimit(TicketRosterLimits.MaxRequestBytes)]` and the bounded read in [`TicketRosterImportController`](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) (`TicketRosterImportController.cs:59,78,81`); [`ImportTicketRosterCommandValidator`](#importticketrostercommandvalidator) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ImportTicketRoster/ImportTicketRosterCommandValidator.cs:24-25`) and [`StartTicketRosterImportCommandValidator`](#startticketrosterimportcommandvalidator) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/StartRosterImport/StartTicketRosterImportCommandValidator.cs:24-25`); the client pre-check and `OpenReadStream` cap in [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload) (`TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:93,108,118`).

### TicketRosterSummaryDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketRosterSummaryDTO.cs:7` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the headline counts of an event's ticket roster for the organizer page.
- **Depends on**: the `EventIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept**: a read-model DTO; see [`TicketRosterImportResultDTO`](#ticketrosterimportresultdto) for the count-contract shape.

### TicketSettings
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketSettings.cs:7` · Level 0 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the options class for the ticket roster (BR-270), bound from the `"Tickets"` configuration section so an organizer retunes the invite cap without a code change (`TicketSettings.cs:3-6`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; bound through `Microsoft.Extensions.Options`.
- **Concept**: options with working defaults. `[Rubric §31, Cost/FinOps]` and `[Rubric §11, Security]` both apply: the invite cap keeps a run under the shared mail relay's daily quota, and the claim budget throttles barcode guessing per account. The binding deliberately omits `ValidateOnStart` (contrast the fail-fast stance in [ADR-070](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/070-fail-fast-configuration-contract.html)): a missing section binds the defaults, which are a working value rather than a misconfiguration (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:102-106`).
- **Walkthrough**: `SectionName = "Tickets"` (`TicketSettings.cs:10`). `MaxInvitesPerRun = 200` (`TicketSettings.cs:17`) leaves headroom under the relay's daily limit of 300 for confirmation and password-reset mail (`TicketSettings.cs:12-16`). `MaxClaimAttemptsPerUser = 10` (`TicketSettings.cs:24`) within `ClaimAttemptWindowMinutes = 60` (`TicketSettings.cs:27`); an attendee claims one or two tickets, so the budget only bites on someone working through barcodes (`TicketSettings.cs:19-23`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the numbers are operational, not domain rules, so they live in configuration with documented defaults instead of in invariants.
- **Where it's used**: bound at `Program.cs:105-106`; [`SendTicketInvitesHandler`](#sendticketinviteshandler) reads the cap as `Math.Max(0, settings.Value.MaxInvitesPerRun)` (`SendTicketInvitesHandler.cs:36,54`); [`ClaimTicketHandler`](#claimtickethandler) counts attempts in the shared cache over the window and fails with `TooManyRequests` past the limit (`ClaimTicketHandler.cs:36,66-71`).

### TicketStatus
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketStatus.cs:7` · Level 0 · enum

- **What it is**: whether a roster ticket still appears in the organizer's latest upload of its source event (BR-268) (`TicketStatus.cs:3-6`).
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept**: a persisted two-state enum; numbers are added, never renumbered (`TicketStatus.cs:5`), the same stability rule as [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod). Here zero is a real value, because every ticket has a status from creation.
- **Walkthrough**: `Live = 0` (`TicketStatus.cs:10`), in the latest upload; `Voided = 1` (`TicketStatus.cs:13`), a later upload of the same source event no longer contains it.
- **Why it's built this way**: voiding instead of deleting keeps an attendee's link and history if the ticket comes back; [`Ticket`](#ticket) toggles between the two states and short-circuits when already there (`Ticket.cs:102,187-190,198-201`).
- **Where it's used**: almost every roster query filters on `Live`: [`GetTicketRosterSummaryHandler`](#getticketrostersummaryhandler) (`GetTicketRosterSummaryHandler.cs:29-38`), [`ExistingAccountLinker`](#existingaccountlinker) (`ExistingAccountLinker.cs:54`), [`TicketLinker`](#ticketlinker) (`TicketLinker.cs:63`), [`PendingTicketInvitationService`](#pendingticketinvitationservice) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/PendingTicketInvitationService.cs:58`), [`SendTicketInvitesHandler`](#sendticketinviteshandler) (`SendTicketInvitesHandler.cs:116`) and [`GetRosterInsightsHandler`](#getrosterinsightshandler) (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:89,323`). The attendee sees it on [`MyTicketDTO`](#myticketdto).

### MyTicketDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/MyTicketDTO.cs:7` · Level 1 · record

- **What it is**: one ticket linked to the caller (UC-51): what the attendee needs to recognize the ticket, never the order email or the barcode (`MyTicketDTO.cs:3-6`).
- **Depends on**: [`TicketStatus`](#ticketstatus) and [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod) (hence Level 1), plus the `TicketIdentifierType` and `EventIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept**: a data-minimizing projection. `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]` assesses whether personal data leaves the server only where needed; the DTO omits the two fields that could be replayed or harvested (order email, barcode) even though the caller owns the ticket.
- **Walkthrough**: `TicketId` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:10`), `EventId` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:13`), `SourceEventName` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:16`), `TicketTypeName` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:19`), `AttendeeFirstName` / `AttendeeLastName` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:22,25`), `Status` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:28`), `LinkMethod` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:31`) and `LinkedOn` (`MyTicketDTO.cs:34`); all `required`.
- **Why it's built this way**: the projection is an expression (`MyTicketProjection.Selector`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/DTOs/MyTicketProjection.cs:15`), so EF selects only these columns; see manual DTO mapping in [ADR-001](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/001-manual-dto-mapping.html).
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`GetMyTicketsHandler`](#getmyticketshandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetMyTickets/GetMyTicketsHandler.cs:20,23`) and by a successful barcode claim in [`ClaimTicketHandler`](#claimtickethandler) (`ClaimTicketHandler.cs:38,44`); exposed by `TicketsController.ClaimAsync` and `GetMineAsync` (`TicketsController.cs:137,155`); rendered by [`MyTicketsPanel`](#myticketspanel) via [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice).

### TicketRosterImportRunDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Imports` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Imports/TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:8` · Level 1 · record

- **What it is**: one committed roster import run (UC-48), as the upload component polls it: server-side progress (`Processed` of `Total`), the outcome counts so far, and on a failed run the machine-readable error code. It carries no ticket holder data (`TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:3-7`).
- **Depends on**: [`TicketRosterImportStatus`](#ticketrosterimportstatus) (hence Level 1), the `TicketImportRunIdentifierType` and `EventIdentifierType` aliases; `ErrorCode` holds one of [`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes`](#ticketrosterimporterrorcodes).
- **Concept**: a polled progress contract for long-running work. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether long operations leave the request path; the commit returns this DTO immediately and the client polls it while the background processor applies the roster in batches. `[Rubric §19, State Management]`: the client derives its "importing" state from the server's `IsActive` instead of keeping its own flag (`TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:85`).
- **Walkthrough**: `RunId`, `EventId`, `Status`, `Total`, `Processed` are `required` (`TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:11,14,17,20,23`). The outcome counts `Added`, `Updated`, `Unchanged` (erased holders included), `Voided`, `Reinstated` and `LinkedExistingAccounts` are optional ints (`TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:26-41`), since they fill in as the run proceeds. `ErrorCode` is nullable (`TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:44`). `IsActive` (`TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:47`) is a computed property: `Status is Queued or Running`, mirroring `TicketImportRun.IsActive` (`TicketImportRun.cs:83`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the counts mirror [`TicketRosterImportResultDTO`](#ticketrosterimportresultdto) so the synchronous and the background paths report the same numbers; keeping `IsActive` on the contract puts the one definition of "still running" where both server and client read it.
- **Where it's used**: mapped by [`TicketImportRunMapping`](#ticketimportrunmapping); returned by [`StartTicketRosterImportHandler`](#startticketrosterimporthandler) (`StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:34,40`) and [`GetTicketRosterImportHandler`](#getticketrosterimporthandler) (`GetTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:15,21`); exposed by [`TicketRosterImportController`](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) (`TicketRosterImportController.cs:38-39,129`); polled by [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload) (`TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:160,217`).

### AdoptionDayDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Roster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Roster/AdoptionDayDTO.cs:4` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: one calendar-day row of report A2 (adoption over time): how many Live tickets had an invite sent and how many were linked to an account on that day, plus the running linked total.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; `DateOnly` from the BCL.
- **Concept**: a plain read-model row; the report family and its small-number rule are introduced on [InsightCount](#insightcount) and [RosterInsightsDTO](#rosterinsightsdto). This row carries raw integers rather than [InsightCount](#insightcount) cells.
- **Walkthrough**: `Day` (`AdoptionDayDTO.cs:7`), `InvitesSent` (`:10`), `AccountsLinked` (`:13`), `CumulativeLinked` (`:16`) and `CumulativePercentLinked` (`:19`), all `init`-only on a `sealed record class` (`:4`). The handler fills one row per day from the first to the last day that saw an invite or a link, so a quiet day in between still gets a zero row (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:148-165`). `CumulativePercentLinked` is a 0-100 percentage to one decimal over the event's current Live ticket total (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:61,163,336-337`), not a 0-1 rate.
- **Why it's built this way**: days are cut on the event's clock (see [InsightTimeBasis](#insighttimebasis)), so an invite sent late in the evening lands on the organizer's day, not the UTC one (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:130-135`).
- **Where it's used**: the `Days` list of [AdoptionTrendDTO](#adoptiontrenddto) (`AdoptionTrendDTO.cs:10`); rendered by [TicketInsightsCsv](#ticketinsightscsv) for the A2 export.

### FollowUpQueueDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Roster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Roster/FollowUpQueueDTO.cs:9` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: report A3, the follow-up queue as four counts: Live tickets invited at least 3 (or 7) days ago and still unlinked, split by single-ticket versus multi-ticket orders (`FollowUpQueueDTO.cs:3-8`).

Per the type's own doc comment, a single-ticket order is a reminder-email candidate, while a ticket of a multi-ticket order is a barcode-claim candidate because one order email cannot tell which holder it is (`FollowUpQueueDTO.cs:5-7`). The 7-day counts are a subset of the 3-day counts (`FollowUpQueueDTO.cs:7`).
- **Walkthrough**: `SingleTicketOrders3Days` (`:12`), `MultiTicketOrders3Days` (`:15`), `SingleTicketOrders7Days` (`:18`), `MultiTicketOrders7Days` (`:21`). The thresholds are handler constants `ReminderDays = 3` and `LateReminderDays = 7` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:43,46`), measured back from `TimeProvider` now (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:188-189`); `BuildFollowUp` sums per-order tallies with `Tickets == 1` versus `Tickets > 1` (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:221-226`).

### InsightCount
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/InsightCount.cs:15` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: one count cell of a ticket insights report under the BR-278 small-number rule: a count of 1 or 2 is withheld, while 0 and 3 or more are reported exactly, so an aggregate can never single out one person (`InsightCount.cs:3-8`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; `Math.Round` with `MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero` from the BCL.
- **Concept introduced, server-side small-number suppression.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance]` assesses whether personal data is minimized and protected by design. Here the rule runs when the cell is *created*, in the factory, so a suppressed cell holds no number at all: neither the API response nor a CSV export ever carries the real value (`InsightCount.cs:6-8`). A client cannot un-hide what was never sent. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether contracts make invalid states hard to express; the two factories are the only places that set the flag consistently with `Count` and `Rate`.
- **Walkthrough**:
  - Constants: `SmallNumberThreshold = 3` (`InsightCount.cs:18`) and `SuppressedText = "fewer than 3"` (`:21`), the text both the report UI and the CSV write in place of a withheld count.
  - State: `Count` is `int?`, null when suppressed (`:24`); `IsSuppressed` (`:27`); `Rate` is `decimal?` (`:34`), the count per unit of the cell's denominator (a 0-1 share for a percentage cell, a per-holder average for a total), rounded to four decimals.
  - `Of(int count)` (`:39-42`): suppressed cell when the count is small, else an exact cell with no rate.
  - `Of(int count, int denominator)` (`:51-58`): suppressed cell (rate suppressed with it) when small; otherwise `Rate = count / denominator` rounded to 4 places away from zero, and a zero or negative denominator yields `0` rather than a division error (`:56`).
  - `IsSmall(int count)` (`:63`): `count is > 0 and < SmallNumberThreshold`, so zero is deliberately exact.
- **Why it's built this way**: zero carries no re-identification risk and "nobody did X" is useful to an organizer, so only 1 and 2 are withheld (`InsightCount.cs:4-5,63`). Suppressing the rate with the count closes the obvious back door of recomputing the count from rate times denominator (`InsightCount.cs:11-12`). The threshold is also reused outside the cell: the A6 domain list drops any company domain under it before taking the top ten (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:261-266`).
- **Where it's used**: every count cell of A6 ([EmailDomainMixDTO](#emaildomainmixdto), [EmailDomainCountDTO](#emaildomaincountdto)) and of the B reports ([TicketTypeCountDTO](#tickettypecountdto), [TicketTypeEngagementDTO](#tickettypeengagementdto), [SponsorReachDTO](#sponsorreachdto), [ArrivalBucketDTO](#arrivalbucketdto)), built by [GetRosterInsightsHandler](#getrosterinsightshandler) and [GetEngagementInsightsHandler](#getengagementinsightshandler). [TicketInsightsCsv](#ticketinsightscsv) writes `SuppressedText` for a withheld cell (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/TicketInsightsCsv.cs:282,291`); the UI displays it through [InsightCountValue](#insightcountvalue). Unit-tested in `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tests/Tickets/Insights/InsightCountTests.cs`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: BR-278 itself is defined in the ADC specifications guide, not in code; the code is the only enforcement point verified here.

### InsightTimeBasis
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/InsightTimeBasis.cs:9` · Level 0 · enum

- **What it is**: which clock a ticket insights report bucketed its days and half hours in: `Utc = 1` (`InsightTimeBasis.cs:12`) or `EventUtcOffset = 2` (`:15`), the event's UTC offset on its first day.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party.
- **Concept**: the report tells its reader which clock it used instead of silently guessing. Conference does not hand Engagement an IANA time-zone id, only the event's first day and the UTC instant it starts, from which the offset follows (`InsightTimeBasis.cs:3-7`). `0` is reserved as unset so a defaulted field never resolves to a real basis, with a justified CA1008 suppression (`InsightTimeBasis.cs:8`).
- **Walkthrough**: the internal [EventClock](#eventclock) resolves it through [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice): a failed lookup, a missing first day, or a derived offset beyond 14 hours all fall back to `Utc` with offset 0; otherwise `EventUtcOffset` with the computed minutes (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/EventClock.cs:44-63`).
- **Why it's built this way**: degrade rather than fail. A Conference outage turns the reports UTC-bucketed and labelled as such (`EventClock.cs:12-14`). The offset is exact on event day and at most an hour off for a day across a daylight-saving change (`EventClock.cs:10-12`).
- **Where it's used**: `RosterInsightsDTO.TimeBasis` (`RosterInsightsDTO.cs:17`) and the matching property of [EngagementInsightsDTO](#engagementinsightsdto).

### RosterHealthDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Roster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Roster/RosterHealthDTO.cs:7` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: report A5, roster health: voided, erased and nameless tickets, duplicate-name counts, and the roster's freshness timestamps (`RosterHealthDTO.cs:3-6`).

- **Walkthrough**:
  - `Voided` (`RosterHealthDTO.cs:10`): tickets no longer in the latest upload (BR-268), status `Voided`.
  - `Erased` (`:13`): any-status tickets whose holder fields were erased with the linked account ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)); the handler detects these by the barcode starting with `Ticket.AnonymizedBarcodePrefix` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:293,324`).
  - `BlankName` (`:19`): Live, non-erased tickets with both attendee name parts empty (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:294,325-327`).
  - `DuplicateNameTickets` (`:22`) and `DuplicateNames` (`:25`): tickets and distinct names that appear on more than one Live ticket (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:306-310,328-329`).
  - `SameOrderDuplicateNameTickets` (`:32`): Live tickets sharing a name within the same order email, most often the buyer's name filled in for blank attendee names (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:330`).
  - `LastTicketAddedOn` (`:35`) and `LastTicketChangedOn` (`:38`): UTC, null on an empty roster, read by two single-row specification queries (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:312-319`).
- **Why it's built this way**: names compare under the database collation, case-insensitive on SQL Server (`RosterHealthDTO.cs:4-5`), so the check runs as a `GROUP BY` on the server instead of loading names into memory (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:299-304`).

- **Caveats / not-in-source**: these are raw integers, not [InsightCount](#insightcount) cells, so a count of 1 or 2 is shown exactly. Whether that is intended under BR-278 (these counts name no person) is not stated in the type.

### RosterInsightsDTO
> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Roster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Roster/RosterInsightsDTO.cs:8` · Level 3 · record

- **What it is**: the roster-only half of one event's ticket insights (UC-56, BR-279): reports A1 to A6 in one response (`RosterInsightsDTO.cs:3-7`). The activity half (B1 to B4) is [EngagementInsightsDTO](#engagementinsightsdto).
- **Depends on**: [TicketTypeFunnelDTO](#tickettypefunneldto), [AdoptionTrendDTO](#adoptiontrenddto), [FollowUpQueueDTO](#followupqueuedto), [GroupOrdersDTO](#groupordersdto), [RosterHealthDTO](#rosterhealthdto), [EmailDomainMixDTO](#emaildomainmixdto), [InsightTimeBasis](#insighttimebasis); the `EventIdentifierType` alias.

- **Walkthrough**: `EventId` (`required`, `:11`), `GeneratedOn` (`:14`), `TimeBasis` (`:17`, default `Utc`) and `UtcOffsetMinutes` (`:20`) describe the run; `Funnel` (`:23`) and `FunnelTotal` (`:26`) are A1; `Adoption` (`:29`) A2; `FollowUp` (`:32`) A3; `GroupOrders` (`:35`) A4; `Health` (`:38`) A5; `DomainMix` (`:41`) A6. Every sub-report defaults to an empty instance, so a roster-less event still serializes complete. [GetRosterInsightsHandler](#getrosterinsightshandler) builds it in one pass: resolve the event clock, then run the funnel, adoption, order and health reads and assemble (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:49-79`).

### BookmarkWriteOutcome

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/BookmarkWriteOutcome.cs:15` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the success value of a bookmark toggle: whether the write was confirmed by the server or kept on the device for later, and the new bookmark id when there is one.
- **Depends on**: no first-party types; only the `UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType` alias (the alias convention is taught in [the primer](00-primer.md)).
- **Concept, "queued" is a success, not a failure.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether the app keeps working through a degraded dependency; here the degraded dependency is the attendee's own network. A star tapped with no signal is not an error the page must show: it is a write the device will deliver later, so it comes back as `Result.Success` with `Queued: true` rather than as a failure. `[Rubric §19, State Management]`: the page needs exactly two facts to settle its optimistic star, and this record carries exactly those two.
- **Walkthrough**: a positional record with two members (`BookmarkWriteOutcome.cs:15`). `Queued` is `true` when the write was kept on the device to be sent when it is back online, or when it cancelled out an earlier queued write of the same session, and `false` when the server confirmed it (doc comment `:6-10`). `BookmarkId` is the server id after a confirmed add and `null` after a remove and after a queued add, "whose id the server has not assigned yet" (`:11-14`). The producer shows every combination: a confirmed add returns `new BookmarkWriteOutcome(Queued: false, bookmark.Id)` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:110`), an add that meets "already bookmarked" and a confirmed remove both return `Queued: false, BookmarkId: null` (`:118`, `:129`), and a successful enqueue returns `Queued: true, BookmarkId: null` (`:211`).
- **Why it's built this way**: a null id after a duplicate add or a queued add is honest rather than lossy: the page keeps the star lit and resolves the id later, either on the next read or by session when the user un-stars it (the comment at `SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:113-114`). Keeping the record in `.Shared` lets Conference's pages read it without referencing Engagement's UI assembly, the same split [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice) relies on.
- **Where it's used**: the return value of `ISessionBookmarkUIService.SetBookmarkedAsync` (`ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:62`), produced by [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) and read by Conference's [`PublicSessionListView`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionlistview) (`PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:164`, `:186`) and [`SessionBookmarkButton`](group-21-conference-ui.md#sessionbookmarkbutton) (`SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:122`).

### CreateBookmarkRequest

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/CreateBookmarkRequest.cs:6` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the two-field request body for "bookmark this session for this user". It is simultaneously the JSON contract of the `POST /bookmarks` endpoint and the CQRS command object the handler consumes; Engagement declares no separate internal command type for the create use case.
- **Depends on**: no first-party types. It uses the two module-scoped identifier aliases `UserIdentifierType` and `SessionIdentifierType` (the alias convention is taught in [the primer](00-primer.md)), which is why the type sits at Level 0.
- **Concept introduced, request-as-command.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether the wire contract is explicit and stable; `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses whether writes flow through a command object and a single handler. Here the two collapse into one type on purpose: [`BookmarksController`](#bookmarkscontroller) injects `ICommandHandler<CreateBookmarkRequest, Result<UserSessionBookmarkDTO>>` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:38`) and passes the deserialized body straight into `createHandler.HandleAsync(request, cancellationToken)` (`BookmarksController.cs:72`), so there is no request-to-command mapping step to keep in sync. The trade-off is that the public contract and the command shape can no longer diverge, which is exactly what the module wants for a request this small.
- **Walkthrough**: two members, both `required` and `init`-only. `UserId` (`CreateBookmarkRequest.cs:9`) names the owner of the bookmark; `SessionId` (`CreateBookmarkRequest.cs:12`) names the session being saved. `required` means neither construction nor JSON deserialization can leave a member unset, and `init` freezes the instance after construction, so no decorator in the [CQRS pipeline](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md) can mutate a command mid-flight.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the payload to two identifiers pushes every other concern to a dedicated place: shape validation to [`CreateBookmarkRequestValidator`](#createbookmarkrequestvalidator) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/Create/CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:9`), business rules (session validity, duplicate detection) to [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler) (`.../Create/CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:23`), and authorization to the controller. Because `UserId` travels in the body rather than being inferred server-side, the controller binds it to the caller: a non-Organizer whose user-identifier claim does not equal `request.UserId` gets a `Forbidden` failure (`BookmarksController.cs:58-70`), the create-side counterpart of the `OwnerOrAdminFilter` on the list endpoints ([ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)). `[Rubric §11, Security]`: without that check any authenticated user could create bookmarks owned by someone else. Note also the `[Idempotent]` attribute on the action (`BookmarksController.cs:50`), justified in the action's own doc comment (`:45-47`): because the body names the (user, session) pair explicitly and a duplicate already answers 409, replaying a retried star is what the attendee meant.
- **Where it's used**: the API entry point `CreateAsync` (`BookmarksController.cs:54-55`); the UI HTTP wrapper [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient), whose `CreateAsync` takes one (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkApiClient.cs:63-64`); and [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice), which constructs one inline when a star is toggled online (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:140`) and enqueues one as the offline-write payload when the device is offline (`SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:201`).

### IBookmarkCountService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/IBookmarkCountService.cs:11` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: the cross-module read contract that lets Conference ask "how many people bookmarked this session?" without referencing an Engagement domain entity, an Engagement DbContext, or an Engagement package beyond `.Shared`.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party beyond the `SessionIdentifierType` alias and the [`ServiceContractAttribute`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#servicecontractattribute) marker it carries (`IBookmarkCountService.cs:1`, `:10`); BCL `Task`, `IReadOnlyDictionary`, `IReadOnlyCollection`, `CancellationToken`.
- **Concept introduced, the extraction-ready cross-module interface.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses whether modules talk through contracts that survive a process split; `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` (Dependency Inversion) assesses whether the consumer depends on an abstraction rather than a concrete collaborator. This interface is the canonical example in ADC: it has three different implementations that a host picks between with no consumer change at all. In-process it is [`BookmarkCountService`](#bookmarkcountservice) (registered with `TryAddScoped` at `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:45`); when Engagement is switched off in a host it is [`DisabledBookmarkCountService`](#disabledbookmarkcountservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:33`); and when Engagement runs as its own process it is [`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter`](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter), swapped in with `Replace` by `AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient()` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/DependencyInjection.cs:52`, called from `MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:431`). That is [ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html) and [ADR-008](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/008-service-extraction-topology.html) made concrete: the C# call site never learns which one it got. The `[ServiceContract]` marker is what declares this intent in code rather than in a comment.
- **Walkthrough**: two methods, both taking an explicit (non-defaulted) `CancellationToken` so every implementation, including the gRPC one, threads cancellation. `GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync(sessionId, cancellationToken)` (`IBookmarkCountService.cs:19`) returns a bare `int` for one session. `GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync(sessionIds, cancellationToken)` (`IBookmarkCountService.cs:28-30`) is the batched form, and its contract is spelled out in the doc comment (`IBookmarkCountService.cs:22-23`): every requested session id is present in the result, and a session with no bookmarks maps to `0`. That sentence is a real contract, not decoration: it is what forces the disabled stub to project zeros rather than return an empty map. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]`: the batch method exists so the speaker dashboard resolves N sessions in one round trip instead of N, which matters most when the call is a network hop rather than a local query.
- **Why it's built this way**: returning plain `int` / `IReadOnlyDictionary` rather than `Result<T>` keeps the contract trivially projectable onto a proto message; a fault surfaces as an exception (over gRPC, a status the caller's resilience pipeline can react to) instead of a failure payload each caller must unwrap. Living in `.Shared` is what keeps the reference direction legal: Conference references Engagement's contract assembly only, which the Conference service project spells out in a comment on its own `ProjectReference` (`MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service.csproj:26`).
- **Where it's used**: Conference's [`GetSessionBookmarkCountHandler`](group-18-conference-application.md#getsessionbookmarkcounthandler) and the batched [`GetSessionBookmarkCountsHandler`](group-18-conference-application.md#getsessionbookmarkcountshandler); on the producing side it is what [`BookmarkCountsGrpcService`](#bookmarkcountsgrpcservice) publishes over the wire.

### PendingTicketInvitationDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Invitations` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Invitations/PendingTicketInvitationDTO.cs:12` · Level 0 · record

- **What it is**: the four facts Identity needs to re-issue a ticket invitation whose link expired: the invitee's first and last name and the event's name and first day (BR-271).
- **Depends on**: no first-party types; BCL `string` and `DateOnly`.
- **Concept, the minimal cross-module answer.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether data crossing a boundary is limited to what the receiver needs. The doc comment states the limit outright (`PendingTicketInvitationDTO.cs:3-7`): "the same name and event details the original invitation carried, and nothing else of the ticket". No ticket id, order email or ticket type leaves Engagement.
- **Walkthrough**: a positional record (`PendingTicketInvitationDTO.cs:12`). `FirstName` and `LastName` are the names the invitation's account is created with (`:8-9`); `EventName` is the conference event's display name (`:10`); `EventStart` is the event's first day as a `DateOnly` (`:11`), a calendar date with no time zone to misread.
- **Why it's built this way**: a positional record maps one-to-one onto the gRPC message the extracted service sends, so the in-process answer and the remote answer are the same shape ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html)).
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`IPendingTicketInvitationService`](#ipendingticketinvitationservice) and its implementations ([`PendingTicketInvitationService`](#pendingticketinvitationservice), [`DisabledPendingTicketInvitationService`](#disabledpendingticketinvitationservice), [`TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter`](#ticketinvitationservicegrpcadapter)); Identity's [`SendSignInLinkHandler`](group-24-identity-module.md#sendsigninlinkhandler) copies its four members into the invite command (`MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/Users/UseCases/SendSignInLink/SendSignInLinkHandler.cs:76-83`).

### SessionScopeSource

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Usage` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Usage/SessionScopeSource.cs:5` · Level 0 · enum

- **What it is**: where the engagement report took the event's session ids from (BR-280), and therefore whether its bookmark and session-feedback counts are exact.
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept, a degraded answer that says it is degraded.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses graceful degradation. When the Conference lookup fails, [`GetEngagementInsightsHandler`](#getengagementinsightshandler) does not fail the report: it falls back to the sessions Engagement itself has seen activity for and stamps the result with this enum, `Conference` on the happy path and `LocalActivity` on the fallback (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:158`, `:184`). `[Rubric §34, Architecture Governance & Documentation]`: the member comments state the consequence precisely, a session "nobody checked into, asked in or polled in is missed, so bookmarks and session feedback can be undercounted" (`SessionScopeSource.cs:10-14`).
- **Walkthrough**: two members, `Conference = 1` (`SessionScopeSource.cs:8`) and `LocalActivity = 2` (`:15`). There is no zero member on purpose: the `CA1008` suppression (`:4`) records that 0 is reserved as the unset value "so a defaulted field never resolves to a real source", following the [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod) precedent.
- **Why it's built this way**: a flag on the payload, rather than a failed request, lets the organizer still read B1 to B4 while the page warns that two columns may be low; [`EngagementInsightsReports`](#engagementinsightsreports) renders that warning when `Report.SessionScope == SessionScopeSource.LocalActivity` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Tickets/Insights/EngagementInsightsReports.razor:11`).
- **Where it's used**: the `SessionScope` property of [`EngagementInsightsDTO`](#engagementinsightsdto) (`EngagementInsightsDTO.cs:35`).

### UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.cs:7` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the bookmark error codes a client branches on, today the single `Duplicate` code.
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept, a shared error code as a compile-time contract.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether clients can rely on stable, machine-readable error identities. The doc comment names the reason the constant lives in `.Shared` (`UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.cs:3-6`): it is "shared by the handler that emits them and the UI service that reads them, so a rename on one side fails the build on the other". A string literal duplicated on both sides would drift silently.
- **Walkthrough**: one constant, `Duplicate = "UserSessionBookmark.Duplicate"` (`UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.cs:13`). Its doc comment (`:9-12`) carries the behavioral rule as well: the caller already has an active bookmark on the session, and a replayed offline create treats that as success "because the star the user asked for exists".
- **Why it's built this way**: offline replay makes a duplicate create a normal outcome rather than an edge case (a queued POST that reached the server before the connection dropped is replayed later), so the client must recognize it precisely. The server emits it from both duplicate paths of [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler), the pre-check and the unique-index catch for a concurrent request, as an `Error.Conflict` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/Create/CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:50`, `:85`).
- **Where it's used**: emitted by [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler); read by [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) to count an online add that meets "already bookmarked" as done (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:220-221`) and by [`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler`](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler) to treat a replayed duplicate as success (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkCreateReplayHandler.cs:46`).

### DisabledBookmarkCountService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/DisabledBookmarkCountService.cs:7` · Level 1 · class (internal sealed)

- **What it is**: the null-object implementation of [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) that a host registers when the Engagement module is switched off. Every count answers zero.
- **Depends on**: [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) only.
- **Concept introduced, the disabled-module stub.** `[Rubric §2, Design Patterns]` (Null Object) and `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` both apply. The module system lets a host boot a subset of modules; a module that is off must still satisfy the interfaces other modules resolve, or the container throws at startup and the whole host fails on a feature nobody asked for. So [`IModule`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#imodule) exposes `RegisterDisabledStubs`, and Engagement's implementation registers this class plus the data-subject export stub (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:31-36`). `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: the degradation is graceful and legible, a session simply shows zero saves instead of erroring.
- **Walkthrough**: `GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync` returns `Task.FromResult(0)` with no query allocated at all (`DisabledBookmarkCountService.cs:10-11`). `GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync` honours the batch contract the interface documents rather than returning an empty map: it projects the requested ids into a dictionary of zeros, `(sessionIds ?? []).Distinct().ToDictionary(id => id, _ => 0)` (`DisabledBookmarkCountService.cs:21-22`). Two guards are packed into that one line and the `<remarks>` above it explains the second (`:14-17`): `?? []` means a caller passing null still gets a usable empty result instead of a `NullReferenceException`, and `Distinct()` mirrors the real [`BookmarkCountService`](#bookmarkcountservice) so a duplicate id collapses instead of throwing out of `ToDictionary`. Note there is no `async` here at all: both methods are synchronous returns wrapped in a completed task.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the stub in `.Shared` beside the interface means any host can register it without referencing Engagement's Application layer, which is precisely the situation in the Conference service, where Engagement's real implementation is not even loaded. The comment in `MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:33-38` records the intended flow, and the pipeline comment at `:326-332` states the ordering rule: the module registration runs first, then `AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient()` `Replace`s whatever is there with the gRPC adapter.
- **Where it's used**: `EngagementModule.RegisterDisabledStubs` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:33`), called by [`ModuleLoader`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#moduleloader) for a disabled module; it is the fallback the Conference service starts from before the gRPC client registration overwrites it.
