### IPendingTicketInvitationService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Invitations` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Invitations/IPendingTicketInvitationService.cs:14` · Level 1 · interface

- **What it is**: the cross-module contract Identity calls to ask "does this address still hold a ticket invitation?", so it can re-issue an invitation whose link expired before the invitee created an account (BR-271).
- **Depends on**: [`PendingTicketInvitationDTO`](#pendingticketinvitationdto) and the [`ServiceContractAttribute`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#servicecontractattribute) marker (`IPendingTicketInvitationService.cs:13`); BCL `Task`, `CancellationToken`.
- **Concept, ownership decides who answers.** `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]` assesses whether each fact has one owning context. The doc comment gives the reason this lives in Engagement and not Identity (`IPendingTicketInvitationService.cs:5-12`): Engagement owns the ticket's state, so it is the only module that knows whether an invitation still stands, and "a voided ticket, or one already linked to an account, holds none". `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`: this is the same extraction-ready shape [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) introduced, three implementations chosen by the host: in-process [`PendingTicketInvitationService`](#pendingticketinvitationservice) (`TryAddScoped` at `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:53`), [`DisabledPendingTicketInvitationService`](#disabledpendingticketinvitationservice) when Engagement is off (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:35`), and [`TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter`](#ticketinvitationservicegrpcadapter) when Engagement runs as its own process, swapped in with `Replace` by `AddEngagementTicketInvitationClient()` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/DependencyInjection.cs:109`, `:114`). See [ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html) and [ADR-059](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/059-module-contract-and-composition.html).
- **Walkthrough**: one member, `GetPendingInvitationAsync(email, cancellationToken)` (`IPendingTicketInvitationService.cs:25`), which returns the invitation's details or `null` when no invitation stands. Its doc comment (`:16-24`) fixes the selection rule so a re-issue announces the same ticket the original run did: a live, unlinked, invited ticket whose order email is the address, compared in the roster's normalized form, preferring the most recently invited event and, within it, the earliest ticket that names an attendee.
- **Why it's built this way**: returning a nullable DTO rather than `Result<T>` keeps the contract projectable onto a proto message, as on [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice); a fault surfaces as an exception. The caller is built for that: Identity's handler documents that a lookup that throws propagates to the framework base, which logs it without the address and still answers success (`MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/Users/UseCases/SendSignInLink/SendSignInLinkHandler.cs:63-67`), so a sign-in request never reveals whether an address holds an invitation.
- **Where it's used**: Identity's [`SendSignInLinkHandler`](group-24-identity-module.md#sendsigninlinkhandler), whose `OnNoAccountAsync` calls it for an address with no account and returns early on `null` (`SendSignInLinkHandler.cs:68`, `:72-74`); exposed over the wire by [`TicketInvitationGrpcService`](#ticketinvitationgrpcservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Grpc/TicketInvitationGrpcService.cs:26`).

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Usage` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Usage/TicketTypeEngagementDTO.cs:8` · Level 1 · record

- **What it is**: one row of report B1: how the linked holders of one ticket type used the app at the event (BR-280).
- **Depends on**: [`InsightCount`](#insightcount), the count cell every member uses.
- **Concept, the small-number rule on every cell.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether aggregate reporting can re-identify a person. Every cell is an [`InsightCount`](#insightcount) rather than an `int`, and the type comment states the rule it follows (BR-278, `TicketTypeEngagementDTO.cs:3-7`); the endpoint's comment says what that means on the wire: "every count of 1 or 2 is withheld on the server" (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:211-212`).
- **Walkthrough**: nine `init` properties, each defaulted so an empty row is valid. `TicketTypeName` is the TicketLeap ticket type, empty on the total row (`TicketTypeEngagementDTO.cs:11`). `LinkedHolders` is the distinct accounts linked to a Live ticket of the type, "the denominator of every rate" (`:14`). Then the activity cells: `CheckedInToEvent` (`:17`), `SessionCheckIns` (`:20`, a total whose rate is the average per holder rather than a share, as the type comment notes at `:5-6`), `Bookmarked` (`:23`), `GaveSessionFeedback` (`:26`), `GaveEventFeedback` (`:29`), `VotedInPoll` (`:32`) and `AskedQuestion` (`:35`).
- **Why it's built this way**: one shape serves both the per-type rows and the total row, which [`EngagementInsightsDTO`](#engagementinsightsdto) carries as `AllTicketTypes` with an empty name (`EngagementInsightsDTO.cs:43-44`), so the UI and the CSV render them with one code path.
- **Where it's used**: the `ByTicketType` and `AllTicketTypes` members of [`EngagementInsightsDTO`](#engagementinsightsdto); built by [`GetEngagementInsightsHandler`](#getengagementinsightshandler).

### UserSessionBookmarkDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmarkDTO.cs:8` · Level 1 · record

- **What it is**: the read contract for one personal-schedule entry: which user saved which session, when, and under what bookmark id.
- **Depends on**: [`IBaseDTO<TIdentifierType>`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#ibasedtotidentifiertype) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.DTOs` (`UserSessionBookmarkDTO.cs:1`, `:8`), and the `UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType`, `UserIdentifierType`, `SessionIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept, the DTO as the module's outward-facing projection.** `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` assesses whether the domain entity leaks past the application boundary: it does not, [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark) never crosses the wire and [`UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper`](#usersessionbookmarkdtomapper) does the projection. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`: implementing `IBaseDTO<T>` is what lets this record flow through the framework's generic read plumbing, for example the `IEntityQueryService<UserSessionBookmark, UserSessionBookmarkDTO, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>` the controller injects (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:42`), with no bookmark-specific query code.
- **Walkthrough**: `Id` satisfies the `IBaseDTO<T>` contract (`UserSessionBookmarkDTO.cs:11`); `UserId` and `SessionId` are the two scalar cross-module references (`:14`, `:17`), scalar rather than navigation properties because the referenced rows live in other services' databases; `CreatedOn` (`:20`) is the audit timestamp. The first three are `required`, `CreatedOn` is not, which is the readable signal that it is server-stamped rather than caller-supplied. There is no `IsDeleted` here: soft-deleted bookmarks are filtered out by the global query filter long before projection.
- **Why it's built this way**: a flat, four-member record keeps the payload cheap for a list endpoint that a phone pages through on a conference floor, and keeps the shape identical whether it is produced in-process or deserialized from HTTP in the UI.
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler) and [`GetUserBookmarksHandler`](#getuserbookmarkshandler) inside a `Result<T>`; declared on both controller actions (`BookmarksController.cs:34`, `:35`, `:51`); deserialized client-side by [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkApiClient.cs:75`), whose create result [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) passes through (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:137`, `:142`).

- **What it is**: one half hour of report B4, the arrival curve: the event check-ins that fell in it, split by the ticket types the arriving accounts hold (BR-280).

### EngagementInsightsDTO

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights.Usage` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/Usage/EngagementInsightsDTO.cs:14` · Level 3 · record

- **What it is**: the whole roster-plus-activity report for one event (UC-56, BR-280): reports B1 to B4 over the linked holders (Live tickets linked to an account), by ticket type.
- **Depends on**: [`TicketTypeEngagementDTO`](#tickettypeengagementdto), [`TicketedVsPresentDTO`](#ticketedvspresentdto), [`SponsorReachDTO`](#sponsorreachdto), [`ArrivalBucketDTO`](#arrivalbucketdto), [`SessionScopeSource`](#sessionscopesource), [`InsightTimeBasis`](#insighttimebasis), and the `EventIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept, aggregate-only reporting that degrades in the open.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`: the type comment fixes the privacy boundary (`EngagementInsightsDTO.cs:3-7`): aggregate only (BR-278), "no name, email address or account id", every count cell under the small-number rule, and a holder whose tickets span two types counts once in each type and once in the totals. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: a failed cross-service lookup "degrades the report instead of failing it, and says so here" (`:9-12`), through four flags: `SessionScope` for the sessions, `SponsorNamesResolved` for sponsor names, and `TimeBasis` plus `EventWindowKnown` for the event's clock.
- **Walkthrough**: header fields first. `EventId` is `required` (`EngagementInsightsDTO.cs:17`); `GeneratedOn` is the UTC compute time (`:20`). The clock: `TimeBasis` defaults to `InsightTimeBasis.Utc` (`:23`) and `UtcOffsetMinutes` is the offset the B4 buckets are stamped at, 0 under UTC (`:26`); `EventWindowKnown` (`:32`) says whether B4 covers the event's own days only or, when false, every event check-in of the event (`:28-31`). The degradation flags: `SessionScope` defaults to `SessionScopeSource.Conference` (`:35`) and `SponsorNamesResolved` to `true` (`:38`). Then the four reports: `ByTicketType` (B1, `:41`) and its total row `AllTicketTypes` with an empty type name (`:44`), `TicketedVsPresent` (B2, `:47`), `SponsorReach` (B3, `:50`) and `Arrivals` (B4, `:53`). Every collection defaults to `[]` and every nested row to `new()`, so an event with no roster serializes as empty reports.
- **Why it's built this way**: the endpoint documents that an event with no roster answers 200 with empty reports and that a failed Conference lookup "degrades the report and is flagged in it rather than failing the request" (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs:211-215`); the defaults and flags on this record are what make both statements true.
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`GetEngagementInsightsHandler`](#getengagementinsightshandler) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetEngagementInsightsHandler.cs:68`) through `GET /tickets/insights/engagement` on [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller), behind `EngagementPermissions.TicketsManage` (`TicketsController.cs:216-217`); fetched by the UI's [`TicketService`](#ticketservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Tickets/TicketService.cs:168-171`), rendered by [`EngagementInsightsReports`](#engagementinsightsreports) and exported by [`TicketInsightsCsv`](#ticketinsightscsv) (`TicketInsightsCsv.cs:193`).

### ISessionBookmarkUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:15` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the narrow UI-side contract that lets the Conference session pages render a bookmark star and toggle it inline, without navigating to an Engagement page and without referencing the Engagement UI assembly.
- **Depends on**: [`BookmarkWriteOutcome`](#bookmarkwriteoutcome), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`ErrorType`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:1`), and the identifier aliases.
- **Concept introduced, the cross-module UI service contract.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses how one module's page composes another module's capability. The pattern here is optional resolution: Conference's pages hold the dependency as a nullable property and ask the container for it rather than injecting it, `BookmarkService = ServiceProvider.GetService<ISessionBookmarkUIService>()` (`MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Public/Sessions/PublicSessionList.razor.cs:141`, and, for the detail page, the same line inside the extracted `SessionBookmarkButton` toggle it renders, `SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:56`), so a host that never called `AddEngagementUI()` simply renders no stars instead of failing to construct the page. [`PublicSessionListView`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionlistview) then takes it as a nullable `[Parameter]` (`PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:71`). `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`: this is the presentation-layer twin of what [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) does for the application layer.
- **Concept, `Result` all the way to the page.** Every member reports its outcome as a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) carrying the API's own errors with their `ErrorType` intact, and the interface doc comment states the rule (`ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:9-13`): the calling page branches instead of catching, and only the caller's own `OperationCanceledException` still propagates. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` and `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]`: a "not there" answer and a "the remove failed" answer are different facts, and a boolean cannot tell them apart. That is spelled out for the delete member (`:28-29`): a missing bookmark answers 404, which arrives as an `ErrorType.NotFound` failure.
- **Concept, one offline-aware write entry point.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` and `[Rubric §19, State Management]`: every bookmark write goes through `SetBookmarkedAsync`, which sends online when it can and otherwise puts the write on the device's offline write queue to be replayed on reconnect ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)). The doc comment (`ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:37-55`) fixes the rules a page can rely on: the newest intent wins and is always issued in full (any write still queued for the same user and session is dropped first); online, an add is sent with an `Idempotency-Key` and an add that meets "already bookmarked" counts as done; a device known to be offline queues at once without trying the network; an online call that fails with a transport fault is queued too, reusing the add's idempotency key so a request that reached the server is deduplicated on replay; any other failure is returned as it is; and a write the queue refuses (`OfflineWrites.QueueFull`, `OfflineWrites.Unavailable`) is returned as a failure, never as queued.
- **Walkthrough**: three members, each shaped by a real UI need.
  - `GetBookmarkedSessionIdsAsync(userId, cancellationToken)` (`ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:20-21`) returns `Result<IReadOnlyDictionary<SessionIdentifierType, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>>`, a map rather than a set. A list page needs both facts at once: which sessions are starred, and the bookmark id it must send to un-star each one, so the dictionary saves a second round trip per row.
  - `DeleteBookmarkAsync(bookmarkId, sessionId, cancellationToken)` (`:32-35`) takes the session id even though the API key alone identifies the row. The doc comment says why (`:24-26`): the session-reminder layer ([ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html) Wave 2) needs to know which session's scheduled local notification to cancel, and the bookmark id cannot answer that after the row is gone.
  - `SetBookmarkedAsync(userId, sessionId, bookmarked, knownBookmarkId, cancellationToken)` (`:62-67`) is the toggle. `bookmarked` is the state the user asked for; `knownBookmarkId` is the id the caller holds, when it holds one. It may be `null` for a star set by a queued add, in which case a remove resolves the id through the session-ids read, and a bookmark that is already gone counts as removed (`:40-42`). It returns a [`BookmarkWriteOutcome`](#bookmarkwriteoutcome) saying whether the write was confirmed or queued, with the new id after a confirmed add (`:61`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the interface lives in `.Shared`, the assembly Conference already references, while its implementation lives in Engagement's UI project. That split is what makes the star a genuinely optional feature of the Conference page rather than a hard dependency. Routing every write through one toggle keeps the offline rules (coalescing, idempotency key reuse, duplicate-as-success) in one implementation, [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:79-129`), instead of in every page that draws a star. All three `CancellationToken` parameters are defaulted here, unlike on [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice), because the callers are Blazor event handlers rather than a generated gRPC client.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:36-41`), registered scoped in [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:35`), consumed by Conference's [`PublicSessionList`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionlist), [`PublicSessionDetail`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessiondetail) (through [`SessionBookmarkButton`](group-21-conference-ui.md#sessionbookmarkbutton), whose toggle calls `SetBookmarkedAsync` at `SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:122`), [`PublicSessionListView`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionlistview) (`PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:164`, `:186`) and [`PublicSessionBookmarkState`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionbookmarkstate) (`PublicSessionBookmarkState.cs:15`). Its nullable-injection convention is cited as precedent by [`ISessionLiveUIService`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#isessionliveuiservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/SessionQuestions/ISessionLiveUIService.cs:4-5`).

### EngagementRoutePaths

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementRoutePaths.cs:8` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the single source of truth for every Engagement URL: the four live-layer routes, the two feedback routes, the three badge check-in routes, the two points routes, the organizer ticket roster and ticket insights routes, and the two deep-link-only self-service QR routes.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. It uses the `SessionIdentifierType`, `EventIdentifierType`, `SponsorIdentifierType` and `RoomIdentifierType` aliases, plus `System.Globalization` (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:1`).
- **Concept, centralized route paths.** `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` assesses whether URL strings are declared once or scattered across `NavigateTo` call sites and `@page` directives. Every route here is either a `const` (parameterless) or a static method (id-carrying), so renaming a route touches one file and the compiler finds the call sites. `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` shows up in an easy-to-miss detail: each interpolated route is built with `string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"...")` (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:12-14`, `:17-18`, `:35`, `:39-40`) rather than plain interpolation, so a culture with non-ASCII digits or a different number format can never produce a URL the router will not match.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Live layer (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:10-14`): `const string HappeningNow = "/happening-now"`, plus `SessionDetails`, `SessionLive` and `SessionPresent`, which build `/conference/sessions/{id}`, `.../live` and `.../present`.
  - Feedback (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:16-18`): `EventFeedback(eventId)` and `SessionFeedback(sessionId)`, whose outputs match the `@page` templates on the two feedback pages.
  - Badge check-in (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:20-23`): `MyBadge = "/my-badge"`, `CheckInScan = "/check-in"`, `OrganizerAttendance = "/organizer/attendance"`, the three routes carried by the pages later in this part.
  - Points (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:25-27`): `MyPoints = "/points"` and `OrganizerPointsOverview = "/organizer/points"`.
  - Tickets (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:29-35`): `OrganizerTickets = "/organizer/tickets"` for the roster, and `OrganizerTicketInsights = "/organizer/tickets/insights"` with its builder `OrganizerTicketInsightsFor(eventId)`, which appends `?eventId={id}` because the insights page is reached from the roster carrying its selected event. The comment at `:29-30` records why the attendee side adds no route: "Link my ticket" lives on the `MyBadge` page.
  - Self-service QR (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:39-40`): `SponsorVisit(sponsorId)` and `RoomCheckIn(roomId)` build `/engage/sponsors/{id}` and `/engage/rooms/{id}`. The comment above them (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:37-38`) records the design decision that matters to a reader: these are deep-link-only landings reached by scanning a printed code, so neither contributes a nav item.
- **Why it's built this way**: methods are used wherever an id is embedded so the interpolation (and its invariant culture) lives in one place; plain `const`s are used for the parameterless routes because they must be usable in attribute and collection-initializer positions, which is exactly how [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) consumes them.
- **Where it's used**: seven of the constants seed the nav items in [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementUIModule.cs:33-42`); the feedback and live builders are called from pages and services that link an attendee onward (`SessionLive.razor.cs`, `SessionFeedback.razor.cs`, `SessionReminderPlanner.cs`, `LiveEventListener.razor.cs`), [`TicketInsights`](#ticketinsights) uses the insights route, the host's `AppActionRouteMap` maps app actions onto these routes, and the QR builders are what a printed sponsor or room code encodes.

### ScanOutcomeKind

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/ScanOutcomeKind.cs:4` · Level 0 · enum (internal)

- **What it is**: the four things one check-in attempt can mean to the organizer holding the phone, quoting the type's own summary (`ScanOutcomeKind.cs:3`). It lives in its own file beside [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan), the page that produces and renders it.
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept, the closed outcome vocabulary behind a UI feed.** `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]` is the reason this is an enum and not a pre-formatted string: the page fans each member out through three separate `switch` expressions, one for the sentence (`OutcomeText`, `CheckInScan.razor.cs:342-349`), one for the alert severity (`SeverityFor`, `:351-358`) and one for the icon (`IconFor`, `:360-367`), so colour never carries the status alone. The markup pairs the severity with the icon on every row (`CheckInScan.razor:114-117`), which is what WCAG 2.1 AA asks for. `[Rubric §27, i18n]`: because the enum stays a symbol until render time, the wording lives entirely in the page's resource file.
- **Walkthrough**: `CheckedIn`, `AlreadyCheckedIn`, `NotABadge`, `Failed` (`ScanOutcomeKind.cs:6-9`). `AlreadyCheckedIn` is not an error state: a repeat scan is a normal thing to happen at a door, so it maps to `Severity.Warning` with a replay icon (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:354`, `:363`) rather than to a failure. `NotABadge` covers a scanner reading a poster or sponsor QR and maps to `Severity.Info` (`:355`). Only `Failed` maps to `Severity.Error` (`:356`).
- **Why it's built this way**: four named cases keep the render-time mapping exhaustive and reviewable in one screen. All three `switch` expressions still carry a `_ =>` default arm (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:348`, `:357`, `:366`) so adding a member cannot throw at runtime, only produce the generic failure presentation until the arms are extended.
- **Where it's used**: carried by [`ScanOutcome`](#scanoutcome) and consumed only inside [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan); it is `internal`, so it never leaves the Engagement UI assembly.

- **Depends on**: nothing first-party (a `string` and an `int`).
- **Concept, the page-local view model.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses whether a page renders raw server contracts or a shape it owns. ### CheckInState

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Rooms` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Rooms/RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:197` · Level 0 · enum (protected, nested)

- **What it is**: the eight states one scan of a printed room QR can put the page in, as seen by the attendee (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:196`). It is nested inside [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin) and is the single field its markup switches on.
- **Depends on**: nothing (a bare `enum`). Its refusal values are produced by the page's mapping switch from the `IsTransient` flag and the [`CheckInErrorCodes`](#checkinerrorcodes) value carried on [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult).
- **Concept introduced, the page-owned outcome enum.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses whether a component's visible states are enumerated or reconstructed ad hoc from a scatter of booleans. This page has exactly one state field, so "confirm", "loading", "recorded", "nothing scheduled here", "code rejected", "event not published", "no answer yet, retry" and "unavailable" are mutually exclusive by construction, and the markup is a flat chain of comparisons (`RoomCheckIn.razor:12`, `:16`, `:31`, `:67`, `:73`, `:81`, `:85`, with the final `else` at `:100`) with no combination to reason about. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` is the other half of the story: the refusals cannot all be told apart by HTTP status, so the state is picked from the server's stable error code carried back on [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult), and its `IsTransient` flag (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:20-25`) separates "the server said no" from "no definitive answer arrived".
- **Walkthrough**: eight members in the order the attendee meets them. `Confirm` (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:200`) is what an interactive arrival shows: the scanned room with a Check in button, and nothing posted yet (set at `:91`, rendered at `RoomCheckIn.razor:16-30`). `Loading` (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:203`) is the initial value of `State` (`:56`), so it covers the prerender, and it covers the in-flight post (`:103`). `Recorded` (`:206`) covers both a fresh check-in and a re-confirmed earlier one; the distinction is `RoomCheckInResultDTO.AlreadyCheckedIn`, not a separate state. `NoCurrentSession` (`:209`) means nothing is scheduled in that room right now, and, per the member comment, an unknown room reads the same way. `NotPublished` (`:212`) means the owning event is not published yet. `CodeRejected` (`:215`) means the scanned code is not the room's current one because the room's QR was re-issued; the markup points the attendee at the code on the door (`RoomCheckIn.razor:73-80`). `Unavailable` (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:218`) is the feature-off answer: per its member comment, the server answered and the answer is no. `Transient` (`:221`) is the absence of a definitive answer (rate limited, timed out, offline), the state the attendee can act on through the Retry button the markup renders beside it (`RoomCheckIn.razor:92-98`).
- **Why it's built this way**: collapsing "unknown room" into `NoCurrentSession` and the feature gate into `Unavailable` is a deliberate disclosure choice: a printed code that produces a distinguishable answer for a room that does not exist would confirm which room ids do exist. Splitting `Transient` off `Unavailable` is the opposite move for the opposite reason: a timeout is not a refusal, so it must not read as "this code is not available", and the markup comment (`RoomCheckIn.razor:87-88`) records that the retry reuses the same attempt key, so a check-in whose first try did land reads as recorded rather than repeated. `Confirm` exists so that opening the link records nothing until its holder taps. See [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html) for the surrounding scan-surface decision.
- **Where it's used**: only inside [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin) (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:56`, `:91`, `:103`, `:123`, `:133-140`, `:151`) and its markup. `protected` rather than `private` so the bUnit component tests can assert the rendered outcome (see [`RoomCheckInTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the doc comment on the `State` property (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:55`) still says "six outcomes"; the enum itself has eight members.

### VisitState

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Sponsors` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Sponsors/SponsorVisit.razor.cs:164` · Level 0 · enum (protected, nested)

- **What it is**: the six states one scan of a printed sponsor-booth QR can put the page in. The sibling of [`CheckInState`](#checkinstate), nested inside [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit), with two fewer members because a sponsor booth has no "what is running here right now" question and its code carries no re-issuable room code.
- **Depends on**: nothing (a bare `enum`); its refusal values are chosen from the `IsTransient` flag and the [`CheckInErrorCodes`](#checkinerrorcodes) value on [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult).
- **Concept**: the page-owned outcome enum is taught on [`CheckInState`](#checkinstate); the same reasoning applies unchanged here.
- **Walkthrough**: `Confirm` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:167`), the booth shown with a Record visit button and nothing posted yet (set at `:81`, rendered at `SponsorVisit.razor:17-31`); `Loading` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:170`), the initial value of `State` (`:51`) and the in-flight state (`:93`); `Recorded` (`:173`), which covers both a first visit and a repeat, split in the markup by `SponsorVisitResultDTO.AlreadyVisited` (`SponsorVisit.razor:34`); `NotPublished` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:176`); `Unavailable` (`:179`); and `Transient` (`:182`), the no-definitive-answer state that renders a Retry button (`SponsorVisit.razor:76-82`). The mapping is a property-pattern `switch` over the outcome (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:119-124`): `IsTransient: true` selects `Transient`, `CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished` selects `NotPublished`, and everything else, including a null code, falls to `Unavailable`.
- **Why it's built this way**: the member comment on `Unavailable` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:178`) folds "feature off" and "unknown sponsor" into one member, an answer the server gave, and the markup comment (`SponsorVisit.razor:86-87`) states the reason: the two are the same sentence to an attendee holding a phone, and naming them apart would only confirm which sponsor codes exist. That makes the collapse a `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` decision (no existence disclosure through error differentiation) as much as a copy decision. An unreachable service is deliberately not part of that collapse: it is `Transient` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:181-182`), because a timeout is no answer at all and the attendee can retry it.
- **Where it's used**: only inside [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit) (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:51`, `:81`, `:93`, `:109`, `:119-124`, `:135`) and its markup; `protected` so [`SponsorVisitTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) can drive it.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the enum's own summary (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:163`) still says "five things"; it has six members, which the `State` property's comment (`:50`) does count as six.

### ScanOutcome

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/ScanOutcome.cs:4` · Level 1 · record (internal sealed)

- **What it is**: one line in the organizer's on-screen scan feed: what happened to a badge, and to whom, in the order the organizer saw it (`ScanOutcome.cs:3`).
- **Depends on**: [`ScanOutcomeKind`](#scanoutcomekind).
- **Concept, the immutable UI event record.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses where transient UI state lives and how it changes. The feed is a plain `List<ScanOutcome>` field on [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:71`) whose entries are never edited after creation: a new scan is inserted at index 0 and the list is trimmed from the tail (`AddOutcome`, `CheckInScan.razor.cs:333-340`, bounded by the `const int MaxOutcomes = 10` at `:24`). Immutable entries plus a bounded list mean the feed cannot grow without limit during a long scanning session and cannot be retroactively rewritten by a later scan.
- **Walkthrough**: a positional `record` with `AttendeeName` and `Kind` (`ScanOutcome.cs:4`). It is constructed in four places on the page, and the differences are the interesting part: `new ScanOutcome(string.Empty, ScanOutcomeKind.NotABadge)` when the scanned text is not a badge payload (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:230`), a named `Failed` when a manual write comes back a failure (`:291`), a `Failed` carrying whatever name the caller had when the response itself is a failure (`:318`), and the success path in `RecordResultAsync`, which resolves a name and picks `AlreadyCheckedIn` or `CheckedIn` from the response (`:328-330`). Where no name is available the page substitutes the localized `Outcome.UnknownAttendee` string (`:329`) rather than rendering an empty row.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the name on the record (instead of re-resolving it at render time) means the feed is pure data by the time the markup runs, so re-rendering never triggers another lookup.
- **Where it's used**: only inside [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan); rendered as one `MudAlert` per entry (`CheckInScan.razor:114-117`).

### OrganizerEventPicker

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/OrganizerEventPicker.razor.cs:14` · Level 3 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for a small event-chooser component shared by the organizer pages. It takes the published events and the currently selected one, tells its host when the organizer picks a different event, and offers the hosts one static loader that resolves the current event and the events to list.
- **Depends on**: [`LiveEventContext`](group-22-engagement-module.md#liveeventcontext) (the event row it lists: a name and a live-window start), [`ILiveEventUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#iliveeventuiservice) and [`LiveEventLookup`](#liveeventlookup) (the three-state current-event read, `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveEventLookup.cs:10`). Externals: Blazor `[Parameter]` / `EventCallback<T>` and the `EventIdentifierType` alias. The markup (the select control) is not in this file.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Three parameters (`OrganizerEventPicker.razor.cs:17-23`): `Events` (`IReadOnlyList<LiveEventContext>`, default empty), `SelectedEventId` (`EventIdentifierType?`) and `OnEventSelected` (`EventCallback<EventIdentifierType>`). The host owns the selection; the picker only reports changes.
  - `OffersAChoice(events)` (`:32-36`) is a public static predicate returning `events.Count > 1`, after an `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull`. It is static so the host pages can call it too, to drop their plain event-name heading while the picker (which already shows the chosen name) is on screen (doc comment `:25-31`).
  - `LoadEventsAsync(liveEventService, cancellationToken)` (`:47-61`) is the public static loader every host runs before it loads anything. It awaits `GetCurrentEventAsync` (`:53`) and returns that [`LiveEventLookup`](#liveeventlookup) with an empty list when there is no current event (`:54-57`), so a host can tell a failed read (`IsFailed`, `LiveEventLookup.cs:19`) from no published event (`LiveEventLookup.cs:22`). Otherwise it reads `GetPublishedEventsAsync` and returns the published list, or the current event alone when that list is empty (`OrganizerEventPicker.razor.cs:59-60`). The doc comment (`:38-46`) states the rule: the current event stays the default, and a failed read of the published list degrades to the current event alone (no picker), never an error.
  - `OrderedEvents` (`:63-65`) sorts by `LiveWindowStartUtc` then by `Name` under `StringComparer.CurrentCulture`, so the list reads chronologically.
  - `OnSelectedEventChangedAsync` (`:67-70`) invokes `OnEventSelected` only when the chosen id is non-null and differs from `SelectedEventId`; re-selecting the current event returns `Task.CompletedTask`, which is why the callback is documented as never raised for the event already selected (`:22`).
- **Why it's built this way**: a single event needs no chooser, so `OffersAChoice` keeps the single-event case unchanged for hosts. Keeping selection state in the host lets each page decide what a change reloads, and putting the load in one static method keeps the "failed read versus no event" distinction identical on every host.
- **Where it's used**: hosted by [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) (`CheckInScan.razor:15`, heading guard at `:36`, loader call at `CheckInScan.razor.cs:87`) and [`OrganizerAttendance`](#organizerattendance) (`OrganizerAttendance.razor:15`, guard at `:36`, loader call at `OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:74`), and used by the ticket pages ([`TicketInsights`](#ticketinsights) and the `Pages/Tickets/TicketRoster.razor.cs` roster page); component-tested through `CheckInScanTests` and `OrganizerAttendanceTests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the select markup and its resource strings live outside this file.

### MyBadge

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/MyBadge.razor.cs:15` · Level 5 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the attendee's own badge page (`@page "/my-badge"`, `MyBadge.razor:1`). It fetches the caller's opaque badge credential, encodes it as a QR code, and renders the attendee's name beside it as plain text.
- **Depends on**: [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice) (`MyBadge.razor.cs:17`), [`BadgePayload`](#badgepayload) (`:66`), and [`MyBadgeDTO`](#mybadgedto) as the value inside the fetch result. Externals: Blazor's `[CascadingParameter] Task<AuthenticationState>` (`:19-20`), MudBlazor's `BreadcrumbItem`/`Icons`, the shared `QrCodeImage`, `PageLoadingState` and `DetailLoadStateContent` components from `MMCA.Common.UI.Components` (the latter driven by [`DetailLoadState`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#detailloadstate)), and an injected `IStringLocalizer<MyBadge>` named `L` declared in the markup (`MyBadge.razor:6`).
- **Concept introduced, the opaque-credential badge.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` and `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` both apply, and the class summary states the rule (`MyBadge.razor.cs:10-14`): the QR carries only the credential, nothing about the person. Anyone photographing a badge across the room learns a GUID, not a name or an email, and the server remains the sole authority on which attendee that credential belongs to (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/Badges/BadgePayload.cs:6-11`). The human-readable name is rendered beside the code as ordinary text (`MyBadge.razor:42`) so an organizer can confirm the badge belongs to the person holding it; it is never inside the code. `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]`: the QR image carries an `AltText` from the resource file, and its `PixelsPerModule="14"` plus `Medium` error correction are documented in the markup comment (`MyBadge.razor:34-35`) as making the code readable at arm's length and tolerant of glare or a fingerprint.
- **Concept, distinguishing "no badge" from "the fetch failed".** `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]`: the page reads the result twice, once for the happy path and once for the shape of the failure. `badgeResult.TryGetValue(out var badge)` unwraps a success (`:64`); `else if (!badgeResult.IsNotFound())` sets the error message only when the failure was something other than a 404 (`:68-73`), and the inline comment (`:70-71`) records that a not-found is simply an attendee who has no badge yet. The markup then has three distinct terminal states, not two: the failed-load body, a `DetailLoadStateContent` in its `Failed` state whose `OnRetry` is `LoadAsync` (`MyBadge.razor:17-22`), the empty-state alert when `_payload` is still null (`:23-28`), and the badge card (`:29-49`).
- **Walkthrough** (teaching order)
  - State: a `CancellationTokenSource` field (`MyBadge.razor.cs:22`), the `LifetimeToken` property (`:24-27`, see below), the breadcrumb list (`:29`), a `protected bool IsLoading` that starts `true` (`:32`), and three privates for the error message, the encoded payload and the display name (`:34-36`).
  - `LifetimeToken => _cts.LifetimeToken()` (`:27`) is the token every await uses. The comment above it (`:24-26`) gives the reason: reading `Token` off a disposed source throws `ObjectDisposedException`, whereas `Dispose` cancels before it disposes, so a load that resumes after the attendee navigated away gets an already-cancelled token and exits through its `OperationCanceledException` path.
  - `OnInitializedAsync` (`:38`) is not `async`: it builds the two-item breadcrumb trail (`:40-44`) and returns `LoadAsync()` (`:46`).
  - `LoadAsync` (`:50`) is the load and, per its summary, also the Retry action (`:49`), which is why it begins by setting `IsLoading = true` and clearing `_loadError` (`:52-53`): a retry starts from the spinner, not from the previous error. Inside a `try` it awaits the cascaded `AuthenticationState` for `state.User.Identity?.Name` (`:57-61`) and calls `CheckInService.GetMyBadgeAsync(LifetimeToken)` (`:63`). Only on a successful unwrap does it compute `_payload = BadgePayload.Format(badge.Credential)` (`:66`).
  - Failure handling is the house pattern: `OperationCanceledException` is swallowed as expected during disposal (`:75-78`), and `IsLoading` is cleared in `finally` (`:79-82`) so the page can never be stuck on the spinner. Because the service returns a `Result`, an ordinary server refusal never reaches a `catch` at all.
  - `Dispose(bool)` / `Dispose()` (`:87-107`) are the standard disposable pattern with a `_disposed` guard, cancelling and disposing the token source so an in-flight fetch stops when the attendee navigates away.
- **Why it's built this way**: encoding the payload on the client from a credential the server issued keeps the QR format in exactly one place, `BadgePayload.Format` ([`BadgePayload`](#badgepayload), `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/Badges/BadgePayload.cs:20`), which is the same class the scanner side parses with (`:30`). Display and check-in cannot drift apart because they share the type and its `mmca-adc:badge:` prefix (`:15`).
- **Where it's used**: routed at `/my-badge` behind a plain `[Authorize]` attribute (`MyBadge.razor:2`), so the route itself admits any signed-in attendee, while the nav item [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) registers for it carries `RequiredRole: RoleNames.Organizer` (`EngagementUIModule.cs:27`), so only organizers see the link in the menu. Its QR is what [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) reads at a session door.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the resource strings and the `QrCodeImage` rendering behaviour live outside this file; this section covers the code-behind and the small amount of markup cited.

### RoomCheckIn

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Rooms` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Rooms/RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:24` · Level 5 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the room QR landing page (`@page "/engage/rooms/{RoomId:int}"`, `RoomCheckIn.razor:1`). An attendee scans the code printed beside a room door, signs in if needed, lands here, sees the room, and taps Check in; the page then records the check-in. The scan never names a session: the server decides which session that room is hosting at this instant. The printed QR also carries the room's check-in code as `?code=`, the proof of presence the server checks.
- **Depends on**: [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice) (the post), [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult) (the return shape), [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto) (the payload), [`CheckInErrorCodes`](#checkinerrorcodes) (the refusal vocabulary), [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice) (the snackbar), [`ViewerTimeZone`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#viewertimezone) (the viewer's clock, `RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:37`), and its own nested [`CheckInState`](#checkinstate). Externals: Blazor `ComponentBase` (`RendererInfo`, `[Parameter]`, `[SupplyParameterFromQuery]`), MudBlazor `BreadcrumbItem` / `MudAlert` / `MudButton` / `MudCard` / `Icons`, and an injected `IStringLocalizer<RoomCheckIn>` named `L` supplied by the markup (`RoomCheckIn.razor:5`).
- **Concept introduced, the confirm-to-write landing page.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses component/behavior separation and render-mode discipline. Arriving from a scan is half the interaction; one tap is the other half. The page prepares the write in `OnParametersSetAsync` and posts it only from `ConfirmAsync`, the Check in button's handler (`RoomCheckIn.razor:24-25`). That makes the Blazor render-mode question load-bearing in a narrower way: a prerendered pass and the interactive pass both run the lifecycle, so the guard at `RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:75-76` (`!RendererInfo.IsInteractive || RoomId == _postedRoomId && CheckInCode == _postedCheckInCode`, compared ordinally) keeps one scan to one prepared attempt, while a scan of a different room, or of the same room with a different code, reusing the routed instance prepares a new one. The class comment (just above `:24`) gives the reason for the tap: a link opened from anywhere (a forwarded message, an app link the phone resolved on its own) records nothing until its holder confirms. `[Rubric §19, State Management]` covers the single-field state model taught on [`CheckInState`](#checkinstate).
- **Concept introduced, the retryable write under one attempt key.** A phone at a crowded door loses packets, so a post that got no answer must be retryable without risking a double record. Each scan gets one `Idempotency-Key`, minted as `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")` when the scan changes (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:87`) and kept in `_attemptKey` (`:53`) for every retry of that scan, the Retry button included. The comment (`:84-86`) gives the reason: a retry whose first try did land replays that first answer instead of reading as a repeat check-in. The server half is the [`IdempotentAttribute`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#idempotentattribute) on the room-visits endpoint (`CheckInsController.cs:194`). `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies through `@attribute [Authorize]` (`RoomCheckIn.razor:2`): the page identifies the attendee from the authenticated session, so a scanned code carries no identity of its own, and the `?code=` value proves presence at the door rather than who is scanning.
- **Walkthrough** (teaching order)
  - `[Parameter] RoomIdentifierType RoomId` (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:27`) is bound from the `{RoomId:int}` route constraint, so an unparseable code never reaches the component. `[SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "code")] string? CheckInCode` (`:33`) reads the room's check-in code from the query string; per its doc comment (`:29-32`) it is absent on a QR printed before the room had a code, which the server accepts until an organizer issues one. The injected [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice), [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice) and [`ViewerTimeZone`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#viewertimezone) follow (`:35-37`), then a `CancellationTokenSource` (`:39`), the `LifetimeToken` property (`:44`), the breadcrumb list (`:46`), the `_postedRoomId` and `_postedCheckInCode` pair holding the scan this instance last showed, posted or is posting (`:48-50`), and the `_attemptKey` string (`:53`) holding the current scan's idempotency key.
  - `LifetimeToken => _cts.LifetimeToken()` (`:44`) is the token every await on the page uses. The comment above it (`:41-43`) records why: reading `Token` off a disposed source throws `ObjectDisposedException`, while `Dispose` cancels before it disposes, so a post that resumes after the attendee navigated away sees an already-cancelled token and exits through its `OperationCanceledException` path.
  - `State` (`:56`) starts at `CheckInState.Loading` and is `protected` with a private setter; `Result` (`:59`) holds the [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto) and is documented as present only in the `Recorded` state.
  - `OnInitialized` (`:61-66`) is a synchronous expression-bodied method that builds the two-item breadcrumb trail, so even the non-interactive prerender has a complete chrome. `OnParametersSetAsync` (`:68`) is not `async`: it returns `Task.CompletedTask` if the render is not interactive or the room and code match the last scan (`:75-79`). Otherwise it records the scan (`:81-82`), mints a fresh `_attemptKey` (`:87`), clears `Result` and moves to `CheckInState.Confirm` (`:89-91`), posting nothing. The comment (`:70-74`) gives the reason the code is part of the guard: rescanning the room's current door code while an out-of-date one is refused on screen changes only `?code`, and must be a new attempt (M247, the SessionLive per-id pattern).
  - `ConfirmAsync` (`:96`) is the Check in button's handler and `RetryAsync` (`:99`) is the Retry button's (`RoomCheckIn.razor:95`); both send `RecordCheckInAsync` for `_postedRoomId` under the current key and do nothing when no scan has been shown.
  - `RecordCheckInAsync` (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:101`) resets `State` to `Loading` and clears `Result` (`:103-104`), copies `_attemptKey` into a local `attemptKey` that identifies the scan this post belongs to (`:106-108`), then awaits `CheckInService.RecordRoomCheckInAsync(roomId, _postedCheckInCode, attemptKey, LifetimeToken)` (`:112`).
  - Right after the await, a stale-scan check (`:115-118`) returns when `attemptKey` no longer equals `_attemptKey`: a newer scan took over the page while this one was in flight, and its own post owns the state.
  - The success branch (`:120-131`) assigns `Result`, moves to `CheckInState.Recorded`, and raises a success toast **only** when `Result?.AlreadyCheckedIn == false` (`:125-128`): a rescan is a normal thing to do, so it renders as information (`RoomCheckIn.razor:33-47`) rather than as a second celebration.
  - The refusal branch (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:133-140`) is a property-pattern `switch` over the outcome: `IsTransient: true` becomes `Transient` (checked first, so a timeout never reads as a refusal), `ErrorCode: CheckInErrorCodes.NoCurrentSession` becomes `NoCurrentSession`, `ErrorCode: CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished` becomes `NotPublished`, `ErrorCode: CheckInErrorCodes.RoomCodeRejected` becomes `CodeRejected` (`:138`), and everything else (including a `null` code) falls through the discard arm to `Unavailable`. This is the client-side consumer of the contract that [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult) exists to carry.
  - `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (LifetimeToken.IsCancellationRequested)` (`:142-145`) is silent only when the page's own token was cancelled, that is when the attendee navigated away; any other exception, including a cancellation the page did not ask for such as a client timeout, lands on `Transient` only when the attempt key is still current (`:147-152`), so a stale scan's failure cannot overwrite a newer scan's state. The `CA1031` suppression around that catch (`:146`, `:148`) carries the reason inline: a fault with no definitive answer is the retryable state, never "not available".
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync` (`:160-166`) runs on the first render only: it awaits `ViewerTime.EnsureResolvedAsync(LifetimeToken)` and calls `StateHasChanged()` when the zone changed, so the recorded time moves from the UTC fallback to the viewer's clock once JS interop is available (doc comment `:155-159`).
  - `FormatCheckedInOn` (`:176-177`) is an instance method that renders the recorded instant through `ViewerTime.Format(checkedInOn.UtcDateTime)`. The XML comment (`:168-175`) gives the reason: the attendee is comparing the timestamp against the clock on the wall beside them, and `DateTimeOffset.ToLocalTime` would read the server's clock on Blazor Server and during prerender. `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` covers both halves of that, the viewer-zone formatting and the fact that every visible string is an `L["..."]` resource lookup ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)).
  - `PointsLine` (`:186-194`) picks the line under a first check-in from the [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto): `PointsPaused` gives the `PointsPaused` string (session points are switched off, nothing is awarded), otherwise `EarnsPoints` selects `Success.PointsHint` ("added to your total") or `NoPointsThisTimeSlot` for a second check-in in the same time slot (doc comment `:179-185`).
  - `Dispose(bool)` / `Dispose()` (`:224-246`) implement the standard disposable pattern with a `_disposed` latch, cancelling and disposing `_cts` so an in-flight post stops when the attendee navigates away.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class comment (just above `RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:24`) states the constraints. The write runs on the interactive render only, once per scan rather than once per page instance, and only after the attendee confirms: a prerender must not spend a round trip, a back button must not read as a second arrival, and a link that reached a phone some other way must not record anything on its own. The server is idempotent per session regardless (a repeat returns `AlreadyCheckedIn`), so the per-scan guard is about not making a pointless call rather than about correctness; the attempt key adds the same guarantee for a retry, which the endpoint replays rather than re-executes. Resolving the session server-side from the room, instead of encoding it in the QR, means the printed code does not change when the schedule moves ([ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html)); only re-issuing the room's check-in code retires an old print, which is what `CodeRejected` reports. The page complements organizer badge scanning at the door rather than replacing it: one session yields one check-in by either path, which is exactly what the "already checked in" branch says (`RoomCheckIn.razor:35-36`).
- **Where it's used**: the target of the room QR rendered on the Conference room detail page (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Rooms/RoomDetail.razor:64`, a `QrCodeButton` over [`ConferenceRoutePaths`](group-21-conference-ui.md#conferenceroutepaths)`.RoomCheckInLink(id, checkInCode)`, `ConferenceRoutePaths.cs:68`) per [ADR-071](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/071-barcode-scanning-and-qr-display.html). The post lands on [`CheckInsController`](#checkinscontroller)'s room-visits endpoint (`CheckInsController.cs:193`, `[Idempotent]` at `:194`, feature-gated on `EngagementFeatures.RoomCheckIn` at `:195`) and is handled by [`RecordRoomCheckInHandler`](#recordroomcheckinhandler). `[Rubric §28, Front-End Testing]`: covered by [`RoomCheckInTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (bUnit), and the architecture suite carries a `RoomCheckInModeTests` contract test. Render-mode background: [ADR-056](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/056-blazor-render-mode-strategy.html).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the confirm card, the outcome copy, the success card, the points hint and the Retry button live in `RoomCheckIn.razor` (`:16-30`, `:31-66`, `:85-99`) and the resource files, not in this code-behind. Whether a given deployment has `EngagementFeatures.RoomCheckIn` on is configuration, not source.

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Sponsors` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Sponsors/SponsorVisit.razor.cs:26` · Level 5 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the sponsor-booth QR landing page (`@page "/engage/sponsors/{SponsorId:int}"`, `SponsorVisit.razor:1`). The attendee scans the booth's printed code with the phone camera, signs in if needed, lands here, and taps Record visit; the page then records the visit.
- **Depends on**: [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice), [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult), [`SponsorVisitResultDTO`](#sponsorvisitresultdto), [`CheckInErrorCodes`](#checkinerrorcodes), [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice), [`ViewerTimeZone`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#viewertimezone) (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:33`), its nested [`VisitState`](#visitstate), and (from the markup) [`ConferenceRoutePaths`](group-21-conference-ui.md#conferenceroutepaths) for the follow-on "all sponsors" link. - **Concept**: the confirm-to-write landing page is taught on [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin); this page is the same shape with no room code and a simpler refusal map. The one difference worth naming is what happens *after* success: `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` assesses whether a dead-end page gives the reader somewhere to go, and this one ends with a filled "all sponsors" button back into the public sponsor list (`SponsorVisit.razor:57-63`), which the room page has no equivalent of because a room scan is followed by sitting down.

  - `[Parameter] SponsorIdentifierType SponsorId` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:29`) instead of a room id, and no query-string code; `LifetimeToken` (`:40`, the same disposed-source guard as on [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin), explained in the comment above it) backs every await; `_postedSponsorId` (`:45`) is a nullable `SponsorIdentifierType` holding the sponsor this instance last posted (or is posting); `_attemptKey` (`:48`) is the current booth's idempotency key; `State` defaults to `VisitState.Loading` (`:51`) and `Visit` holds a [`SponsorVisitResultDTO`](#sponsorvisitresultdto) (`:54`).
  - `OnInitialized` (`:56-61`) only builds the breadcrumbs; `OnParametersSetAsync` (`:63`) carries an inline comment naming the pattern it follows (`:65-66`): the visit is a write, so it stays off the prerender pass, and the interactive instance is the one that owns the round trip (the [`ADCHome`](group-21-conference-ui.md#adchome) pattern). The guard is `!RendererInfo.IsInteractive || SponsorId == _postedSponsorId` (`:67`), so a deep link to another booth reusing the routed instance (M247, the SessionLive per-id pattern) prepares a new attempt. Past the guard it records the sponsor (`:72`), mints one attempt key per scanned booth (`:77`, comment `:74-76` citing A-27), clears `Visit` and moves to `VisitState.Confirm` (`:79-81`), posting nothing.
  - `ConfirmAsync` (`:86`) backs the Record visit button (`SponsorVisit.razor:25-26`) and `RetryAsync` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:89`) backs the Retry button (`SponsorVisit.razor:79`); both send `RecordVisitAsync` for `_postedSponsorId` under the same key, exactly as on the room page.
  - `RecordVisitAsync` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:91`) resets `State` to `Loading` and clears `Visit` (`:93-94`) before calling `CheckInService.RecordSponsorVisitAsync(sponsorId, _attemptKey, LifetimeToken)` (`:98`).
  - A stale-scan check (`:101-104`) returns when `sponsorId != _postedSponsorId`, because a newer scan took over the page while this one was in flight. Unlike the room page, the check compares sponsor ids rather than attempt keys, since a booth scan has no code that can change on its own.
  - Success (`:106-117`) sets `Visit`, moves to `VisitState.Recorded`, and toasts only on a first visit (`Visit?.AlreadyVisited == false`, `:111-114`).
  - The refusal map (`:119-124`) is a property-pattern `switch` with fewer arms than the room page's: `IsTransient: true` selects `Transient`, only `CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished` is distinguished among the refusals, and everything else is `Unavailable`. There is no room-style "nothing scheduled here" or "code rejected" case, because a booth is not on a schedule and its QR carries no code.
  - `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (LifetimeToken.IsCancellationRequested)` (`:126-129`) stays silent only when the attendee navigated away; `catch (Exception) when (sponsorId == _postedSponsorId)` (`:131-136`, inside the same inline `CA1031` suppression as the room page) maps any other fault to `Transient`, only for the current scan.

  - `Dispose(bool)` / `Dispose()` (`:185-207`) are the same disposable pattern over `_cts`.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class comment (just above `SponsorVisit.razor.cs:26`) says the write runs on the interactive render only and once per scanned sponsor, and that the server is idempotent per sponsor regardless of the guard, so the per-sponsor guard is about not making a pointless round trip rather than about correctness; a retry under the same attempt key is replayed by the endpoint's `[Idempotent]` attribute (`CheckInsController.cs:159`) rather than re-executed. The single confirm tap (`SponsorVisit.razor:19`) keeps a link opened outside a booth from recording a visit on its own while costing an attendee at the booth one tap; [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html) records the attendee-self-recorded scan surfaces this page belongs to.
- **Where it's used**: the target of the sponsor QR rendered on the Conference sponsor detail page (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Sponsors/SponsorDetail.razor:73`, a `QrCodeButton` over [`ConferenceRoutePaths`](group-21-conference-ui.md#conferenceroutepaths)`.SponsorVisitLink`, `ConferenceRoutePaths.cs:65`). The post lands on [`CheckInsController`](#checkinscontroller)'s sponsor-visits endpoint (`CheckInsController.cs:158`, feature-gated on `EngagementFeatures.SponsorVisits` at `CheckInsController.cs:160`, see [`EngagementFeatures`](#engagementfeatures) and [ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html)) and is handled by [`RecordSponsorVisitHandler`](#recordsponsorvisithandler). Component-tested by [`SponsorVisitTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the confirm card, the success card, the points hint, the "already visited" copy and the Retry button live in `SponsorVisit.razor` (`:17-31`, `:32-64`, `:69-83`) and its resources. How many points a visit earns is decided server-side by the points earn rules, not here.

### AttendeeSearchPanel

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:16` · Level 7 · class (partial, `DataGridListPageBase<AttendeeSummary>`)

- **What it is**: the manual check-in fallback, a paged, sortable, mobile-aware search over the Identity users endpoint with a per-row check-in action. It is a component, not a page: it has no `@page` directive and is embedded by [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan).
- **Depends on**: [`DataGridListPageBase<TDto>`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#datagridlistpagebasetdto) as its base (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:16`), [`IAttendeeLookupService`](#iattendeelookupservice) plus [`AttendeeSummary`](#attendeesummary) and [`AttendeeSearchField`](#attendeesearchfield) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Lookups/IAttendeeLookupService.cs:15`, `:39`), [`MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#mobileinfinitescrolllisttitem), and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) for the mobile fetch signature (`:3`, `:79`). Externals: MudBlazor `MudDataGrid`/`GridState`/`GridData`, and an injected `IStringLocalizer<AttendeeSearchPanel>` (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:5`).
- **Concept introduced, extracting a list surface out of a page.** `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` and `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]`: the class summary records the reason for the split (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:10-15`), namely that the page owns the scan loop and its own cancellation while the grid keeps the shared base's behaviour (server paging, mobile card layout, state restore) unchanged. Inheriting the framework base rather than hand-rolling a grid is what buys the mobile path: `[Rubric §22, Responsive & Cross-Browser]` shows in `ReloadActiveLayoutAsync` (`:59-60`), which delegates to the base's protected `ReloadActiveLayoutAsync(_infiniteList)` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.cs:1746-1755`): on a phone with a card list it saves the filter state and resets the list from page 1, otherwise it reloads the grid, so the same filter change reloads whichever layout is live.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Contract with the base: `Title` from the localizer (`:19`) and `GridRef => _dataGrid` (`:32`), which is how the base drives `ReloadServerData()`; `OnMobileDataRequestedAsync` (`:55`) routes the base's mobile hook back through the same reload, and `RetryLoadAsync` (`:57`) is what the empty-state retry button calls.
  - Parameters from the host page: `CanCheckIn` (`:24`) gates the per-row action, and `OnCheckIn` (`:27`) is the `EventCallback<AttendeeSummary>` raised by `CheckInAsync` (`:127`). The component performs no write of its own; it reports which row was actioned and lets the page decide.
  - Filter persistence: `SaveFilters` / `RestoreFilters` (`:39-52`) round-trip the search term and the chosen field through the base's state store, with `Enum.TryParse` falling back to `LastName` if the stored value is unreadable (`:49-51`).
  - Search handling: `OnSearchChangedAsync` and `OnSearchFieldChangedAsync` (`:62-72`) each set a field and return `ReloadActiveLayoutAsync()` directly (they are plain `Task`-returning methods, not `async`). The markup wires the text field with `Immediate="true" DebounceInterval="300"` (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:12`), so typing does not fire a request per keystroke, a `[Rubric §23, Front-End Performance]` detail.
  - Data loading: `LoadServerData` (`:74-77`) is `LoadServerDataAsync(state, SearchAsync, ApplySearchTerm)`, handing the base the private `SearchAsync` (`:96-103`) as its fetch delegate. `SearchAsync` passes the filter bag to `AttendeeLookup.SearchAsync(filters, page, pageSize, sortColumn, sortDirection, cancellationToken)` verbatim (doc comment `:90-95`): the grid's column operators on LastName, FirstName and Email, and the search box's entry under the field's own key or under the `~search` alias the base class moves it to when that column is also filtered, so both apply. `FetchMobilePageAsync` (`:79-88`) builds a filter bag, applies the search term, calls `SearchAsync` with `"LastName"` / `"asc"` (`:87`) and returns `Task<Result<(IReadOnlyList<AttendeeSummary> Items, int TotalItems)>>`, pinning the sort since the card layout has no sort UI. The markup binds it through `FetchPageResult` (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:30`), the `Result`-aware overload, which is what lets a failed page render `ListNoRecordsContent` with `LoadFailed` and a retry rather than an empty list (`:86`).
  - `ApplySearchTerm` (`:109-125`) is the load-bearing piece and its doc comment explains it (`:105-108`, echoed in the markup at `:15`): the Identity users endpoint **ANDs** its filters, so one search box broadcast across email, first name and last name would match nobody. The single term is therefore applied to exactly the field the organizer picked, as a `"contains"` filter (`:116-124`).
- **Why it's built this way**: an organizer at a door needs the fallback to be fast and forgiving, and the shared base already solved paging, mobile layout and state restore for every other list in the app. Raising an `EventCallback` instead of calling the check-in service directly keeps the write path (and its scope, target and error reporting) in one place, the page. `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]`: both action buttons carry a per-row `aria-label` built from the attendee's display name (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:43`, `:79`), so a screen-reader user hears which person a "Check in" button belongs to.
- **Where it's used**: rendered unconditionally near the bottom of the scan page, `<AttendeeSearchPanel CanCheckIn="CanCheckIn" OnCheckIn="ManualCheckInAsync" />` (`CheckInScan.razor:127`). The comment above it (`CheckInScan.razor:122-123`) states the intent: on web and Windows heads there is no camera, so this search **is** the check-in surface.
