### CheckInScan

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/CheckInScan.razor.cs:21` · Level 10 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the organizer check-in surface (`@page "/check-in"`, `[Authorize(Roles = RoleNames.Organizer)]`, `CheckInScan.razor:1-2`). On a head with a camera it loops the shared barcode scanner and posts each badge payload; everywhere else the manual search below the scan area is the whole page. Both paths write through the same endpoints and report the attendee by name.
- **Depends on**: [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice), [`IAttendeeLookupService`](#iattendeelookupservice), [`ISessionLookupService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#isessionlookupservice), [`ILiveEventUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#iliveeventuiservice), [`IBarcodeScannerService`](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#ibarcodescannerservice) and [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice) (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:26-31`); the shared contracts [`BadgePayload`](#badgepayload), [`CheckInScope`](#checkinscope), [`CheckInAttendeeRequest`](#checkinattendeerequest), [`ManualCheckInRequest`](#manualcheckinrequest), [`CheckInResultDTO`](#checkinresultdto); [`LiveEventContext`](group-22-engagement-module.md#liveeventcontext) and [`SessionInfo`](group-22-engagement-module.md#sessioninfo); [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`ErrorType`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype) (`:4`); [`ScanOutcome`](#scanoutcome) / [`ScanOutcomeKind`](#scanoutcomekind) for the feed; and the [`AttendeeSearchPanel`](#attendeesearchpanel) and [`OrganizerEventPicker`](#organizereventpicker) components.
- **Concept introduced, the capability-gated scan loop.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` and the device-capability abstraction of [ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html) meet here. `ScannerAvailable => Scanner.IsSupported` (`:46`, with the ADR named in the comment at `:45`) is the whole capability switch: the markup renders the scan card only when it is true (`CheckInScan.razor:78`), and every head that cannot open a camera falls through to the manual panel with no conditional compilation and no per-platform page. Camera permission is asked once, before the loop: `Scanner.EnsureCameraAccessAsync` (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:210`) returning `false` toasts a `Snackbar.CameraDenied` warning and returns (`:210-214`), so a denial leaves the organizer on the page with the reason and the manual search rather than on a camera surface that stays black (comment `:208-209`). `[Rubric §11, Security]`: scanned text is untrusted input, so `BadgePayload.TryExtractCredential` screens it before any request goes out (`:228`), and a poster or sponsor QR is reported as a skipped scan rather than an error (comment `:224-227`). `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]`: `CanCheckIn` (`:49-50`) refuses to start a scan or a manual write until a target exists, and the markup renders an inline "pick a target" alert when it is false (`CheckInScan.razor:69-73`).
- **Walkthrough** (teaching order)
  - Constants and state: `MaxOutcomes = 10` bounds the on-screen feed (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:24`); the `CancellationTokenSource` (`:33`), `LifetimeToken` (`:38`), `IsLoading` (`:43`), `_loadError`, `_liveEvent`, the `_events` list of published events that feeds the [`OrganizerEventPicker`](#organizereventpicker) (`:54`), `_sessions` and `_selectedSessionId` (`:52-56`), the `_loadGeneration` counter (`:63`, explained below), the scope field (`:68`), the `_isScanning` flag and the `_outcomes` list (`:70-71`).
  - `LifetimeToken => _cts.LifetimeToken()` (`:38`) is the token every await on the page uses (catalog load, the camera-access check, `Scanner.ScanAsync`, both writes, the name lookup). The comment above it (`:35-37`) explains that reading `Token` off a disposed source throws `ObjectDisposedException`; because `Dispose` cancels before it disposes, a handler resuming after navigation gets a cancelled token and stops through its `OperationCanceledException` path.
  - Default scope: `_scope = CheckInScope.Session` with a comment that is real operational knowledge (`:65-68`, repeated for the reader in the markup at `CheckInScan.razor:43-45`), namely that the conference runs door and arrival check-in through TicketLeap, so session check-in is the working path and `Event` scope is kept for future info-desk use.
  - `OnInitializedAsync` (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:73`) is not `async`: it builds the breadcrumbs and returns `RunLoadAsync(LoadEventAsync)` (`:81`).
  - `LoadEventAsync` (`:85-101`) calls [`OrganizerEventPicker`](#organizereventpicker)`.LoadEventsAsync(LiveEventService, LifetimeToken)` (`:87`). A failed read sets the localized load error and returns (`:88-93`), so an outage shows the failed-load body with Retry rather than reading as "no published event". Otherwise it stores the current event and the picker's events (`:95-96`) and, when there is a current event, awaits `LoadSessionsAsync(_liveEvent.EventId)` (`:97-100`).
  - Event switching: `OnEventSelectedAsync` (`:107`) is the handler the picker's `OnEventSelected` callback targets (`CheckInScan.razor:15`). It ignores an id not in `_events` (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:109-113`), calls `StopScanning()` and sets `_liveEvent` to the chosen event (`:115-116`), and returns `ReloadSessionsAsync(eventId)` (`:117`).
  - `RetryLoadAsync` (`:124-125`) is the `OnRetry` target of the failed-load body (`CheckInScan.razor:25`): it reloads the selected event's sessions, or runs `LoadEventAsync` again when no event was resolved because the event read failed (doc comment `CheckInScan.razor.cs:120-123`). `ReloadSessionsAsync` (`:128-133`) clears the session choice and session list (sessions belong to one event) and returns `RunLoadAsync(() => LoadSessionsAsync(eventId))`.
  - `RunLoadAsync(Func<Task> load)` (`:136-159`) is the one loading wrapper. It bumps `_loadGeneration` first, so anything in flight now belongs to an older generation (`:138-140`), clears `_loadError` and sets `IsLoading` (`:141-142`), awaits the load (`:146`), swallows a disposal-time `OperationCanceledException` (`:148-151`), and in `finally` clears `IsLoading` only when the generation is unchanged (`:152-158`), so a superseded load cannot hide the spinner of a newer selection.
  - `LoadSessionsAsync` (`:162-182`) is the shared session loader. It snapshots the generation, awaits the `Result`-returning catalog lookup (`:166`), and drops the result if the generation moved while it was in flight (`:167-170`), so a slow earlier load never overwrites a newer selection's list. A failed result sets the load error (`:172-176`); otherwise it filters sessions to the given event id, ordering by start time with `?? DateTime.MaxValue` so unscheduled sessions sort last, then by title under `StringComparer.CurrentCulture` (`:178-181`).
  - Target selection: `OnScopeChangedAsync` stops any running scan when the scope changes (`:184-189`), which prevents a scan started against one target from continuing under another; `OnSessionChanged` just records the selection (`:191`).
  - `StartScanningAsync` (`:198-249`) is the loop. It refuses to start twice or without a target (`:200-203`), runs the camera-access check described above (`:210-214`), then repeatedly awaits `Scanner.ScanAsync(LifetimeToken)` while `_isScanning` holds and cancellation has not been requested (`:216-218`). A `null` payload means cancelled, and the loop ends quietly (`:219-222`, doc comment `:193-197`). A non-badge payload adds a `NotABadge` outcome, calls `StateHasChanged()` immediately, and continues (`:228-233`): the repaint is deliberate, because the next `ScanAsync` waits on the camera and the operator must see why that code was skipped in the meantime (comment `:224-227`). Otherwise it submits and calls `StateHasChanged()` so the feed paints between scans (`:235-237`), with a `BL0012` suppression whose inline reason says the same thing (`:236`).
  - `SubmitScanAsync` (`:253-267`) builds a [`CheckInAttendeeRequest`](#checkinattendeerequest) carrying the credential, the scope, the event id and, only in session scope, the selected session (`:255-261`). It does not catch anything: the write (`CheckInByCredentialAsync(request, LifetimeToken)`, `:265`) returns a `Result` that `RecordResultAsync` turns into a `Failed` row while the loop keeps scanning, and a genuine cancellation propagates to the loop's own handler (`:263-266`).
  - `ManualCheckInAsync` (`:270-308`) is the fallback the panel raises. It toasts a warning when no target is selected (`:272-276`), builds a [`ManualCheckInRequest`](#manualcheckinrequest) by user id (`:280-286`), and on a failed result adds a named `Failed` outcome (`:291`) plus a toast whose wording depends on *why* it failed: a refusal the API stated is shown verbatim through `result.LocalizedErrorMessage(L)`, while an `ErrorType.Unexpected` fault keeps the page's own wording instead of raw diagnostic text (`:293-298`). `[Rubric §11, Security]` and `[Rubric §13, Observability & Operability]`: that branch is the boundary between what an organizer may read and what belongs in the logs.
  - `RecordResultAsync` (`:314-331`) turns one response into an outcome. A failed `Result` becomes a `Failed` row (`:316-320`). The scan path has no name to start from because a badge carries only a credential, so it resolves one via `AttendeeLookup.GetDisplayNameAsync(checkIn.UserId, LifetimeToken)` (`:322-326`); the manual path already has one and skips the lookup. Finally the response's `AlreadyCheckedIn` flag selects the outcome kind (`:330`), which is how a repeat scan reads as a recognisable warning instead of an error.
  - Presentation helpers `OutcomeText` / `SeverityFor` / `IconFor` (`:342-367`) and the bounded `AddOutcome` (`:333-340`), covered under [`ScanOutcomeKind`](#scanoutcomekind).
  - `Dispose(bool)` (`:371-386`) clears `_isScanning` **before** cancelling and disposing the token source (`:380-382`), so the loop's condition fails on the next iteration as well as its await being cancelled.
- **Why it's built this way**: one page serving both a camera head and a keyboard head is a deliberate choice, and it is only affordable because the scan capability is behind an injected interface. Treating a duplicate as a first-class outcome rather than an error is the other design decision that matters at a real door: the organizer needs to see who the badge belongs to either way, which is why [`CheckInResultDTO`](#checkinresultdto) carries `AlreadyCheckedIn` instead of returning a conflict (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInResultDTO.cs:3-7`, `:14`).
- **Where it's used**: routed at `/check-in`, Organizer-only, and surfaced in the nav by [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) with the same role requirement (`EngagementUIModule.cs:39`). It writes through [`CheckInService`](#checkinservice) to the [`CheckInsController`](#checkinscontroller) endpoints. Component-tested by `CheckInScanTests` and `CheckInScanOutcomeTests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: what the camera actually does on each platform is behind [`IBarcodeScannerService`](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#ibarcodescannerservice) (`EnsureCameraAccessAsync` at `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Capabilities/Media/IBarcodeScannerService.cs:22`) and is covered in the device-capability chapter, not here.

### OrganizerAttendance

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:17` · Level 10 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the organizer attendance rollup for the current event, or another published event chosen through the picker (`@page "/organizer/attendance"`, `[Authorize(Roles = RoleNames.Organizer)]`, `OrganizerAttendance.razor:1-2`): one headline arrival figure plus one row per session that has at least one check-in.
- **Depends on**: [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice), [`ILiveEventUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#iliveeventuiservice), [`ISessionLookupService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#isessionlookupservice) (`OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:19-21`), [`OrganizerEventPicker`](#organizereventpicker) (its event loader and the picker component), [`AttendanceStatsDTO`](#attendancestatsdto) and [`SessionAttendanceDTO`](#sessionattendancedto), and its own nested [`SessionAttendanceRow`](#sessionattendancerow). Externals: MudBlazor `MudSimpleTable`/`BreadcrumbItem`, `System.Globalization` in the markup (`OrganizerAttendance.razor:3`), the shared `DetailLoadStateContent` failed-load body, and an injected `IStringLocalizer<OrganizerAttendance>` (`:7`).
- **Concept, client-side enrichment across a service boundary.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` and `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` both apply. The class summary states the situation (`OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:11-15`): the stats endpoint reports session identifiers only, because Engagement owns check-ins and Conference owns the session catalog, so titles are resolved through [`ISessionLookupService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#isessionlookupservice). This page does it in the client, and `BuildSessionRowsAsync` documents the choice (`:189-193`): the whole catalog is fetched once rather than one request per row, because a busy conference day reports dozens of sessions at a time. That is the N+1 avoidance rule applied to a UI join.
- **Walkthrough**
  - State: the token source (`:23`), the `LifetimeToken` property (`:28`, the disposed-source guard explained in the comment above it), breadcrumbs (`:30`), `IsLoading` (`:33`), the error string, event name, the raw `_stats` and the projected `_rows` (`:35-38`), then the picker state: `_events` (`:39`, the published events) and `_selectedEventId` (`:40`), plus `_loadGeneration` (`:47`), a counter bumped to supersede every stats load already in flight (doc comment `:42-46`).
  - `OnInitializedAsync` (`:49`) is not `async`: it builds the breadcrumbs and returns `LoadEventAsync()` (`:57`).
  - `LoadEventAsync` (`:64-103`) is both the initial load and the Retry action while no event has been resolved (doc comment `:60-63`). It bumps `_loadGeneration` (`:66-68`), clears the error and sets `IsLoading` (`:69-70`), then calls [`OrganizerEventPicker`](#organizereventpicker)`.LoadEventsAsync(LiveEventService, LifetimeToken)` (`:74`). A failed read sets the localized load error and returns (`:75-80`), so an outage is not shown as "no published event"; no current event returns quietly (`:82-85`); otherwise it stores the selected id, name and picker events (`:87-89`) and awaits `LoadStatsAsync(liveEvent.EventId)` (`:90`). It swallows a disposal-time cancellation (`:92-95`), and the `finally` clears `IsLoading` only when the generation is unchanged (`:96-102`).
  - `OnEventSelectedAsync` (`:106`) is the picker callback target (`OrganizerAttendance.razor:15`). It ignores an id not in `_events` (`OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:108-112`), swaps in the selected id and name (`:114-115`), and returns `ReloadStatsAsync(eventId)` (`:116`).
  - `RetryLoadAsync` (`:123-124`) is the `OnRetry` target of the failed-load body (`OrganizerAttendance.razor:25`): it reloads the selected event's figures, or runs `LoadEventAsync` again when the event read itself failed (doc comment `OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:119-122`).
  - `ReloadStatsAsync` (`:127-153`) bumps `_loadGeneration` first, so anything in flight now belongs to an older generation (`:129-131`), clears `_stats`, `_rows` and the error and sets `IsLoading` (`:133-136`), then awaits `LoadStatsAsync` under the same swallow-cancel and generation-gated `finally` as the initial load (`:138-152`).
  - `LoadStatsAsync` (`:156-187`) is the shared loader: it fetches the rollup with `GetAttendanceStatsAsync(eventId, LifetimeToken)` (`:160`), drops the result if a newer selection superseded it (`:161-164`), sets the localized load error and returns on a failed `Result` (`:166-170`), builds the rows (`:172`), re-checks the generation (`:173-176`), stores `_stats` (`:178`), and if the row build returned `null` clears the rows and raises the load error (`:179-184`), otherwise assigns `_rows` (`:186`).
  - `BuildSessionRowsAsync` (`:194`) returns `Task<List<SessionAttendanceRow>?>` instead of assigning state itself: it short-circuits to an empty list when the rollup has no session rows, avoiding a pointless catalog fetch (`:196-199`). The catalog fetch itself uses `SessionLookup.GetAllAsync(LifetimeToken)` (`:201`). A failed catalog fetch returns `null` (`:202-205`), which `LoadStatsAsync` turns into cleared rows plus the same load error rather than silently rendering untitled rows. Otherwise it projects each DTO into a [`SessionAttendanceRow`](#sessionattendancerow), substituting the localized `Sessions.DeletedTitle` when the catalog does not know the session (`:210-215`). The comment (`:207-209`) gives the reasoning: the catalog holds every live session of every edition, so a checked-in session missing from it was deleted after the check-ins were recorded, and its row is kept because the attendance happened. Sorting is `OrderByDescending(Count)` then `ThenBy(Title, StringComparer.CurrentCulture)` (`:216-217`), a culture-aware tie-break, so the busiest sessions lead.
  - `Dispose` (`:220-242`) is the same disposable pattern as the other check-in pages.
- **Why it's built this way**: sorting and labelling once, on load, keeps the markup a pure loop over `_rows` (`OrganizerAttendance.razor:68`) with no I/O in the render path. `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]`: that markup is a real `MudSimpleTable` with a `<caption>`, `<th scope="col">` headers and a `<th scope="row">` per session (`OrganizerAttendance.razor:59-76`), not a styled `div` grid, so a screen reader announces the counts with their session names. `[Rubric §27, i18n]`: both the headline figure and each row count are formatted `ToString("N0", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)` (`:44`, `:72`).
- **Where it's used**: routed at `/organizer/attendance` and surfaced as an Organizer-only nav item by [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) (`EngagementUIModule.cs:40`). Its numbers come from the same check-in rows that [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) writes. Component-tested by `OrganizerAttendanceTests`.

### EngagementUIModule

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementUIModule.cs:22` · Level 11 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the Engagement module's UI descriptor. It implements [`IUIModule`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iuimodule) to contribute seven navigation items, one invisible layout component, and its own assembly for Blazor component discovery.
- **Depends on**: [`IUIModule`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iuimodule), [`NavItem`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#navitem) and [`NavSection`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#navsection) from `MMCA.Common.UI.Common`, [`RoleNames`](group-24-identity-module.md#rolenames), [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths), [`LiveEventListener`](#liveeventlistener), MudBlazor `Icons`, and `System.Reflection`.
- **Concept, the pluggable UI module descriptor.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses how a modular monolith composes its front end without the host hard-coding each module's menu: every module ships an `IUIModule`, and the shared shell merges their nav items, layout components and assemblies ([ADR-067](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/067-ui-module-shell-composition.html)). `[Rubric §25, Navigation & IA]`: the menu is declarative data here, not imperative wiring, including where each item sits: a `Section`, an optional `Group` key and an `Order`. `[Rubric §11, Security]`: four of the seven items pass `RoleNames.Organizer` as their required role (`:39-42`) so the shared `NavMenu` hides them from attendees; this is menu trimming, and the real enforcement remains the `[Authorize(Roles = ...)]` attribute on each page. `[Rubric §27, i18n]`: per the [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html) comment (`:27-28`), each `Title` and `Group` is a resource **key**, resolved by `NavMenu` against the co-located `EngagementUIModule.resx` pair at render time through the `typeof(EngagementUIModule)` title-resource pointer passed to every item, so the labels localize instead of being hard-coded English.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Two group keys (`:24-25`): `GroupConferenceDay = "Nav.Group.ConferenceDay"` and `GroupAttendeesAccess = "Nav.Group.AttendeesAccess"`. Per the class remarks (just above `:22`), the Administration groups are described once in [`ConferenceUIModule`](group-21-conference-ui.md#conferenceuimodule), which owns the organizer layout; this module only names their keys.
  - `NavItems` (`:29-43`) is a collection expression of seven entries, each pairing a resource key, a centralized route and an icon. Three sit in `NavSection.User`, the signed-in user section beside the profile entry: `Nav.HappeningNow` to `HappeningNow` (`:33`, `Order = -90`), `Nav.MyPoints` to `MyPoints` (`:34`, `Order = -70`) and `Nav.MyBadge` to `MyBadge` (`:37`, `Order = -60`). The negative orders sort them ahead of the framework's Notification Inbox (order 0), per the class remarks. The comment above `HappeningNow` (`:31-32`) gives the reason for the user section: the page is `[Authorize]`, and the General section also renders for anonymous visitors, which offered them a link that only ends at the sign-in page; the comment above `MyBadge` (`:36`) says it is for every signed-in user because the badge page is also where an attendee links a ticket. Four sit in `NavSection.Admin` with the Organizer role: `Nav.CheckIn` to `CheckInScan` (`:39`, Conference day group, `Order = 1`), `Nav.Attendance` to `OrganizerAttendance` (`:40`, Conference day, `Order = 2`), `Nav.PointsOverview` to `OrganizerPointsOverview` (`:41`, Conference day, `Order = 3`), and `Nav.TicketRoster` to `OrganizerTickets` (`:42`, Attendees and access group, `Order = 1`).
  - `LayoutComponentTypes` (`:45`): `[typeof(LiveEventListener)]`, an invisible component the shell renders on every page; the class summary says it joins the event live channel while the event is live.
  - `Assembly` (`:47`): `typeof(EngagementUIModule).Assembly`, so Blazor's router and component discovery can find this module's routable pages.
- **Why it's built this way**: exposing nav, layout components and the assembly as read-only properties lets the host treat every module identically, and keeping the descriptor beside the routes it points at means adding a page is a two-line change in one project. Note what is deliberately absent: the two self-service QR routes (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:39-40`) and the ticket insights route contribute no nav item, the first because they are reachable only by scanning a printed code, the second because it is reached from the roster page.
- **Where it's used**: registered as a singleton `IUIModule` by [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection-3)'s `AddEngagementUI` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:90`); consumed by the shared shell's `NavMenu` and router. The architecture suite's `PermissionCoverageTests` also reads it.

### DependencyInjection

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:24` · Level 12 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the Engagement UI composition root. One static class exposing an `AddEngagementUI()` extension on `IServiceCollection` that registers every Engagement UI service (bookmarks and their offline replay, reminders, feedback, check-in, points, tickets, lookups, the live layer, notification scoping) plus the [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) descriptor.
- **Depends on**: `IServiceCollection` and `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions` (for `TryAddSingleton`), the Engagement UI service interfaces and implementations, [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice) and [`ISessionLiveUIService`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#isessionliveuiservice) from `.Shared`, the Common offline write queue ([`OfflineWriteQueue`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#offlinewritequeue), [`IOfflineWriteHandler`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritehandler)), and [`IUIModule`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iuimodule) plus [`INotificationScopeProvider`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#inotificationscopeprovider) from the Common UI framework.
- **Concept, `extension(IServiceCollection)` registration.** `[Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]` and `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assess whether a slice owns its own wiring: this is the single place the Engagement UI declares its services, so a host calls `AddEngagementUI()` and stays ignorant of the internals. The C# preview `extension(IServiceCollection services)` block (`DependencyInjection.cs:26`) is the DI-registration idiom used across the codebase (see the primer on [`extension(T)` members](00-primer.md#c-extensiont-types-read-this-once)), which is what lets `AddEngagementUI` read as an instance method on the collection.
- **Walkthrough**: `AddEngagementUI()` (`:32`) registers in labelled groups, all scoped (per circuit) unless noted.
  - Bookmarks (`:34-35`): [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice) to [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice).
  - Offline bookmark toggles (`:37-44`): `AddOfflineWriteQueue()` (`:42`) plus one replay handler per queued kind, [`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler`](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler) and [`BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler`](#bookmarkdeletereplayhandler) (`:43-44`). The comment (`:37-41`) records the scope of the guarantee: the queue is available on any host that registered a device store, and on a Blazor Server circuit the queued writes are kept in the browser's storage through JS interop, so the queue works only while the circuit is up ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)).
  - [`SessionReminderCoordinator`](#sessionremindercoordinator) (`:48`), registered as a concrete type. The comment ([ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html) Wave 2, `:46-47`) records that it keeps local notifications in sync with bookmarks and is a pure no-op on hosts whose local-notification service is unsupported.
  - Feedback (`:50-53`): [`IQuestionLookupService`](#iquestionlookupservice) to [`QuestionLookupService`](#questionlookupservice), [`IEventFeedbackUIService`](#ieventfeedbackuiservice) to [`EventFeedbackService`](#eventfeedbackservice), [`ISessionFeedbackUIService`](#isessionfeedbackuiservice) to [`SessionFeedbackService`](#sessionfeedbackservice).
  - Badge check-in (`:55-57`): [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice) to [`CheckInService`](#checkinservice), the one service behind the attendee badge, both organizer write paths and the attendance rollup.
  - Points (`:59-61`): [`IPointsUIService`](#ipointsuiservice) to [`PointsService`](#pointsservice).
  - Tickets (`:63-65`): [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice) to [`TicketService`](#ticketservice), covering the organizer roster (upload, invites, funnel, delete) and the attendee's own tickets and barcode claim.
  - Cross-module lookups (`:67-69`): [`ISessionLookupService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#isessionlookupservice) to [`SessionLookupService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#sessionlookupservice) and [`IAttendeeLookupService`](#iattendeelookupservice) to [`AttendeeLookupService`](#attendeelookupservice), the two contracts the check-in surfaces use to name sessions and people that other services own.
  - Live layer (`:71-74`): [`ILivePollUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#ilivepolluiservice), [`ILiveEventUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#iliveeventuiservice), [`INowNextService`](#inownextservice); Wave 2 adds [`ISessionQuestionUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#isessionquestionuiservice) and [`ISessionLiveUIService`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#isessionliveuiservice) (`:76-79`).
  - Notification scoping (`:81-87`): `services.TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System)` then a plain `AddScoped<INotificationScopeProvider, CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider>()`. Both lines carry load-bearing comments (`:81-85`): the plain `AddScoped` deliberately **overrides** the null provider that `AddNotificationUI` registers with `TryAddScoped`, so the two calls stay order-independent; and `TimeProvider`, which drives [`CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider`](#currenteventnotificationscopeprovider)'s cache expiry, is a `TryAdd` because `AddOfflineWriteQueue` above (and `AddUIShared` on the heads that call it) already registers the system clock.
  - Module descriptor (`:89-90`): `AddSingleton<IUIModule, EngagementUIModule>()`, a singleton because the descriptor is immutable metadata, while everything else is scoped since it holds per-circuit state.
  - Returns `services` (`:92`) for fluent chaining.
- **Why it's built this way**: one extension method per module UI keeps registration cohesive and lets a host compose modules by convention. The `TryAdd` versus `Add` choices are the part worth reading closely: `TryAdd` where this module is a *fallback* provider (`TimeProvider`), plain `Add` where it must *win* over a framework default (the notification scope provider). `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]`: getting that pair wrong is exactly how the notification bell would silently stop scoping to the current event.
- **Where it's used**: called by the Blazor UI host's startup when the Engagement module is enabled, alongside the other modules' `AddXUI()` calls.

### BookmarkOfflineWrites

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Bookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkOfflineWrites.cs:10` · Level 0 · static class (internal)

- **What it is**: the names the bookmark feature uses on the Common offline write queue: the two write kinds and the coalesce key.
- **Depends on**: the `UserIdentifierType` and `SessionIdentifierType` aliases. Externals: `System.Globalization`.
- **Concept introduced**: the queue itself is taught at [`IOfflineWriteQueue`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritequeue). What these constants carry: a **kind** routes a queued write to its [`IOfflineWriteHandler`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritehandler), and is versioned (`.v1`) because a queued write can outlive an app update; a **coalesce key** names the writes that supersede one another, so one user's toggles of one session collapse to the newest intent.
- **Walkthrough**: `CreateKind = "Engagement.Bookmark.Create.v1"` (`BookmarkOfflineWrites.cs:13`, payload a [`CreateBookmarkRequest`](#createbookmarkrequest)), `DeleteKind = "Engagement.Bookmark.Delete.v1"` (`:16`, payload a [`BookmarkDeletePayload`](#bookmarkdeletepayload)), and `CoalesceKey(userId, sessionId)` (`:22-23`), which formats `bookmark:{userId}:{sessionId}` with the invariant culture. The user is part of the key, so another user's toggle of the same session on a shared device never cancels this user's queued write.
- **Why it's built this way**: the toggle service and both replay handlers must agree on these strings exactly, so they live once ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)).
- **Where it's used**: [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) (`SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:91`, `:197-208`), [`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler`](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler) (`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler.cs:32`), [`BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler`](#bookmarkdeletereplayhandler) (`BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler.cs:27`). The per-user scoping is tested by `Offline_AnotherUsersToggleOfTheSameSession_DoesNotCancelThisUsersQueuedWrite` (`SessionBookmarkSetBookmarkedTests.cs:261`).

### InsightLoadState<T>

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Tickets.Insights` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Tickets/Insights/InsightLoadState.cs:8` · Level 0 · sealed class (internal, generic)

- **What it is**: the load state of one report group on the ticket insights page (UC-56). The roster group (A) and the engagement group (B) each own one, so a slow or failed group never holds back the other (type doc at `InsightLoadState.cs:3-6`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; `T` is the group's report DTO, constrained `where T : class` (`:9`).
- **Concept introduced, a per-region load state with a generation guard.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses how UI state is modelled and kept consistent. Instead of one page-wide `isLoading` flag, each independent region owns a small state machine (loading, loaded, unavailable with a reason, failed and retryable), and `Generation` (`:27`, doc at `:23-26`) lets a load that started under an older selection drop its result, so a slow earlier load never overwrites a newer one.
- **Walkthrough** (`InsightLoadState.cs:8-66`): read-only state `IsLoading` (`:12`, starts `true`), `Failed` (`:15`), `Message` (`:18`), `Value` (`:21`) and `Generation` (`:27`). `Begin()` (`:31-39`) bumps the generation, resets every field to loading and returns the new generation. `Succeed(value)` (`:43-47`), `Unavailable(message)` (`:51-55`, a reason such as the feature being off or the permission revoked) and `Fail()` (`:58-62`, a failure a retry may fix) each end loading with one outcome; `Stop()` (`:65`) ends it with none, for a cancelled load.
- **Where it's used**: [`TicketInsights`](#ticketinsights) holds `_roster` and `_engagement` instances (`TicketInsights.razor.cs:54-55`) and maps each group's [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) onto one in `Apply<T>` (`:206`): success, a 404 as feature-off ([ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html)), a 403 as forbidden, anything else as a failure.

### SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:25` · Level 0 · sealed record (generic)

- **What it is**: the return shape of one self-service check-in post, a sponsor booth visit or a room check-in. It carries the recorded payload, the server's stable error code, or a flag saying the attempt got no definitive answer at all, so the calling page can pick its state without catching an exception.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; it is closed over [`SponsorVisitResultDTO`](#sponsorvisitresultdto) and [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto) at the two call sites, and its `ErrorCode` values come from [`CheckInErrorCodes`](#checkinerrorcodes). Externals: BCL only, with a `where TResult : class` constraint (`SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:26`) so the nullable `Value` means exactly "absent".
- **Concept introduced, the result envelope for a refusal that is not a fault.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` and `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` both apply: the type doc (`SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:3-13`) explains that the landing pages must tell three server answers apart (no session running in this room, event not published, and the flat "unavailable" a disabled feature or unknown target produces), that all three arrive as ordinary non-success responses, and that **two of them share the same 404 status**. A result carrying only a message would force the page to parse localized prose; an exception would force a `try`/`catch` around a normal outcome. Carrying the code as data is what makes the page's mapping a `switch` expression over constants. The envelope also keeps a refusal apart from a non-answer: a rate limit, a timeout, a 5xx, a dropped network or a sign-in that could not be refreshed is not the server saying no, so it travels as `IsTransient` (param doc at `SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:20-24`) and the page offers a Retry instead of telling the attendee the code is not available. Note this is deliberately **not** the framework's [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), which the other four members of the same interface do return: this is a UI-layer transport envelope for one narrow HTTP pattern, so it stays small and local rather than reusing an abstraction whose error vocabulary it does not need.
- **Walkthrough** (`SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:25-29`): three positional members, `Value` (the recorded outcome, null when the server refused), `ErrorCode` (null when the response carried none: a bare feature-gate 404 or an unparseable body, per the param doc at `:16-19`) and `IsTransient`, which defaults to `false` (`:25`) so every refusal construction stays a two-argument call and only the no-answer branches name the flag. One computed member, `IsSuccess => Value is not null` (`:29`), so success is derived from the payload rather than tracked as a further field that could disagree with it. Construction is centralized in [`CheckInService`](#checkinservice)`.PostSelfCheckInAsync` (`CheckInService.cs:172-208`): the success branch deserializes `TResult` and pairs it with a null code (`:178-182`); a 401 still standing after the refresh attempt, or a retryable status still standing after the in-place retries, returns `IsTransient: true` (`:184-187`), as do a transport failure (`:191-194`) and an `HttpClient` timeout, which surfaces as a cancellation the caller never requested (`:195-200`); any other non-success passes null with whatever `ReadErrorCodeAsync` extracted from the RFC 9457 problem body (`:189`, defined at `:393-428`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the four other members on the same service run through `HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync` and answer with a framework [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) (`CheckInService.cs:55-70`, `:108-124`, `:131-146`), because an organizer facing a broken scan wants a typed failure to surface. The two attendee-facing self-service writes must not, because every refusal is a sentence the landing page renders calmly to someone holding a phone in a hallway, and an unanswered attempt is a Retry button rather than a refusal. The method doc records both rules (`CheckInService.cs:155-171`). Keeping the generic on the payload lets one private helper serve both endpoints with no duplication ([ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html)).
- **Where it's used**: returned by [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice)`.RecordSponsorVisitAsync` and `.RecordRoomCheckInAsync` (`ICheckInUIService.cs:58`, `:70`), implemented at `CheckInService.cs:85` and `:97`, consumed by [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit) (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:98`, mapping `IsTransient` to [`VisitState`](#visitstate)`.Transient` at `:112`) and [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin) (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:87`, mapping it to [`CheckInState`](#checkinstate)`.Transient` at `:110`). Page-tested through [`SponsorVisitTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) and [`RoomCheckInTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).

- **What it is**: the Razor component that renders one report cell as text: the count, optionally followed by its rate as a share or an average.

- **Concept introduced**: none new; it is the cell-level formatter for the insights tables. `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` applies: every number is formatted with `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` and the count-plus-rate phrasing comes from resource keys, so word order is the translator's choice, not the code's.

### ICheckInUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/ICheckInUIService.cs:20` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the single UI contract for every QR badge check-in surface: the attendee's own badge, the organizer scan and manual fallback writes, the two attendee self-service scans, and the organizer attendance rollup.
- **Depends on**: [`MyBadgeDTO`](#mybadgedto), [`CheckInAttendeeRequest`](#checkinattendeerequest), [`ManualCheckInRequest`](#manualcheckinrequest), [`CheckInResultDTO`](#checkinresultdto), [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult), [`SponsorVisitResultDTO`](#sponsorvisitresultdto), [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto), [`AttendanceStatsDTO`](#attendancestatsdto), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), and the `SponsorIdentifierType` / `RoomIdentifierType` / `EventIdentifierType` aliases. The UI service abstraction itself is taught on [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice).
- **Concept introduced, two error contracts in one interface.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether a contract's failure semantics are legible from its signatures, and this interface is the clearest example in the module because it deliberately carries **two**. Four methods return a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), the ordinary shape for this module: a refusal is a typed failure the page renders. Two methods return [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult) instead, because those two are the endpoints an attendee reaches by scanning a printed code, and every refusal there has to be told apart by a stable error CODE and rendered as a calm sentence. The type doc states exactly that split (`ICheckInUIService.cs:13-18`). The same two methods are also the only ones whose idempotency key is the caller's to supply, because the page reuses it across its own Retry; the two organizer writes carry a key too, but [`CheckInService`](#checkinservice) mints it internally per check-in (`CheckInService.cs:140-145`). The class doc on [`CheckInService`](#checkinservice) (`CheckInService.cs:16-19`) states the other axis: every call is authenticated, the badge read is caller-scoped ("my badge"), and the three organizer calls are role-gated server-side, so `[Rubric §11, Security]` lives on the server, not in this contract.
- **Walkthrough** (`ICheckInUIService.cs:20-85`):
  - `GetMyBadgeAsync(ct)` (`:27`) fetches the signed-in attendee's own badge credential; an attendee with no badge answers `ErrorType.NotFound`, which the badge page renders as its empty state (`:22-26`).
  - `CheckInByCredentialAsync(request, ct)` (`:34-36`) checks an attendee in from a scanned or typed badge payload; organizer only (`:30`).
  - `ManualCheckInAsync(request, ct)` (`:44-46`) is the fallback used when a badge cannot be scanned; organizer only (`:40`). Both post through the shared `PostCheckInAsync` (`CheckInService.cs:131`), whose doc (`:126-130`) records that a repeat check-in is reported through `AlreadyCheckedIn` rather than as a failure, so there is no conflict branch to interpret.
  - `RecordSponsorVisitAsync(sponsorId, idempotencyKey, ct)` (`:58-61`) records the caller's visit to one sponsor booth; the doc states a repeat visit is a success carrying `AlreadyVisited`, not a failure (`:50`).
  - `RecordRoomCheckInAsync(roomId, checkInCode, idempotencyKey, ct)` (`:71-75`) checks the caller into whatever session the scanned room is hosting right now. The doc sentence at `:64-65` is the whole design of that surface: **the session is never sent**, the server resolves it from the room and the configured grace window, which is why a printed room code never expires when the schedule moves. The nullable `checkInCode` (`:68`) is the room's check-in code the scanned QR carried, if any, and travels in the request body.
  - The `idempotencyKey` on both self-service writes (param docs at `:53-56` and `:69`) is one key per attendee attempt, reused by every retry of it, the page's Retry included, so the server's idempotency filter replays the first answer instead of reporting a second visit. The pages mint it with `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")` (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:77`, `RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:87`), and both server endpoints carry `[Idempotent]` (`CheckInsController.cs:159`, `:194`).
  - `GetAttendanceStatsAsync(eventId, ct)` (`:82-84`) fetches the attendance rollup for one event; organizer only (`:78`, enforced by `[HasPermission]` at `CheckInsController.cs:213`).
- **Why it's built this way**: one interface rather than one per surface keeps the whole check-in vocabulary, and the single `checkins` resource it maps to (`CheckInService.cs:31`), in one reviewable place; the six methods correspond one-for-one to the six endpoints on [`CheckInsController`](#checkinscontroller) ([ADR-071](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/071-barcode-scanning-and-qr-display.html) for the scan surfaces, [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html) for the check-in and points model).
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [`CheckInService`](#checkinservice) (`CheckInService.cs:26`), registered scoped (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:57`), and injected into five pages: [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:26`), [`MyBadge`](#mybadge) (`MyBadge.razor.cs:17`), [`OrganizerAttendance`](#organizerattendance) (`OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:19`), [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin) (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:35`, passing the code it was opened with at `:112`) and [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit) (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:31`). Server-side the whole controller sits behind `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.CheckIn)]` (`CheckInsController.cs:39`) with the two self-service writes gated again individually (`:160`, `:195`), see [`EngagementFeatures`](#engagementfeatures) and [ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html).

### BookmarkApiClient

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Bookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkApiClient.cs:21` · Level 4 · sealed class (internal)

- **What it is**: the three bookmark HTTP calls (read the session-id map, create, delete), shared by [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) and the two offline replay handlers.
- **Depends on**: [`AuthenticatedServiceBase`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#authenticatedservicebase), [`ITokenStorageService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itokenstorageservice), [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), [`ProblemDetailsResultReader`](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), [`IdempotencyHeaders`](group-08-auth.md#idempotencyheaders), [`CreateBookmarkRequest`](#createbookmarkrequest), [`UserSessionBookmarkDTO`](#usersessionbookmarkdto), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`, `System.Net.Http.Json`, `System.Globalization`.
- **Concept introduced, constructed rather than resolved to break a DI cycle.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses, among other things, whether dependencies point the right way and stay intentional. The type doc (`BookmarkApiClient.cs:11-14`) states the constraint: the offline write queue takes the replay handlers in its constructor and the toggle service takes the queue, so a shared registered client would close that circle. Each consumer therefore `new`s its own instance from the factory and token storage it already holds (`SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:43`, `BookmarkCreateReplayHandler.cs:29`, `BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler.cs:24`). The class is `internal`, so the choice stays invisible outside the assembly.
- **Walkthrough** (`BookmarkApiClient.cs:21-100`):
  - `Endpoint = "bookmarks"` (`:24`); `NewCreateKey()` (`:28`) exposes the base class's `NewIdempotencyKey()` so the caller can pick a create's key before the first attempt.
  - `GetSessionIdsAsync(userId, ct)` (`:34-52`) GETs `bookmarks/session-ids?userId=` (invariant formatting) under the shared `RetryPolicy` and reads a `Dictionary<SessionIdentifierType, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>`, so a caller learns both "is it starred" and "which id deletes it".
  - `CreateAsync(request, idempotencyKey, ct)` (`:63-78`) stamps the given key on the per-operation client (`:69`) before the retried POST; the doc (`:54-58`) records the two effects: a retried or replayed create is answered from the server's replay cache (ADR-017), and the key lets the shared retry policy treat the POST as replay-safe.
  - `DeleteAsync(bookmarkId, ct)` (`:84-99`) DELETEs `bookmarks/{id}`; a bookmark that is not there is a `NotFound` failure (`:80`).
- **Why it's built this way**: nothing here throws for a server answer (`:16-18`): responses come through [`ProblemDetailsResultReader`](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader) with the API's `ErrorType` intact, and transport faults become `Http.TransportFailure` failures through [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), which is the code [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice) keys its queue fallback on ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)).
- **Where it's used**: [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice), [`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler`](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler), [`BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler`](#bookmarkdeletereplayhandler).

### CheckInService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/CheckInService.cs:26` · Level 4 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the single HTTP client for every badge and scan surface in the module, implementing [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice) against the `checkins` resource (`CheckInService.cs:31`). It carries six calls with three different audiences: the attendee reading their own badge, the organizer scanning or manually checking someone in, and the attendee self-recording a sponsor booth or room visit. The two self-service writes also carry their own bounded retry, token-refresh replay and caller-supplied idempotency key, because the attendee is standing at the booth or the door when they fire; the two organizer writes carry an internally minted key so a retried scan is replayed rather than counted twice.
- **Depends on**: [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice), [`AuthenticatedServiceBase`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#authenticatedservicebase), [`ITokenStorageService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itokenstorageservice), [`ITokenRefresher`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itokenrefresher) (optional, `CheckInService.cs:29`), [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), [`ProblemDetailsResultReader`](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), [`IdempotencyHeaders`](group-08-auth.md#idempotencyheaders), [`MyBadgeDTO`](#mybadgedto), [`CheckInAttendeeRequest`](#checkinattendeerequest), [`ManualCheckInRequest`](#manualcheckinrequest), [`CheckInResultDTO`](#checkinresultdto), [`SponsorVisitRequest`](#sponsorvisitrequest), [`SponsorVisitResultDTO`](#sponsorvisitresultdto), [`RoomCheckInRequest`](#roomcheckinrequest), [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto), [`AttendanceStatsDTO`](#attendancestatsdto), [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`, `System.Net` (`HttpStatusCode`), `System.Text.Json` (`JsonDocument`), `System.Net.Http.Json` (`JsonContent`, `ReadFromJsonAsync`), `System.Globalization`, and the `System.Threading.Lock` behind the single-flight refresh.
- **Concept introduced, two failure dialects in one client.** The authenticated-HTTP shape is taught at [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient); what is new here is that this class deliberately reports failure two different ways depending on who is looking at the screen. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether a client contract preserves the distinctions the server actually makes. The four organizer and badge calls answer with a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), carrying the server's own error code and type. The two attendee self-service calls do not: they return a [`SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>`](#selfcheckinoutcometresult) carrying only a raw error-code string, because the QR landing pages have to tell "no session is running in this room" from "the owning event is not published" and **both arrive as HTTP 404** (`CheckInService.cs:155-171`, and the outcome record's own doc at `SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:3-13`). A status code alone cannot pick the state, so the code is read out of the problem body and handed to the page. The same doc adds a third answer (`:162-170`): an attempt that got no definitive answer is **not** a refusal. A 408, 409 (the same key still in flight), 429 or 5xx is retried in place, a 401 is refreshed and replayed once, and whatever is still unanswered comes back as `IsTransient`, which the page offers a Retry for; only the caller's own cancellation propagates. `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` is the reason the pages then collapse several of the refusal codes into one message: see [`CheckInState`](#checkinstate) and [`VisitState`](#visitstate).
- **Walkthrough** (public calls first, then the self-service send pipeline)
  - The primary constructor (`:26-29`) takes the factory, the token storage and an optional `ITokenRefresher` defaulting to `null`; the param doc (`:22-25`) records that a host registering no refresher reports a 401 on a self check-in as transient instead of replaying it. `SelfCheckInMaxAttempts = 3` (`:37`, the first send plus two retries, kept small because the page's Retry covers anything longer) and `MaxRetryAfter` of 5 seconds (`:43`) bound the in-place retries. `_refreshSync` and `_refreshInFlight` (`:45-46`) hold the shared refresh, and the internal settable `Delay` delegate (`:52`) lets a test run the retries without waiting out the real delays.
  - `GetMyBadgeAsync` (`:55-70`) GETs `checkins/my-badge`. The comment (`:65-67`) records the contract precisely: a 404 arrives as a `NotFound` **failure** rather than the old `null`, so "this attendee has no badge" stays a distinguishable state while the badge page renders exactly the empty surface it rendered for `null`. The server action is `CheckInsController.GetMyBadgeAsync` (`CheckInsController.cs:64`).
  - `CheckInByCredentialAsync` (`:73-76`) and `ManualCheckInAsync` (`:79-82`) are one-line delegations to `PostCheckInAsync`, differing only in the relative URL: the root `checkins` and `checkins/manual`. Both server endpoints are permission-gated on `EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage` and marked `[Idempotent]` (`CheckInsController.cs:104-105`, `:128-129`), so the client does no role check of its own.
  - `RecordSponsorVisitAsync` (`:85-93`) and `RecordRoomCheckInAsync` (`:96-105`) build their requests inline ([`SponsorVisitRequest`](#sponsorvisitrequest) with the sponsor id; [`RoomCheckInRequest`](#roomcheckinrequest) with the room id and the scanned `CheckInCode`, `:103`) and delegate to `PostSelfCheckInAsync` together with the caller's `idempotencyKey`. Neither call passes an attendee identity: the server takes it from the token, so a scanned code can only ever check in the person holding the phone. Each also has its own feature gate on the server (`CheckInsController.cs:160`, `:195`).
  - `GetAttendanceStatsAsync` (`:108-124`) GETs `checkins/stats?eventId=` with invariant formatting (`:116`) and returns the [`AttendanceStatsDTO`](#attendancestatsdto) rollup; the endpoint is permission-gated the same way as the writes (`CheckInsController.cs:213`).
  - `PostCheckInAsync<TRequest>` (`:131-153`) is the `Result`-returning poster shared by the two organizer writes. Its doc comment (`:126-130`) records why there is no conflict branch: a repeat check-in comes back with `AlreadyCheckedIn` set rather than as a 409, so the caller has one success shape to interpret. It stamps one freshly minted `IdempotencyHeaders.IdempotencyKey` on the per-operation client (`:145`) before the retried POST; the comment (`:140-144`) gives the reason: a scan whose response is lost on the venue network is retried and the server replays the first answer instead of "already checked in", and without a key the retry policy would resend a POST only when it failed before being sent. The key is minted once, outside the retried delegate.
  - `PostSelfCheckInAsync<TRequest, TResult>` (`:172-208`) is the outcome-returning poster, and notably the one path in the class that does **not** go through [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor) or the reader. It rejects a blank key up front (`:179`), sends through `SendSelfCheckInAsync`, and on success reads the payload with `ReadFromJsonAsync` and wraps it (`:185-189`). A 401 or a retryable status that is still standing becomes `IsTransient: true` (`:191-194`); any other non-success becomes `new SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>(null, await ReadErrorCodeAsync(...))` (`:196`), so a refusal is data, not an exception. An `HttpRequestException` (`:198-201`) and an `OperationCanceledException` the caller did not ask for, which is how `HttpClient.Timeout` surfaces (`:202-207`), are both transient too.
  - `SendSelfCheckInAsync` (`:216-243`) runs the retrying send on an authenticated client (`:223-226`) and returns that response unless it is a 401 with a refresher available (`:228-231`). Then it acquires a refreshed token (`:233-237`), disposes the rejected response and replays the write once on a client built with the new token (`:239-242`). The doc (`:210-215`) explains why storage is not simply re-read: the stored token can still look fresh by the client clock after the server rejected it.
  - `SendWithRetriesAsync` (`:250-278`) loops until it gets a definitive answer or runs out of attempts, with the backoff starting at one second (`:258`) and doubling after each wait (`:276`). Only the last attempt lets a transport failure propagate (`throwOnTransportFailure: retriesLeft == 0`, `:263`); earlier ones come back as a null response and wait the current backoff (`:267`).
  - `TrySendOnceAsync` (`:283-308`) builds a fresh `HttpRequestMessage` per attempt, since a sent message cannot be sent again (`:291-297`), and stamps every one with the same `IdempotencyHeaders.IdempotencyKey` header (`:298`).
  - `RetryWait` (`:315-324`) answers null, meaning final, on the last attempt or a non-retryable status, and otherwise prefers the server's `Retry-After` over the backoff; a requested wait past `MaxRetryAfter` also ends the attempt (`:323`) rather than holding the page on its loading state. `IsRetryableStatus` (`:331-334`) is 408, 409, 429, or any 5xx except 501 and 505, and `RetryAfter` (`:337-352`) reads either header form, clamped at zero.
  - `TryAcquireRefreshedTokenAsync` (`:360-374`) is single-flight under `_refreshSync`: two check-ins landing on one rejected token share one rotation, because on MAUI a second rotation presenting the same refresh token is read as reuse and revokes the session (BR-206, per the doc at `:354-359`). Each caller waits on the shared task with its own token (`:373`), while `AcquireRefreshedTokenAsync` (`:376-393`) runs under `CancellationToken.None` (`:380`), so one caller giving up never cancels the refresh for another. A blank token, an `InvalidOperationException` (no JS interop during SSR prerender) or an `HttpRequestException` yields `null` (`:381-392`), which leaves the 401 standing and the outcome transient.
  - `ReadErrorCodeAsync` (`:400-435`) walks the problem body's `errors` array and returns the first element's `code` string (`:417-425`). Everything else yields `null`: an empty body (`:407-408`), a body with no `errors` array (`:411-415`), a non-string code, or a `JsonException` from an HTML error page or a bare challenge (`:429-434`, with the comment naming that case). `null` is a meaningful value here, it is what the pages render as the generic "unavailable" state.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class doc (`:16-19`) sets the rule that every call is authenticated, including the badge read, because the badge is caller-scoped rather than public (`CheckInsController.cs:64`). The split between the two posters is the client-side consequence of a server design decision recorded in [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html): organizer scanning and attendee self-service produce the same domain writes but face very different humans, so the refusal vocabulary is stable ([`CheckInErrorCodes`](#checkinerrorcodes)) and the client passes it through untranslated. Retrying any of the four writes is only safe because every attempt of one operation carries the same key and all four server endpoints are `[Idempotent]` (`CheckInsController.cs:104`, `:128`, `:159`, `:194`): a replayed first answer can never be counted as a second check-in or visit.
- **Where it's used**: registered scoped as [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:57`) and injected by five surfaces: [`MyBadge`](#mybadge) (`MyBadge.razor.cs:17`, called at `:63`), [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:26`, called at `:265`, `:288`), [`OrganizerAttendance`](#organizerattendance) (`OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:19`, called at `:160`), [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin) (`RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:35`, called at `:112`) and [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit) (`SponsorVisit.razor.cs:31`, called at `:98`). The whole controller sits behind the `EngagementFeatures.CheckIn` gate (`CheckInsController.cs:39`), so a deployment with the feature off answers 404 to every one of these calls.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: [`CheckInServiceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) covers mostly the self-service path: response disposal on success and failure (`:39`, `:67`), the idempotency key on both writes (`:88`, `:100`), a 429 honoring `Retry-After` under the same key (`:119`), the bounded retry ending transient (`:139`), a `Retry-After` past the cap (`:154`), the 401 refresh-and-replay and its unrefreshable case (`:167`, `:185`), repeated transport failure and an `HttpClient` timeout (`:200`, `:212`), and caller cancellation propagating (`:223`). Two tests cover the organizer key: a retried organizer check-in resends the same non-empty key (`:241`) and each manual check-in mints a fresh one (`:265`). The badge read and the stats read are exercised indirectly through the bUnit page tests ([`MyBadgeTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), [`CheckInScanTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), [`OrganizerAttendanceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), [`RoomCheckInTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), [`SponsorVisitTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)), which mock the interface rather than the transport. Which error codes a given server build emits is the API's contract, not this file's.

### BookmarkCreateReplayHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Bookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkCreateReplayHandler.cs:24` · Level 9 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the offline write handler that replays a queued bookmark create (kind [`BookmarkOfflineWrites`](#bookmarkofflinewrites)`.CreateKind`) when the device reconnects or the queue retries.
- **Depends on**: [`IOfflineWriteHandler`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritehandler), [`PendingWrite`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#pendingwrite), [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient), [`BookmarkOfflineWrites`](#bookmarkofflinewrites), [`CreateBookmarkRequest`](#createbookmarkrequest), [`UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes`](#usersessionbookmarkerrorcodes), [`SessionReminderCoordinator`](#sessionremindercoordinator), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`.
- **Concept introduced**: the queue and handler contract is taught at [`IOfflineWriteQueue`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritequeue) and [`IOfflineWriteHandler`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritehandler); the toggle-side half is at [`SessionBookmarkUIService`](#sessionbookmarkuiservice). `[Rubric §29, Resilience]` applies: a replay must be safe to run after the original may already have reached the server, and this one is, because it reuses the queued key and treats "already bookmarked" as done.
- **Walkthrough** (`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler.cs:24-54`): it builds its own [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient) (`:29`) and claims `Kind => BookmarkOfflineWrites.CreateKind` (`:32`). `ReplayAsync` (`:35-53`) reads the payload as a [`CreateBookmarkRequest`](#createbookmarkrequest) (`:39`), answering a validation failure `Bookmarks.Replay.InvalidPayload` when it cannot (`:41-42`); posts it with `write.IdempotencyKey` (`:45`), the same key the online attempt used; returns any failure other than `UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.Duplicate` (`:46-49`); and then notifies the reminder layer of the add (`:51`) before succeeding (`:52`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the toggle service picks the create's key before its online attempt and queues the write under that same key, so a POST that reached the server before the connection dropped is answered from the replay cache instead of running twice ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)).
- **Where it's used**: registered through `services.AddOfflineWriteHandler<BookmarkCreateReplayHandler>()` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:43`); registration is asserted by `SessionBookmarkSetBookmarkedTests.AddEngagementUI_RegistersTheOfflineQueue_AndBothBookmarkReplayHandlers` (`SessionBookmarkSetBookmarkedTests.cs:30`).

### BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Bookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler.cs:19` · Level 9 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the offline write handler that replays a queued bookmark removal (kind [`BookmarkOfflineWrites`](#bookmarkofflinewrites)`.DeleteKind`), resolving the bookmark id by session when the queued write did not know it.
- **Depends on**: [`IOfflineWriteHandler`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritehandler), [`PendingWrite`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#pendingwrite), [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient), [`BookmarkOfflineWrites`](#bookmarkofflinewrites), [`BookmarkDeletePayload`](#bookmarkdeletepayload), [`SessionReminderCoordinator`](#sessionremindercoordinator), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`.
- **Concept introduced**: none new beyond [`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler`](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler); the difference is that a delete is idempotent by outcome rather than by key, so it carries no idempotency key and instead treats "not there" as removed.
- **Walkthrough** (`BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler.cs:19-67`): own [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient) (`:24`), `Kind => BookmarkOfflineWrites.DeleteKind` (`:27`). `ReplayAsync` (`:30-66`) reads a [`BookmarkDeletePayload`](#bookmarkdeletepayload) (`:34`, invalid payload at `:36-37`). With no `BookmarkId` (`:40-53`) it reads the session-id map, returns a failed read as a failure (`:44-47`), and takes the id for the session if present (`:49-52`). With an id (`:55-62`) it deletes, returning any failure except `NotFound` (`:58`). Either way it then notifies the reminder layer of the removal (`:64`) and succeeds (`:65`): a session that is not in the map, or a 404, means the bookmark is already gone.
- **Why it's built this way**: a star set by a queued add has no id on the device, and an add then remove while offline coalesces to a single delete; resolving by session on replay is what lets that delete be a clean no-op when the add never reached the server ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html); tested by `Offline_AddThenRemove_LeavesExactlyOneQueuedDelete_ThatReplaysAsANoOpWithoutTheBookmark`, `SessionBookmarkSetBookmarkedTests.cs:232`).
- **Where it's used**: registered through `services.AddOfflineWriteHandler<BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler>()` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:44`).

### SessionBookmarkUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Bookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:36` · Level 9 · sealed class

- **What it is**: a cross-module service implementing [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice), used by the **Conference** UI to read bookmark state and toggle bookmarks inline. Every successful read or mutation also feeds the session-reminder layer, and a toggle that cannot reach the server is kept on the device's offline write queue and replayed later.
- **Depends on**: [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice), [`BookmarkApiClient`](#bookmarkapiclient) (constructed, `:43`), [`ITokenStorageService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itokenstorageservice), [`SessionReminderCoordinator`](#sessionremindercoordinator) (injected as a concrete class, `:39`), [`IOfflineWriteQueue`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#iofflinewritequeue) and [`OfflineWriteOptions`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#offlinewriteoptions), [`IConnectivityStatusService`](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#iconnectivitystatusservice), [`BookmarkOfflineWrites`](#bookmarkofflinewrites), [`BookmarkDeletePayload`](#bookmarkdeletepayload), [`BookmarkWriteOutcome`](#bookmarkwriteoutcome), [`CreateBookmarkRequest`](#createbookmarkrequest), [`UserSessionBookmarkDTO`](#usersessionbookmarkdto), [`UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes`](#usersessionbookmarkerrorcodes), [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor) (for `TransportErrorCode`). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`.
- **Concept introduced, the side effect on the write path, and the offline fallback.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses where derived client state is kept in step with the server. Local session reminders are exactly that kind of derived state: they are only correct if they track the bookmark set, and the bookmark set can change from any page or any device. Putting the reminder calls **inside this one service**, rather than in each component that toggles a bookmark, is what makes that hold regardless of entry point. The ordering is the load-bearing part: HTTP first, reminder only after a confirmed success. The class doc adds the guarantee that makes this safe to read (`:19-24`): nothing here throws for a server answer, the response is read through [`ProblemDetailsResultReader`](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader) with the API's own [`ErrorType`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype) intact and transport faults become failures through [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), so the reminder layer is driven **only** by outcomes the server actually confirmed. `[Rubric §29, Resilience]`: reminder failures are swallowed inside the coordinator, so they never surface to the bookmark caller; and a toggle that never got an answer is not lost, it goes on the Common offline write queue and is replayed by [`BookmarkCreateReplayHandler`](#bookmarkcreatereplayhandler) and [`BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler`](#bookmarkdeletereplayhandler) (`:25-29`). The rule that picks the queue is narrow on purpose: only a request that never got an answer falls back to the queue, a refusal is an answer (`IsTransportFailure`, `:215-217`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `GetBookmarkedSessionIdsAsync` (`:46-60`) reads the map through `BookmarkApiClient.GetSessionIdsAsync` (`:49`), a `Dictionary<SessionIdentifierType, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>`, which is why a page can render a bookmark toggle **and** know the id needed to delete it from one call. A failure is re-wrapped with its original errors and returns early (`:51-54`), so the reminder call is unreachable on that path. On success it calls `reminderCoordinator.ResyncAsync([.. bookmarks.Keys], cancellationToken)` (`:57`) with the comment naming the intent: this response is the authoritative set, so it is the right moment to heal drift caused by another device.
  - `DeleteBookmarkAsync` (`:63-76`) DELETEs by bookmark id and calls `NotifyBookmarkRemovedAsync(sessionId, ...)` only on a confirmed delete (`:70-73`). A 404 is a `NotFound` failure and therefore does **not** notify here.
  - `SetBookmarkedAsync(userId, sessionId, bookmarked, knownBookmarkId, ct)` (`:79-135`) is the toggle, answering a [`BookmarkWriteOutcome`](#bookmarkwriteoutcome). First it cancels any write still queued for the same user and session (`:91`, the newest intent wins and is always issued in full, comment at `:86-90`: a create queued after a transport failure may already have reached the server, so the opposite toggle must still reach it as a remove). It picks the create's idempotency key before any attempt (`:96`, comment at `:93-95`) so a queued retry carries the same key. A device that already knows it is offline queues at once (`:100-103`). Online, an add that succeeds returns `Queued: false` with the new id (`:108-111`); an add that meets `UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.Duplicate` notifies the reminder layer and counts as done with no id (`:113-119`); a transport failure queues, any other failure is returned (`:121-123`). A remove that succeeds returns `Queued: false` (`:126-130`); its transport failure queues likewise (`:132-134`).
  - `CreateOnlineAsync` (`:137-150`) posts the [`CreateBookmarkRequest`](#createbookmarkrequest) with the chosen key and notifies the add only on success (`:144-147`).
  - `RemoveOnlineAsync` (`:157-182`) resolves a missing id through the session-id read (`:166`); a session not in the map is already removed and succeeds (`:172-175`), and a 404 from the delete also counts as success (`:180-181`).
  - `EnqueueAsync` (`:189-213`) queues one complete write under `BookmarkOfflineWrites.CoalesceKey(userId, sessionId)` (`:197`): a create of kind `CreateKind` carrying the chosen key (`:199-203`), or a delete of kind `DeleteKind` carrying a [`BookmarkDeletePayload`](#bookmarkdeletepayload) (`:204-208`). A write the queue refuses comes back as a failure, never as queued (`:210-212`).
  - `IsTransportFailure` (`:215-217`) matches `HttpResultExecutor.TransportErrorCode`; `IsDuplicate` (`:219-221`) matches `UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.Duplicate`.
  - The coordinator members these calls use are `ResyncAsync` (`SessionReminderCoordinator.cs:71`), `NotifyBookmarkAddedAsync` (`:60`) and `NotifyBookmarkRemovedAsync` (`:64`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the class doc (`:13-18`) records both reminder halves: the wiring lives here so reminders track bookmarks no matter which page toggled them ([ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html) Wave 2), and reminder failures never reach the bookmark caller. The offline half follows [ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html); the registration comment (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:37-41`) notes that on a Blazor Server circuit the queued writes live in the browser's storage through JS interop, so the queue works only while the circuit is up. The coordinator is registered scoped alongside this service (`DependencyInjection.cs:48`) and is a no-op on hosts whose local-notification capability is unsupported, which is why a web-only host pays nothing for the reminder coupling.
- **Where it's used**: registered scoped as [`ISessionBookmarkUIService`](#isessionbookmarkuiservice) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:35`); resolved **optionally** by the Conference public pages, which call `ServiceProvider.GetService<ISessionBookmarkUIService>()` and null-check the result ([`PublicSessionList`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionlist) at `PublicSessionList.razor.cs:38`, `:141`; [`SessionBookmarkButton`](group-21-conference-ui.md#sessionbookmarkbutton), the toggle the detail page renders, at `SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:33`, `:56`, calling `SetBookmarkedAsync` at `:122`), passed down as a nullable parameter to [`PublicSessionListView`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionlistview) (`PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:71`, toggling at `:164`, `:186`), and taken by [`PublicSessionBookmarkState`](group-21-conference-ui.md#publicsessionbookmarkstate) (`PublicSessionBookmarkState.cs:15`). That optional resolution is the extraction story in practice: Conference renders correctly in a host where the Engagement UI module is not registered at all. Covered by [`SessionBookmarkUIServiceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (the HTTP contract) and `SessionBookmarkSetBookmarkedTests` (the online and offline toggle paths, `SessionBookmarkSetBookmarkedTests.cs:47-313`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the dependency is on the concrete [`SessionReminderCoordinator`](#sessionremindercoordinator), not an interface, so a test of this service has to construct a real coordinator; the test suite does exactly that, assembling an inert one from mocks (`SessionBookmarkUIServiceTests.cs:180-193`). Whether a reminder is actually scheduled is decided inside the coordinator and [`SessionReminderPlanner`](#sessionreminderplanner), not here.
