### AttendeeLookupService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Lookups` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Lookups/AttendeeLookupService.cs:19` · Level 7 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the HTTP implementation of [`IAttendeeLookupService`](#iattendeelookupservice) over the Identity users roster, served by `POST users/search` (`:25`, Organizer only, BR-51): the generic paged entity contract (filters with their operators, sort, paging) carried in the request body. Search reads straight through to the API with the caller's filters verbatim; the by-identifier lookup is answered from an in-memory roster snapshot this class builds and refreshes itself, up to five pages of 500 sorted by Email (class doc, `:8-18`).
- **Depends on**: [`IAttendeeLookupService`](#iattendeelookupservice), [`AttendeeSummary`](#attendeesummary), the private wire shapes [`SearchBody`](#searchbody), [`SearchFilter`](#searchfilter) and [`AttendeeRow`](#attendeerow), [`AuthenticatedServiceBase`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#authenticatedservicebase), [`ITokenStorageService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itokenstorageservice), [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), [`ProblemDetailsResultReader`](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), [`PagedCollectionResult<T>`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#pagedcollectionresultt). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`, `TimeProvider`, `PostAsJsonAsync` (`System.Net.Http.Json`).
- **Concept introduced, the scoped roster snapshot with single-flight and a negative-cache window.** This is the most stateful class in the group, and each piece of that state answers a specific failure of the naive version. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether repeated work is avoided on a hot path, and the hot path here is real: an organizer scanning badges at a door produces a stream of identifier lookups, many of them for codes the roster does not know. The naive implementation refetched the entire roster on every unrecognised code, which the comment at `:101-102` records as the defect this design fixes. Three mechanisms combine:
  1. **The snapshot** (`_rosterNames`, `:45`), an identifier-to-name map built once per scanning session.
  2. **Single flight** (`_rosterLoad`, `:48`, documented at `:47` as "published so concurrent misses share it instead of stampeding"), so several misses arriving together await one load.
  3. **A negative-cache window** (`RosterRecheckInterval`, 60 seconds, `:41`), so a miss against a fresh snapshot is reported as a genuine unknown instead of triggering a refetch, while a miss against a stale one refetches and lets an attendee who registered mid-conference resolve on a later scan (`:36-40`).

  `[Rubric §14, Testability]` shows in the constructor: `TimeProvider? timeProvider = null` (`:22`) defaulting to `TimeProvider.System` (`:43`) is what makes the 60-second window testable without a real 60-second wait, and [`AttendeeLookupServiceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) uses exactly that with a hand-rolled advanceable clock (`AttendeeLookupServiceTests.cs:54`, `:278`). `[Rubric §19, State Management]` covers the lifetime question: the service is registered **scoped** (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:69`), so the snapshot lives and dies with the Blazor circuit rather than being a process-wide cache of attendee names. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` is the reason search is a POST: a search term is often an attendee's email address, and a body keeps it out of the URL that request telemetry and ingress logs retain (class doc, `:9-12`; see [`SearchBody`](#searchbody)).
- **Walkthrough** (constants, then the two public members, then the loader)
  - The constants encode the sizing decisions: `Endpoint = "users/search"` (`:25`), `RosterPageSize = 500` (`:28`, matching the server's page cap noted as BR-11) and `MaxRosterPages = 5` (`:34`), whose comment (`:30-33`) gives both reasons for the bound, five pages cover 2500 accounts (far above the real attendee count) and a paging bug therefore cannot loop forever.
  - `SearchAsync` (`:53-80`) takes the caller's `filters` bag (a `Dictionary<string, (string Operator, string Value)>`) and delegates the request body to the private static `BuildSearchBody` (`:63`, `:171-195`). That builder copies paging always, the sort column and direction only when non-blank (`null` otherwise), and every filter as a [`SearchFilter`](#searchfilter) carrying its own operator; a value-less operator (is empty, is not empty) travels with a `null` value, and an entry with no operator is dropped (doc, `:166-170`; loop `:179-187`). The operator is part of each filter, so the service does not decide "contains" for the caller. The resulting [`SearchBody`](#searchbody) is posted with `PostAsJsonAsync` inside the base class's `RetryPolicy` (`:67-69`). The response is read as a `PagedCollectionResult<AttendeeRow>` (`:71-72`) and `Map`ped, on success only, into the page of [`AttendeeSummary`](#attendeesummary) rows plus `PaginationMetadata.TotalItemCount` (`:74-78`).
  - `GetDisplayNameAsync` (`:83-120`) is the interesting one, and it reads as four ordered guards. A snapshot hit returns immediately (`:87-90`). Otherwise, if a load is already in flight, the caller awaits **that** task and reads its result rather than starting a second one (`:92-96`). Otherwise, if the snapshot exists and is younger than `RosterRecheckInterval` measured against the injected clock, the miss is answered `null` (`:98-104`), with the comment naming the behavior this replaced. Only past that does it start a load, publish it to `_rosterLoad` (`:106-107`), await it, and stamp `_rosterLoadedAtTicks` (`:110-111`). The `finally` (`:113-117`) clears `_rosterLoad` even on failure, with the comment giving the reason: a failed load must leave the next miss free to retry rather than be told "recently loaded".
  - `LoadRosterAsync` (`:131-164`) pages the roster with `SearchAsync` itself, an empty filter bag (`[]`), 500 rows per page, sorted by `Email` ascending (`:137-143`). The sort is not cosmetic: it is what makes page boundaries stable across the several requests that make up one snapshot, so a row cannot be skipped by shifting between calls. A page the API refuses simply `break`s the loop (`:145-148`), and the doc above says why that is acceptable (`:126-128`): the roster is a naming convenience behind `GetDisplayNameAsync`, whose contract is already "null when the account cannot be named", so a partial snapshot degrades to that answer instead of failing a check-in. The loop also stops early when a page comes back empty or the accumulated count reaches the server's reported total (`:157-160`).
  - `ToSummary` (`:208-209`) and the private wire shapes close the file: [`SearchBody`](#searchbody) (`:198-203`), [`SearchFilter`](#searchfilter) (`:206`) and [`AttendeeRow`](#attendeerow) (`:216-221`), the last deliberately narrower than what the endpoint returns (`:211-215`); its identifier member is `Id`, the name the generic paged row uses.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class doc (`:14-17`) states the split: search straight through with the caller's filters verbatim, by-identifier from a snapshot, and a miss against a snapshot older than `RosterRecheckInterval` refreshes it. That is the same catalog-versus-one-row thinking as [`SessionLookupService`](#sessionlookupservice), here forced by the transport: the by-identifier question is not one the paged search contract asks, so the snapshot exists for that reason rather than because of a performance target. The constants are sized for one conference (about 2500 accounts, at a real observed attendance far below that), not for a general-purpose directory.
- **Where it's used**: [`AttendeeSearchPanel`](#attendeesearchpanel) drives `SearchAsync` from both its data-grid loader (`AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:77`, through its private `SearchAsync` at `:96-103`) and its mobile infinite-scroll loader (`:87`); [`CheckInScan`](#checkinscan) calls `GetDisplayNameAsync` after a scan resolves to an identifier (`CheckInScan.razor.cs:325`). `[Rubric §14, Testability]`: [`AttendeeLookupServiceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) cover the snapshot behaviors, one roster fetch for repeated unknown ids (`AttendeeLookupServiceTests.cs:23`), a known id answered from the snapshot (`:39`), a refetch past the recheck interval that resolves a new attendee (`:54`), concurrent misses sharing one load (`:76`) and the five-page, 500-row, Email-sorted roster read (`:210`), plus the wire contract: filters posted verbatim in the body (`:101`), an email term kept out of the URL (`:133`), the search alias sent beside the column filter (`:155`), a value-less operator sent without a value (`:172`), and rows and total mapped (`:188`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: four things are worth knowing before relying on this class.
  - The `Users/search` endpoint is `[HttpPost("search")]` gated on `IdentityPermissions.UsersRead` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.API/Controllers/UsersController.cs:261-262`, BR-51), so a non-organizer caller gets a `Forbidden` failure out of `SearchAsync`, not an empty list, and `null` out of `GetDisplayNameAsync`.
  - The search is a POST that `RetryPolicy` may re-send. That is harmless only because the search writes nothing, which the server records on the endpoint with a `[NonIdempotent(...)]` attribute whose reason also keeps the page of attendee data out of the replay cache (`UsersController.cs:263`).
  - `MaxRosterPages * RosterPageSize` is a hard 2500-account ceiling on the snapshot. Past it, ids on later pages would never resolve by name, and nothing logs or surfaces that.
  - The single-flight guarantee rests on `_rosterLoad` being assigned (`:107`) before any yield point, with no lock taken and the field neither `volatile` nor interlocked. On the single-threaded Blazor circuit context that holds, and the concurrency test exercises it, but the class is not written to be shared across threads and its scoped registration is what keeps it from being.

### LiveEventContext

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveEventContext.cs:13` · Level 0 · sealed record

- **What it is**: the UI's read-only view of the currently published event's live window: the event id and name, its IANA time zone, and the UTC start/end of the window during which the live layer (polls and session Q&A) is active. It is a `sealed record` with two small behaviors attached, not a bare DTO.
- **Depends on**: `EventIdentifierType` (the Conference module's identifier alias), BCL `DateTime` and `TimeZoneInfo`. No NuGet or first-party service dependencies; this is a pure value.
- **Concept introduced, client-side re-derivation of a server-enforced window.** The doc comment (`LiveEventContext.cs:4`) is explicit that the window uses "the same math the backend enforces": StartDate 00:00 local through EndDate + 1 day 00:00 local, converted to UTC via the event's zone. The UI does not invent its own liveness rule, it mirrors the authoritative one so the ambient [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener) and the [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) page light up at exactly the moment the API would accept a vote. `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses how derived UI state is kept consistent with its source of truth; the record centralizes the "am I live" decision in one value both surfaces call, rather than scattering time-zone arithmetic across components. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` applies mildly: `IsLiveAt` is a pure comparison, so an ambient listener can re-evaluate it without a round trip.
- **Walkthrough**: the primary constructor (`LiveEventContext.cs:13-18`) captures `EventId`, `Name`, `TimeZoneId`, `LiveWindowStartUtc`, and `LiveWindowEndUtc`. `IsLiveAt(DateTime utcNow)` (`:22-23`) returns true when `utcNow` is inside the half-open window: note the inclusive lower bound and the exclusive `< LiveWindowEndUtc` upper bound matching the parameter doc that calls the end "exclusive" (`:12`). `ToEventLocal(DateTime utcNow)` (`:30-31`) converts a UTC instant into the event's local time via `TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeFromUtc` over `TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById(TimeZoneId)`, with no fallback: the doc comment states the id always resolves because [EventInvariants](group-17-conference-domain.md#eventinvariants)`.EnsureTimeZoneIsValid` guards every write path (`:25-28`).
- **Why it's built this way**: making the record own both the window and the "is it live / what is local time" helpers keeps the liveness contract in a single testable value. The conversion trusts the domain invariant instead of defensively catching `TimeZoneNotFoundException`, so an invalid zone is prevented where it is written rather than papered over where it is read.
- **Where it's used**: produced by [LiveEventService](#liveeventservice) from Conference event data; consumed by the [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) page and the ambient [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener) to decide whether to show live surfaces.

### LiveWindowStartTimer

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveWindowStartTimer.cs:12` · Level 0 · sealed class

- **What it is**: a one-shot wait, on the injected `TimeProvider`, for an event's live window to open, so a conference-day page opened before the window starts its live behavior at the moment the window opens instead of waiting for an unrelated re-render (class doc, `LiveWindowStartTimer.cs:3-11`, M267, the M254 pattern of [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener)).
- **Depends on**: BCL only: `TimeProvider`, `ITimer`, `Lock`, `IAsyncDisposable`. The window start it waits for comes from a [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext).
- **Concept introduced, a long wait run as capped steps on an injectable clock.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses whether time-driven UI state changes when the time arrives rather than when something happens to re-render. The class doc names the constraint that shapes the design (`:8-9`): a timer delay above about 49.7 days throws, and the next event can be months away, so the wait runs in steps of at most `MaxStep`, one day (`:15`), and each tick re-reads the clock and re-arms until the window has actually opened. `[Rubric §14, Testability]` applies because every clock read and every timer comes from the `TimeProvider` passed in, so a fake clock can advance across the window start without a real wait.
- **Walkthrough**
  - State (`:17-22`): a `Lock`, the clock, the window start, the callback, the current `ITimer`, and a disposed flag.
  - `ArmUntil(timeProvider, windowStartUtc, onOpened)` (`:36-56`) null-checks both references (`:38-39`) and, under the lock, takes ONE clock read (`:45`) that decides both whether to arm and how long to wait, so the window cannot open between the check and the arm and leave a negative delay (`:43-44`). It is a no-op after disposal, once already armed (`_onOpened` is set), or when the window has already started (`:46-49`). The remarks (`:31-35`) give the caller its ordering rule: call it BEFORE the caller's own "is the window open yet" check, so if the window opens between the two reads either this arms or the later check sees it open.
  - `ArmStep(utcNow)` (`:77-87`), called under the lock, clamps a negative remaining wait to zero (`:80`), disposes any previous timer, and creates a one-shot timer (`Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` period) for the smaller of the remaining wait and `MaxStep` (`:82-86`). The comment (`:75-76`) records why the clamp exists: a negative delay never fires, or throws on a timer thread.
  - `OnTick` (`:89-110`) returns at once after disposal (`:94-97`), re-arms when the clock is still short of the window start (`:99-104`), and otherwise captures the callback under the lock and invokes it outside it (`:106`, `:109`), fire-and-forget from the timer thread.
  - `DisposeAsync` (`:59-73`) sets the disposed flag and detaches the timer under the lock (`:62-67`), then awaits the timer's disposal outside it (`:69-72`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the page already has a render loop; what it lacks is a trigger at a known future instant. A self-contained handle with a single arm and a dispose keeps the stepping, the clamp and the race reasoning out of the page, and the page only states which instant and what to run.
- **Where it's used**: [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) holds one as a field (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/HappeningNow/HappeningNow.razor.cs:67`), arms it with the live event's `LiveWindowStartUtc` and a callback routed through `InvokeAsync` once its sessions load (`HappeningNow.razor.cs:113`), and disposes it in its own `DisposeAsync` (`HappeningNow.razor.cs:366`). Covered by `LiveWindowStartTimerTests` in `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Tests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the callback runs on a timer thread, not the renderer's dispatcher, which is why the page passes `() => InvokeAsync(...)`. The returned task is discarded (`:109`), so a fault in the callback is not observed by this class.

### LiveEventLookup

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveEventLookup.cs:10` · Level 1 · sealed record

- **What it is**: the three-state outcome of resolving the current published event: the read failed, it succeeded with no published event, or it found one (`LiveEventLookup.cs:3-9`). It is what [ILiveEventUIService](#iliveeventuiservice)`.GetCurrentEventAsync` returns.
- **Depends on**: [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext) only.
- **Concept introduced, separating "nothing there" from "could not ask".** `[Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety]` assesses whether a failure state is shown as a failure. The type doc states the split (`:6-8`): a page tells the first two states apart, so an outage shows its load error with Retry instead of the "no published event" state, while the ambient live layer reads only `LiveEvent` and stays dormant on both. `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]` applies because the outage still degrades quietly for the ambient listener; only a page that can offer Retry surfaces it.
- **Walkthrough**: a private constructor (`:12-16`) so the only instances are the three named ones: the static `Failed` (`:19`, `IsFailed` true) and `None` (`:22`) singletons, and `Found(liveEvent)` (`:42-46`), which null-checks its argument (`:44`). `LiveEvent` (`:25`) is the event or `null`; `IsFailed` (`:28`) is the flag. A hand-written `Deconstruct` (`:33-37`) lets a caller unpack both in one statement.
- **Why it's built this way**: a nullable return could not carry the third state, and a full [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) would force every ambient consumer to unwrap a failure it handles identically to absence. A record with two properties keeps the common path (`LiveEvent is null`) unchanged while giving a page the one extra bit it needs.
- **Where it's used**: produced by [LiveEventService](#liveeventservice) (`LiveEventService.cs:27`, `:37`). [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) deconstructs it and sets its load error only when `eventsFailed` (`HappeningNow.razor.cs:103-108`); it also reaches [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener), [CheckInScan](#checkinscan), [OrganizerAttendance](#organizerattendance), [MyTicketsPanel](#myticketspanel), [TicketInsights](#ticketinsights) and [TicketRoster](#ticketroster-1) through the same call, and the UI test suites build it through `Found`, `None` and `Failed`.

- **What it is**: the two-rule validator for the room-QR self check-in request. The room id must be a positive number, and the optional room check-in code, when present, must fit the code length Conference stores.

### SessionLiveUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/SessionLiveUIService.cs:10` · Level 1 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the Engagement-side implementation of the [ISessionLiveUIService](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#isessionliveuiservice) extension point: it maps a session id to the route of that session's Live page, so the Conference session-detail page can light up a Live button only when the Engagement module is enabled.

When Engagement is absent, no implementation is registered and the Live button stays off. `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses whether modules collaborate through boundaries that survive extraction into separate services; this is the UI-layer version of that discipline, a capability advertised only when its owner is running. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` applies through Dependency Inversion: Conference depends on the interface, not on the concrete route builder.
- **Walkthrough**: `GetSessionLivePath(SessionIdentifierType sessionId)` (`SessionLiveUIService.cs:13`) delegates straight to `EngagementRoutePaths.SessionLive(sessionId)` (`:14`). The class is a `sealed` expression-bodied one-liner carrying `/// <inheritdoc />`; all it does is put an Engagement route behind a Conference-visible contract.
- **Why it's built this way**: routing knowledge for the Live page belongs to Engagement, so Engagement owns the string; Conference only needs the abstraction to conditionally render a link.

### ILiveEventUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/ILiveEventUIService.cs:7` · Level 2 · interface

- **What it is**: the UI-facing contract for resolving the current published event and its live window. Two methods: `GetCurrentEventAsync`, returning a three-state [LiveEventLookup](#liveeventlookup), and `GetPublishedEventsAsync`, returning a nullable list of [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext).
- **Depends on**: [LiveEventLookup](#liveeventlookup), [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext) and BCL `Task`/`CancellationToken`.
- **Concept introduced, absence and failure kept apart at a UI boundary, without a `Result`.** The doc comment (`ILiveEventUIService.cs:10-11`) says the current-event read resolves "in three states: the event, no published event, or a failed read (the API is unavailable or unreadable)". Neither state throws: "no live event" is a first-class, expected return that the ambient listener handles by staying dormant, and a failed read is a flag a page can turn into a load error with Retry. Note the contrast with its sibling contracts: [ILivePollUIService](#ilivepolluiservice) and [ISessionQuestionUIService](#isessionquestionuiservice) answer with [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and its error list; this interface carries only the one bit a page needs (`IsFailed`), because no caller acts on why the read failed. The cross-event read, `GetPublishedEventsAsync`, still collapses failure into `null`. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` applies through Dependency Inversion: components depend on this abstraction, not on the HTTP-bound implementation, so tests can substitute a fake. `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses how the UI layer separates data-resolution contracts from rendering; this interface is that boundary for the live layer.
- **Walkthrough**: `Task<LiveEventLookup> GetCurrentEventAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)` (`ILiveEventUIService.cs:14`). The type-level doc names both consumers explicitly, the Happening Now page and the ambient `LiveEventListener` (`:4-5`). `Task<IReadOnlyList<LiveEventContext>?> GetPublishedEventsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)` (`:22`) returns every published event's context (its own time zone and live window) for a caller that spans events, the bookmark reminder planner, so each session is read against its own event rather than the current one; it too answers `null` when the API is unavailable (`:18-20`).
- **Why it's built this way**: a two-method interface is the minimum surface the [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) page, the ambient listener and the cross-event reminder planner need, keeping the contract easy to fake and hard to misuse.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [LiveEventService](#liveeventservice); consumed by [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow), [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener), [CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider](#currenteventnotificationscopeprovider), [SessionReminderCoordinator](#sessionremindercoordinator), [OrganizerEventPicker](#organizereventpicker), [CheckInScan](#checkinscan), [OrganizerAttendance](#organizerattendance), [MyTicketsPanel](#myticketspanel), [TicketInsights](#ticketinsights), and [TicketRoster](#ticketroster-1).

### LiveBroadcastPatch

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveBroadcastPatch.cs:22` · Level 2 · internal static class

- **What it is**: two small helpers that apply a live broadcast payload directly onto a page's in-memory list, patching a poll's tallies or a question's upvote count in place, so the page does not have to refetch from the API to show a fresh count.
- **Depends on**: [`LivePollResultsDTO`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollresultsdto) and [`SessionQuestionDTO`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestiondto) (the two list element types it rewrites) and [`SessionQuestionUpvoteChangedPayload`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionupvotechangedpayload) (the upvote broadcast body). Externals: `System.Text.Json` with `JsonSerializerOptions.Web`.
- **Concept introduced, patch-on-broadcast instead of reload-on-broadcast.** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` and `[Rubric §23, Front-End Performance]` assess whether a real-time surface scales with the number of connected clients. The naive pattern is to treat a broadcast as a "something changed" ping and refetch; the comment at [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow)`.razor.cs:135-137` records what that costs in practice, V votes times C viewers becoming V*C authenticated refetches under burst voting. The broadcasts here already carry the fresh counts (BR-229/BR-238, `LiveBroadcastPatch.cs:10-11`), so the payload is the update, not a notification of one. `[Rubric §19, State Management]` is the discipline that makes it safe: these two helpers are the **only** events treated this way. Every structural event (a poll opened or closed, a question posted or answered) still reloads, so the optimization is confined to counters where a lost update self-corrects on the next broadcast.
- **Concept, the boolean fallback contract.** Both methods return `false` for anything they cannot apply (`:48`, `:52`, `:80`, `:84`), and the caller reloads. That is what keeps the fast path from becoming a correctness risk: an unknown poll id, an unknown question id or an unparsable body all degrade to the behavior the page would have had without the patch at all.
- **Walkthrough**:
  - `TryApplyPollResults(polls, payloadJson, preserveMyVote)` (`:42-68`) deserializes the payload as a [`LivePollResultsDTO`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollresultsdto) (`:46`), finds the matching entry by `PollId` (`:50`), drops the payload as stale when its `TalliedAtTicks` is older than the entry's (`:54-57`), and otherwise replaces the entry in place (`:59-61`). The `preserveMyVote` flag is the subtle parameter and its doc (`:34-40`) is the reason it exists: the broadcast strips per-user data, so an attendee circuit passes `true` and carries the current entry's `MyVoteOptionId` across the patch, or the marker rendering the viewer's own vote would vanish; the projector view passes `false` because it shows no personal vote and a stale marker must not survive into its list.
  - `TryApplyUpvoteCount(questions, payloadJson)` (`:74-100`) is the twin: deserialize [`SessionQuestionUpvoteChangedPayload`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionupvotechangedpayload) (`:78`), find by `Id` (`:82`), apply the same staleness check against a per-list marker (`:86-90`), record the new marker (`:92`), and rewrite only the `UpvoteCount` with a `with` expression (`:93`), leaving every other field of the question untouched.
  - **Out-of-order guard (L206).** Broadcasts are computed at dispatch and enqueued unordered, so a stale count can arrive after a fresher one. Each payload carries `TalliedAtTicks`, the moment its count was read, and one older than the last applied for that poll or question is ignored yet still reported as handled (`return true`), so the caller does not reload (class doc, `:11-17`). A poll keeps its marker on the list entry itself; a question's marker lives in a `ConditionalWeakTable` keyed weakly by the page's question list (`:29`), because `SessionQuestionDTO` carries no marker of its own. A reload replaces the list and so starts clean.
  - Both wrap the work in `try`/`catch (JsonException)` (`:64-67`, `:96-99`), catching the parse failure specifically rather than swallowing everything.
- **Why it's built this way**: `internal static` with no injected state (bar the weak-keyed marker table) is the honest shape. There is nothing to configure and nothing to mock: the input is a list and a string, the output is a bool, and the three pages that use it call it identically. Using `with` expressions on the record DTOs rather than mutating them keeps the list elements immutable values, which is what lets a page compare or re-render without worrying that a background patch aliased an object it already handed to a component.
- **Where it's used**: by the three conference-day pages, each guarding the call with the channel's event name so an unrelated broadcast never reaches it. [SessionLive](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlive) routes both events through one `switch` and reloads on `null` (`SessionLive.razor.cs:192-199`, patching at `:190` and `:192` with `preserveMyVote: true`); [PresenterView](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview) handles them as two early-return branches with `preserveMyVote: false` (`PresenterView.razor.cs:140`, `:127`); [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) patches only poll results and falls back to `ReloadPollsAsync` (`HappeningNow.razor.cs:172`, `:145`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class is `internal`, so nothing outside `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI` can call it, and no dedicated test class for it exists in the repository. Its behavior is exercised only through the pages that call it.

### ILivePollUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/ILivePollUIService.cs:15` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the full UI contract for the live-poll layer: read open polls (event-wide or per session) with tallies and the caller's own vote, cast or change a vote, and drive the organizer lifecycle (create, open, close, delete), plus a session-scoped manage list.
- **Depends on**: [LivePollResultsDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollresultsdto), [LivePollDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolldto), [CreateLivePollRequest](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#createlivepollrequest) (all `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.LivePolls`, imported at `ILivePollUIService.cs:1`), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) (`MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions`, `:2`), and the `LivePollIdentifierType`/`LivePollOptionIdentifierType`/`EventIdentifierType`/`SessionIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept introduced, a Result-typed UI contract: a server refusal is data, not an exception.** The type doc states it outright (`ILivePollUIService.cs:11-12`): "Every member answers with a `Result`: a server refusal is data the page renders, never an exception. Only the caller's own cancellation still propagates." Every one of the ten members returns `Task<Result>` or `Task<Result<T>>`, so a 403 from a poll the caller may not manage, or a 412 from a stale open, arrives as a value a Blazor page can bind to an alert. `[Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety]` assesses whether failure states are renderable rather than fatal; typing the contract on `Result` removes the try/catch from every consuming page. A second idea also appears here, **two result shapes for two audiences**: read-and-vote methods return [LivePollResultsDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollresultsdto) (tallies plus the caller's own vote) while the manage views return the richer [LivePollDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolldto). `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` covers that fit-the-shape-to-the-consumer split. `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies through the explicit note that manage operations require `engagement:live:manage` and that "the API enforces this regardless of what the UI renders" (`:8-9`): the UI contract never pretends to be the security boundary.
- **Walkthrough**: attendee and reader path: `GetOpenPollsAsync` (`ILivePollUIService.cs:18`), `GetOpenSessionPollsAsync` (`:21`), `GetResultsAsync` (`:24`), `CastVoteAsync` (`:27`, which returns the fresh tallies so a vote needs no follow-up read). Manage path: `GetEventPollsAsync` (`:30`, ALL polls of an event) and `GetSessionManagePollsAsync` (`:36`), whose doc records that the session list is "open to the session's assigned speakers as well as organizers (BR-236), unlike the event-wide manage list" (`:33-34`). Lifecycle: `CreateAsync` (`:39`, creates as Draft), `OpenAsync` (`:42`) and `CloseAsync` (`:45`), each taking a `byte[] rowVersion` alongside the id, and `DeleteAsync` (`:48`, "must not be Open"). The `rowVersion` parameter on the two transitions is the optimistic-concurrency token of [ADR-035](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/035-optimistic-concurrency.html): the caller must state which version of the poll it saw. Every method takes a trailing `CancellationToken`.
- **Why it's built this way**: grouping the whole poll lifecycle behind one interface lets the various poll surfaces ([HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow), [SessionLive](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlive), [SessionLiveModerationPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivemoderationpanel), [PresenterView](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview)) inject a single dependency and lets tests fake it wholesale, while the `Result` return type keeps every one of those pages free of HTTP error handling.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [LivePollUIService](#livepolluiservice); consumed by the live-poll Blazor pages and panels.

### ISessionQuestionUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/ISessionQuestionUIService.cs:15` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the UI contract for the session Q&A layer: attendees read approved questions and submit their own, moderators work a queue (approve / dismiss / mark-answered), and anyone can upvote or remove an upvote.
- **Depends on**: [SessionQuestionDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestiondto) and [SubmitQuestionRequest](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#submitquestionrequest) (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.SessionQuestions`, imported at `ISessionQuestionUIService.cs:1`), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), and the `SessionIdentifierType`/`SessionQuestionIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept introduced, two views of the same queue.** `GetQuestionsAsync` (`ISessionQuestionUIService.cs:18`) returns the attendee view (every approved question plus the caller's own pending/dismissed ones), while `GetModerationQueueAsync` (`:21`) returns all statuses with Pending first. The same two disciplines as its poll sibling appear verbatim: every member answers with a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and only caller cancellation propagates (`:11-12`), and moderation needs organizer/admin or an assigned-speaker claim with "the API enforces this regardless of what the UI renders (BR-236)" (`:8-9`). `[Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety]` assesses how submission and moderation flows are shaped; the split read methods keep an attendee from seeing another attendee's un-approved question while giving moderators the full picture. `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies through the server-authoritative moderation note.
- **Walkthrough**: reads: `GetQuestionsAsync` (`:18`), `GetModerationQueueAsync` (`:21`). Submit: `SubmitAsync` (`:24`), whose doc notes the question "starts at the event's moderation default (BR-233)". Moderation: `ApproveAsync` (`:27`), `DismissAsync` (`:30`), `MarkAnsweredAsync` (`:33`), each taking `(SessionQuestionIdentifierType id, byte[] rowVersion, CancellationToken)` so the write is conditional on the version the moderator saw ([ADR-035](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/035-optimistic-concurrency.html)) and two moderators racing cannot silently overwrite each other. Upvoting: `UpvoteAsync` (`:36`) and `RemoveUpvoteAsync` (`:39`), each returning `Result<int>`, the fresh upvote count, so the button can re-render from the response.
- **Why it's built this way**: one interface spans attendee, moderator, and voter roles so a session Live page injects a single service; the API remains the enforcer, so the contract can expose the moderation methods without granting rights. Returning the count from the upvote verbs saves a follow-up read on the hottest interaction in the room.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [SessionQuestionUIService](#sessionquestionuiservice); consumed by [SessionLive](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlive), [SessionLiveModerationPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivemoderationpanel), [SessionLiveQuestionPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivequestionpanel), and [PresenterView](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview).

### LivePollUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LivePollUIService.cs:14` · Level 4 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the HTTP implementation of [ILivePollUIService](#ilivepolluiservice), calling the Gateway's `/LivePolls` routes with an authenticated client, a retry pipeline, and Problem-Details-to-`Result` translation.
- **Depends on**: [AuthenticatedServiceBase](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#authenticatedservicebase) (base class supplying `CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync`, `RetryPolicy`, and `NewIdempotencyKey`), [HttpResultExecutor](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor) and [ProblemDetailsResultReader](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), [ConcurrencyETag](group-08-auth.md#concurrencyetag) and [IdempotencyHeaders](group-08-auth.md#idempotencyheaders) (`MMCA.Common.Shared.Http`), [ILivePollUIService](#ilivepolluiservice) and the poll DTO/request records, plus `IHttpClientFactory` and [ITokenStorageService](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itokenstorageservice) (`LivePollUIService.cs:14-16`).
- **Concept introduced, the two-halves translation of an HTTP call into a `Result`.** Every method here has the same skeleton: the body is wrapped in `HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync(..., cancellationToken)` and ends in a `ProblemDetailsResultReader.ReadAsync` call. Those two do complementary jobs: the reader converts a *response* (an RFC 9457 Problem Details body from the API back into the original [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error) list, preserving [ErrorType](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype)), and the executor converts the *absence* of a response (a refused connection, DNS failure, dropped socket, or `HttpClient` timeout) into a transport failure, while rethrowing an `OperationCanceledException` that the caller's own token caused. Together they are what makes the `Result`-typed contract in [ILivePollUIService](#ilivepolluiservice) honest. Between them sits `RetryPolicy.ExecuteAsync` from the base. `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]` assesses whether resilience and error translation are applied uniformly; every method here gets all three for free by construction. `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` applies because each call acquires a bearer-token-bearing client via `CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync`.
- **Walkthrough**: `Endpoint = "livepolls"` (`LivePollUIService.cs:18`). Reads: `GetOpenPollsAsync` (`:21`) GETs `livepolls/open?eventId=` built with `string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...)` (`:29`), and `read.Map(...)` widens `List<LivePollResultsDTO>` to `IReadOnlyList<...>` (`:35`); `GetOpenSessionPollsAsync` (`:40`) is the same call keyed by `sessionId` (`:48`); `GetResultsAsync` (`:59`) GETs `livepolls/{pollId}/results` (`:67`); `GetEventPollsAsync` (`:105`) GETs `livepolls?eventId=` (`:113`) and `GetSessionManagePollsAsync` (`:124`) GETs `livepolls/manage?sessionId=` (`:132`), both returning [LivePollDTO](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepolldto) lists. The two creating writes carry an idempotency key as a default header on the per-operation client: `CastVoteAsync` (`:77`) adds `IdempotencyHeaders.IdempotencyKey` with `NewIdempotencyKey()` (`:92`) then POSTs a [CastVoteRequest](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#castvoterequest) (`:94`) to `livepolls/{pollId}/votes` (`:97`), and `CreateAsync` (`:143`) does the same (`:155`) before POSTing the [CreateLivePollRequest](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#createlivepollrequest) (`:158-159`). The long comments at `:86-91` and `:151-154` explain the placement precisely: the key is minted ONCE outside the retry pipeline, because generating it inside the retried delegate would give every attempt a fresh key and leave the server nothing to deduplicate on, turning a retried vote into a second write. Lifecycle: `OpenAsync` (`:167`) and `CloseAsync` (`:171`) both delegate to `PostLifecycleAsync(pollId, action, rowVersion, ...)` (`:189`), which formats the row version with `ConcurrencyETag.Format` (`:196`) and mints one idempotency key per logical transition, also outside the retried delegate (`:201`): the open and close endpoints are `[Idempotent]`, so a retry after a lost response replays the stored answer rather than failing its own precondition (`:198-200`). Per attempt it then builds a fresh `HttpRequestMessage` carrying both `ConcurrencyETag.IfMatchHeaderName` and that same key (`:209-211`), because a sent request message cannot be re-sent by the retry pipeline (`:203-205`); a stale-view open or close answers 412 Precondition Failed. `DeleteAsync` (`:175`) DELETEs `livepolls/{pollId}` (`:182`) with neither a precondition nor a key.
- **Why it's built this way**: the public methods are expression-bodied and return the `HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync` task directly rather than awaiting it, since there is no continuation to run after it. Folding the repeated client / retry / read ceremony into shared helpers keeps each method down to its URL and payload, so the class reads as a faithful map of the interface onto REST routes. The idempotency-key and If-Match placements are the two spots where that ceremony genuinely matters, and both carry an in-code explanation so a later edit does not quietly move them inside the retry delegate ([ADR-035](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/035-optimistic-concurrency.html), [ADR-021](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/021-consumer-inbox-idempotency.html)).
- **Where it's used**: registered as the `ILivePollUIService` in the Engagement UI module; injected into [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow), [SessionLivePollPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivepollpanel), [SessionLiveModerationPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivemoderationpanel), and [PresenterView](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview).

### SessionQuestionUIService

- **What it is**: the HTTP implementation of [ISessionQuestionUIService](#isessionquestionuiservice), calling the Gateway's `/SessionQuestions` routes with the same executor + retry + reader shape as [LivePollUIService](#livepolluiservice).

What differs is the count-returning upvote pair and the moderation helper. `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]` and `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` apply for the same inherited-resilience and token-flow reasons as its poll sibling.
- **Walkthrough**: `Endpoint = "sessionquestions"` (`SessionQuestionUIService.cs:18`). Reads: `GetQuestionsAsync` (`:21`) GETs `sessionquestions?sessionId=` (`:29`) and `GetModerationQueueAsync` (`:40`) GETs `sessionquestions/moderation?sessionId=` (`:48`), each widening the deserialized `List<SessionQuestionDTO>` via `read.Map` (`:35`, `:54`). `SubmitAsync` (`:59`) mints an idempotency key outside the retry pipeline (`:72`) before POSTing the [SubmitQuestionRequest](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#submitquestionrequest) (`:75-76`); the comment (`:67-71`) names the concrete failure it prevents, an attendee whose submit times out over conference wifi posting the same question twice. Moderation: `ApproveAsync` (`:84`), `DismissAsync` (`:88`), and `MarkAnsweredAsync` (`:92`) each delegate to `PostModerationAsync(id, action, rowVersion, ...)` (`:129`) with the action strings `"approve"`, `"dismiss"`, and `"answered"`; that helper formats `ConcurrencyETag.Format(rowVersion)` (`:136`), mints one idempotency key per logical transition outside the retried delegate (`:141`), because the endpoints are `[Idempotent]` and a retry after a lost response should replay the stored answer rather than fail its own precondition (`:138-140`), and builds a fresh `HttpRequestMessage` per attempt carrying `If-Match` and that key (`:149-151`), so "two moderators racing surface as 412 Precondition Failed" (`:144`). Upvotes: `UpvoteAsync` (`:96`) adds a per-click idempotency key as a default header (`:104`), since the upvote endpoint is `[Idempotent]` and a retry after a lost response then replays the count instead of being skipped (`:102-103`), and POSTs `sessionquestions/{id}/upvotes` with a null body (`:107`); `RemoveUpvoteAsync` (`:115`) DELETEs the same route (`:122`) with no key. Both deserialize the fresh count with `ProblemDetailsResultReader.ReadAsync<int>` (`:110`, `:125`), and neither carries a precondition.
- **Why it's built this way**: like its poll sibling, the public methods return the `HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync` task directly instead of awaiting it. One private helper (`PostModerationAsync`) collapses the repeated conditional-POST ceremony for the three moderation verbs, leaving each public method to state only its action string. Every POST carries an idempotency key minted once per logical operation (submit, upvote, the three moderation verbs), the moderation verbs add If-Match on top, and the remove-upvote DELETE carries neither; in each case the key lives outside the retried delegate so every attempt shares it.
- **Where it's used**: registered as `ISessionQuestionUIService`; consumed by [SessionLive](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlive), [SessionLiveModerationPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivemoderationpanel), [SessionLiveQuestionPanel](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlivequestionpanel), and [PresenterView](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview).

### LiveChannelSubscription

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveChannelSubscription.cs:16` · Level 5 · sealed class

- **What it is**: a join-once / leave-once handle for one live notification channel, held as a field by the conference-day pages that listen for real-time events. It owns the two pieces of state and the join and leave sequences those pages used to repeat inline, so a page states only which channel it wants and what to do with an event (class doc, `:5-9`).
- **Depends on**: [`NotificationHubService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#notificationhubservice) (`:1`, passed in per join rather than injected). Externals: `IAsyncDisposable`, `IDisposable`, `GC.SuppressFinalize`.
- **Concept introduced, the component-owned resource handle.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses where transient client state lives and who is responsible for tearing it down. The remarks block (`:11-14`) is the whole design in three sentences: this is **not** a DI service. A page `new`s one up as a field, so the handle's lifetime is the component's, nothing has to be registered or scoped, and disposal is a no-op for a handle that never joined. Compare that with the alternative of a scoped service tracking channel membership: it would outlive the component and would have to be told when the component went away. Here the component's own `DisposeAsync` is the only teardown signal needed, and `LeaveAsync` covers the one case where a component outlives its channel. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`: two pages held the identical field pair and repeated the same three-step join and two-step leave; folding that into one type means a change to the join protocol happens once.
- **Walkthrough**
  - The four fields (`:18-21`) are the hub service, the handler subscription token, the optional connection-restored subscription token, and the channel key. All are nullable and all are set and cleared together.
  - `IsJoined` (`:27`) reports simply whether `_channelKey` is non-null. Its doc (`:23-26`) names the exact job it does: the pages call it as the already-joined guard inside `OnAfterRenderAsync`, which is deliberately **not** `firstRender`-gated (BR-229 / BR-238). See [`HappeningNow`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) at `HappeningNow.razor.cs:144`, [`SessionLive`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlive) at `SessionLive.razor.cs:200` and [`PresenterView`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview) at `PresenterView.razor.cs:159` for the guard in place.
  - `JoinAsync(hubService, channelKey, handler, resync = null)` (`:43-61`, not `async`) null-checks the hub service (`:49`), returns `Task.CompletedTask` early when a key is already recorded so a second call is a no-op (`:51-54`), then assigns the fields and subscribes the handler through `OnChannelEvent` (`:56-58`) **before** returning the `JoinChannelAsync` task (`:60`). The ordering is the load-bearing part and the doc says why (`:30-32`): the key is recorded before the join is awaited, so `IsJoined` already answers true for any render that interleaves with the in-flight join. Without that, a render landing mid-join would see `false` and start a second join.
  - The optional `resync` callback (`:37-42`) is subscribed through the hub's `OnConnectionRestored` only when one is passed (`:59`). Its doc gives the reason it exists: SignalR delivers nothing that was sent while the connection was down, so a page passes a re-read of what it shows live, run once for each restored connection. It runs off the renderer's dispatcher, so a page routes its reload through `InvokeAsync`, and the hub isolates and logs one that throws. `[Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]` applies: a dropped conference-wifi connection self-heals the page's live state instead of leaving it silently stale.
  - `LeaveAsync` (`:70-88`) captures the service and key locally, then disposes both subscriptions and nulls all four fields **before** awaiting (`:77-82`), so `IsJoined` already answers false for any render that interleaves with the leave and a restored connection no longer runs the old channel's re-read. It calls `LeaveChannelAsync` only when both service and key were present (`:84-87`). That returns the handle to its never-joined state so `JoinAsync` can attach it to another channel: a routed page Blazor reuses across a route-parameter change (one session's Live page to another's) leaves the old channel here before joining the new one. A no-op for a handle that is not joined.
  - `DisposeAsync` (`:91-96`) is just `await LeaveAsync()` followed by `GC.SuppressFinalize` (`:95`). A handle that never joined therefore disposes cleanly with no hub traffic.
- **Why it's built this way**: real-time listening on a Blazor page is a resource with a strict pairing (subscribe and join on the way in, unsubscribe and leave on the way out) that the render loop can interleave with. Making the handle a plain field with an idempotent join and an idempotent dispose puts both halves in one place a reader can check at a glance.
- **Where it's used**: [`HappeningNow`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow) holds one for the **event** channel (`HappeningNow.razor.cs:58`, joined at `:156-158` via `LivePollChannel.ForEvent`, disposed at `:371`), and [`SessionLive`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionlive) (`SessionLive.razor.cs:72`, joined at `:207-209`, disposed at `:395`) and [`PresenterView`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#presenterview) (`PresenterView.razor.cs:59`, joined at `:166-168`, disposed at `:261`) each hold one for the **session** channel via `LivePollChannel.ForSession`. All three guard the join with `RendererInfo.IsInteractive` as well, which keeps the prerender pass and the bUnit suite off the hub (`HappeningNow.razor.cs:144`). The `resync` path is covered by `LiveChannelResyncTests` in `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Tests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class is not thread-safe. `JoinAsync` reads and writes `_channelKey` around an await with no lock, which holds on the single-threaded Blazor circuit context the pages run on and is not written to be shared beyond it. Unlike earlier shapes, leaving is no longer only disposal: `LeaveAsync` is public, so one handle can move from channel to channel.

### LiveEventService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.SessionLive` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveEventService.cs:17` · Level 9 · sealed class

- **What it is**: the implementation of [ILiveEventUIService](#iliveeventuiservice): it fetches the live, else next, else most recently ended published event from the Conference API and computes its live window into a [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext), answering a [LiveEventLookup](#liveeventlookup) that keeps "no published event" apart from "the API is down" (type doc, `LiveEventService.cs:8-16`).
- **Depends on**: [ILiveEventUIService](#iliveeventuiservice), [LiveEventLookup](#liveeventlookup), [CurrentEventSelector](group-17-conference-domain.md#currenteventselector) (the shared selection plus window math), [EventDTO](group-17-conference-domain.md#eventdto) and [PagedCollectionResult&lt;T&gt;](group-01-result-error-handling.md#pagedcollectionresultt), [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext), and the two primary-constructor dependencies `IHttpClientFactory` and `TimeProvider` (`LiveEventService.cs:17`). For the read it composes [HttpResultExecutor](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), `IdempotentReadRetry` and [ProblemDetailsResultReader](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), the same read composition as its sibling [SessionLookupService](#sessionlookupservice) (`:51-53`). It uses the plain `"APIClient"` (`:57`), not the authenticated base: the published-events read is public.
- **Concept introduced, fail-soft resolution that still names the failure.** The read is internally `Result`-shaped (the executor turns every fault into a failed [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result)), and the public contract reduces that to one flag rather than an error list: the type doc states that any "transport, payload or timeout failure (a captive portal answering 200 with HTML, a dropped body, the client timeout) degrades to `LiveEventLookup.Failed`, never an exception, so the live layer simply stays dormant while a page can still tell the outage apart from "no published event"; only the caller's own cancellation propagates" (`LiveEventService.cs:12-15`). `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses graceful degradation under a dependency outage; here an unavailable Conference API turns the ambient live layer off instead of erroring a page, and a page that can retry shows its load error with Retry (`:25-26`). `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` applies because the same public, output-cached events read backs this call. The cross-event `GetPublishedEventsAsync` keeps the older shape: failure is `null`, indistinguishable at the call site from nothing to plan.
- **Walkthrough**: both public methods share one private read, `ReadPublishedEventsAsync` (`:49`), which returns the published `EventDTO` list or `null` when the read failed. It wraps the call in `HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync(..., cancellationToken)` (`:54-66`); inside the delegate it creates the `"APIClient"` (`:57`), issues `IdempotentReadRetry.GetAsync` against the relative URI `events?includeFKs=false&includeChildren=false` (`:58-61`), and reads the response with `ProblemDetailsResultReader.ReadAsync<PagedCollectionResult<EventDTO>>` (`:63-64`). When `read.TryGetValue(out var wrapper)` succeeds it returns the published subset as a list via a null-safe `wrapper?.Items?.Where(e => e.IsPublished) ?? []` (`:68-70`), otherwise `null`. `GetCurrentEventAsync` (`:20-38`) returns `LiveEventLookup.Failed` when the read is `null` (`:23-28`), else hands `CurrentEventSelector.SelectCurrentOrNext` that list with accessor lambdas for start date, end date, and time zone (`:30-34`) and the injected clock's `timeProvider.GetUtcNow().UtcDateTime` (`:35`), so a test can pin "now" with a fake `TimeProvider`; a null selection returns `LiveEventLookup.None`, a hit returns `LiveEventLookup.Found(ToContext(...))` (`:37`). `GetPublishedEventsAsync` (`:41-45`) maps every published event through `ToContext` into a list, or `null` when the read failed, which is what lets the bookmark reminder planner read each session against its own event. The static `ToContext` (`:73-84`) computes `(startUtc, endUtc)` from `CurrentEventSelector.GetLiveWindowUtc(StartDate, EndDate, TimeZone)` (`:75-76`) and constructs the [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext) from the event id, name, time zone, and window (`:78-83`). There is no `try`/`catch` in the class: the executor, not this file, names the fault set.
- **Why it's built this way**: delegating both "which event" and "what window" to [CurrentEventSelector](group-17-conference-domain.md#currenteventselector) means the UI and the API share one implementation of the conference-day math, which is what lets [LiveEventContext](#liveeventcontext) claim to mirror the backend window exactly. Returning `Failed` and `None` as distinct values keeps the ambient listener silent in both cases while letting a page offer Retry only when retrying could help.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the call comment names the executor's fault set as "transport, JSON, IO, client timeout" (`:51-53`), but the executor's own internals are not in this file; see [HttpResultExecutor](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor). Only the caller's cancellation propagates, so a page's lifecycle method never sees a read failure from this service.
- **Where it's used**: registered as `ILiveEventUIService`; consumed by [HappeningNow](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#happeningnow), the ambient [LiveEventListener](#liveeventlistener), [CheckInScan](#checkinscan), [OrganizerAttendance](#organizerattendance), [MyTicketsPanel](#myticketspanel), [TicketInsights](#ticketinsights), and [TicketRoster](#ticketroster-1); the Conference UI's `EventLookupService` also references it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Events/EventLookupService.cs`).

### RecordRoomCheckInHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.RecordRoomCheckIn` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/RecordRoomCheckIn/RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:44` · Level 12 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the attendee-facing self check-in from a room's printed QR. The request names a room; the SERVER decides which session that room is hosting right now and records a session check-in for the caller.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) and its [RoomSessionInfo](group-17-conference-domain.md#roomsessioninfo) result, [ICurrentUserService](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice), [CheckInSettings](#checkinsettings) and `PointsSettings` via `IOptions<T>`, `SessionTimeSlotPoints` (called statically), [ErasedUserGuard](group-22-engagement-module.md#eraseduserguard), [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), [CheckIn](#checkin), [RoomCheckInResultDTO](#roomcheckinresultdto), [ICommandHandler&lt;in TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult); externals: `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>`.
- **Concept introduced, server-side resolution as the anti-abuse property.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` (assesses whether authority for a decision sits with the party that can be trusted with it) and `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` in passing. The class doc states the property (`RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:19-43`): because only the room travels in the request, a shared room link records nothing outside the session's window, and nobody can name a session they are not standing in. Worth contrasting with the organizer paths, where the client does send a session id: there the caller is a trusted organizer, here the caller is the beneficiary of the write. The second teachable point is the answer-shape rule in `MapRoomLookupFailure` (`:136-156`): an unknown room and a room with nothing scheduled deliberately produce the SAME attendee-facing error, because distinguishing them would leak which room ids exist. Transport-level failures still propagate unchanged, so a Conference outage is not misreported as an empty schedule. The third is proof of presence: a room that has a check-in code requires the scan to carry the current one, so a QR printed before the organizer rotated the code, or a room id typed in by hand, records nothing and sends the attendee back to the door code (`:138-141`).
- **Walkthrough**: seven constructor dependencies (`:44-51`, including `IOptions<PointsSettings>`), one `HandleAsync` (`:54-134`).
  - Caller identity from the token, never the request (`:60-64`): `RequireUserId("CheckIns.Forbidden")`, the same guard the organizer handlers use.
  - Erased-account guard (`:66-69`, L207): [ErasedUserGuard](group-22-engagement-module.md#eraseduserguard)`.EnsureNotErasedAsync` refuses an erased account's still-valid token, so no check-in is left under its id.
  - Cross-module resolution (`:74-76`): `GetCurrentRoomSessionInfoAsync(command.RoomId, command.CheckInCode, settings.Value.RoomCheckInGraceMinutes, ...)`. The scanned code travels to Conference, which owns the room's current code and answers the comparison. The grace window travels in the call rather than living in Conference because it is this module's policy (`:71-73`); its default is 15 minutes (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInSettings.cs:21`), and the setting's own doc (`CheckInSettings.cs:16-20`) explains that a zero-grace window would reject the entire pre-session queue.
  - Failure triage (`:77-78`): the result is unwrapped with `if (!sessionInfo.TryGetValue(out var current))`, so the success path holds the resolved `current` without a `Value!` dereference, and every failure goes through `MapRoomLookupFailure` (`:150-156`). An error whose code is Conference's `RoomCheckInCodeDTO.RejectedErrorCode` (`"Room.CheckInCodeRejected"`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Rooms/RoomCheckInCodeDTO.cs:24`) becomes this module's `RoomCodeRejected()` validation error (`:152-153`, defined at `:158-162` with code `CheckInErrorCodes.RoomCodeRejected`, target `CheckInCode`); otherwise a `NotFound` collapses to the shared `NoCurrentSession()` error (`:155`, defined at `:164-168` with code `CheckInErrorCodes.NoCurrentSession`); anything else is passed through verbatim. Both codes are constants on [CheckInErrorCodes](#checkinerrorcodes) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInErrorCodes.cs:16`, `:22`).
  - Published gate (`:80-81`): an unpublished event fails even when a session resolves, and the failure is the processor's shared `EventNotPublished(...)` with this handler named as the source (`CheckInProcessor.cs:29-33`), so the error still points at the entry point the caller used.
  - Points eligibility (`:85-104`), asked before the write. `pointsSettings.Value.GetPointsFor(PointsActivityType.SessionCheckIn) <= 0` sets `pointsPaused` (`:88`), the awarder's own per-rule kill switch, so a paused rule never promises an award. Only when points are live does it call `SessionTimeSlotPoints.HasEarlierOverlappingCheckInAsync` (`:92-99`); a failure there fails closed and nothing is written (`:100-101`), and `earnsPoints = !earlierInSlot.Value` (`:103`) reflects the once-per-time-slot rule. This also lets an attendee already checked in to another, overlapping session switch rooms without staff: the check-in is still recorded here.
  - The write goes through `CheckInProcessor.RecordAsync` (`:108-117`) with `CheckInScope.Session`, the event id Conference reported, `sponsorId: null`, and `checkedInByUserId: userId`. That last argument is the only field that distinguishes a self check-in from a door scan (`:27-28`), which is what keeps the two operationally separable while everything downstream (points award, attendance rollup, export posture) treats them identically. Idempotency lives inside `RecordAsync`: it looks for an existing row on the same scope-specific predicate the organizer paths use (`CheckInProcessor.cs:200-219`) and, when it finds one, returns `AlreadyRecorded: true` with the ORIGINAL `CheckedInOn` rather than writing again (`CheckInProcessor.cs:73-77`).
  - The response (`:125-133`) carries the session title Conference returned plus `AlreadyCheckedIn` and `CheckedInOn` from the outcome, and `EarnsPoints` and `PointsPaused` (`:131-132`); the Information log fires only on a genuinely new row (`:122-123`). `timeProvider.GetUtcNow()` supplies the timestamp inside the processor (`CheckInProcessor.cs:85`), so the flow is testable without wall-clock dependence (`[Rubric §14, Testability]`).
- **Why it's built this way**: writing an ordinary session check-in rather than a new row type means [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler), the rollups, and the privacy export need no change at all to cover the self-service surface.
- **Where it's used**: [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) resolves it as `ICommandHandler<RoomCheckInRequest, Result<RoomCheckInResultDTO>>` (`CheckInsController.cs:49,203`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class doc still opens with "Only the room travels in the request" (`:20-21`), while the request now also carries the optional `CheckInCode` that this handler forwards to Conference (`:75`). The anti-abuse property it describes holds (no session id travels), but the sentence is narrower than the code.

### RecordSponsorVisitHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.RecordSponsorVisit` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/RecordSponsorVisit/RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:37` · Level 12 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: records the caller's visit to one sponsor booth, scanned from the sponsor's printed deep-link QR. The row is a [CheckIn](#checkin) with `Scope = Sponsor` whose `CheckedInByUserId` equals its `UserId`, which is what marks it self-recorded.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) and its [SponsorLiveInfo](group-17-conference-domain.md#sponsorliveinfo) result, [ICurrentUserService](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice), [ErasedUserGuard](group-22-engagement-module.md#eraseduserguard), [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), [SponsorVisitResultDTO](#sponsorvisitresultdto), [ICommandHandler&lt;in TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult); externals: `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>`.
- **Concept introduced, where to draw the reuse line, and a written-down accepted trade-off.** `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` and `[Rubric §11, Security]`. The doc comment (`RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:20-35`) is the most instructive part of the file and rewards reading in full. It argues first that this flow is deliberately not a third branch inside `CheckInProcessor.ExecuteAsync`: that entry point resolves its own target through Conference, and this flow asks a different question (the sponsor lookup) and answers in a different shape (the sponsor name), so folding it in would make the organizer path carry conditionals for a question it never asks. The reuse line is drawn one level lower instead: the caller check, the not-published failure, and the idempotent record all still run through [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), just through `RecordAsync` and `EventNotPublished` rather than `ExecuteAsync`. Splitting a helper by which half is genuinely shared, rather than sharing the whole entry point, is the transferable lesson. Then the doc states the trade-off honestly (`:25-32`): the deep-link URL is shareable, exactly like the badge QR, and the live window is deliberately not enforced. What makes sharing worthless is the combination of gates: the owning event must be published, the filtered unique index caps the award at one per sponsor per attendee, the configured value is low with `0` turning it off entirely ([PointsSettings](#pointssettings)), and the feature flag answers 404 when the surface is retired. Rotating tokens and date windows were considered and rejected as inconsistent with the badge QR. Documenting a rejected alternative next to the accepted risk is what makes this an architecture decision rather than an oversight.
- **Walkthrough**: five constructor dependencies (`:37-42`), one `HandleAsync` (`:45-101`).
  - `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(command)` (`:49`) and the caller from the token (`:51-55`), same `CheckIns.Forbidden` guard as the room flow.
  - Erased-account guard (`:57-60`, L207): [ErasedUserGuard](group-22-engagement-module.md#eraseduserguard)`.EnsureNotErasedAsync` refuses an erased account's still-valid token, so no booth visit is left under its id.
  - Sponsor lookup (`:64-68`): `GetSponsorLiveInfoAsync` proves the sponsor exists and returns its owning event plus display name, so a QR printed for a sponsor that was later pulled records nothing (`:62-63`). The result is unwrapped with `if (!sponsorInfo.TryGetValue(out var sponsor))` (`:67-68`), so the success path holds `sponsor` without a `Value!` dereference. Unlike the room flow, failures pass through unchanged, since a nonexistent sponsor id is not the same kind of enumeration risk as a room schedule.
  - Published gate (`:70-71`), the same shared `EventNotPublished` error as the other check-in paths, sourced to this handler.
  - The write through `CheckInProcessor.RecordAsync` (`:77-86`) with `CheckInScope.Sponsor`, `sessionId: null`, the sponsor id, and `checkedInByUserId: userId`. Idempotency again lives in the processor: a `(UserId, SponsorId, Scope == Sponsor)` predicate (`CheckInProcessor.cs:242-243`) means a second scan of the same booth reports the ORIGINAL visit instead of writing a second row. The comment names the filtered unique index on `(UserId, SponsorId) WHERE [Scope] = 2` as the race backstop (`:73-75`).
  - The response carries the sponsor name (`:94-100`) so the attendee's confirmation screen needs no second cross-module call, and the Information log fires only on a genuinely new visit (`:91-92`).
- **Why it's built this way**: returning the same DTO shape on both the fresh and repeat paths means the client renders one screen, and the `AlreadyVisited` flag is presentation, not an error the user has to interpret.
- **Where it's used**: [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) (`CheckInsController.cs:48,168`).

### CreateBookmarkRequestValidator

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.UseCases.Create` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/Create/CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:9` · Level 1 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the shape gate in front of [CreateBookmarkHandler](#createbookmarkhandler). Two rules, both saying the same thing about a different identifier: a bookmark needs a real user and a real session.
- **Depends on**: [CreateBookmarkRequest](#createbookmarkrequest), the `UserIdentifierType` / `SessionIdentifierType` aliases; externals: FluentValidation (`AbstractValidator<T>`, `RuleFor`, `NotEqual`, `WithMessage`, `WithErrorCode`).
- **Concept introduced, the request validator and where it sits in the command pipeline.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` (assesses whether a contract states its own preconditions and reports violations in a machine-readable form) and `[Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]` (assesses whether everything one use case needs lives in the use case's own folder). The wiring is worth learning once because every validator in this unit rides it. Validators are never resolved by name: `ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>()` in the module's composition root (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`) scans the assembly and registers each `AbstractValidator<T>` as `IValidator<T>`. At request time [ValidatingCommandDecorator&lt;TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#validatingcommanddecoratortcommand-tresult) receives `IEnumerable<IValidator<TCommand>>` and runs ALL of them, not just the first registration (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/UseCases/Decorators/ValidatingCommandDecorator.cs:19-22,32-37`), so a module-authored validator and a framework one both get their say and the caller sees every broken rule in one response. Either way the validation runs before the handler sees the command, and a handler is free to assume the structural rules already held. The other thing to notice is `WithErrorCode`: the string `"UserSessionBookmark.UserId.Required"` (`CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:16`) is a stable code a client can branch on, which a localized message never is.
- **Walkthrough**: a block-bodied constructor with two rules (`CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:11-22`).
  - `UserId` must not equal `default(UserIdentifierType)` (`CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:13-16`). The alias is `int` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Shared/MMCA.ADC.Identity.GlobalUsings.IdentifierType.cs:2`), so this rejects an unset zero. Writing it as `NotEqual(default(...))` rather than `GreaterThan(0)` keeps the rule correct if the alias ever changes width or becomes a struct id.
  - `SessionId` gets the identical treatment against `default(SessionIdentifierType)` (`CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:18-21`), also an `int` alias (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/MMCA.ADC.Conference.GlobalUsings.IdentifierType.cs:20`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the validator deliberately checks only what it can decide without touching a database or another module. Ownership (may this caller bookmark for this user) is enforced in [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller) against the caller's user-identifier claim (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:71-77`, [ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)), and session eligibility (BR-49, BR-91) is a cross-module call inside the handler. Three checks, three layers, none duplicated.
- **Where it's used**: applied automatically to every `CreateBookmarkRequest` command entering the pipeline; the request itself arrives from `BookmarksController.CreateAsync` (`BookmarksController.cs:61-84`).
