### EngagementFeatures

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/EngagementFeatures.cs:10` · Level 1 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the module's eight feature-flag names as `const string`s. Each constant is simultaneously the key read from the `"FeatureManagement"` configuration section and the argument to a `[FeatureGate(...)]` attribute on a controller, so a flag flip turns a whole surface off without a code change.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party beyond the `[FeatureFlag]` attribute (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/FeatureFlags/FeatureFlagAttribute.cs:32`) and [`FeatureFlagLifetime`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#featureflaglifetime) each constant is decorated with; nothing external. The file's only `using` is the namespace that attribute lives in (`EngagementFeatures.cs:1`). That is what lets Shared-layer callers, API controllers, and configuration authors all name the same string without any of them referencing each other.
- **Concept, module-scoped feature flags as compile-time constants.** The sibling explanation for the pattern lives with [ConferenceFeatures](group-17-conference-domain.md#conferencefeatures); this section covers what is specific to Engagement. Three mechanisms meet here. First, `const string` (not `static readonly`) means the value is inlined at the use site, which is why it can be used in an attribute argument and in an `[InlineData]` in a test. Second, every constant carries `[FeatureFlag(FeatureFlagLifetime.Permanent, Owner = "ADC Engagement")]` (`EngagementFeatures.cs:21,33,45,58,70,82,94,107`), so [`FeatureFlagRegistry`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#featureflagregistry) records ownership and lifetime for all eight flags rather than treating them as untracked strings. Third, the runtime behavior of a disabled flag is not the default from `Microsoft.FeatureManagement.Mvc`: MMCA.Common registers [DisabledFeatureHandler](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#disabledfeaturehandler) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.API/FeatureManagement/DisabledFeatureHandler.cs:14`), which sets an RFC 9457 `ProblemDetails` body with `Status = 404` and the title `"Feature not available"` (`:18-26`). So a gated route answers 404 in the same envelope as every other failure from [ApiControllerBase](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#apicontrollerbase), and the endpoint reads to an outside caller as simply not existing rather than as forbidden. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether concerns like this are applied uniformly at one point rather than re-implemented per endpoint: the gate is a single attribute on a controller class, and the disabled response shape is one handler in the framework. `[Rubric §11, Security]` shows in the choice of 404 over 403: a disabled surface leaks nothing about whether the capability exists. `[Rubric §29, Resilience and Business Continuity]` applies to the conference-day intent recorded in the doc comments: these are kill switches an organizer can throw mid-event, and each is explicitly `Permanent`, never subject to `FeatureFlagRegistry`'s `RemoveBy` check for `Temporary` flags.
- **Walkthrough**: eight constants, all prefixed `Engagement.` so keys stay unambiguous in a shared configuration file, and all decorated `[FeatureFlag(FeatureFlagLifetime.Permanent, Owner = "ADC Engagement")]`.
  - `SessionBookmarks = "Engagement.SessionBookmarks"` (`EngagementFeatures.cs:22`) gates create, list, and delete for the personal schedule; applied at [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:34`). Its `<para>` (`EngagementFeatures.cs:16-19`) states why the lifetime is `Permanent`: a shipped capability switch a conference chooses to run with or without, not a rollout toggle, so it carries no removal date.
  - `LivePolls = "Engagement.LivePolls"` (`:34`) gates the conference-day live layer (author, open, close, vote, results). Its summary names two controllers (`:26`), and both carry the gate: [LivePollsController](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollscontroller) (`LivePollsController.cs:39`) and [LivePollVotingController](#livepollvotingcontroller) (`LivePollVotingController.cs:34`). Its `<para>` (`:28-31`) names it the conference-day kill switch for the live layer, kept so an organizer can shed it mid-event.
  - `CheckIn = "Engagement.CheckIn"` (`:46`) gates QR badge check-in (my badge, scan, manual, attendance stats); applied at [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) (`CheckInsController.cs:39`).
  - `SponsorVisits = "Engagement.SponsorVisits"` (`:59`) gates the attendee-facing sponsor booth-visit endpoint (`CheckInsController.cs:160`). The doc comment (`:48-57`) names the operational contrast worth remembering: this flag makes every printed sponsor QR inert, while setting the `Points:SponsorVisit` award (20 points at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/appsettings.json:33`) to zero is the softer switch that keeps the visit recorded but stops the award; its `<para>` (`:53-56`) reiterates that the flag itself is `Permanent`, not a rollout toggle.
  - `RoomCheckIn = "Engagement.RoomCheckIn"` (`:71`) gates the attendee-facing room self check-in endpoint (`CheckInsController.cs:195`). The comment (`:61-69`) states why it is not folded into `SponsorVisits`: the two surfaces are printed and retired independently, so each needs its own switch.
  - `Points = "Engagement.Points"` (`:83`) gates the whole points surface (my points, leaderboard, opt-in, organizer overview); applied at [PointsController](#pointscontroller) (`PointsController.cs:34`).
  - `SessionQA = "Engagement.SessionQA"` (`:95`) gates session Q&A (submit, list, moderate, upvote); applied at [SessionQuestionsController](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#sessionquestionscontroller) (`SessionQuestionsController.cs:36`). Its `<para>` (`:89-92`) again names it a conference-day kill switch an organizer can shed mid-event.
  - `Tickets = "Engagement.Tickets"` (`:108`) gates the whole ticket roster surface (roster upload and delete, invites, summary, barcode claim, my tickets); applied at [TicketsController](#ticketscontroller) (`TicketsController.cs:39`) and [TicketRosterImportController](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) (`TicketRosterImportController.cs:34`). Its summary (`:97-101`) frames it for a conference that does not invite its TicketLeap ticket holders, and its `<para>` (`:102-105`) gives the same `Permanent` reasoning as `SessionBookmarks`.
  - Note the nesting on `CheckInsController`: the class carries `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.CheckIn)]` (`:39`) and two of its actions carry a second gate (`:160`, `:195`), so those two routes need *both* flags on. Turning `CheckIn` off retires the badge surface and the two attendee self-serve routes together; turning `SponsorVisits` off retires only the booth game.
- **Why it's built this way**: [ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html) is the decision record. Flag granularity here follows a printed-artifact and capability rule rather than a code-structure rule: each constant corresponds to something an organizer might need to retire on its own, which is why sponsor visits and room check-in are separate constants even though they share a controller, and why one `Tickets` constant covers two controllers that together make up one capability. Keeping the constants in the Shared assembly (not the API assembly) is what lets tests, the service host, and other layers name a flag without taking a controller dependency. Declaring every one of the eight `[FeatureFlag(FeatureFlagLifetime.Permanent, ...)]` with an explicit `Owner` records, in the attribute itself, that these are durable operational switches an organizer relies on, not rollout debt due for cleanup; each doc comment's `<para>` restates that same intent per flag (ADR-031).
- **Where it's used**: as `[FeatureGate(...)]` arguments on the eight Engagement controllers listed above, and as configuration keys. All eight appear in the standalone service host's `"FeatureManagement"` section, all set to `true`: `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/appsettings.json:17-25`. The same host passes the class's assembly to `services.AddReloadableFeatureFlags(b.Configuration, typeof(EngagementFeatures).Assembly)` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:130`), which per its comment (`:124-129`) layers stored overrides from the service's own database over the `"FeatureManagement"` configuration so an organizer can flip a kill switch without a new revision; [AdminFeatureFlagsController](#adminfeatureflagscontroller) serves those overrides at `Admin/Engagement/FeatureFlags` (`AdminFeatureFlagsController.cs:21`). The constants are also asserted directly in the API tests, for example `EngagementFeatures.Points` at `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Tests/Controllers/PointsControllerTests.cs:186`, `EngagementFeatures.Tickets` at `TicketsControllerTests.cs:289` and `TicketRosterImportControllerTests.cs:123`, and the per-action gate theory at `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Tests/Controllers/CheckInsControllerTests.cs:347-348`, which pins that `RecordSponsorVisitAsync` carries `SponsorVisits` and `RecordRoomCheckInAsync` carries `RoomCheckIn`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class doc comment (`EngagementFeatures.cs:5-9`) says the constants are used with `[FeatureGate]` attributes *and* the `IFeatureGated` marker interface (`:8`). The attribute half is real; the marker half is not exercised by this module. No Engagement command implements [IFeatureGated](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#ifeaturegated) today (the only ADC implementor is Conference's `RefreshFromSessionizeCommand`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Events/UseCases/RefreshFromSessionize/RefreshFromSessionizeCommand.cs:13`), so every Engagement flag is enforced at the HTTP boundary only, never inside the CQRS pipeline. The effective value of a flag at run time is the configuration value with any stored override applied; which overrides exist in a given environment lives in that service's database and is not determinable from source.

### CheckInAttendeeRequestValidator

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.CheckInAttendee` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/CheckInAttendee/CheckInAttendeeRequestValidator.cs:9` · Level 2 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the validator for the organizer scanning path. Four rules covering the badge credential, the scope, the event, and the conditionally required session.
- **Depends on**: [CheckInAttendeeRequest](#checkinattendeerequest), [CheckInScope](#checkinscope), the `EventIdentifierType` alias; externals: FluentValidation (`NotEmpty`, `IsInEnum`, `NotEqual`, `NotNull`, `When`).
- **Concept introduced, the conditional rule.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` (assesses whether a request that means different things in different modes states which fields each mode requires). The request is one payload serving two scopes, so a flat "all fields required" rule set would be wrong for an event-scope check-in and a flat "nothing required" set would let a session check-in arrive with no session. FluentValidation's `.When(...)` states the mode-specific half declaratively (`CheckInAttendeeRequestValidator.cs:33`) instead of pushing an `if` into the handler. `IsInEnum()` is the second thing worth naming: a C# enum backed by `int` will happily deserialize an out-of-range number, so an enum field is not self-validating and the rule at `:18-21` is the check that makes it so.
- **Walkthrough**: four rules in the constructor (`CheckInAttendeeRequestValidator.cs:11-34`).
  - `Credential` `NotEmpty()` with message "Badge credential is required." and code `"CheckIn.Credential.Required"` (`:13-16`). Presence only: whether the credential decodes and whether it names a real badge are decided in the handler, and both failures are answered identically there for anti-oracle reasons.
  - `Scope` `IsInEnum()` with code `"CheckIn.Scope.Invalid"` (`:18-21`).
  - `EventId` not `default(EventIdentifierType)` with code `"CheckIn.EventId.Required"` (`:23-26`).
  - `SessionId` `NotNull()` with code `"CheckIn.SessionId.Required"`, guarded by `.When(x => x.Scope == CheckInScope.Session)` (`:29-33`). The comment above it (`:28`) states the asymmetry outright: the event is required for both scopes, only the session is scope-conditional.
- **Why it's built this way**: the event stays mandatory even for a session scan although the shared core will later overwrite it with the event Conference reports for that session ([CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:145-149,195-198`). Requiring it keeps the request self-describing for logs and clients; letting the server value win keeps a stale organizer screen from filing attendance under the wrong event.
- **Where it's used**: runs ahead of [CheckInAttendeeHandler](#checkinattendeehandler) (`CheckInsController.cs:103,114`).

### CreateBookmarkHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.UseCases.Create` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/Create/CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:18` · Level 9 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the create-or-reactivate use case for a session bookmark. It enforces BR-21 (no duplicate), BR-49 and BR-91 (the session must be bookmarkable), and BR-135 (re-bookmarking revives the soft-deleted row instead of inserting a new one).
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [ISessionBookmarkValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#isessionbookmarkvalidationservice) (Conference-owned), [UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper](#usersessionbookmarkdtomapper), [IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector), [UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark), [BookmarkManagementDomainService](group-22-engagement-module.md#bookmarkmanagementdomainservice) (called statically, not injected), [ErasedUserGuard](group-22-engagement-module.md#eraseduserguard) (called statically), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) / [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), [ICommandHandler&lt;in TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult); externals: `ILogger<T>` with `[LoggerMessage]` source generation.
- **Concept introduced, the reactivating create and the pre-check-plus-index pair.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` (assesses whether soft-delete semantics are honored on the write path, not just filtered on reads), `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`, and `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`. Two ideas live here. First, under a soft-delete-everywhere policy ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)) a "create" is not always an insert: the row may already exist with `IsDeleted = true`, and inserting a second one would both violate the unique index and orphan the audit trail. Second, a uniqueness pre-check in application code is never the guarantee, only the pleasant path: two concurrent requests can both pass it, so the database index has to be the real rule and the handler has to translate its violation back into the same domain error. Both patterns recur in [PointsAwarder](#pointsawarder), which is the best evidence they are the module's convention rather than one-off defensiveness.
- **Walkthrough**: five constructor dependencies (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:18-23`), then one `HandleAsync` (`:26-94`).
  - Erased-account guard before anything else (`:30-34`, L207): `ErasedUserGuard.EnsureNotErasedAsync(unitOfWork, command.UserId, nameof(CreateBookmarkHandler), ...)` refuses a still-valid token belonging to an erased account, so it cannot reactivate the bookmark its erasure soft-deleted nor leave a new one under its id; a failure is returned as-is.
  - Cross-module eligibility next (`:36-39`): `ValidateSessionForBookmarkAsync` is a Conference contract, satisfied in-process in the monolith and by a gRPC client when the modules run as separate services ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html)). This is the reciprocal half of the bidirectional pair: Conference calls Engagement's [BookmarkCountService](#bookmarkcountservice) in the other direction, which is exactly why the AppHost deliberately omits a reciprocal `WaitFor`.
  - BR-21 duplicate check (`:43-54`) via `ExistsAsync`, returning `Error.Conflict` with code [UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes](#usersessionbookmarkerrorcodes)`.Duplicate` (`:50`), the shared constant whose value is `"UserSessionBookmark.Duplicate"` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.cs:13`). Naming the code once in the Shared assembly lets a client or a test branch on the same string the handler emits, rather than on a literal repeated at each failure site.
  - BR-135 revival lookup (`:56-61`): one call to `FindIncludingDeletedAsync` with `asTracking: true`, which returns the matching rows already partitioned into `(Active, SoftDeleted)` and lets the handler discard the active half with `_`. The framework calls this "the resurrection read" and documents both halves of the contract (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Persistence/IRepository.cs:198-217`): dropping the query filter means "include soft-deleted rows" and nothing more (the tenant filter stays in force), and `asTracking: true` is required because the row is about to be mutated rather than inserted, since an untracked source would leave the reactivation silently unsaved.
  - The decision itself is delegated to [BookmarkManagementDomainService](group-22-engagement-module.md#bookmarkmanagementdomainservice) (`:63-66`): `BookmarkManagementDomainService.CreateOrReactivate(deletedBookmark, ...)` is called as a static method, not through an injected instance, and returns either a fresh aggregate or the revived one. The handler unwraps it in one step with `if (!bookmarkResult.TryGetValue(out var bookmark))` (`:65-66`), so a failure returns the domain service's errors and the success path holds a non-null `bookmark` with no `Value!` dereference. The handler only decides persistence: `AddAsync` runs solely when there was no deleted row to revive (`:68-71`).
  - The save is wrapped in a filtered catch (`:73-89`). `uniqueConstraintViolationDetector.IsUniqueConstraintViolation(exception)` recognizes the unique index on `(UserId, SessionId)` firing, logs at Debug, and returns the SAME conflict error the pre-check produces, built from the same `UserSessionBookmarkErrorCodes.Duplicate` constant (`:84-88`), so a lost insert race reads to the caller as an ordinary 409 instead of a 500. Note the detector is INJECTED rather than a static helper, which is what keeps the provider-specific error classification swappable per database engine.
  - Success logs at Information and returns the mapped DTO (`:91-93`). Both log lines are `[LoggerMessage]` partials (`:96-100`), so the message templates are compiled rather than formatted per call.
- **Why it's built this way**: reactivation preserves the audit fields and any scalar references pointing at the bookmark, which is the whole point of soft delete; and pushing the create-or-reactivate choice into a domain service keeps the invariant testable without a database.
- **Where it's used**: resolved as `ICommandHandler<CreateBookmarkRequest, Result<UserSessionBookmarkDTO>>` by [BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller) (`BookmarksController.cs:38,79`), which performs the ownership check first and returns 201 with a `/bookmarks/{id}` location on success (`BookmarksController.cs:81-83`). Registered by the convention scan (`DependencyInjection.cs:94`) and therefore wrapped by the decorator pipeline, so validation, logging, and the transaction are already applied around it.

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.DeleteRoster` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/DeleteRoster/DeleteTicketRosterHandler.cs:18` · Level 9 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the post-event roster delete (BR-274, UC-53). Every ticket of one event, of every source event and every status, is soft-deleted, and a later upload for the same event starts from an empty roster.

- **Concept introduced, the bulk delete that still goes through the aggregate.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` (assesses whether soft-delete and audit semantics hold on every write path, bulk ones included). A set-based `DELETE` would be faster, but it would skip both the soft-delete default ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)) and the audit stamping on save.   - A tracked `GetAllAsync` over every ticket with the event's id (`:34-39`), with no status filter, because the rule covers every status.
  - The loop counts the tickets whose `Delete()` succeeded (`:41-46`).
  - Zero deletes returns success with no save (`:48-49`): an event with no roster, or a repeated request, changes nothing and is harmless.
  - Otherwise one `SaveChangesAsync` and an Information log with the count (`:51-52`, partial at `:57-58`). The command is [ITransactional](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#itransactional), so the whole set commits or none of it does.
- **Why it's built this way**: idempotent-by-outcome (an empty roster is a success, not a NotFound) lets an organizer repeat the action without reading an error, and the import guard keeps a concurrent run from resurrecting rows the delete just removed.
- **Where it's used**: resolved by [TicketsController](#ticketscontroller) as `ICommandHandler<DeleteTicketRosterCommand, Result>` (`TicketsController.cs:47,302-304`), which answers 204 for a success (`:288-289`). Tested in `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/Tickets/UseCases/DeleteTicketRosterHandlerTests.cs`, and used by `ProcessTicketRosterImportHandlerTests.cs` alongside the import run.

### SendTicketInvitesHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.SendTicketInvites` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/SendTicketInvites/SendTicketInvitesHandler.cs:33` · Level 9 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the invite run (BR-270, UC-49). It sends one invite per distinct order email of an event's eligible tickets (Live, unlinked, not yet invited, carrying an email), capped per run, and reports how many emails are left for the next run.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) and its [EventLiveInfo](group-17-conference-domain.md#eventliveinfo), [TicketSettings](#ticketsettings), [TicketImportRunGuard](#ticketimportrunguard), [Ticket](#ticket), [SendTicketInvitesRequest](#sendticketinvitesrequest), [TicketInvitesResultDTO](#ticketinvitesresultdto), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) / [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), [ICommandHandler&lt;in TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult); externals: `IOptions<T>`, `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>`.
- **Concept introduced, the capped, re-runnable batch whose emails ride the outbox.** `[Rubric §10, Messaging & Integration]` (assesses whether a side effect and the state change that justifies it commit together). Each invited ticket is stamped `InvitedOn`, and one ticket per email raises [TicketHolderInvited](group-24-identity-module.md#ticketholderinvited) before the save, so the outbox captures the events in the same transaction as the stamps ([ADR-003](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/003-outbox-dual-dispatch.html); doc comment `SendTicketInvitesHandler.cs:18-25`): a failed save emails nobody, and a re-run emails only tickets not yet stamped. `[Rubric §29, Resilience and Business Continuity]` shows in the cap: `MaxInvitesPerRun` (default 200, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/TicketSettings.cs:17`) bounds one run's work, and the `Remaining` count tells the organizer to run again rather than letting one request send an unbounded batch.
- **Walkthrough**: five constructor dependencies (`:33-38`), `HandleAsync` (`:41-84`), three private helpers.
  - Null guard, then the import guard (`:45-50`): while the event's roster import run is active the run is refused, because the import is still writing the roster the invites would read (`:29-30`).
  - `ReadEligibleOrdersAsync` (`:107-130`) filters on the four eligibility conditions (`:115-119`), reads tracked only when not a dry run (`asTracking: !dryRun`, `:120`), so a dry run's copies cannot be saved, and groups by order email in upload order: the email whose earliest ticket id came first goes first, ties broken by the email (`:126-128`).
  - The cap is clamped at zero with `Math.Max` and applied with `Take` (`:54-55`); the result DTO counts emails sent, tickets covered and emails remaining (`:56-63`). A dry run or an empty batch returns here (`:65-66`), before any Conference call.
  - `ReadEventDetailsAsync` (`:89-102`) asks Conference for the event's name and start date. A NotFound passes through as-is (`:92-93`); any other failure, or a peer that returns a blank name or a default date, becomes `"Ticket.Invites.EventDetailsUnavailable"` (`:95-101`), so the run sends nothing and can be retried rather than mailing an invite that cannot name its event.
  - One `invitedOn` from `TimeProvider` for the whole run (`:72`), then `InviteOrder` per email (`:73-78`): every ticket of the email is `MarkInvited` (`:134-139`), and the announcer is the earliest ticket that names an attendee (`:141-144`), which calls `AnnounceInvitation` with the event's name and start date (`:146`). The doc comment (`:22-24`) says why the announcer matters: a new account created from the invite carries that attendee's name, which is what lets the `UserRegistered` name match link the right ticket of a multi-ticket order (BR-272).
  - One save, then an Information log with the three counts (`:80-81`, partial at `:149-150`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the cap, the stamp-before-send ordering and the fail-closed event read together make the action safe to repeat: whatever happened last time, running it again sends only what is still owed.
- **Where it's used**: resolved by [TicketsController](#ticketscontroller) as `ICommandHandler<SendTicketInvitesRequest, Result<TicketInvitesResultDTO>>` (`TicketsController.cs:43`) for `POST /tickets/invites` (`:63`), whose `[Idempotent]` (`:64`) replays the first response so a retried request does not read "0 sent" (`:58-61`). [PendingTicketInvitationService](#pendingticketinvitationservice) names its announcer rule as the one it mirrors (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/PendingTicketInvitationService.cs:23,83`). Tested in `SendTicketInvitesHandlerTests.cs`.

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.StartRosterImport` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/StartRosterImport/StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:28` · Level 9 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the synchronous half of a roster import (UC-48 step 3). It refuses a bad file at once, then records a [TicketImportRun](#ticketimportrun) with its staged roster and schedules the processing and a privacy backstop in the same transaction.

- **Concept introduced, refuse synchronously, process durably.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` (assesses whether long work leaves the request path without losing the guarantee that it runs). Everything that can refuse the file is checked here so the organizer reads it at once (`StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:16-19`); the batched work then runs as internal commands ([ADR-114](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/114-internal-commands-durable-job-queue.html)) scheduled inside the same transaction as the run row, so a rolled-back start leaves neither a run nor queued work (`:75-76`). `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy and Data Governance]` shows in the second schedule: an expiry command at `TicketImportRun.AbandonAfter` (30 minutes, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketImportRun.cs:37`) is the backstop that ends a stalled run and clears its staged holder data.
- **Walkthrough**: six constructor dependencies (`:28-34`), the public `AlreadyRunningCode` constant (`:37`), `HandleAsync` (`:40-85`), two private helpers.
  - The event must exist: a failure from `GetEventLiveInfoAsync`, NotFound included, is returned as-is (`:47-49`).
  - The parser turns the bytes into a roster, its errors surfacing unchanged (`:51-53`).
  - Barcode collision check against the event's existing tickets, read with `ignoreQueryFilters: true` (`:55-59`) so soft-deleted rows count too, through `TicketRosterApplier.FindBarcodeConflict` (`:60-62`).
  - `RetireActiveRunAsync` (`:91-110`) finds a Queued or Running run for the event (`:93-97`). A live one refuses the commit with `TicketImportRunGuard.AlreadyRunning` (`:102-105`); one that has stopped moving is failed with `TicketImportRun.AbandonedErrorCode` and saved first (`:107-109`), so the one-active-run-per-event index never sees two.
  - `TicketImportRun.Create` with the entry count and `TicketRosterStaging.Serialize(roster)` (`:69-71`), `AddAsync` (`:73`), then a save inside the transaction so the run has its id for the two payloads (`:75-77`).
  - `ScheduleAsync` (`:113-125`) queues `ProcessTicketRosterImportInternalCommand(runId)` now (`:115-119`) and `ExpireTicketRosterImportInternalCommand(runId)` after `AbandonAfter` (`:121-124`); both carry only the run id. A scheduling failure fails the command, and the transaction with it (`:79-81`).
  - Success logs the run, event and total (`:83`, partial at `:127-128`) and returns the run DTO (`:84`).
- **Why it's built this way**: an organizer uploading a file needs the file-level verdict in the response, but applying hundreds of rows on the request path would tie the request to the batch. Splitting at the run row gives both, and the abandon rule means a crashed run never blocks the event's next upload for longer than `AbandonAfter`.
- **Where it's used**: resolved by [TicketRosterImportController](#ticketrosterimportcontroller) (`TicketRosterImportController.cs:38`) on the commit path of `POST /tickets/roster`, answering 202 Accepted with the run DTO (`:111-115`). Tested in `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/Tickets/UseCases/RosterImports/StartTicketRosterImportHandlerTests.cs`.

### CheckInAttendeeHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.CheckInAttendee` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/CheckInAttendee/CheckInAttendeeHandler.cs:21` · Level 12 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the organizer scanning path. A scanned (or typed) badge credential comes in, the server resolves it to an attendee, and the shared check-in core records the result.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice), [ICurrentUserService](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice) plus its [CurrentUserServiceExtensions](group-06-validation.md#currentuserserviceextensions) guard, [BadgePayload](#badgepayload), [AttendeeBadge](#attendeebadge), [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), [CheckInResultDTO](#checkinresultdto), [IReadRepository&lt;TEntity, TIdentifierType&gt;](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ireadrepositorytentity-tidentifiertype), [ICommandHandler&lt;in TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult); externals: `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>`.
- **Concept introduced, the anti-oracle error and the credential as the sole authority.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` (assesses whether error responses and logs avoid handing an attacker information) and `[Rubric §1, SOLID]`. Three security decisions are visible in this small file, each with a comment saying why. First, the attendee is NEVER taken from the request: the credential is the only input and the badge row is the sole authority on whose badge it is, while the organizer comes from the caller's token (`CheckInAttendeeHandler.cs:15-20`). Second, a malformed payload and a well-formed but unknown credential return the SAME error (`:43-48`, `:55-58`, via the shared `BadgeNotFound()` helper at `:79-83`), because a scanner able to distinguish them would be an oracle for guessing valid credentials. Third, the scanned credential is deliberately absent from the log line (`:85-86`): it is a bearer value, and a log carrying it would be a badge anyone with log access could replay.
- **Walkthrough**: five constructor dependencies (`:22-26`), one `HandleAsync` (`:29-77`).
  - `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(command)` (`:33`), then the caller guard: `currentUserService.RequireUserId("CheckIns.Forbidden")` (`:35-41`). That is the framework's `extension(ICurrentUserService)` member (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Extensions/CurrentUserServiceExtensions.cs:35-46`), which collapses the read-then-null-check-then-fail block into one call returning `Result<UserIdentifierType>` and defaults the classification to `ErrorType.Forbidden`. All four check-in handlers in this unit open the same way with the same code string.
  - `BadgePayload.TryExtractCredential(command.Credential, out var credential)` (`:45`), a `Try` shape so a malformed scan is an ordinary branch rather than an exception.
  - Badge lookup through `GetReadRepository` (`:50-54`), not `GetRepository`: nothing about the badge is mutated here, and using the read repository states that. `asTracking: false` reinforces it.
  - Delegation to [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor)`.ExecuteAsync` with `badge.UserId` (`:60-69`). Everything from target validation through idempotency to the write lives there, which is why this handler is short.
  - Logging only on success (`:71-74`): `result.TryGetValue(out var checkIn)` unwraps the [CheckInResultDTO](#checkinresultdto) without a null-forgiving dereference, and the log carries its repeat flag so an operator can see at a glance whether a scan wrote a row or reported an existing one.
- **Why it's built this way**: the two organizer entry points differ ONLY in how the attendee is identified, so the identification is all that lives in each handler and the shared rules live once in the processor (`CheckInProcessor.cs:10-21`), which is a static helper precisely so neither handler gains a dependency it does not own.
- **Where it's used**: [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) resolves it as `ICommandHandler<CheckInAttendeeRequest, Result<CheckInResultDTO>>` (`CheckInsController.cs:45,114`). The check-in it writes is what later drives [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler) through the [AttendeeCheckedIn](#attendeecheckedin) integration event.

### FeedbackAnswerModel

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Feedback` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Feedback/FeedbackAnswerModel.cs:26` · Level 2 · class (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the form model for one answer on the two attendee feedback pages. It is the two-way binding target behind every question field, the single declaration site for the free-text length rule that both pages enforce, and the one place that turns an answer back into the string it posts.
- **Depends on**: [`QuestionDTO`](group-17-conference-domain.md#questiondto) (its `AnswerValueMaxLength` constant, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Questions/QuestionDTO.cs:32`) and the `OptionalEmail` attribute from `MMCA.Common.UI.Validation`. Externals: `System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations` (`[MaxLength]`). It is consumed through [`ModelValidation`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#modelvalidation)`.ForProperty` and [`DataAnnotationsModelValidator`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#dataannotationsmodelvalidator), both from `MMCA.Common.UI`.
- **Concept introduced, the annotated form model as the one rule declaration.** `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` assesses whether input rules are declared once or restated per field. The naive Blazor shape writes a `MaxLength` on the markup, a `Counter` beside it, and a hand-rolled length check in the submit path: three copies of the same number that drift independently. Here the `[MaxLength]` attribute at `FeedbackAnswerModel.cs:36` is the rule, `AnswerValueMaxLength` (`:33`) is the number, and the markup reads the constant for both the input cap and the character counter (`EventFeedback.razor:97-98`, `SessionFeedback.razor:108-109`). `[Rubric §19, State Management]` covers the other half of its job: each page's [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid) holds a `Dictionary<QuestionIdentifierType, FeedbackAnswerModel>` of in-progress answers (`FeedbackAnswers.cs:25`) rather than editing the DTO it will eventually post, so an unsaved edit never round-trips through a server contract. `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]`: the `ErrorMessage` is not a sentence but a resource key, `"Field.MaxLengthError"`, resolved by each page's own localizing validator ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)), so the shared model produces a per-page translation without the model knowing anything about locales.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `public const int AnswerValueMaxLength = QuestionDTO.AnswerValueMaxLength` (`FeedbackAnswerModel.cs:33`) does not restate the number; it reads the one declaration on the shared contract, `QuestionDTO.AnswerValueMaxLength = 4000` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Questions/QuestionDTO.cs:32`). The server invariants read the same constant: `EventInvariants.AnswerValueMaxLength` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Events/EventInvariants.cs:60`) and `SessionInvariants.AnswerValueMaxLength` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Sessions/SessionInvariants.cs:38`), and those in turn size the columns (`EventQuestionAnswerConfiguration.cs:26`, `SessionQuestionAnswerConfiguration.cs:26`). So the form cap, the domain invariant and the column width are one number with one owner, and a value the form accepts is a value the table can hold.
  - `TextValue` (`:37`) is the `string?` bound by the plain text question type (the email type does not bind it directly), and carries the `[MaxLength(AnswerValueMaxLength, ErrorMessage = "Field.MaxLengthError")]` annotation (`:36`).
  - `EmailValue` (`:46-50`) is a second view of the same stored value: its getter and setter read and write `TextValue` (`:48-49`), so only one string is ever stored and submitted. It exists so the EMAIL question type gets its own rules without touching the text rules: `[OptionalEmail(ErrorMessage = "Field.EmailError")]` (`:44`, attribute at `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Validation/OptionalEmailAttribute.cs:25`) lets a blank answer pass (whether an answer is required stays per-question data) while a non-blank one must be a valid address, and the same `[MaxLength]` (`:45`) still caps the length. The markup binds it for the email case (`EventFeedback.razor:82`, `SessionFeedback.razor:93`).
  - `RatingValue` (`:53`) is a plain `int` with no annotation, because a rating is picked from a star control rather than typed (the markup's `RATING` branch, `EventFeedback.razor:52`, `SessionFeedback.razor:63`). Zero is the unanswered sentinel.
  - `AnswerValue(string? questionType)` (`:58-68`) is the bridge back to the wire. Any type other than `"Rating"` (ordinal, case-insensitive, `:60`) posts `TextValue` (`:62`); a rating posts its number formatted with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` when `RatingValue > 0`, and `null` otherwise (`:65-67`). [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid) calls it for the required-answer check, the submit payload and the blanked-answer list, so an untouched rating counts as unanswered everywhere and is never posted.
  - The three value members are settable properties, deliberately. MudBlazor binds them two-way with `@bind-...` (for example `@bind-Value` on `EmailValue`, `EventFeedback.razor:82`), which needs a writable property, so a `record` with `init`-only members could not serve as the target. The mutability is a consequence of the binding contract, not a lapse from the workspace's `required`/`init` default.
- **Why it's built this way**: the type doc (`FeedbackAnswerModel.cs:8-25`) records the one design tension worth understanding. Both pages render a *dynamic* question list, so whether a given answer is required is per-question data (`QuestionDTO.IsRequired`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Questions/QuestionDTO.cs:53`), not a property of the model. A `[Required]` attribute here would apply to every question at once and would be wrong for most of them, so required stays on the field's own `Required="@question.IsRequired"` parameter (the `Required` parameter on each field in `EventFeedback.razor`) and only the length rule, which genuinely is per-value, is declared on the model. Lifting the model to a public file-level type shared by both pages, rather than a private nested holder per page, is what makes one declaration serve both forms.
- **Where it's used**: seeded one instance per question by `FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>.SetQuestions` (`FeedbackAnswers.cs:54`), populated by its `PreFill` (`:79`, `:83`), read through `AnswerValue` on submit, and reset in place by its `ClearSavedAnswer` (`:134-135`). A *separate* prototype instance is constructed in each page's `OnInitialized` purely to build the validation delegates (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:88-90`, `SessionFeedback.razor.cs:88-90`), one for `TextValue` and one for `EmailValue`: `ModelValidation.ForProperty` validates the value handed to it rather than the instance, so one prototype serves the whole dynamic list.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: nothing here enforces the length. The attribute is inert until a validator runs it; the enforcement path is the pages' `_validateAnswerText` and `_validateAnswerEmail` delegates on the client and the Conference invariants on the server.

### LeaderboardOptInChanged

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Points.DomainEvents` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/DomainEvents/LeaderboardOptInChanged.cs:15` · Level 2 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the in-process domain event the [LeaderboardOptIn](#leaderboardoptin) aggregate raises when an attendee joins the public leaderboard, rejoins it, or leaves it.
- **Depends on**: [BaseDomainEvent](group-04-events-outbox.md#basedomainevent), [DomainEntityState](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate), the `LeaderboardOptInIdentifierType` / `UserIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept introduced, the one-event-per-aggregate shape (BR-60).** `[Rubric §4, DDD]` (assesses whether state changes are named domain facts rather than inferred from rows) and `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`. Instead of `LeaderboardOptInCreated` plus `LeaderboardOptInDeleted`, the module raises ONE record carrying a `DomainEntityState` discriminator (`LeaderboardOptInChanged.cs:16`). The doc comment states the convention (`:8-9`) and the module holds to it for all three of its aggregates in this unit. The payload discipline is the second lesson: the comment says outright that the event carries no display name because "the event is a signal, not a publication channel" (`LeaderboardOptInChanged.cs:9-10`). A subscriber running in the same unit of work can load anything else it needs, and a fat payload would go stale between raise and dispatch.
- **Walkthrough**: a three-member positional record (`LeaderboardOptInChanged.cs:15-19`): `State`, `LeaderboardOptInId`, `UserId`. Raised from three call sites on the aggregate, and each one tells you something: `Create` raises `Added` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/LeaderboardOptIn.cs:75`), reactivation of a previously soft-deleted opt-in raises `Added` again rather than a distinct "reactivated" fact (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:98`), and the soft delete raises `Deleted` (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:114`). A subscriber therefore never has to know whether a row is new or revived, which is exactly the information a leaderboard projection does not care about.
- **Why it's built this way**: opting out of the leaderboard is a privacy action ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html) distinguishes soft delete from erasure), so it must be a first-class fact and not a silently flipped flag.
- **Where it's used**: raised by the aggregate and asserted by the domain tests (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tests/Points/LeaderboardOptInTests.cs:72,101,135`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: no handler subscribes to this event anywhere in current ADC source. It is a published extension point that the framework's [DomainEventDispatcher](group-04-events-outbox.md#domaineventdispatcher) will deliver the moment one is written, not shipped behavior. Contrast [UserSessionBookmarkChanged](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) below, which does have a subscriber.

### ManualCheckInRequestValidator

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.ManualCheckIn` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/ManualCheckIn/ManualCheckInRequestValidator.cs:9` · Level 2 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the validator for the organizer's manual fallback. Structurally the same four rules as [CheckInAttendeeRequestValidator](#checkinattendeerequestvalidator), with one substitution.
- **Depends on**: [ManualCheckInRequest](#manualcheckinrequest), [CheckInScope](#checkinscope), the `UserIdentifierType` / `EventIdentifierType` aliases; externals: FluentValidation.
- **Concept reinforced**: the conditional rule and the enum check taught in the previous section apply unchanged, including the identical `.When(x => x.Scope == CheckInScope.Session)` guard and the same comment about the event staying required for both scopes (`ManualCheckInRequestValidator.cs:28-33`).
- **Walkthrough**: the one line that differs is the first rule (`ManualCheckInRequestValidator.cs:13-16`): `UserId` not `default(UserIdentifierType)` with code `"CheckIn.UserId.Required"`, where the scan path validates a badge `Credential` instead. That single substitution is the whole difference between the two paths at this layer, and it is the security-relevant one: on this endpoint the attendee is named by the caller, so the endpoint itself is organizer-only rather than the badge row being the authority. `Scope` (`:18-21`), `EventId` (`:23-26`) and the conditional `SessionId` (`:29-33`) are line-for-line the scan validator's rules, messages and error codes included.
- **Why it's built this way**: identical error codes across the two paths mean a client shows the same message whichever way an organizer records the check-in, which matters because the two surfaces sit side by side on the same organizer screen.
