### PointsEntryChanged

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Points.DomainEvents` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/DomainEvents/PointsEntryChanged.cs:17` · Level 2 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the domain event raised when one award lands in the points ledger. It carries the whole award: who earned it, for what activity, and how many points.
- **Depends on**: [BaseDomainEvent](group-04-events-outbox.md#basedomainevent), [DomainEntityState](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate), [PointsActivityType](#pointsactivitytype), the `PointsEntryIdentifierType` / `UserIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept reinforced, the same BR-60 shape as [LeaderboardOptInChanged](#leaderboardoptinchanged), with an honest caveat in the doc.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` (assesses whether the storage model matches the domain's mutability) and `[Rubric §4, DDD]`. The comment (`PointsEntryChanged.cs:8-10`) says the ledger is append-only, so in practice `State` is always `Added`, and that the discriminator is carried anyway to keep one event shape across the module. That is a deliberate small redundancy in favor of consistency, and the file says so rather than leaving a reader to wonder why a never-deleted entity carries a delete state.
- **Walkthrough**: five positional members (`PointsEntryChanged.cs:17-23`): `State`, `PointsEntryId`, `UserId`, `ActivityType`, `Points`. Unlike the other two events in this unit, this one carries the value, because the awarded points are a SNAPSHOT of what the rule was worth at earn time (see [PointsAwarder](#pointsawarder)) and cannot be re-derived from configuration afterwards. Raised exactly once inside the `PointsEntry.Create` factory, after the four invariants pass (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/PointsEntry.cs:96-101`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the value is the payload a future subscriber (a live points ticker, an audit trail) would otherwise have to guess at, and guessing it from today's [PointsSettings](#pointssettings) would give the wrong answer for any award earned before a mid-conference retune. Note the entry's own `Id` is still `default` when the event is captured (`PointsEntry.cs:91-97`, the identity is generated by the INSERT), so the useful correlation keys are the user and the activity, not the entry id.
- **Where it's used**: raised by [PointsEntry](#pointsentry) and asserted by the domain tests (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tests/Points/PointsEntryTests.cs:36,46`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: current source contains no subscriber to this event.

### SelfHttpWarmupTask

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/SelfHttpWarmupTask.cs:23` · Level 2 · class (sealed, internal)

- **What it is**: the Engagement service's startup warm-up. Once Kestrel is listening it replays the hot bookmarks read against this host's own endpoint so routing, authentication, and the middleware pipeline are JIT-compiled before a real attendee request arrives.
- **Depends on**: [SelfHttpWarmupTaskBase](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#selfhttpwarmuptaskbase) from `MMCA.Common.Aspire.Warmup`; externals: ASP.NET Core (`IServer`, `IHostApplicationLifetime`, `IHostEnvironment`), `IConfiguration`, `ILogger<T>`.
- **Concept reinforced, the cold-start warm-up task ([ADR-025](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/025-startup-warmup-readiness.html)).** `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` (assesses whether first-request latency after a restart or scale-out is managed rather than paid by a user) and `[Rubric §13, Observability & Operability]` (assesses that readiness reflects an instance's real ability to serve). The class doc states the contract (`SelfHttpWarmupTask.cs:6-17`): the base class discovers the bound cleartext address, waits for the host lifetime, and issues the configured GETs; the runner registered by `AddWarmupReadiness()` inside `AddServiceDefaults()` holds `/health/ready` not-ready until the task has had its chance, so the orchestrator does not route traffic into a cold instance. Failures are logged and fall back to lazy warm-up on the first real request rather than blocking startup.
- **Walkthrough**: a primary-constructor class forwarding all five dependencies to the base (`SelfHttpWarmupTask.cs:23-29`) and overriding three members.
  - `Paths` (`SelfHttpWarmupTask.cs:33-36`), one entry: `bookmarks?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10`. The comment above it (`:31-32`) ties the string to the attendee bookmark list under the module-wide `[Authorize]` policy ([BookmarksController](#bookmarkscontroller), `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:35`).
  - `Name => "SelfHttpWarmup"` (`:39`) and `WarmupPaths => Paths` (`:42`), the base's two abstractions.
  - `RequireSuccessStatusCode => false` (`:49`), the interesting override. The controller requires an authenticated caller, so the unauthenticated self-request is refused by design. The XML comment (`:44-48`) makes the argument: the refusal still traverses Kestrel, routing, authentication, and the whole middleware pipeline, which is exactly where the cold-start JIT cost lives, so treating a 401 as a failure would log a spurious warning on every startup.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class doc (`SelfHttpWarmupTask.cs:9`) draws the contrast with Conference's warm-up, which also populates an output cache. This service caches nothing (its base output-cache policy is `NoCache`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:160`), so the task buys pipeline JIT only, and it says so rather than pretending to prime a cache it cannot reach. The Identity service ships a same-named task with the same posture over its own hot read ([SelfHttpWarmupTask](group-24-identity-module.md#selfhttpwarmuptask)).
- **Where it's used**: registered with `services.AddWarmupTask<SelfHttpWarmupTask>()` in the Engagement service host (`Program.cs:166`), where the surrounding comment (`Program.cs:162-165`) repeats the rationale for an operator reading the host file.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the base type decides how the bound address is discovered and whether the run is skipped under the Testing environment; this file supplies only the paths and the status-code policy.

### TicketInvitationGrpcService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service.Grpc` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Grpc/TicketInvitationGrpcService.cs:26` · Level 2 · class (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the server-side gRPC endpoint that lets the Identity service ask Engagement whether an email address holds a pending ticket invitation, so Identity can re-issue an invitation whose link expired before the invitee had an account (BR-271, per the class doc at `TicketInvitationGrpcService.cs:9-13`).
- **Depends on**: [`IPendingTicketInvitationService`](#ipendingticketinvitationservice) (primary constructor, `:26`) and the [`PendingTicketInvitationDTO`](#pendingticketinvitationdto) it returns; the generated base `TicketInvitationService.TicketInvitationServiceBase` and the messages from `ticket_invitation.proto` (namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts.V1`, `:3`); the `IsServiceCaller()` extension from [`ServiceCallerClaimsPrincipalExtensions`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#servicecallerclaimsprincipalextensions) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.Grpc/Authentication/ServiceCallerClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs:21`). Externals: `Grpc.Core` (`ServerCallContext`, `RpcException`), `System.Globalization`.
- **Concept, a service-only lookup that answers the minimum.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether authorization is enforced at every boundary rather than assumed from the caller. The answer to this call says whether an address holds a ticket, which is itself personal information, so the class enforces "services only" twice: the host maps it under the `ServiceCaller` policy (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:278`, `ServiceTokenDefaults.ServiceCallerPolicy` at `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.Grpc/Authentication/ServiceTokenDefaults.cs:29`), and the method itself throws `PermissionDenied` unless `context.GetHttpContext().User.IsServiceCaller()` holds (`TicketInvitationGrpcService.cs:40-43`). The doc (`:14-19`) explains why no user token is ever in play: the one caller is Identity's anonymous sign-in link request, which has no user to forward, so Identity's client always presents its own service token. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses data minimization: the reply carries only what a new invitation needs (first and last name, the event's name and its first day) and never the ticket id, the barcode or the order (`:20-23`, the response at `:52-61`).
- **Walkthrough**: `MaxEmailLength = 320` (`:30`) bounds the input. The one override, `GetPendingTicketInvitation` (`:33`), null-guards both arguments (`:37-38`), runs the service-caller check (`:40-43`), then answers `Found = false` without touching the database for a blank address or one longer than the cap (`:45-48`). Otherwise it awaits `inner.GetPendingInvitationAsync(request.Email, context.CancellationToken)` (`:50`) and maps a `null` to `Found = false`, or a hit to `Found = true` plus the names and `EventStart` formatted as `"yyyy-MM-dd"` with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` (`:52-61`), a date-only string because the invitation needs the first day, not an instant.
- **Why it's built this way**: the same thin server-bridge shape as [`BookmarkCountsGrpcService`](#bookmarkcountsgrpcservice) and [`UserEngagementExportGrpcService`](#userengagementexportgrpcservice): the lookup rules live in the in-process service, reused identically in-process and over the wire, and this class owns only the wire posture and the projection ([ADR-012](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/012-grpc-host-transport.html)). The in-method caller check duplicates the endpoint policy on purpose, so a mapping change in `Program.cs` cannot silently open the lookup.
- **Where it's used**: mapped at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:278`; its client half is [`TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter`](#ticketinvitationservicegrpcadapter). Covered by [`TicketInvitationGrpcServiceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), the integration [`TicketInvitationGrpcTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), and the posture checks in `GrpcViewAsPostureTests`.

### UserSessionBookmarkChanged

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.UserSessionBookmarks.DomainEvents` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/DomainEvents/UserSessionBookmarkChanged.cs:21` · Level 2 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the domain event the [UserSessionBookmark](#usersessionbookmark) aggregate raises when a bookmark is created, reactivated, or soft-deleted. It is the one event in this unit with a live subscriber.
- **Depends on**: [BaseDomainEvent](group-04-events-outbox.md#basedomainevent), [DomainEntityState](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate), the `UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType` / `UserIdentifierType` / `SessionIdentifierType` aliases.
- **Concept introduced, the identity hole in a create-time domain event.** `[Rubric §4, DDD]` and `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` (assesses whether the code accounts for what the database, not the object graph, actually decides). The BR-60 single-event shape is the same one [LeaderboardOptInChanged](#leaderboardoptinchanged) teaches, but this file adds a lesson those two do not. The `BookmarkId` parameter doc (`UserSessionBookmarkChanged.cs:12-18`) says the field is ZERO whenever a brand-new bookmark raises `Added`: identity is generated by the INSERT, the positional record captures the value before that INSERT runs, and nothing re-stamps it afterwards. A reactivated bookmark does carry its real id, because that row already exists. The consequence is stated in the same doc and is the part to remember: handlers correlate on `UserId` and `SessionId`, which are both set before the event is raised, and never on `BookmarkId`. That is a general trap with value-captured events over database-generated keys, not a quirk of this aggregate.
- **Walkthrough**: four positional members (`UserSessionBookmarkChanged.cs:21-26`): `State`, `BookmarkId`, `UserId`, `SessionId`. Three raise sites, and the shape earns its keep at each: `Create` raises `Added` with the still-zero id and a comment saying so (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmark.cs:55-57`); `Reactivate` raises `Added` again, and only when `Undelete()` succeeded (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:69-73`), which is BR-135 in one line, so a subscriber counting bookmarks sees "one more bookmark exists" for both a fresh star and a revived one; `Delete` raises `Deleted`, and only when the soft delete actually flipped (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:84-88`), so a second delete of an already-deleted bookmark raises nothing and subscribers cannot observe a duplicate fact.
- **Why it's built this way**: carrying `SessionId` as well as `UserId` means a subscriber can act on the session dimension without loading the aggregate, which is exactly what the one subscriber does.
- **Where it's used**: [UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler](#usersessionbookmarkcacheevictionhandler) subscribes as `IDomainEventHandler<UserSessionBookmarkChanged>` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/DomainEventHandlers/UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler.cs:43-46`) and broadcasts an output-cache eviction to Conference so its cached session reads stop serving a stale bookmark count. Its doc explains why the DOMAIN event is the right hook (`:23-30`): the create path has a bespoke handler, but the delete path runs on the framework's generic `DeleteEntityCommand` and has no ADC handler at all, whereas the aggregate raises this one event on all three paths that move a count. Also raised in the domain tests (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tests/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmarkTests.cs:45,58,77,105`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the per-session bookmark count Conference consumes is served by a live query in [BookmarkCountService](#bookmarkcountservice), not by projecting this event; the subscriber only invalidates Conference's cache of that number. Do not read the event as the backing mechanism for the count itself.

### FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Feedback` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Feedback/FeedbackAnswers.cs:15` · Level 3 · class (internal sealed, generic)

- **What it is**: the answer state of one feedback form, shared by the session and the event feedback pages: the questions in display order, one [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel) per question, the ids of the answers already saved, and the required questions left unanswered at the last submit. `TAnswerId` (constrained to `struct`, `FeedbackAnswers.cs:16`) is the saved answer's identifier type, so the same class serves both pages.
- **Depends on**: [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel), [`QuestionDTO`](group-17-conference-domain.md#questiondto), the `QuestionIdentifierType` alias. Externals: `System.Globalization`, LINQ.
- **Concept introduced, page state as a plain class beside a thin page.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses whether components stay containers while logic lives in testable types. The class doc (`FeedbackAnswers.cs:6-13`) states the split: the pre-fill, required-answer and submit-payload rules live here in one place, while each page keeps the service calls and every user-visible side effect (toasts, navigation, the dirty flag). `[Rubric §19, State Management]`: the page discards a stale form by replacing one object (`_answerState = new()`) rather than clearing four fields, and the generic parameter is what lets [`SessionFeedback`](#sessionfeedback) (`FeedbackAnswers<SessionQuestionAnswerIdentifierType>`) and [`EventFeedback`](#eventfeedback) (`FeedbackAnswers<EventQuestionAnswerIdentifierType>`) share it without a base page class. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]`: the required gate here covers what `MudForm` cannot, because a star rating is not a form input (`:30-34`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - State (`:18-35`): the private `_missingRequired` set (`:18`) and `_existingAnswerIds` map from question to saved answer id (`:19`); the public `Questions` list (`:22`) and `Answers` dictionary (`:25`), both privately settable; `HasExistingFeedback` (`:28`), true when any saved id exists, which picks the page's "Update" versus "Submit" button text; and `MissingRequired` (`:35`), the read-only view the markup binds to each field's inline error (`EventFeedback.razor:61`, `:75`).
  - `HasSavedAnswer` (`:40`) and `TryGetSavedAnswerId` (`:46-47`) expose the saved ids, which is what drives the per-question Clear button and the delete call.
  - `SetQuestions` (`:51-55`) orders the questions by `Sort` (`:53`) and starts one blank model per question (`:54`).
  - `PreFill` (`:63-86`) takes `(QuestionId, AnswerId, AnswerValue)` tuples. The caller filters to its own session or event first, because questions are shared across sessions and events and a foreign answer would match by question id (the doc at `:57-61`). It skips a question that is not on the form (`:69-72`), records the saved id (`:74`), and writes a `Rating` question's value through `int.TryParse` with the invariant culture into `RatingValue` (`:76-79`) and anything else into `TextValue` (`:83`).
  - `FlagMissingRequiredAnswers` (`:93-103`) clears the set and adds every required question whose `AnswerValue` is blank, for every question type, returning `true` when any gap exists.
  - `PendingAnswers` (`:107-112`) projects the answered questions into the one POST-as-upsert payload, leaving blanks out.
  - `BlankedSavedAnswers` (`:120-125`) is the counterpart: the saved answers the reader has since blanked. The doc (`:114-118`) names the bug it prevents: the upsert has no delete semantics and `PendingAnswers` drops blanks, so without this list a submit would report success while the old answer survived on the server.
  - `ClearSavedAnswer` (`:129-137`) forgets a saved id the server deleted and blanks its model (`TextValue = null`, `RatingValue = 0`, `:134-135`; `EmailValue` follows `TextValue`).
- **Why it's built this way**: every rule that decides "is this answered" routes through [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel)`.AnswerValue`, so the required check, the payload and the blanked list cannot disagree about what an unanswered rating is. Keeping I/O out means the class has no dependencies to fake and the pages stay within the code-behind size convention the class doc cites.
- **Where it's used**: held as `_answerState` by [`EventFeedback`](#eventfeedback) (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:65`) and [`SessionFeedback`](#sessionfeedback) (`SessionFeedback.razor.cs:65`), and bound from both pages' markup. Exercised through the page component tests ([`EventFeedbackTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), [`SessionFeedbackTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class is `internal`, so it is not part of the Engagement UI assembly's public surface; no dedicated unit-test class for it was established from the brief's usage sites.

### IPointsAwarder

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/Services/IPointsAwarder.cs:19` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the single write path into the points ledger. One method: award the configured points for one activity, or do nothing when the rule is off or the attendee already earned that exact award.
- **Depends on**: [PointsActivityType](#pointsactivitytype), [PointsSubjectKeys](#pointssubjectkeys) (named in the parameter docs), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), the `UserIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept introduced, the deliberately vocabulary-free contract.** `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` (assesses whether abstractions are stated in terms the layer owns rather than in terms of an outer concern) and `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`. The doc comment argues the design explicitly (`IPointsAwarder.cs:10-17`): neither this interface nor the [PointsEntry](#pointsentry) entity names an event, a session, a check-in, or any other ADC concept. An award is a user, an activity, an opaque subject key, and a timestamp. That is what would make lifting the ledger (the entity, this awarder, and the read queries) into MMCA.Common a MOVE rather than a rewrite, and it is the same "extract reusable infrastructure, keep the vocabulary local" instinct the workspace applies everywhere. The ADC-specific part stays in the thin award adapters that translate a module event into an (activity, subjectKey) pair, for example [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler). `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` also applies at the interface-segregation level: one method, one reason to call it.
- **Walkthrough**: `Task<Result> AwardAsync(UserIdentifierType userId, PointsActivityType activity, string subjectKey, DateTime occurredOnUtc, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)` (`IPointsAwarder.cs:35-40`). The return contract is the part to read carefully (`IPointsAwarder.cs:30-34`): the result succeeds when the award EXISTS after the call, whether this call created it, an earlier call did, or the rule is configured to award nothing. It fails only when the entry itself is invalid, which the doc calls a caller bug rather than a retryable condition. Callers therefore never need to distinguish "awarded" from "already awarded", which is what lets a broker redelivery run straight through.
- **Why it's built this way**: stating idempotency, the per-rule kill switch, and the value snapshot once in the contract (`IPointsAwarder.cs:6-9`) means each new earn rule is a small adapter rather than a re-derivation of the same three concerns.
- **Where it's used**: registered by hand as scoped (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:90`, with the comment at `:76-82` explaining that a plain service is invisible to the handler convention scan below it) and implemented by [PointsAwarder](#pointsawarder). Consumers resolve it from their own scope: [AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler) (`.../Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler.cs:48`), [EventFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler](#eventfeedbacksubmittedpointshandler) (`.../EventFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:38`), [SessionFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler](#sessionfeedbacksubmittedpointshandler) (`.../SessionFeedbackSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:40`), and [SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler](#sessionquestionsubmittedpointshandler) (`.../Points/DomainEventHandlers/SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler.cs:78`).

### EngagementBrokerConsumers

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:20` · Level 4 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: the list of integration events the Engagement service host subscribes to on the broker, held in one static `Register` method that the host hands to `AddBrokerMessaging`.
- **Depends on**: [`IBrokerConsumerBuilder`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#ibrokerconsumerbuilder) and the six event contracts it registers: [`AttendeeCheckedIn`](#attendeecheckedin), [`SessionFeedbackSubmitted`](group-17-conference-domain.md#sessionfeedbacksubmitted), [`EventFeedbackSubmitted`](group-17-conference-domain.md#eventfeedbacksubmitted), [`UserDeleted`](group-24-identity-module.md#userdeleted), [`UserRegistered`](group-24-identity-module.md#userregistered) and [`UserEmailVerified`](group-24-identity-module.md#useremailverified).
- **Concept, the subscription list as an assertable value.** `[Rubric §6, Event-Driven Architecture]` assesses whether the events a service consumes are explicit and checkable rather than implied by wiring. The class doc (`EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:9-12`) gives the reason for the file: kept out of `Program.cs`, the subscriptions this host declares can be asserted without booting the host (the `ConferenceBrokerConsumers` precedent). `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`: the remarks (`:13-19`) record the topology decision that makes a shared event safe. Every subscription lands on this host's one queue (`MessageBus:QueueName`), and Conference consumes `UserRegistered` and `UserDeleted` on its own queue, so each registration (the BR-272 ticket link here, the BR-207 speaker auto-link there) and each erasure reaches both services instead of the two competing for one copy.
- **Walkthrough**: `Register(IBrokerConsumerBuilder consumers)` (`:24`) chains six `RegisterIntegrationEventConsumer<T>()` calls (`:26-31`): `AttendeeCheckedIn` (the check-in points award), `SessionFeedbackSubmitted` and `EventFeedbackSubmitted` (the feedback points awards), `UserDeleted` (the per-aggregate erasure handlers), and `UserRegistered` plus `UserEmailVerified` (the ticket-link handlers). Each registration routes a delivered message through the framework's inbox-guarded consumer ([`IntegrationEventConsumer<TEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#integrationeventconsumertevent)) to the in-process handlers for that event, for example [`AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler`](#attendeecheckedinpointshandler), [`UserDeletedPointsHandler`](#userdeletedpointshandler) and [`UserRegisteredTicketLinkHandler`](#userregisteredticketlinkhandler).
- **Why it's built this way**: a broker subscription that silently disappears stays invisible until points or erasures stop happening, so the list is a plain value a unit test can read and a bicep test can compare against the deployed Service Bus topology. Redelivery is safe because the consumer side is idempotent ([ADR-021](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/021-consumer-inbox-idempotency.html)), and the transport is the framework's own broker layer ([ADR-118](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/118-message-transport-library-policy.html)). The check-in and points flow these subscriptions serve is [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html).
- **Where it's used**: passed as `EngagementBrokerConsumers.Register` to `AddBrokerMessaging` in the host (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:224`, with the numbered comment at `:178-186`). Asserted by [`BrokerConsumersTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) and cross-checked against the infrastructure template by `BrokerTopologyBicepTests`.

### EventFeedback

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Feedback` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Feedback/EventFeedback.razor.cs:17` · Level 4 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the attendee event-feedback page (`@page "/feedback/event/{EventId:int}"`, `EventFeedback.razor:1`). It loads the event name and its dynamic question set, pre-fills any answers the attendee already submitted, posts the answered questions back as a single atomic upsert (BR-107, per the class doc comment at `EventFeedback.razor.cs:13-16`), then deletes any saved answer the attendee blanked. A refused submit reports the server's own stated message and lists its field errors in the page's `ErrorSummary`, while an unexpected fault keeps a generic toast. A failed load offers a Retry, while an event that does not exist does not. The route id arrives already typed (`[Parameter] EventIdentifierType EventId`, `:25`) and a change of that id reloads the form in place.
- **Depends on**: [`IQuestionLookupService`](#iquestionlookupservice), [`IEventFeedbackUIService`](#ieventfeedbackuiservice), [`IEventLookupService`](group-21-conference-ui.md#ieventlookupservice), [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice), [`QuestionDTO`](group-17-conference-domain.md#questiondto), [`EventQuestionAnswerDTO`](group-17-conference-domain.md#eventquestionanswerdto), [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid) (the answer state, `:65`), [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel), [`ModelValidation`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#modelvalidation), [`DataAnnotationsModelValidator`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#dataannotationsmodelvalidator), [`LatestLoadGuard`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#latestloadguard) (the superseding-load guard, `:40`) and [`DetailLoadState`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#detailloadstate) (through the markup's `DetailLoadStateContent`, `EventFeedback.razor:27`). Externals: Blazor `NavigationManager`, MudBlazor `MudForm` / `BreadcrumbItem`, `System.Globalization`, and from the markup an injected `IStringLocalizer<EventFeedback>` `L` (`EventFeedback.razor:8`) plus the shared `UnsavedChangesGuard` (`EventFeedback.razor:12`) and `ErrorSummary` (`EventFeedback.razor:125`) components. The failure path also uses the `Result` type's `HasErrorType` / `NotifyOnFailure` helpers and `ErrorType.Unexpected` (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:263`, `:270`), and the submit and delete awaits take `LifetimeToken`.
- **Concept**: the dynamic feedback form (the answer state, the validation delegates, the required-answer gate, the `UnsavedChangesGuard` pairing and the `StateHasChanged`-before-navigate ordering) is taught on [`SessionFeedback`](#sessionfeedback) and is the same shape here: both pages hold their questions, answers, saved ids and missing-required set in one [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid), here closed over `EventQuestionAnswerIdentifierType` (`:65`). The submit strategy matches the session page: `SubmitFeedbackAsync` calls `FeedbackService.SubmitAnswersAsync` once with the whole answered set (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:218`), so the server applies the batch atomically and there is nothing partial left to report. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` still applies: an unanswered required question, rating included, is caught locally before any request (`:199-203`), an empty submit on an all-optional form sends no batch (`:216`), and a failed submit leaves `_isDirty` set so the same Submit button retries. Two things carry over from the session page. First, the submit and delete awaits read `LifetimeToken` (`:32`, `_cts.LifetimeToken()`) instead of `_cts.Token`: reading `Token` off a disposed source throws `ObjectDisposedException`, whereas `Dispose` cancels before it disposes, so a handler resuming after navigation gets a cancelled token and exits through its `OperationCanceledException` path. Second, a refused submit goes through `ReportSubmitFailure` (`:261-271`): an `ErrorType.Unexpected` result (a 500, transport failure or timeout) keeps the generic `Snackbar.SubmitFailed` toast (`:263-267`), while any other refusal is stored in `_submitResult` (`:80`, `:269`) so `ErrorSummary` lists its field errors after the snackbar times out, and `NotifyOnFailure` toasts the server's own message (`:270`; ADR-027 Decision 9 carve-out per the method's doc comment). `_submitResult` is cleared at the start of each submit (`:206`).
- **Walkthrough of what differs from [`SessionFeedback`](#sessionfeedback)**
  - There is no precondition gate and no `_preconditionMessage`: an event either loads or it does not. `OnInitialized` (`EventFeedback.razor.cs:85-97`) builds both validation delegates, `_validateAnswerText` and `_validateAnswerEmail`, from one prototype [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel) and one `DataAnnotationsModelValidator(L)` (`:87-90`), and also builds the breadcrumb trail (`:91-96`).
  - Loading is parameter-driven. `OnParametersSetAsync` (`:99-108`) compares `EventId` with `_loadedEventId` (`:39`); a feedback deep link to another event while this form is open reuses the routed instance with only a new `EventId`, so a new id starts `LoadFormAsync` (`:110`) and an unchanged id does nothing.
  - `LoadFormAsync` (`:110-185`) first calls `_load.Begin()` (`:113`), which supersedes and cancels the previous event's load, then resets everything that belonged to the previous form, `_loadNotFound` and `_answerState = new()` included (`:116-122`). It resolves the event name from `EventLookup.GetAllAsync(token)` (`:127`), setting a localized `_loadError` when the lookup itself fails (`:131`); when the id is absent from it, it also sets `_loadNotFound` (`:141-142`). That flag (`:61`) picks the markup's `DetailLoadStateContent` state (`EventFeedback.razor:27`): `NotFound` for an event that does not exist, otherwise `Failed` with a Retry wired to `LoadFormAsync`. Each await is followed by `token.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` (`:128`, `:148`, `:160`), so a superseded load stops rather than writing stale state. The rest (the `"Event"` questions handed to `_answerState.SetQuestions` at `:156`, the saved answers fetched at `:159`) matches the session page step for step. A cancelled load is swallowed (`:173-176`), and `IsLoading` is cleared only when `_load.IsCurrent(generation)` still holds (`:177-184`), so a superseded load leaves the flag to the load that replaced it.
  - The pre-fill applies the same cross-entity guard in the page: `_answerState.PreFill` receives only answers whose `EventId` matches the current event (`:169-171`, the filter at `:170`), because questions are shared across events.
  - `SubmitFeedbackAsync` (`:187-253`) validates the form, then runs `_answerState.FlagMissingRequiredAnswers()`, and returns with a `Snackbar.RequiredFields` warning if either fails (`:189-203`). It takes `pending` from `_answerState.PendingAnswers()` (`:212`); if it is non-empty it posts the whole set in one call to `SubmitAnswersAsync(EventId, ...)` (`:216-218`), and on failure calls `ReportSubmitFailure` and returns with `_isDirty` still set (`:219-223`). It then deletes every saved answer the attendee blanked, from `_answerState.BlankedSavedAnswers()`, through `TryDeleteSavedAnswerAsync`, stopping at the first failed delete with the form still dirty (`:229-235`), so a submit never reports success while an old answer survives. Only then does it clear `_isDirty` and toast `Snackbar.FeedbackSubmitted` with `pending.Count` (`:237-238`). The id is the typed parameter, so there is no parse step.
  - `DeleteAnswerAsync` (`:273-288`) and the submit's blanked-answer loop share `TryDeleteSavedAnswerAsync` (`:296-312`): it returns `true` when no saved id exists, calls `FeedbackService.DeleteAnswerAsync(EventId, answerId, LifetimeToken)` (`:303`), toasts `Snackbar.ClearAnswerFailed` and returns `false` on failure (`:306-307`), and otherwise calls `_answerState.ClearSavedAnswer` (`:310`). A cleared answer leaves `_isDirty` as it is (`:277-278`): the delete commits only that answer on the server, so unsaved edits to other answers keep the unsaved-changes guard armed.
  - `NavigateBack` (`:314-315`) returns to the Conference event detail route, formatting the id with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`. The disposable pattern (`:317-340`) cancels and disposes `_cts` and disposes `_load` (`:328-330`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the page owns orchestration only, all I/O goes through injected UI service interfaces, which keeps it testable under bUnit and swappable per host. A single batch `SubmitAnswersAsync` call removes the partial-save case entirely: a refusal means nothing was written, so the retry story is a plain resend rather than a per-question accounting. Reloading from `OnParametersSetAsync` behind a `LatestLoadGuard` means a route change to a different event cannot leave the previous event's questions or answers on screen, or let a slow earlier load overwrite a newer one. Sharing the answer state with [`SessionFeedback`](#sessionfeedback) through [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid) rather than through a base page class keeps each page self-contained while the answer rules exist once.
- **Where it's used**: rendered at `/feedback/event/{EventId:int}`, reached from the public event detail page's `SubmitFeedback` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Public/Events/PublicEventDetail.razor.cs:196`). The same route is also expressed as [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths)`.EventFeedback(eventId)` (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:17`). Its dependencies are registered by the Engagement UI [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection-3). Component-tested by [`EventFeedbackTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the markup, the resource strings and `UnsavedChangesGuard`'s own behavior live outside this file; this section covers the code-behind plus the bindings its members exist to serve.

### SessionFeedback

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Feedback` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Feedback/SessionFeedback.razor.cs:16` · Level 6 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the attendee session-feedback page (`@page "/feedback/session/{SessionId:int}"`, `SessionFeedback.razor:1`). It checks three business preconditions before it will render the question form at all, then loads the dynamic question set, pre-fills any answers the attendee already submitted, posts the whole form back in one atomic call, and deletes any saved answer the attendee blanked. The question, answer and saved-id state sits in a [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid) instance closed over `SessionQuestionAnswerIdentifierType` (`:65`), so this class holds the lifecycle, the preconditions and the I/O.
- **Depends on**: [`IQuestionLookupService`](#iquestionlookupservice), [`ISessionFeedbackUIService`](#isessionfeedbackuiservice), [`IEntityService<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#ientityservicetentitydto-tidentifiertype) (bound as `IEntityService<SessionDTO, SessionIdentifierType>`, `SessionFeedback.razor.cs:20`), [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice), [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid), [`LatestLoadGuard`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#latestloadguard), [`DetailLoadState`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#detailloadstate) (through the markup's `DetailLoadStateContent`, `SessionFeedback.razor:27`), [`SessionDTO`](group-17-conference-domain.md#sessiondto), [`QuestionDTO`](group-17-conference-domain.md#questiondto), [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel), [`ModelValidation`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#modelvalidation) and [`DataAnnotationsModelValidator`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#dataannotationsmodelvalidator), [`SessionStatuses`](group-17-conference-domain.md#sessionstatuses)`.IsEligible` for the BR-49 check, plus the `IsNotFound()` result extension from `MMCA.Common.UI.Common`. Externals: Blazor `NavigationManager`, MudBlazor `MudForm` / `BreadcrumbItem`, and from the markup an injected `IStringLocalizer<SessionFeedback>` `L` (`SessionFeedback.razor:8`), the shared `UnsavedChangesGuard` component (`SessionFeedback.razor:12`) and `ErrorSummary` (`SessionFeedback.razor:136`). The failure path also uses the `Result` helpers `HasErrorType` / `NotifyOnFailure` with `ErrorType.Unexpected` (`SessionFeedback.razor.cs:291`, `:298`).
- **Concept introduced, the precondition-gated dynamic form.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` assesses component/logic separation: the markup lives in `SessionFeedback.razor`, the behavior in this `partial class`, and the form's answer state in [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid), so the page's flow is reviewable apart from its layout and its state rules. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` is the load-bearing category here and it shows up four times. First, `CheckPreconditions` (`SessionFeedback.razor.cs:191`) refuses *before* rendering inputs, so when feedback is not permitted the attendee gets one sentence explaining why rather than a form that fails on submit. Second, validation is declarative and single-sourced: `_validateAnswerText` (`:73`) and `_validateAnswerEmail` (`:77`) are two delegates built from [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel)'s annotations (`TextValue` and `EmailValue`) and handed to the text and email fields respectively, so the 4000-character rule is never written twice and the email-format rule lives on the model rather than in the page. Third, a required check covers what `MudForm` cannot: a star rating is not a form input, so form validation never blocks an unanswered required rating, and the missing-required set on the answer state (`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>.MissingRequired`, filled by `FlagMissingRequiredAnswers`, called at `:227`) does, for every question type, and drives the inline error on each question's field (`SessionFeedback.razor:72`, `:86`). Fourth, `UnsavedChangesGuard IsDirty="_isDirty"` wraps the page, so navigating away with unsaved edits prompts first. The dynamic part is the interesting one: the questions are data, not markup, so the render branches on the DTO's `QuestionType`. A `RATING` question gets the star control (`SessionFeedback.razor:63`); anything else goes through a `switch` over `question.QuestionType?.ToUpperInvariant()` (`SessionFeedback.razor:88`) that picks an email `MudTextField` bound to `EmailValue` and validated by `_validateAnswerEmail` (`case "EMAIL"`, `:90-93`) or a three-line multiline `MudTextField` (`:106`), and each field's required flag and `RequiredError` come from the DTO rather than from the page. `[Rubric §19, State Management]` covers the answer state; `[Rubric §27, i18n]` covers the fact that every visible string, error messages included, is an `L["..."]` lookup.
- **Walkthrough** (teaching order)
  - Injected services (`SessionFeedback.razor.cs:18-22`) and the `[Parameter] SessionIdentifierType SessionId` (`:24`) arrive from the route. The parameter is the typed id alias, and the route template carries the `:int` constraint (`SessionFeedback.razor:1`), so the router parses it and the page needs no parse step.
  - `LifetimeToken` (`:31`, `_cts.LifetimeToken()`) is the token the submit and delete awaits use. Reading `Token` off a disposed `CancellationTokenSource` throws `ObjectDisposedException`; `Dispose` cancels before it disposes, so a handler resuming after the attendee navigated away gets a cancelled token and stops through its `OperationCanceledException` path (`:28-30`).
  - `IsLoading` / `IsSubmitting` (`:41-42`) and `SubmitButtonText` (`:44-55`) drive the chrome: the button reads "Submitting" while a post is in flight, then "Update" or "Submit" depending on `_answerState.HasExistingFeedback` (`:53`). The private state fields hold the load error (`:57`), the `_loadNotFound` flag that says the error reports a session that does not exist rather than a failed load (`:59-60`), the precondition message (`:61`), the session title (`:62`), the `_answerState` (`:65`), the `MudForm` reference (`:66`), the `_isDirty` flag (`:67`), the two validation delegates (`:73`, `:77`) and `_submitResult` (`:80`), the last submit's refusal kept so `ErrorSummary` can list its field errors. `MarkDirty` (`:82`) is the one-line handler every input's `@bind-...:after` calls.
  - `OnInitialized` (`:85-97`) builds both delegates once, by handing a throwaway [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel) prototype, the `model => model.TextValue` and `model => model.EmailValue` selectors and one `DataAnnotationsModelValidator(L)` to `ModelValidation.ForProperty` (`:87-90`), and builds the three-item breadcrumb trail (`:91-96`). The strongly-typed `ForProperty` overload (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Validation/ModelValidation.cs:69`) is the right one here because these fields have no `For` expression and the value being validated has not been written to a model yet; the localizer resolves the `ErrorMessage` resource key ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)).
  - Loading is parameter-driven. `OnParametersSetAsync` (`:99-108`) compares `SessionId` with `_loadedSessionId` (`:38`); a feedback deep link to another session while this form is open reuses the routed instance with only a new `SessionId`, so a new id starts `LoadFormAsync` (`:110`) and an unchanged id does nothing. `LoadFormAsync` begins with `_load.Begin()` (`:113`), which supersedes and cancels the previous session's load, and resets everything that belonged to the previous form, including `_loadNotFound = false` and `_answerState = new()` (`:116-123`).
  - It then loads the session through `SessionService.GetByIdAsync(SessionId, false, token)` (`:128`). The failure branch (`:130-139`) splits the two reasons apart: `_loadNotFound = sessionResult.IsNotFound()` (`:134`) picks the page's own "session not found" wording for a genuine 404 and the generic load failure for anything else (`:135-137`). The same flag drives the markup's `DetailLoadStateContent` (`SessionFeedback.razor:27`), which offers a Retry wired to `LoadFormAsync` for a failed load and none for a session that does not exist.
  - `CheckPreconditions(session)` runs next (call at `:143`), and a returned message stops the load **before** any questions are fetched (`:144-148`). Only then does it load the `"Session"` questions (`:151`), hand them to `_answerState.SetQuestions` (`:160`), fetch the attendee's saved answers (`:163`), and pre-fill with `_answerState.PreFill` over only the answers whose `SessionId` matches this session (`:171-175`, the filter at `:174`): questions are shared across sessions, so a foreign answer would otherwise match by question id. Each await is followed by `token.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` (`:129`, `:152`, `:164`); `OperationCanceledException` is swallowed as expected on disposal or supersession (`:177-180`), and in `finally` `IsLoading` is cleared only when `_load.IsCurrent(generation)` still holds (`:181-188`), so a superseded load leaves the flag to the load that replaced it.
  - `CheckPreconditions` (`:191-213`) encodes three rules, each returning a localized message. BR-91 rejects service sessions (`session.IsServiceSession`, `:194`). BR-49 rejects any session [`SessionStatuses`](group-17-conference-domain.md#sessionstatuses)`.IsEligible` does not allow, an unset `Status` or `"Accepted"` (case-insensitive) are the only eligible values (`:200`), the same shared allow-list Conference applies elsewhere. BR-16 rejects unscheduled sessions, where `StartsAt` or `EndsAt` is null (`:207`), because session feedback is a time-gated action. Returning `null` means feedback is allowed.
  - `SubmitFeedbackAsync` (`:215`) validates the form and toasts a warning if it is invalid (`:222`), then runs `_answerState.FlagMissingRequiredAnswers()` and toasts the same `Snackbar.RequiredFields` warning and returns when it reports a gap (`:227-231`), so an unanswered required rating, or an entirely empty submit on a form with a required question, never reaches the server. It then takes the answered questions as a `pending` list of `(QuestionId, AnswerValue)` tuples from `_answerState.PendingAnswers()` (`:240`), which drops blanks. An empty list (possible only when every question is optional) sends no batch, rather than a request the batch endpoint would refuse as empty (`:242-244`). Otherwise it makes **one** call, `FeedbackService.SubmitAnswersAsync(SessionId, pending, LifetimeToken)` (`:246`), which the interface documents as applied atomically server-side (`IFeedbackUIService.cs:66-73`). `_submitResult` is reset to `null` first (`:234`). A failure therefore wrote nothing: the page calls `ReportSubmitFailure(result)` (`:249`, defined `:289-299`) and returns with `_isDirty` still set, so the same Submit button retries. That method keeps the generic `Snackbar.SubmitFailed` toast for an `ErrorType.Unexpected` result (a 500, transport failure or timeout, `:291-295`, the ADR-027 Decision 9 carve-out), and otherwise stores the result in `_submitResult` (`:297`) so `ErrorSummary` (`SessionFeedback.razor:136`) lists the field errors after the snackbar times out, and `NotifyOnFailure` toasts the server's own stated message (`:298`). After the batch it deletes each saved answer the attendee has since blanked (`_answerState.BlankedSavedAnswers()`), through the same `TryDeleteSavedAnswerAsync` the Clear button uses, and returns with the form still dirty at the first failed delete (`:254-263`): the upsert has no delete semantics, so without this step the submit would report success while the old answer survived. On success it clears `_isDirty` (`:265`), toasts the count (`:266`), then calls `StateHasChanged()` **before** `NavigateBack()` (`:269`, `:271`); the inline comment (`:267`) and the `BL0012` suppression note (`:268`) explain why: the flush lets `UnsavedChangesGuard`'s `IsDirty` parameter update before `NavigateTo` fires the `LocationChanging` handler, otherwise the guard would prompt over changes that were just saved.
  - `DeleteAnswerAsync` (`:301-316`) clears one previously-saved answer through `TryDeleteSavedAnswerAsync` (`:324-340`) and toasts `Snackbar.AnswerCleared` when it succeeds. That helper returns `true` when there is no saved id (`:326-329`), calls `FeedbackService.DeleteAnswerAsync(SessionId, answerId, LifetimeToken)` (`:331`), toasts `Snackbar.ClearAnswerFailed` and returns `false` on failure (`:332-336`), and otherwise calls `_answerState.ClearSavedAnswer(questionId)` (`:338`), which removes the id and resets the model (`TextValue` and `RatingValue`; `EmailValue` follows `TextValue`). A clear leaves `_isDirty` as it is (`:305-306`): the delete commits only that answer on the server, so unsaved edits to other answers keep the unsaved-changes guard armed.
  - `NavigateBack` (`:342-343`) returns to the Conference session detail route through `EngagementRoutePaths.SessionDetails(SessionId)`. The wire string for each answer comes from [`FeedbackAnswerModel`](#feedbackanswermodel)`.AnswerValue`, which the answer state calls.
  - `Dispose(bool)` / `Dispose()` (`:345-368`) implement the standard disposable pattern, cancelling and disposing `_cts` and disposing `_load` (`:356-358`) so in-flight loads stop when the attendee leaves.
- **Why it's built this way**: pushing the three business rules into one `CheckPreconditions` method keeps the render path binary (either a precondition message or the form) and makes each BR individually reviewable and individually testable. Keeping the answer state in [`FeedbackAnswers<TAnswerId>`](#feedbackanswerstanswerid) means the page replaces one object to discard a stale form, the pre-fill, required-gate, payload and blanked-answer rules can be read without the lifecycle code around them, and [`EventFeedback`](#eventfeedback) runs the identical rules. The single batch submit is the more consequential choice, and [`EventFeedback`](#eventfeedback) makes the same one: because the server applies a whole session form atomically, there is no partially-saved state to report to the attendee, so the failure path is a plain retry rather than a "3 of 5 saved" message. The cancellation-token discipline (the disposal-safe `LifetimeToken` on submit and delete, the superseding `LatestLoadGuard` token on load), the split between a stated refusal and an unexpected fault in `ReportSubmitFailure`, and the `StateHasChanged`-before-navigate ordering are correctness, not style.
- **Where it's used**: rendered at `/feedback/session/{SessionId:int}`, reached from the public session detail page's `SubmitFeedback` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Public/Sessions/PublicSessionDetail.razor.cs:318`). The same route is also expressed as [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths)`.SessionFeedback(sessionId)` (`EngagementRoutePaths.cs:18`). Its dependencies are registered by the Engagement UI [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection-3). Component-tested by [`SessionFeedbackTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the markup, the resource strings and `UnsavedChangesGuard`'s own behavior live outside this file. The BR numbers in the comments are the page's own claim about which business rule it implements; the authoritative statements live in the ADC specifications guide, not in this file.

### PointsAwarder

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.Services` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/Services/PointsAwarder.cs:30` · Level 10 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the only implementation of [IPointsAwarder](#ipointsawarder). It writes one award idempotently, or writes nothing when the rule is switched off or the account has been erased.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [PointsSettings](#pointssettings) via `IOptions<T>`, [PointsEntry](#pointsentry), [ErasedUserGuard](#eraseduserguard), [IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector), [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result); externals: `IOptions<T>`, `ILogger<T>` with `[LoggerMessage]`.
- **Concept introduced, the configuration kill switch and the value snapshot.** `[Rubric §17, DevOps & Deployment]` (assesses whether operational levers are configuration rather than code), `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`, and `[Rubric §11, Security]` in its anti-abuse sense. Three ideas are stated once here so no earn rule has to restate them. (1) The stored `Points` value is a SNAPSHOT of the configured award at the moment it was earned (`PointsAwarder.cs:14-17`), so retuning the economy mid-conference changes what the NEXT award is worth and never rewrites history: a total is always explainable by what the rules said when it was earned. (2) The unique index on `(UserId, ActivityType, SubjectKey)` is the source of truth for both idempotency and anti-farming (`:20-23`), which is what makes a replayed broker message and a farmed scan both land exactly once. (3) A configured `0` is a per-rule kill switch that takes one earn rule out of service without a deploy.
- **Walkthrough**: four constructor dependencies (`PointsAwarder.cs:30-34`), one method (`:37-96`).
  - Kill switch (`:44-52`): `settings.Value.GetPointsFor(activity)`; when the value is `<= 0` it logs at Debug and returns success without writing. `GetPointsFor` maps each of the six activities to its configured property and returns `0` only for an activity it does not map (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Points/PointsSettings.cs:49-59`). Every mapped property carries a non-zero default (`PointsSettings.cs:19-38`), so a missing configuration entry keeps its default award, and switching a rule off takes a deliberate `0`, which is what the comment at `:44-46` states. Writing nothing (rather than a zero-value row) keeps the ledger free of entries that would otherwise have to be filtered out of every read.
  - Erased-account guard (`:54-61`): `ErasedUserGuard.EnsureNotErasedAsync` checks the [ErasedUser](#eraseduser) record for the user (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/ErasedUsers/ErasedUserGuard.cs:26-70`). The guard itself returns a Forbidden failure, but here it is turned into a success no-op, logged at Debug, exactly like the disabled rule above, so the calling adapter does not log its award-rejected warning. Because every points adapter (the Conference feedback event included) comes through this method, the one check covers them all (`:54-56`).
  - Idempotency pre-check (`:65-74`): `ExistsAsync` on `(UserId, ActivityType, SubjectKey)`. The comment (`:65-66`) enumerates what lands here: a repeat scan, a second answer to the same feedback form, and a broker redelivery. All three leave as a clean success.
  - Create (`:76-78`): `PointsEntry.Create` validates its own invariants and returns a [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/PointsEntry.cs:76-104`), unwrapped with `TryGetValue(out var entry)` so the entry is non-null on the success branch. A failure here is the one case that propagates as a failure, because it means the caller passed something invalid.
  - Save with a race backstop (`:80-92`): the same `IsUniqueConstraintViolation` filter as [CreateBookmarkHandler](#createbookmarkhandler), but the verdict is the opposite one. Here a lost race is a SUCCESS (`:85-91`), because "the award the caller wanted now exists" is exactly the outcome requested; a bookmark create, by contrast, is a user-visible action whose duplicate the user should be told about.
  - Five `[LoggerMessage]` partials (`:98-111`): rule disabled, erased account, already awarded, and lost race all log at Debug, while an actual award logs at Information, so the conference-day log volume tracks real awards rather than no-ops.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class doc is explicit that the pre-check "is not the rule" (`:22-23`). Reading the index as the authority and the pre-check as an optimization is what keeps the concurrent case correct rather than merely unlikely.
- **Where it's used**: registered as `IPointsAwarder` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:90`) and called by the four award adapters listed under [IPointsAwarder](#ipointsawarder). Read back by [PointsService](#pointsservice) and by the data-subject export, where the ledger and the check-in history are exported as separate collections (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Exports/UserEngagementExportService.cs:55-57,117`).

### BookmarkCountsGrpcService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service.Grpc` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Grpc/BookmarkCountsGrpcService.cs:30` · Level 9 · class (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the server-side gRPC endpoint that publishes Engagement's in-process [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) over the wire. It is the counterpart of [`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter`](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter): the adapter runs inside Conference and speaks gRPC out, this service runs inside Engagement and answers.
- **Depends on**: [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) (injected via primary constructor, `:24`), and the generated proto base `BookmarkCountService.BookmarkCountServiceBase` plus the four messages from `bookmark_count.proto` (namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts.V1`, `:2`). Externals: `Grpc.Core` (`ServerCallContext`).
- **Concept, the server-side bridge.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`, `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`. This is the producer half of the pattern whose consumer half is taught in [Group 13](group-13-grpc-contracts.md): the module keeps one C# interface, the proto generates an abstract server base, and this thin subclass forwards one to the other. Because the interface did not change when Engagement moved out of the monolith, neither Conference's call sites nor Engagement's [`BookmarkCountService`](#bookmarkcountservice) had to change; only this bridge and its client twin were added. It mirrors, on the Engagement side, Conference's [`SessionBookmarksGrpcService`](group-20-conference-api-grpc.md#sessionbookmarksgrpcservice), completing the bidirectional Conference-Engagement gRPC pair.
- **Concept, a documented unauthenticated trust boundary.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether every exposed surface has a stated authorization posture. This endpoint is mapped **without** `.RequireAuthorization()` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:255`, with the reasoning restated at the call site, `:326-332`), and the class doc (`:11-22`) argues why the requirement is not addable rather than merely absent: the Conference callers serve `[AllowAnonymous]` output-cached REST endpoints (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/Speakers/SpeakerSessionsController.cs:71` and `:87`), so a cache-miss request from an anonymous visitor carries no bearer for [`JwtForwardingClientInterceptor`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#jwtforwardingclientinterceptor) to forward, and the public speaker pages would break. The exposure is bounded by the payload (aggregate counts per session id, no PII and no user ids on the wire) and by the network boundary: the Engagement container app's ingress is `external: false` (`MMCA.ADC/infra/main.bicep:1921`), so the endpoint stays on the internal service network and the Gateway never routes it. Contrast [`UserEngagementExportGrpcService`](#userengagementexportgrpcservice), which is mapped `.RequireAuthorization()` (`Program.cs:271`) because it carries personal data.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `GetBookmarkCountForSession(request, context)` (`:28-40`): null-guards both arguments with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` (`:32-33`), awaits `inner.GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync(request.SessionId, context.CancellationToken)` (`:35-37`), threading the gRPC call's own cancellation token (and therefore the client's deadline) through to the database, then wraps the `int` in a response message (`:39`).
  - `GetBookmarkCountsForSessions(request, context)` (`:43-61`): the batch rpc. It materializes the repeated field with a collection expression, `[.. request.SessionIds]` (`:51`), calls the interface's batch method, then projects the returned dictionary into repeated `SessionBookmarkCount` messages via `AddRange(... Select(...))` (`:55-59`).
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the wire endpoint a paper-thin forwarder means the real read logic (a `COUNT` under the soft-delete filter, over the `SessionId` index [`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration`](#usersessionbookmarkconfiguration) declares) lives once and is reused identically in-process and over gRPC. The endpoint is published through `AddGrpcServiceDefaults()` (`Program.cs:318`), which also installs the [`GrpcResultExceptionInterceptor`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#grpcresultexceptioninterceptor) and gRPC reflection; for these methods the interceptor has nothing to translate, since the interface returns bare values rather than a `Result`.
- **Where it's used**: mapped at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:255`, served over the service's `Http2`-only cleartext (h2c) endpoint ([ADR-012](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/012-grpc-host-transport.html)). Its remote caller is Conference.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class doc's own citations have drifted further. It names lines 385 and 405 of `SpeakersController.cs` (`:15-16`), a file that now has only 374 lines, and `infra/main.bicep:1289-1295` (`:20`), but the anonymous bookmark-count actions it describes have since moved out of `SpeakersController.cs` entirely, to `SpeakerSessionsController.cs:71` and `:87`, and the Engagement internal ingress is now at `infra/main.bicep:1921`. The argument still holds; only the citations are stale.

### ManualCheckInHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.UseCases.ManualCheckIn` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/ManualCheckIn/ManualCheckInHandler.cs:19` · Level 12 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the organizer's manual fallback for when a badge will not scan. No credential is involved: the attendee is named in the request, and after an erased-user check everything is the same core the scan path runs.
- **Depends on**: [IUnitOfWork](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [IEventLiveValidationService](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice), [ICurrentUserService](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice), [ErasedUserGuard](#eraseduserguard), [CheckInProcessor](#checkinprocessor), [CheckInResultDTO](#checkinresultdto), [ICommandHandler&lt;in TCommand, TResult&gt;](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult); externals: `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>`.
- **Concept reinforced, the shared core with a per-entry-point difference.** `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` and `[Rubric §11, Security]`. Compared with [CheckInAttendeeHandler](#checkinattendeehandler), the credential extraction and badge lookup are simply absent; `command.UserId` goes into the processor as given. The doc comment carries the compensating control (`ManualCheckInHandler.cs:14-18`): an organizer-only endpoint backs it, which is what makes naming another user acceptable here and unacceptable on the attendee-facing flows in this unit. The payoff is stated in the same comment: a manual check-in and a scanned one produce identical rows and events, so nothing downstream needs to know which door the check-in came through. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`: because the attendee id arrives in the request body, the handler first runs `ErasedUserGuard.EnsureNotErasedAsync` (`:44`, guard at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/ErasedUsers/ErasedUserGuard.cs:26`) and returns its failure unchanged (`:45-48`). The comment (`:41-43`) names the risk: an organizer working from a stale roster must not leave a check-in under an erased id that no erasure will ever revisit ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)).
- **Walkthrough**: five constructor dependencies (`:19-24`), one `HandleAsync` (`:27-67`). `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(command)` (`:31`), the same `RequireUserId("CheckIns.Forbidden")` caller guard as the scan path (`:33-37`, the organizer id taken at `:39`), the erased-user guard on `command.UserId` (`:44-48`), the delegation to `CheckInProcessor.ExecuteAsync` (`:50-59`), and a success-only Information log, gated on the same `result.TryGetValue(out var checkIn)` unwrap as the scan path (`:61-64`), whose template differs from the scan path only by the word "manually" (`:69-75`), which is what lets an operator tell the two apart in the logs even though the rows are identical.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the fallback on exactly the same core avoids the classic drift where the rarely used path slowly stops enforcing a rule the main path gained. The erased-user check sits in front of that core because this is the entry point where the attendee id is typed in rather than resolved from a badge.
- **Where it's used**: [CheckInsController](#checkinscontroller) (injected at `CheckInsController.cs:46`, called from `ManualCheckInAsync` at `:134`).

### UserEngagementExportGrpcService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service.Grpc` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Grpc/UserEngagementExportGrpcService.cs:27` · Level 12 · class (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the server-side gRPC endpoint that publishes Engagement's in-process [`IUserEngagementExportService`](#iuserengagementexportservice) to the Identity service, so Identity can fold a user's Engagement-owned personal data into the aggregated data-subject export document. Same server-bridge shape as [`BookmarkCountsGrpcService`](#bookmarkcountsgrpcservice), with two extra concerns: only the subject (or a privileged caller) may read the export, and timestamps and enums have to survive a proto3 wire crossing.
- **Depends on**: [`IUserEngagementExportService`](#iuserengagementexportservice) (primary constructor, `:27`) and its DTOs from `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Exports` (`:4`); the generated base `UserEngagementExportService.UserEngagementExportServiceBase` and the messages from `user_engagement_export.proto` (namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts.V1`, `:3`); the framework's [`GrpcWireFormat`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#grpcwireformat) from `MMCA.Common.Grpc` (`:6`); `IsServiceCaller()` from [`ServiceCallerClaimsPrincipalExtensions`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#servicecallerclaimsprincipalextensions) (`MMCA.Common.Grpc.Authentication`, `:7`), `GetUserId()` / `HasRole` from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Auth` (`:8`, see [`ClaimsPrincipalExtensions`](group-08-auth.md#claimsprincipalextensions)), and [`RoleNames`](group-24-identity-module.md#rolenames)`.Organizer` (`:5`). Externals: `Grpc.Core` (`ServerCallContext`, `RpcException`), `System.Globalization` (`:1`).
- **Concept, cross-service data-subject export as a purpose-built read contract.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether a real data-subject-access and portability path exists; `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses talking through explicit contracts. Identity owns the export document but not Engagement's data, so it depends only on the narrow interface; this class is the producer half over the wire, twin to the client-side [`UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapter`](#userengagementexportservicegrpcadapter). The class doc (`:12-19`) enumerates session bookmarks, submitted session questions, the points ledger, leaderboard participation, and check-in history; the method also forwards poll votes, question upvotes and ticket records, which the doc comment does not name (`:96-125`). Unlike the bookmark-count endpoint, this one is mapped `.RequireAuthorization()` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:271`, with the contrast drawn at `:252`), which is the posture difference personal data justifies.
- **Concept, the subject check behind a forwarded token.** `[Rubric §11, Security]`. The edge forwards the end user's JWT, so an authenticated caller is not yet an authorized one: the method throws `PermissionDenied` unless the caller's own user id equals `request.UserId`, the caller is a service, or the caller holds `RoleNames.Organizer`, the export privilege Identity's export endpoint grants (`:38-45`). Without it any signed-in user could request another user's export by id.
- **Concept, proto3 has no nulls and no `DateTime`.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`. Three encoding decisions are made here and mirrored exactly on the client:
  - **Timestamps**: SQL Server hands back `DateTimeKind.Unspecified` values, and the round-trip "O" format omits the `Z` marker for that kind, so each value goes through `GrpcWireFormat.FormatUtc` (`:62`, `:69`, `:78`, `:100`, `:105`), which stamps `DateTimeKind.Utc` before formatting (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.Grpc/GrpcWireFormat.cs:42-43`). The format is written once in the framework and called by both ends of the contract. The doc comment (`:20-25`) is careful about what this is: the stored values are already UTC, so this restores a marker rather than converting an instant. `CheckedInOn` is a `DateTimeOffset`, already carrying its offset, and is formatted as-is with `"O"` (`:92-94`); the ticket's `InvitedOn` and `LinkedOn` are also formatted directly with `"O"` (`:119`, `:124`).
  - **Absent values**: an absent leaderboard name travels as the empty string (`:55-57`), an absent `SessionId`/`SponsorId` as `0` (`:87-90`), and an absent ticket `OrderEmail` or `InvitedOn` as the empty string (`:116-119`), each with the comment naming the client-side inverse.
  - **Enums**: `ActivityType` (`:73-75`), `Scope` (`:82-84`) and the ticket's `LinkMethod` (`:121-123`) cross as their numeric values, justified in place: the points activity numbers are part of the idempotency key, the scope numbers are named literally in the SQL index filters ([`CheckInConfiguration`](#checkinconfiguration), `CheckInConfiguration.cs:25-27`), and the link-method numbers are persisted, so none is ever renumbered.
- **Walkthrough**: one overridden method, `GetUserEngagementExport(request, context)` (`:31-128`). It null-guards both arguments (`:35-36`), runs the subject check (`:41-45`), awaits `inner.GetUserEngagementExportAsync(request.UserId, context.CancellationToken)` (`:47-49`), then builds the response: the two scalar leaderboard fields in the initializer (`:51-58`), then seven `AddRange(... Select(...))` projections filling the repeated fields: bookmarks (`:59-63`), submitted questions with their `Text` (`:64-70`), points entries (`:71-79`), check-ins (`:80-95`), poll votes (`:96-101`, `LivePollId`, `OptionId` and a `FormatUtc` `CreatedOn`), question upvotes (`:102-106`, `QuestionId` and a `FormatUtc` `CreatedOn`) and tickets (`:107-125`: event id, source event name, external ticket id, ticket type, attendee names, order email, invite and link timestamps, link method).
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the endpoint a thin forwarder leaves the real work (server-side projections that the soft-delete query filter already narrows to active rows) in [`UserEngagementExportService`](#userengagementexportservice), reused identically in-process and over gRPC ([ADR-012](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/012-grpc-host-transport.html)). Because the read returns a DTO rather than a `Result`, the [`GrpcResultExceptionInterceptor`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#grpcresultexceptioninterceptor) has no failure trailer to translate and a transport fault becomes a gRPC status the caller's resilience pipeline handles; the subject check is the one deliberate `RpcException`.
- **Where it's used**: mapped at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:271`. Its remote caller is Identity's [`ExportUserDataHandler`](group-24-identity-module.md#exportuserdatahandler) via [`UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapter`](#userengagementexportservicegrpcadapter). Covered by [`UserEngagementExportGrpcServiceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), the integration `UserEngagementExportGrpcTests`, `UserDataExportGrpcCallerTests` and the posture checks in `GrpcViewAsPostureTests`.
