### UserDeletedPointsHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.IntegrationEventHandlers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedPointsHandler.cs:38` · Level 8 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the erasure handler for the leaderboard. When Identity deletes an account, this takes the entry off the public board and overwrites the display name it published there. It is the one consumer in this folder that awards nothing.
- **Depends on**: [`ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent) closed over Identity's [`UserDeleted`](group-24-identity-module.md#userdeleted) (`:40`), [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:50`), the [`IRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#irepositorytentity-tidentifiertype) it obtains for [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin) (`:51`) and that aggregate's own `Delete()` / `EraseDisplayName()` members (`:69`, `:81`). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` (`:96-103`).
- **Concept introduced, cross-database erasure by event.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether a deletion promise actually reaches every copy of the data. Under database-per-service ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)) Identity cannot delete a row in the Engagement database, so an erasure has to travel as an event and be carried out by the owning service. The class comment (`:13-21`) names the exact scope: the leaderboard is the one place Engagement holds a name rather than a scalar id, `LeaderboardOptIn.DisplayName` is a snapshot the attendee published at opt-in, and without this handler that name would keep sitting in the table after the account was erased. It also names what is deliberately left alone: the points ledger, because a `PointsEntry` carries a scalar user id and an opaque subject key and names nobody, the same posture already applied to session bookmarks. That is the [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html) distinction between soft-delete for lifecycle and erasure for personal data, applied per column rather than per table. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` covers the retry posture stated at `:26-27`: exceptions are deliberately not caught, so a failure is logged once by the base and then propagates, and the outbox and the broker retry it rather than acking it away with a log line (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/DomainEvents/ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase.cs:26-33`). The award adapters share that exception posture, because they share the base; what differs is what they do with a *rejected* award, which they log and move past, whereas this handler has no such branch: a missed point is a nuisance, a missed erasure is a broken promise.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleScopedAsync` (`:43-46`) is the override; the base has null-guarded the event and opened the per-delivery scope. The body takes the user id (`:48`), then reaches the scoped [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:50`) and a tracked repository for [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin) (`:51`) out of the supplied provider.
  - The read (`:56-61`) is the subtle line. It passes `asTracking: true` (mutations follow) and `ignoreQueryFilters: true`, and the comment (`:53-55`) explains that the flag is load-bearing here for the opposite reason it is used on the join path: an attendee who left the board earlier still has a soft-deleted row carrying the published name, and a filtered read would walk straight past the very row that has to be erased.
  - The loop (`:65-84`) does two independent things per row. If the row is not already deleted it calls `Delete()` and, on failure, logs and moves to the next row rather than aborting the batch (`:67-77`). If the display name is not already erased it calls `EraseDisplayName()` (`:79-83`). Either action sets `changed`.
  - When nothing changed the handler logs and returns without a save (`:86-90`); otherwise it saves once for the whole batch and logs the row count (`:92-93`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the two-flag loop is what makes the handler idempotent in both directions (`:22-25`): an account that never joined the board has no row and writes nothing, and an account already off the board with an erased name reaches the same end state and writes nothing again. At-least-once delivery makes redelivery normal, so that property is a requirement rather than a nicety.
- **Where it's used**: registered as a singleton by the convention scan (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`, `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/DependencyInjection.ModuleScanning.cs:58-63`), with the consumer wired at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:29`; the host's composition comment (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:201-205`) records that this is the one consumer here that earns nothing. Covered by [`UserDeletedPointsHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the privacy commitment the comment cites (PRIVACY.md section 5) lives in the ADC repo's private docs, not in this file. What `EraseDisplayName()` writes in place of the name is defined on [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin).

### AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.IntegrationEventHandlers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/IntegrationEventHandlers/AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandler.cs:45` · Level 12 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the award adapter for check-ins. It turns an [`AttendeeCheckedIn`](#attendeecheckedin) into the (activity, subject key) pair the ledger understands and hands it to [`IPointsAwarder`](#ipointsawarder). It is the richest of the award adapters because the incoming scope is a string that has to be mapped, and because session check-ins are also gated by a once-per-time-slot rule (`:27-36`).
- **Depends on**: [`ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent) closed over [`AttendeeCheckedIn`](#attendeecheckedin) (`:48`), [`IPointsAwarder`](#ipointsawarder) (`:69`), [`SessionTimeSlotPoints`](#sessiontimeslotpoints) (`:93-99`), [`IEventLiveValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) (`:94`), [`ErrorType`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype) (`:104`), [`CheckInScopeNames`](#checkinscopenames) (`:122`, `:129`, `:140`), [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) and [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys) (`:124-125`, `:132-133`, `:143-144`). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, `IUnitOfWork`, `StringComparison.Ordinal`, source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` (`:153-160`).
- **Concept introduced, treating an unknown contract value as data, not as a fault.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses how a consumer behaves when the producer is ahead of it. The class comment (`:20-26`) states the rule: the scope arrives as a wire string rather than an enum, so a value this build has never heard of is normal contract evolution, and the handler logs a warning and awards nothing instead of throwing and dead-lettering a message that no retry could ever fix. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` is the practical consequence: an unmappable payload cannot wedge the queue. The time-slot lookup deliberately takes the opposite stance for a genuine fault (`:30-35`): when Conference cannot be reached the handler throws so the delivery is retried, rather than awarding in breach of the rule or silently dropping a legitimate award. `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` is the same boundary its siblings keep, stated in this file's own words (`:18-19`): all the ADC vocabulary lives here and the awarder below it knows nothing about events or sessions.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleScopedAsync` (`:51-79`) is the override. The base has already null-guarded the event and opened the delivery scope, so the first thing the body does is call `TryMapAward` (`:56`), before resolving anything: an unmappable event costs no service resolution and no database work, only the warning at `:58`.
  - For a `SessionCheckIn` activity only (`:62`), it then asks `HasEarlierCheckInInTimeSlotAsync` (`:63`, defined at `:87-111`) whether an earlier overlapping session check-in already earned the slot. If so it logs at Information (`:65`, `:156-157`) and returns without awarding; event and sponsor awards never reach this check. The helper delegates to [`SessionTimeSlotPoints`](#sessiontimeslotpoints)`.HasEarlierOverlappingCheckInAsync` (`SessionTimeSlotPoints.cs:52`), resolving the `IUnitOfWork` and [`IEventLiveValidationService`](group-17-conference-domain.md#ieventlivevalidationservice) from the delivery scope (`:93-94`). Its failure policy (`:101-110`): success returns the answer, a `NotFound` from Conference means the rule cannot apply so the award proceeds (`:104-105`), and any other failure throws `InvalidOperationException` naming the error codes, which fails the delivery so it is retried.
  - Then it resolves the scoped [`IPointsAwarder`](#ipointsawarder) from the supplied provider (`:69`) and awards with the event's `CheckedInOn.UtcDateTime` (`:71-76`). A rejected award is logged at Warning with the activity, the user and the subject key (`:78-79`), not rethrown.
  - `TryMapAward` (`:117`) is three ordinal string comparisons in scope order. `Event` maps to `PointsActivityType.EventCheckIn` scoped by `PointsSubjectKeys.ForEvent` (`:122-126`). `Session` maps to `SessionCheckIn` only when the payload actually carries a session id, using a property pattern (`:129-134`). `Sponsor` maps to `SponsorVisit` under the same condition on the sponsor id (`:140-145`), and the comment above it (`:137-139`) explains why a Sponsor scope with no sponsor id falls through to the same log-and-skip as an unknown scope: an award scoped to nothing would collide with every other sponsor-less payload on the ledger's uniqueness rule.
  - The fall-through sets `activity = default`, an empty subject key, and returns `false` (`:148-150`), which is the single exit the caller's guard reads.
- **Why it's built this way**: this handler is where the module's most interesting delivery property lives. The event is published by the same service that consumes it, so the check-in write and the award are two separate transactions joined by the broker (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:207-214`). That keeps the scan endpoint's latency independent of the points write and lets the award retry on its own. The same comment records the fallback if a deployment ever has trouble with the round trip (`:215-217`): the award could move to an in-module domain event handler on the same `CheckIn` creation, which is a one-file change because the module already awards session-question points that way, through [`SessionQuestionSubmittedPointsHandler`](#sessionquestionsubmittedpointshandler).
- **Where it's used**: registered as a singleton by the convention scan (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`, `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/DependencyInjection.ModuleScanning.cs:58-63`), which is why the base opens a scope per delivery (`:23-27`); the consumer is wired at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:26`. Covered by [`AttendeeCheckedInPointsHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: how many points each activity is worth, and whether a rule is switched off, is decided inside [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) from configuration, not here.

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Points/MyPoints.razor.cs:16` · Level 5 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the attendee's own points page (`@page "/points"`, `MyPoints.razor:1`, `@attribute [Authorize]`, `MyPoints.razor:2`). It shows the running total, the ledger entries behind it, the leaderboard opt-in switch, and the public board.

- **Concept introduced, making a stateful child control follow the server.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses who owns a visible piece of state. A `MudSwitch` keeps its own checked state, and Blazor re-parameterizes a child only when a parameter actually changes, so after a rejected write the control would keep showing what the attendee clicked while the page holds what the server accepted. The page solves it with a render key: `_switchGeneration` (`:55`) is bound as `@key` on the switch (`MyPoints.razor:74`) and incremented whenever the server's value disagrees with the requested one (`:167-170`), which re-mounts the control and forces it to drop its internal state. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` covers the second decision in the same method: a failed write and a failed read-back are reported differently (`:133-136`), because conflating them made a refresh blip force the switch back to the pre-write value and show the opposite of the server state. A third decision sits on the failed-write branch: `SaveErrorMessage` (`:180-183`) looks for the one refusal the attendee can fix, the error code `Points.DisplayNameUnavailable` (`DisplayNameUnavailableCode`, `:26`, raised for a caller with no display name on their token), and answers it with its own localized advice (`Error.DisplayNameUnavailable`); every other failure keeps the generic `Error.SaveFailed`, so the server's diagnostic text is never surfaced (`:173-179`). `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` covers both the `L["..."]` resource lookups and the culture-aware timestamp rendering ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)).
- **Concept introduced, a page that reads failures instead of catching them.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` and `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` both show in one detail: `LoadAsync` returns [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) (`:95`) rather than throwing, and it composes the two service calls by propagating their errors (`:98-101`, `:108-111`). The only exception the page catches is `OperationCanceledException` on disposal (`:81-84`, `:153-156`), so the error state is driven by a value the UI service returned, not by an exception type the page has to recognize. `SaveErrorMessage` follows the same rule: it branches on the `Code` of the returned errors, not on an exception type.
- **Walkthrough** (teaching order)
  - `EntryPageSize` (`:19`) fixes the activity feed at 20 entries per read; `DisplayNameUnavailableCode` (`:26`) names the one refusal code the page recognizes; the injected [`IPointsUIService`](#ipointsuiservice) (`:28`) and [`ViewerTimeZone`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#viewertimezone) (`:29`), a `CancellationTokenSource` (`:31`) and the breadcrumb list (`:38`) follow. `LifetimeToken` (`:36`) wraps `_cts.LifetimeToken()`: reading `Token` off a disposed source throws `ObjectDisposedException`, and `Dispose` cancels before it disposes, so a load or handler that resumes after the attendee navigated away gets a cancelled token and stops through its `OperationCanceledException` path (comment `:33-35`). Every service call below passes `LifetimeToken` rather than `_cts.Token`. `IsLoading` is `protected` with a private setter (`:41`) so component tests can observe the first load.
  - The private state (`:43-49`) is a load error, a save error, an in-flight save latch, the total, the opt-in flag, the entries and the board. `_switchGeneration` (`:55`) is the render key described above.
  - `OnInitializedAsync` (`:57`) is not `async`: it builds the two-item breadcrumb trail (`:59-63`) and returns the task of `LoadPageAsync` (`:65`).
  - `LoadPageAsync` (`:69`) is the whole load cycle and, per its doc comment (`:68`), also the Retry action: the markup's error alert binds it as `OnRetry` (`MyPoints.razor:21`). It sets `IsLoading` and clears the previous load error first (`:71-72`), so a retry starts from the loading state rather than leaving the old error on screen, then awaits `LoadAsync` and sets the localized load error when it comes back a failure (`:76-79`), swallows `OperationCanceledException` as expected on disposal (`:81-84`), and clears `IsLoading` in `finally` (`:85-88`).
  - `LoadAsync` (`:95`) makes two calls: the caller's ledger (`:97`) and the public board (`:107`). Each is unwrapped with `TryGetValue` and short-circuits into `Result.Failure` carrying the service's own errors (`:98-101`, `:108-111`). Both are re-read after an opt-in change, because joining adds a row to the board and leaving removes one (`:91-94`).
  - `OnParticipationChangedAsync` (`:123`) returns early when a save is already in flight (`:125-128`), latches `_isSaving` and clears the previous save error (`:130-131`), then writes through `SetLeaderboardParticipationAsync` (`:139`). A failed write sets the message chosen by `SaveErrorMessage(write)` (`:140-143`); a successful write followed by a failed refresh sets the refresh-failed message instead and adopts the requested value locally (`:144-151`) so the key guard below does not re-mount the switch back onto a stale reading.
  - `SaveErrorMessage` (`:180-183`) is an expression-bodied method that tests `write.Errors.Any(...)` for an error whose `Code` equals `DisplayNameUnavailableCode` under `StringComparison.Ordinal`, returning the display-name advice when it matches and the generic save message otherwise.
  - `ActivityLabel` (`:192-202`) maps each [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) member to a resource key by an explicit switch rather than by enum name, so a renamed member breaks the build instead of silently rendering a missing key (`:185-191`).
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync` (`:209-215`) calls `ViewerTime.EnsureResolvedAsync(LifetimeToken)` on the first render only, once JS is available, and calls `StateHasChanged` when the zone changed, so award times move from the UTC fallback to the viewer's clock.
  - `FormatOccurredOn` (`:225-226`) delegates to `ViewerTime.Format`. The comment (`:217-222`) gives the reason: `ViewerTimeZone.Format` reads an `Unspecified` value as UTC, so a serializer that drops the UTC marker cannot shift the reading, whereas `DateTime.ToLocalTime` would use the server's clock on Blazor Server and during prerender.
  - `Dispose(bool)` / `Dispose()` (`:230-250`) are the standard disposable pattern with a `_disposed` latch, cancelling and disposing `_cts` so an in-flight load stops when the attendee navigates away.
- **Why it's built this way**: the page makes one promise, that the switch shows the server's state and not the click's, and both the key bump and the split error messages exist to keep it. Everything else is orchestration only: all I/O goes through [`IPointsUIService`](#ipointsuiservice), which keeps the page testable under bUnit and swappable per host.
- **Where it's used**: routed at `/points`, the value of [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths)`.MyPoints` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementRoutePaths.cs:26`). Component-tested by [`MyPointsTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the tables, the empty states and every visible string live in `MyPoints.razor` and the resource files. Whether the page is reachable at all depends on the `Engagement.Points` feature gate on [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller), which is configuration. The refusal code is raised by `SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler` (named in the `DisplayNameUnavailableCode` comment, `:23`); the page only recognizes the code string.

### BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure.Caching` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Caching/BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessor.cs:35` · Level 4 · sealed class

- **What it is**: a `BackgroundService` that turns "a bookmark changed" into at most one cross-service cache eviction every ten seconds per replica. It drains the capacity-one flag held by [`BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal`](#bookmarkcacheevictionsignal) and publishes an `OutputCacheEvictionRequested` for the Conference session tag, so Conference's cached session reads and batched star counts stop serving stale numbers.
- **Depends on**: [`BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal`](#bookmarkcacheevictionsignal) (`:36`), [`UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler`](#usersessionbookmarkcacheevictionhandler) for the `SessionsCacheTag` constant (`:73`), [`BestEffort`](group-03-querying-specifications.md#besteffort) (`:62`). Externals: `BackgroundService`, `IServiceScopeFactory`, `TimeProvider`, `ILogger`, `IEventBus`, `OutputCacheEvictionRequested`.
- **Concept introduced, coalescing with a flag and a pacing delay.** `[Rubric §10, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether a hot write path can hammer a shared cache. Two pieces cooperate. The signal is a `Channel<bool>` bounded at one with `BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite` (`BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:27-33`), so any number of `Request()` calls made while one is pending collapse into that one (`:42`). The processor then sleeps `PacingWindow` (ten seconds, `:46`) after each broadcast (`:79`). Together the pacing, not the bookmark rate, sets the eviction rate: at a session changeover hundreds of attendees star sessions in the same minute, and an eviction per star would keep the session cache permanently cold and send every read to Conference's database (the signal's remarks, `BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:11-18`). The pacing window is worst-case six evictions a minute per replica (doc comment `:41-45`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `ExecuteAsync` (`:52`) loops on `signal.Reader.WaitToReadAsync` and does a single `TryRead` to empty the flag (`:60`), so anything raised after that read is the next broadcast's business.
  - The publish runs inside `BestEffort.ExecuteAsync` (`:62`) under the operation name `"bookmark-cache-evict-broadcast"` (`:49`). It opens a fresh async scope (`:67`), resolves `IEventBus` (`:68`) and publishes `OutputCacheEvictionRequested` with `Tags = [UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler.SessionsCacheTag]` (`:70-75`). A failed publish is a Warning plus a metric, never an exception out of the loop.
  - `Task.Delay(PacingWindow, timeProvider, stoppingToken)` (`:79`) takes the injected `TimeProvider`, so tests drive the pacing with a fake clock rather than waiting ten real seconds.
  - An `OperationCanceledException` raised while the host is stopping is caught and ends the loop (`:82`); a request still pending at that moment is covered by Conference's TTL backstop (comment `:84`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the eviction is a convenience over a TTL, not a correctness mechanism, so it is best effort and never blocks or fails the bookmark command that raised it (the signal's `Request` never blocks or fails, `BookmarkCacheEvictionSignal.cs:21-22`). The processor is a long-lived singleton, so it opens a scope per publish rather than holding a scoped bus. The wider caching story is [ADR-040](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/040-authenticated-output-caching-for-public-reads.html), the helper is [ADR-096](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/096-best-effort-side-effects.html) and the in-process work-queue shape is [ADR-121](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/121-ephemeral-in-process-work-queue.html).
- **Where it's used**: raised through the signal by [`UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler`](#usersessionbookmarkcacheevictionhandler); the signal and processor are registered in the module's Application and Infrastructure `DependencyInjection.cs`, and the Conference service host references it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs`). Covered by `BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessorTests` (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure.Tests/Caching/BookmarkCacheEvictionProcessorTests.cs`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: one flag per replica, so with several Engagement replicas each broadcasts independently; the code does not dedupe across replicas. The Conference-side TTL value is not defined in this file.

### ExpireTicketRosterImportInternalCommand

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.ExpireRosterImport` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ExpireRosterImport/ExpireTicketRosterImportInternalCommand.cs:14` · Level 4 · record (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the delayed privacy backstop of one roster import run. A durable internal command whose whole payload is the run id (`:14`), handled by [`ExpireTicketRosterImportHandler`](#expireticketrosterimporthandler).
- **Depends on**: [`IInternalCommand`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#iinternalcommand) (`:1`, `:14`) and [`InternalCommandNameAttribute`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#internalcommandnameattribute), which names it `Engagement.ExpireTicketRosterImport.v1` (`:13`); the `TicketImportRunIdentifierType` alias. No externals.
- **Concept introduced, a deadline scheduled as a second command.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether personal data has a bounded lifetime. The doc comment (`:5-11`) states the contract: the command is scheduled in the same transaction as the run and falls due [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun)`.AbandonAfter` later, which is 30 minutes (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketImportRun.cs:37`). When it runs, a still-active run is ended as abandoned and any run's staged roster is cleared, so the uploaded file's holder data cannot outlive the run by more than that window. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` covers the failure it exists for: it only matters when [`ProcessTicketRosterImportInternalCommand`](#processticketrosterimportinternalcommand) never got to end the run because its row dead-lettered (`:8-10`). The doc cites ADR-005 (erasure) and [ADR-114](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/114-internal-commands-durable-job-queue.html) (the durable internal-command queue).
- **Walkthrough**: a positional record with one member, `RunId` (`:14`). The versioned name on the attribute (`:13`) is what the internal-command queue identifies the row by, not the CLR type name.
- **Where it's used**: scheduled by [`StartTicketRosterImportHandler`](#startticketrosterimporthandler) with the `TicketImportRun.AbandonAfter` delay, right after the processing command (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/StartRosterImport/StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:121-123`); handled by [`ExpireTicketRosterImportHandler`](#expireticketrosterimporthandler). Named in `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.ADC.Architecture.Tests/Cqrs/CommandValidatorCoverageTests.cs` and exercised by `ExpireTicketRosterImportHandlerTests` and `StartTicketRosterImportHandlerTests`.

### ITicketUIService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Tickets/ITicketUIService.cs:20` · Level 4 · interface (public)

- **What it is**: the UI-side contract for everything ticket-related a page can do. Organizers dry-run, import, track, invite, link, summarize, report on and delete an event's TicketLeap roster; an attendee reads their own tickets and claims one by barcode. Eleven members, every one returning a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) or `Result<T>`.
- **Depends on**: [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result); the `EventIdentifierType` alias; the DTOs [`TicketRosterImportResultDTO`](#ticketrosterimportresultdto), [`TicketRosterImportRunDTO`](#ticketrosterimportrundto), [`TicketInvitesResultDTO`](#ticketinvitesresultdto), [`TicketAccountLinkResultDTO`](#ticketaccountlinkresultdto), [`TicketRosterSummaryDTO`](#ticketrostersummarydto), [`RosterInsightsDTO`](#rosterinsightsdto), [`EngagementInsightsDTO`](#engagementinsightsdto) and [`MyTicketDTO`](#myticketdto). Externals: `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`, `CancellationToken`.
- **Concept introduced, dry run then commit over the same bytes.** `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` assesses whether a destructive action can be previewed first. `DryRunRosterAsync` (`:33`) reports the counts the commit would produce and writes nothing (`:22-24`); `StartRosterImportAsync` (`:48`) then commits the reviewed file as a background run and answers the queued run, with a conflict when the event's previous run is still active (`:39-42`). Both take the file as `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` rather than a stream, because the page reads the picked file once and posts the same bytes twice: a browser file stream cannot be read twice (`:28-29`). `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]` covers the shape: pages depend on this interface, so the transport stays out of the components and bUnit tests substitute it. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` shows in the insights docs: the roster report is aggregate only and its domain-mix cells carry the server-applied small-number rule (`:92-96`), and every count of 1 or 2 in the activity report arrives already withheld (`:103-107`).
- **Walkthrough**

  | Member | File:Line | What it answers |
  |--------|-----------|-----------------|
  | `DryRunRosterAsync(eventId, content, fileName)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:33` | the would-be counts, nothing written |
  | `StartRosterImportAsync(eventId, content, fileName)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:48` | the queued import run |
  | `GetRosterImportAsync(eventId)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:60` | the latest run's status and processed-of-total; NotFound when there is none (`:54-57`) |
  | `SendInvitesAsync(eventId, dryRun)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:70` | one invite per eligible order email, up to the per-run cap (`:64-66`) |
  | `LinkExistingAccountsAsync(eventId)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:81` | tickets linked to existing confirmed accounts, re-runnable (`:75-78`) |
  | `GetSummaryAsync(eventId)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:88` | the roster adoption funnel |
  | `GetRosterInsightsAsync(eventId)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:99` | roster-only reports A1 to A6 |
  | `GetEngagementInsightsAsync(eventId)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:110` | roster-plus-activity reports B1 to B4, degraded rather than failed on a cross-service lookup failure (`:105-106`) |
  | `DeleteRosterAsync(eventId)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:117` | deletes the whole roster after the event |
  | `GetMyTicketsAsync()` | `ITicketUIService.cs:123` | the caller's linked tickets, the caller taken from the token |
  | `ClaimAsync(eventId, barcode)` | `ITicketUIService.cs:133` | the claimed ticket; NotFound for an unknown barcode, Conflict for one linked elsewhere or voided (`:125-129`) |

  The first nine are organizer-only (`engagement:tickets:manage`, `:22-24`); the last two are the attendee's.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [`TicketService`](#ticketservice) and registered as `services.AddScoped<ITicketUIService, TicketService>()` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:65`). Injected by [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload), [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster-1), [`TicketInsights`](#ticketinsights) and [`MyTicketsPanel`](#myticketspanel), and substituted in their bUnit tests (`TicketRosterTests`, `TicketRosterUploadImportRunTests`, `TicketInsightsTests`, `TicketRosterFailureWordingTests`, `MyBadgeTests`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the permission is enforced by the server endpoints, not by this interface; the doc comments only name it.

### ProcessTicketRosterImportInternalCommand

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.ProcessRosterImport` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ProcessRosterImport/ProcessTicketRosterImportInternalCommand.cs:21` · Level 4 · record (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the durable trigger that applies one committed roster import run in batches (`:6-11`). Like its sibling [`ExpireTicketRosterImportInternalCommand`](#expireticketrosterimportinternalcommand), the payload is the run id only (`:21`).
- **Depends on**: [`IInternalCommand`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#iinternalcommand) and [`IHasTimeout`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#ihastimeout) (`:1-2`, `:22`); [`InternalCommandNameAttribute`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#internalcommandnameattribute) naming it `Engagement.ProcessTicketRosterImport.v1` (`:20`).
- **Concept introduced, the markers a background command leaves off.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]` assesses how commands opt into pipeline behavior; here the omissions are the design, and the remarks (`:12-18`) justify each. It is neither `IRequiresPermission` nor `IFeatureGated`: the organizer's permission and the feature flag were checked when the run started, and a refusal at this point would retry into a dead letter with the staged roster still on the run. It is not `ITransactional` either: each batch commits on its own so the processed count other replicas read moves as the run goes ([ADR-107](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/107-transaction-execution-contract.html)). `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`: the holder data stays on the run, where every ending of the run clears it, so the internal-command row, kept for the queue's retention window, never holds a name or an address (`:7-10`).
- **Walkthrough**: the positional `RunId` (`:21`) and one member, `Timeout => TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)` (`:28`), the per-attempt execution budget. Its doc (`:24-27`) ties it to the backstop: ten minutes sits well under `TicketImportRun.AbandonAfter` (30 minutes, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/TicketImportRun.cs:37`), so the expiry never fires on a run that is still applying batches.
- **Why it's built this way**: the queue is [ADR-114](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/114-internal-commands-durable-job-queue.html)'s durable internal-command store, so an upload survives a restart between the commit and the processing.
- **Where it's used**: scheduled with no delay by [`StartTicketRosterImportHandler`](#startticketrosterimporthandler) (`StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:115-117`) and handled by [`ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler`](#processticketrosterimporthandler). The host comments in `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:168-177` and `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Service/Program.cs:340` name it as the reason the verified-user lookup edge must accept a service token: the import runs with no `HttpContext`, so there is no organizer bearer to forward.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the retry count and back-off between attempts belong to the internal-command processor's configuration, not to this record.

### OrganizerPointsOverview

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Points/OrganizerPointsOverview.razor.cs:19` · Level 5 · class (partial)

- **What it is**: the code-behind for the organizer rollup of the points game (`@page "/organizer/points"`, `OrganizerPointsOverview.razor:1`, `@attribute [Authorize(Roles = RoleNames.Organizer)]`, `OrganizerPointsOverview.razor:2`): how many attendees are playing, what the economy has paid out, which mechanic the room actually used, and the newest awards.

Externals as on [`MyPoints`](#mypoints): MudBlazor `BreadcrumbItem` / `Icons`, and an injected `IStringLocalizer<OrganizerPointsOverview>` (`OrganizerPointsOverview.razor:7`).
- **Concept introduced, distinguishing "no data yet" from "the read failed".** There is no write on this surface, so none of the switch-state machinery [`MyPoints`](#mypoints) needs appears here, but the load does one thing its sibling does not. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` assesses whether the UI tells the truth about what happened: the load unwraps the [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) with `TryGetValue` and, when it is a failure, checks `IsNotFound()` before deciding (`:62-72`). A not-found rollup leaves `_overview` null so the page keeps rendering its empty state, and only a real failure becomes the error state; the comment (`:68-70`) records that this preserves the behavior the older null-returning service produced. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` is the other point worth teaching: the class comment (`:13-17`) states that the recent entries carry NO attendee identity by design, because the overview endpoint reports activity, points and timestamps only. An organizer can watch the game move without seeing who earned what, and the only published identities anywhere in this feature are the leaderboard names attendees opted in to. `[Rubric §11, Security]` covers the role gate, which is declared on the markup rather than in this file.

- **Why it's built this way**: the two helper methods are duplicated across the two points pages rather than shared, the same trade-off the feedback pages make with their nested answer holder: each page stays self-contained and independently editable, and the duplicated code is two small pure functions with no state.
- **Where it's used**: routed at `/organizer/points`, the value of [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths)`.OrganizerPointsOverview` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementRoutePaths.cs:27`). Its data comes from [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller)'s overview endpoint (`PointsController.cs:126`) via [`GetPointsOverviewHandler`](#getpointsoverviewhandler). Component-tested by [`OrganizerPointsOverviewTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the stat cards, the per-activity table and the recent-entry table live in `OrganizerPointsOverview.razor`, not in this code-behind.

### TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter.cs:14` · Level 5 · class (internal sealed)

- **What it is**: the client-side gRPC adapter that implements [`IPendingTicketInvitationService`](#ipendingticketinvitationservice) on top of the generated `TicketInvitationService.TicketInvitationServiceClient` (`:14-15`, BR-271). It is what Identity resolves when a sign-in link is requested for an address that holds no account yet and it needs to know whether a ticket invitation still stands.
- **Depends on**: [`IPendingTicketInvitationService`](#ipendingticketinvitationservice) and [`PendingTicketInvitationDTO`](#pendingticketinvitationdto) from `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Invitations` (`:3`); the generated client and its `GetPendingTicketInvitationRequest` message (`:2`). Externals: `System.Globalization` (`:1`), the Grpc.Net client factory.
- **Concept, the third same-interface transport swap.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`. This is the pattern [`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter`](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter) introduced: the consumer keeps depending on the C# interface and the generated types never leave this assembly (class doc `:7-13`). `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: `CallDeadline` is a static five seconds (`:20`), and the comment (`:17-19`) gives this caller's reason: Identity is answering an anonymous request, so a hung (not refused) Engagement peer must fail fast instead of holding it. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`: the wire answer is a `Found` flag plus the event's first day as a `yyyy-MM-dd` string, and an answer whose date does not parse is treated as no invitation rather than sent with a default date (`:32-38`).
- **Walkthrough**: `GetPendingInvitationAsync(email, cancellationToken)` (`:23-41`) guards `email` with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` (`:25`), calls `GetPendingTicketInvitationAsync` with `deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.Add(CallDeadline)` and the caller's token (`:27-30`), returns `null` when `Found` is false or `DateOnly.TryParseExact(..., "yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...)` fails (`:34-38`), and otherwise builds `new PendingTicketInvitationDTO(FirstName, LastName, EventName, eventStart)` (`:40`).
- **Why it's built this way**: transport failures are not caught here; they propagate to the caller, which logs them and sends nothing (`:11-12`), so an Engagement outage can never change the answer an anonymous caller sees.
- **Where it's used**: registered by [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection-4)`.AddEngagementTicketInvitationClient()` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/DependencyInjection.cs:108-117`), which the Identity service calls at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Service/Program.cs:307`. The consumer is [`SendSignInLinkHandler`](group-24-identity-module.md#sendsigninlinkhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/Users/UseCases/SendSignInLink/SendSignInLinkHandler.cs:49`). Its server-side twin is [`TicketInvitationGrpcService`](#ticketinvitationgrpcservice); its disabled stub is [`DisabledPendingTicketInvitationService`](#disabledpendingticketinvitationservice) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:35`). Covered by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Services/MMCA.ADC.Services.Tests/Invitations/TicketInvitationGrpcServiceTests.cs`.

### TicketService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Tickets/TicketService.cs:25` · Level 5 · class (public sealed)

- **What it is**: the HTTP implementation of [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice) over the `tickets` endpoints (`Endpoint`, `:29`). Every call is authenticated; the roster, invite, summary and delete calls are permission-gated on the server, while claim and my-tickets take the attendee from the token (class doc `:15-19`).
- **Depends on**: [`AuthenticatedServiceBase`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#authenticatedservicebase) (`:27`), which supplies `CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync`, the shared `RetryPolicy` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:37`) and `NewIdempotencyKey` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:61`); [`HttpResultExecutor`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#httpresultexecutor), [`ProblemDetailsResultReader`](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), [`IdempotencyHeaders`](group-08-auth.md#idempotencyheaders) and [`ImportConventions`](group-08-auth.md#importconventions); the request bodies [`SendTicketInvitesRequest`](#sendticketinvitesrequest) and [`ClaimTicketRequest`](#claimticketrequest). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`, `MultipartFormDataContent`, `ReadOnlyMemoryContent`, `MediaTypeHeaderValue`.
- **Concept introduced, one idempotency key per logical write, minted outside the retry.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether a retried request can double-apply. The remarks (`:20-24`) state the rule: the four writes the API marks `[Idempotent]` (roster upload, invites, link-existing, claim) carry one `Idempotency-Key` per logical operation, added to the client's default headers before `RetryPolicy.ExecuteAsync` runs (`:77`, `:113`, `:132`, `:234`), so every attempt states the same key and a retried send replays the first answer instead of running twice. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` covers the upload: retrying a multipart post is normally unsafe because a stream is consumed, but the bytes are already in memory (at most `TicketRosterLimits.MaxFileBytes`, checked by the page), so each attempt builds a fresh form over them (`:79-81`, `:87-94`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `DryRunRosterAsync` (`:32-37`) and `StartRosterImportAsync` (`:40-45`) both delegate to `PostRosterAsync<T>` with `dryRun: true` or `false`.
  - `PostRosterAsync<T>` (`:67-102`) posts one multipart form to `tickets/roster` (`:96`); the dry run answers 200 with the counts and the commit 202 with the queued run (`:65-66`). The parts are the file as `text/csv` (`:91`) named `roster.csv` when the picked name is blank (`:92`), `eventId` (`:93`) and the dry-run part named by `ImportConventions.DryRunFieldName` (`:94`). The comment (`:85-86`) records why the names matter: they bind to the controller's `IFormFile` parameter and two `[FromForm]` arguments, and a renamed part binds to its default and fails validation.
  - `GetRosterImportAsync` (`:48-63`) reads `tickets/roster/import?eventId=` (`:56`), the progress poll for the background run.
  - `SendInvitesAsync` (`:105-122`) posts a JSON `SendTicketInvitesRequest` to `tickets/invites` (`:115-117`); `LinkExistingAccountsAsync` (`:125-141`) posts an empty body to `tickets/link-existing?eventId=` (`:134-136`); `GetSummaryAsync` (`:144-159`) reads `tickets/summary` (`:152`).
  - `GetRosterInsightsAsync` (`:162-165`) and `GetEngagementInsightsAsync` (`:168-171`) share `GetInsightsAsync<T>` (`:173-186`), which builds `tickets/insights/{kind}` (`:179`) for the kinds `roster` and `engagement`.
  - `DeleteRosterAsync` (`:189-204`) sends `DELETE tickets/roster?eventId=` (`:197`) and reads it with the non-generic `ProblemDetailsResultReader.ReadAsync` (`:202`).
  - `GetMyTicketsAsync` (`:207-220`) reads `tickets/mine` (`:214`) and maps the `List<MyTicketDTO>` to `IReadOnlyList<MyTicketDTO>` (`:218`).
  - `ClaimAsync` (`:223-244`) throws on a blank barcode before any I/O (`:228`), trims it into a `ClaimTicketRequest` (`:236`) and posts to `tickets/claim` (`:238`).
- **Why it's built this way**: every method wraps its work in `HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync` and reads the response through `ProblemDetailsResultReader`, so a server ProblemDetails becomes a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) failure the page can branch on rather than an exception it has to catch.
- **Where it's used**: registered at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:65`; reached through [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice) by [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload), [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster-1) (including its `TicketRoster.Invites.razor.cs` partial), [`TicketInsights`](#ticketinsights) and [`MyTicketsPanel`](#myticketspanel). The server side is [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller) and [`TicketRosterImportController`](#ticketrosterimportcontroller).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: which routes each controller actually serves is defined server-side; this file only fixes the client URLs.

### ExpireTicketRosterImportHandler

- **Depends on**: [`ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult) (`:17`), [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:15`), [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun) and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>` with source-generated `[LoggerMessage]`.
- **Concept, a backstop that is harmless when it is late.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether a redelivered or stale job can do damage. `HandleAsync` (`:20-42`) returns success with no write when the run is gone (`:30-31`) or already ended with no staged roster (`:33-34`), so the normal case, where processing finished long before the 30-minute timer, is a no-op. Otherwise it calls `run.Fail(TicketImportRun.AbandonedErrorCode, now)` (`:36`) and saves (`:41`). `[Rubric §13, Observability & Operability]`: the Warning `LogAbandoned` (`:45-46`) fires only when `Fail` reports that it ended the run (`:36-39`), and it records how far the run got (`Processed` of `Total`) and that the staged roster was cleared.

- **Caveats / not-in-source**: what `Fail` clears on a run that has already ended, and when it returns `false`, is decided in [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun); this handler saves at `:41` either way.

### BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter.cs:14` · Level 9 · class (internal sealed)

- **What it is**: a hand-written **client-side** adapter that implements the C# interface [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) on top of the proto-generated gRPC client. It is what Conference resolves for `IBookmarkCountService` now that Engagement runs as its own process.
- **Depends on**: [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice) from `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks` (`:2`); the generated `BookmarkCountService.BookmarkCountServiceClient` and the request/response messages from `bookmark_count.proto` (namespace `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts.V1`, `:1`). Externals: the Grpc.Net client factory that supplies the injected client.
- **Concept, the gRPC adapter (same interface, different transport).** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses whether modules talk through explicit, extractable contracts; `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses stable wire contracts. The in-process [`BookmarkCountService`](#bookmarkcountservice) and this remote adapter implement the *same* interface, so a consumer swaps transport by swapping one DI registration and never edits a call site ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html), [ADR-008](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/008-service-extraction-topology.html)). Watch the name overlap: the generated proto service type is also called `BookmarkCountService` (in `...Contracts.V1`), and this adapter's primary constructor takes its nested `BookmarkCountServiceClient` (`:14-15`); that generated type is distinct from the Application-layer class of the same name.
- **Concept, the per-call deadline as a second, tighter budget.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`. `CallDeadline` is a static `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)` (`:20`) applied to both calls (`:32`, `:48`), and the comment (`:17-19`) explains the reasoning: the shared resilience pipeline's 30s attempt / 90s total budget answers a *refused* peer well, but a *hung* peer would otherwise stall a caller's request, and bookmark counts sit inline in speaker-dashboard responses. A deadline turns "hung" into a fast `DeadlineExceeded` status the caller's Polly pipeline can act on.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync(sessionId, cancellationToken)` (`:23-36`): builds a `GetBookmarkCountForSessionRequest { SessionId = sessionId }` (`:28-31`), passes `deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.Add(CallDeadline)` plus the caller's token (`:32-33`), and returns `response.Count` (`:35`). The interface returns a plain `int`, not a `Result<int>`, so there is no failure trailer to parse: a transport fault surfaces as an `RpcException`.
  - `GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync(sessionIds, cancellationToken)` (`:39-52`): the batch form. It fills the repeated `SessionIds` field with `AddRange` (`:43-44`), sends the same deadline (`:48`), and rebuilds a dictionary from the repeated response pairs with `response.Counts.ToDictionary(c => c.SessionId, c => c.Count)` (`:51`). This is the N+1 avoidance for a speaker dashboard listing many sessions: one round trip instead of one per session.
- **Where it's used**: registered by [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection-4)`.AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient()`, which the Conference service calls at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:359`. Its server-side twin is [`BookmarkCountsGrpcService`](#bookmarkcountsgrpcservice).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the dictionary rebuild assumes the server never returns duplicate `SessionId` pairs; `ToDictionary` would throw on a duplicate key. Nothing in this file enforces that, it rests on the server projecting from a dictionary in the first place (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Grpc/BookmarkCountsGrpcService.cs:61-65`).

### ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.ProcessRosterImport` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ProcessRosterImport/ProcessTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:29` · Level 11 · class (public sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the handler for [`ProcessTicketRosterImportInternalCommand`](#processticketrosterimportinternalcommand). It applies a committed run's staged roster to the event's tickets in batches, voids the tickets the file no longer lists, links tickets to existing confirmed accounts, and completes the run; any fault ends the run as failed.
- **Depends on**: [`ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult) (`:34`), [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:30`), [`IVerifiedUserLookupService`](group-24-identity-module.md#iverifieduserlookupservice) (`:32`), [`TicketImportRun`](#ticketimportrun), [`Ticket`](#ticket), [`TicketRosterStaging`](#ticketrosterstaging), [`TicketRosterApplier`](#ticketrosterapplier), [`TicketRosterCounts`](#ticketrostercounts), [`ExistingAccountLinker`](#existingaccountlinker), [`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes`](#ticketrosterimporterrorcodes) and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>` with `[LoggerMessage]`.
- **Concept introduced, resumable batches with committed progress.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether long work survives a crash midway. Each pass of the loop takes `roster.Entries.Skip(run.Processed).Take(BatchSize)` (`:116`), applies it, then records the batch on the run and saves (`:122-123`), so the run's `Processed` count and the tickets it describes commit together. An `OperationCanceledException` (host shutdown or the attempt's timeout) is rethrown (`:74-78`) and the retry resumes at the committed progress. `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`: barcodes the file moves between its own tickets are parked first, in their own save, so no batch ever holds one barcode twice whichever batches the two tickets fall in (`:107-111`). The load reads every ticket of the event with `ignoreQueryFilters: true` (`:99-104`), so filtered rows are in the set the applier compares against.
- **Concept introduced, failing the run on a clean context.** `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`. The catch-all (`:80`) carries a scoped `CA1031` suppression whose justification is on the pragma itself (`:79`): any fault fails the run in a fresh scope, is logged, and the handler returns success so the queue does not retry a run already marked failed. `FailInFreshScopeAsync` (`:145-159`) creates a new scope (`:147`), reloads the run there, fails it and saves, because the original context may still hold the change set that faulted (doc `:144`). A failed `Result` from `ApplyAsync` takes the same path with its first error code (`:68-72`). `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`: a redelivery after the run ended applies nothing, but if a staged roster is somehow still present it is anonymized and saved anyway (`:53-64`), so the guarantee that a finished run holds no file data is unconditional.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `BatchSize = 100` (`:37`) and `FailedCode = TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.Failed` (`:40`) are public constants.
  - `HandleAsync` (`:43-88`) loads the run tracked (`:49-52`), handles the ended-run redelivery (`:53-64`), then runs `ApplyAsync` inside the try (`:66-85`).
  - `ApplyAsync` (`:90-142`) deserializes the staged roster and fails with `Ticket.Import.StagingUnreadable` when it cannot (`:92-96`), builds a `TicketRosterApplier` over the loaded tickets (`:105`), parks swapped barcodes (`:109-111`), loops the batches with `addNew: true` (`:114-124`), saves the voids from `VoidMissing` (`:126-127`), calls `ExistingAccountLinker.LinkEventAsync` (`:129-135`), and completes the run with the voided count and the linked count, which is `0` when the link step failed (`:137-138`). A lookup failure therefore never fails the upload, matching the host comment at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:168-177`.
  - Three `[LoggerMessage]` methods (`:161-168`): Information on completion with the counts, Error with the exception on a fault, Warning when a run ends as failed.
- **Why it's built this way**: the command is deliberately not transactional (see its section), so this handler owns its commit points; the durable queue is [ADR-114](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/114-internal-commands-durable-job-queue.html) and the per-handler transaction contract is [ADR-107](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/107-transaction-execution-contract.html).
- **Where it's used**: dispatched by [`InternalCommandProcessor`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#internalcommandprocessor) for the row [`StartTicketRosterImportHandler`](#startticketrosterimporthandler) schedules (`StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:115-117`). Its progress is what [`GetTicketRosterImportHandler`](#getticketrosterimporthandler) answers and [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload) polls through [`TicketService`](#ticketservice)`.GetRosterImportAsync`. Covered by `ProcessTicketRosterImportHandlerTests`.

- **What it is**: the client-side gRPC adapter for the data-subject export, the remote twin of the in-process [`UserEngagementExportService`](#userengagementexportservice). It implements [`IUserEngagementExportService`](#iuserengagementexportservice) on top of the generated export client and is what Identity resolves.
- **Depends on**: [`IUserEngagementExportService`](#iuserengagementexportservice) and its DTOs from `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Exports` (including [`UserEngagementTicketExportDTO`](#userengagementticketexportdto)), plus [`CheckInScope`](#checkinscope), [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) and [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod) from the module's Shared project (`:3-6`); the generated `UserEngagementExportService.UserEngagementExportServiceClient` and its messages (`:2`); the framework's [`GrpcWireFormat`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#grpcwireformat) (`:7`). Externals: `System.Globalization` (`:1`), the Grpc.Net client factory.
- **Concept, the same-interface transport swap plus wire rehydration.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`, `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`. This is the export sibling of [`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter`](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter): the same interface as the in-process implementation, so consumers swap one DI registration ([ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html)). It also owns the inverse of every encoding decision the server made, and each inverse is written next to the decision it undoes.
- **Concept, parsing defensively across a rolling deploy.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`. The five `DateTime` fields are read with `GrpcWireFormat.ParseUtc` (`:46`, `:53`, `:62`, `:80`, `:85`), which parses with `DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal | DateTimeStyles.AdjustToUniversal` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.Grpc/GrpcWireFormat.cs:37`, `:61-62`) so that a peer replica still emitting the marker-less form (new Identity code running against an old Engagement replica during a rolling deploy) does not yield `Kind=Unspecified`, and `AssumeUniversal` alone would yield `Kind=Local`. The comment there (`GrpcWireFormat.cs:32-36`) also records why `RoundtripKind` is deliberately absent: `DateTime.Parse` **rejects** it alongside either `Assume*` or `AdjustToUniversal` with an `ArgumentException`, and its purpose (preserving a non-UTC kind) is the opposite of what this contract wants. The one parser in this file, `ParseRoundtripOffset` (`:119-123`), keeps the offset the server emitted rather than folding it into UTC, with `AssumeUniversal` covering an offset-less value from an old peer (`:116-118`). It reads the three `DateTimeOffset` fields: `CheckedInOn` (`:74`) and the ticket's `InvitedOn` and `LinkedOn` (`:98`, `:103`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `CallDeadline` (`:26`), a 5-second static, applied at `:38`. The comment (`:23-25`) gives the same reasoning as the bookmark adapter with an export-specific twist: the aggregation is best-effort per section, so a hung peer should degrade its section quickly rather than stall the export request.
  - `GetUserEngagementExportAsync(userId, cancellationToken)` (`:29-114`): sends a `GetUserEngagementExportRequest { UserId = userId }` with the deadline and the caller's token (`:33-39`), then rebuilds `UserEngagementExportDTO` from the seven repeated fields with collection expressions: bookmarks (`:43-47`), submitted questions (`:48-54`, including the question `Text` at `:52`), points entries (`:55-63`, casting the numeric `ActivityType` back to its enum at `:59`), check-ins (`:64-75`, casting `Scope` back at `:68`, mapping a `0` `SessionId`/`SponsorId` back to `null` at `:72-73`, and parsing `CheckedInOn` as a `DateTimeOffset` at `:74`), poll votes (`:76-81`, into [`UserEngagementPollVoteExportDTO`](#userengagementpollvoteexportdto)), question upvotes (`:82-86`, into [`UserEngagementQuestionUpvoteExportDTO`](#userengagementquestionupvoteexportdto)) and tickets (`:87-104`, into [`UserEngagementTicketExportDTO`](#userengagementticketexportdto)). The ticket mapping copies six string fields (`:89-94`), maps an empty `OrderEmail` and an empty `InvitedOn` back to `null` (`:97-98`, comment `:96`), and casts the numeric `LinkMethod` back to [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod) (`:102`), lossless because those values are persisted and never renumbered (`:100-101`). Finally `IsOnLeaderboard` (`:105`) and the empty-string-to-null mapping for `LeaderboardDisplayName` (`:110-112`), whose comment (`:107-109`) notes the same mapping also covers an old peer that never sets the field at all.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class doc (`:11-19`) states the resilience posture, transport failures propagate to the caller (Identity's [`ExportUserDataHandler`](group-24-identity-module.md#exportuserdatahandler)), which degrades the Engagement section to `Available = false` rather than failing the whole export. Best-effort cross-service aggregation: a peer outage never sinks an entire data-subject export. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`.
- **Where it's used**: registered by [`DependencyInjection`](#dependencyinjection-4)`.AddEngagementUserExportClient()`, called from `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Service/Program.cs:304`. Covered by `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Services/MMCA.ADC.Services.Tests/Exports/UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapterTests.cs`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the comment above `ParseRoundtripOffset` (`:116-117`) still calls check-in timestamps "the one DateTimeOffset on this contract", while the ticket fields at `:98` and `:103` now go through the same parser; the code is consistent, only that comment is narrower than the usage.

### DependencyInjection

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/DependencyInjection.cs:19` · Level 13 · class (public static)

- **What it is**: the Engagement `*.Contracts` DI facade (one of several `DependencyInjection` classes in this module; this is the extraction-wiring one). Three C# `extension(IServiceCollection)` members a consuming host calls to swap Engagement's in-process cross-module registrations for their gRPC-backed adapters: bookmark counts for Conference, and the data-subject export and the pending ticket invitation lookup for Identity (class doc `:12-18`).
- **Depends on**: the generated `BookmarkCountServiceClient` / `UserEngagementExportServiceClient` / `TicketInvitationServiceClient` (`:3`), [`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter`](#bookmarkcountservicegrpcadapter), [`UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapter`](#userengagementexportservicegrpcadapter), [`TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter`](#ticketinvitationservicegrpcadapter), [`IBookmarkCountService`](#ibookmarkcountservice), [`IUserEngagementExportService`](#iuserengagementexportservice), [`IPendingTicketInvitationService`](#ipendingticketinvitationservice) (`:4-6`), `AddTypedGrpcClient<TClient>` from `MMCA.Common.Grpc` (`:7`, defined at `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.Grpc/DependencyInjection.cs:99`) and `WithServiceToken()` from `MMCA.Common.Grpc.Authentication` (`:8`, defined at `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.Grpc/Authentication/ServiceTokenHttpClientBuilderExtensions.cs:28`). Externals: `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` and its `ServiceCollectionDescriptorExtensions.Replace` (`:1-2`).
- **Concept, the adapter-swap wiring lives in the contracts package.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`, `[Rubric §17, DevOps & Deployment]`, `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`. [ADR-007](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/007-grpc-extraction.html) requires each extracted service to publish a `*.Contracts` project holding the proto definitions *and* the DI wiring, so a consumer depends on that thin package rather than on the full module. The C# `extension(IServiceCollection services)` block (`:21`) adds the methods directly onto the collection (see [primer §4](00-primer.md#c-extensiont-types-read-this-once)).
- **Concept, `Replace` rather than `TryAdd`.** `[Rubric §2, Design Patterns]`. Every method does the same two things: register a typed client, then replace one interface binding.

  | Method | File:Line | What it swaps |
  |--------|-----------|----------------|
  | `AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient(serviceName = "engagement")` | `DependencyInjection.cs:46-55` | registers `BookmarkCountServiceClient` (`:48`), then `services.Replace(ServiceDescriptor.Scoped<IBookmarkCountService, BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter>())` (`:52`) |
  | `AddEngagementUserExportClient(serviceName = "engagement")` | `DependencyInjection.cs:79-88` | registers `UserEngagementExportServiceClient` (`:81`), then `services.Replace(ServiceDescriptor.Scoped<IUserEngagementExportService, UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapter>())` (`:85`) |
  | `AddEngagementTicketInvitationClient(serviceName = "engagement")` | `DependencyInjection.cs:108-117` | registers `TicketInvitationServiceClient` with `.WithServiceToken()` (`:110`), then `services.Replace(ServiceDescriptor.Scoped<IPendingTicketInvitationService, TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter>())` (`:114`) |

  At the moment of the call the container already holds *some* binding for the interface: either the real in-process implementation (when the Engagement module is enabled in that host) or the disabled stub ([`DisabledBookmarkCountService`](#disabledbookmarkcountservice) / [`DisabledUserEngagementExportService`](#disableduserengagementexportservice) / [`DisabledPendingTicketInvitationService`](#disabledpendingticketinvitationservice), registered by [`EngagementModule`](#engagementmodule)`.RegisterDisabledStubs`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:31-35`). `TryAdd` would silently lose to it; `Replace` guarantees the gRPC adapter wins either way, which the inline comments state at `:50-51`, `:83-84` and `:112-113`.
- **Concept, one client that presents its own identity.** `[Rubric §11, Security]`. The first two clients forward the caller's bearer; the ticket-invitation client cannot, because the Identity request it serves is anonymous. Its doc (`:95-100`) says the server maps the edge under the service-only `ServiceCaller` policy, so the client opts in to the service token with `WithServiceToken()`, and the calling host must register `AddServiceTokenClient`.
- **Walkthrough**: `AddTypedGrpcClient<T>` is what makes each method two lines instead of twenty, it wires the client to Aspire service discovery (`http://{serviceName}`), the [`JwtForwardingClientInterceptor`](group-13-grpc-contracts.md#jwtforwardingclientinterceptor) and the Polly resilience handler, all from `MMCA.Common.Grpc` (documented at `:26-28` and `:60-62`). All three methods return `IServiceCollection` for chaining (`:54`, `:87`, `:116`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the default `serviceName = "engagement"` matches the AppHost resource name, so the common call site is argument-free. `[Rubric §33, Developer Experience]`. The XML docs on all three methods (`:38-42`, `:70-75`, `:101-104`) spell out the one ordering requirement: call them **after** [`ModuleLoader`](group-14-module-system-composition.md#moduleloader)`.DiscoverAndRegister(...)`, so the in-process or stub registration is already in the container for `Replace` to find. That is an ordering constraint the compiler cannot enforce, which is why every method repeats it. The hosts meet it by registering each client in their `ConfigurePipeline` after `.Register(moduleHost.RegisterModules)`.
- **Where it's used**: `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:359` registers `AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient()` (after the module step at `:358`); `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Service/Program.cs:304` and `:307` register `AddEngagementUserExportClient()` and `AddEngagementTicketInvitationClient()` (after `:303`), with the service-token rationale in the comment at `:281-287`. The AppHost documents the edges of the resulting topology, including why the Conference-to-Engagement reverse edge gets no reciprocal `WaitFor` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosting/MMCA.ADC.AppHost/Program.cs:274-276`, against the Engagement-to-Conference edge at `:269`), and the Identity-to-Engagement edge at `:285-294`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: no method sets a per-call deadline; the 5-second budgets live in the three adapters themselves (`BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter.cs:20`, `UserEngagementExportServiceGrpcAdapter.cs:26`, `TicketInvitationServiceGrpcAdapter.cs:20`), so a host that registered a different implementation of the same interfaces would not inherit them.

### AttendeeBadgeInvariants

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Badges` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Badges/AttendeeBadgeInvariants.cs:9` · Level 6 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the one invariant rule for [`AttendeeBadge`](#attendeebadge): a badge must be bound to a real user.
- **Depends on**: [`CommonInvariants`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants) (`AttendeeBadgeInvariants.cs:16`) and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result).
- **Concept**: the static invariant class beside its aggregate is taught in [group 02](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants). `[Rubric §4, DDD]` assesses whether invariants are stated where the model can enforce them: keeping them in a static class that the factory composes means each rule is individually named, individually testable, and reusable by any future mutator on the same aggregate.
- **Walkthrough**: one method. `EnsureUserIdIsValid(userId, source)` (`:15-16`) delegates to `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault` with the stable error code `"AttendeeBadge.UserId.Invalid"`, the message, the calling member name for attribution, and `nameof(userId)` as the target. The `source` parameter is passed by its caller as `nameof(Create)` (`AttendeeBadge.cs:42`), which is what puts the failing member into the error rather than a stack trace.
- **Why it's built this way**: a badge carries almost no state (an owner and an opaque credential, `AttendeeBadge.cs:21-24`), and the credential is generated internally, so there is exactly one thing a caller can get wrong. The class is still written out rather than inlined into the factory so the badge follows the same shape as every other aggregate in the module, including its much larger sibling [`CheckInInvariants`](#checkininvariants).
- **Where it's used**: [`AttendeeBadge.Create`](#attendeebadge) (`AttendeeBadge.cs:42`) is the only caller in the module.

### CheckInInvariants

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.CheckIns` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/CheckIns/CheckInInvariants.cs:10` · Level 6 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the five invariant rules for [`CheckIn`](#checkin). Four are simple id and enum checks; the fifth encodes the rule that makes one aggregate able to carry three different check-in shapes.
- **Depends on**: [`CommonInvariants`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants) (`EnsureIdIsNotDefault` at `CheckInInvariants.cs:17`, `:24`, `:31`, and `EnsureEnumIsDefined` at `:102`), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error) (`Error.Invariant` at `:88` and `:93`), plus [`CheckInScope`](#checkinscope) (`:45`) and the `UserIdentifierType` / `EventIdentifierType` / `SessionIdentifierType` / `SponsorIdentifierType` aliases (solution-wide `global using`, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)). No externals beyond the BCL.
- **Concept introduced, the discriminated-shape invariant.** `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]` assesses whether the model can express an illegal state. This aggregate is a polymorphic row: a Session check-in must name a session and must not name a sponsor, a Sponsor visit is the mirror image, and an Event check-in names neither. `EnsureTargetMatchesScope` states that rule once, in the domain, so no handler and no controller can persist a row that belongs to two shapes at once (`:33-38`). `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` is the reason it matters beyond tidiness: the storage layer builds three filtered unique indexes on the same table, one per scope ([`CheckInConfiguration`](#checkinconfiguration), `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/CheckIns/CheckInConfiguration.cs:49-63`), and a row with two targets set would be visible to two of them. The invariant and the index filters are two statements of one rule, which the doc comment names explicitly (`:34-36`).
- **Walkthrough** (teaching order)
  - `EnsureUserIdIsValid` (`:16-17`), `EnsureEventIdIsValid` (`:23-24`) and `EnsureCheckedInByUserIdIsValid` (`:30-31`) are three `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault` delegations with stable codes (`"CheckIn.UserId.Invalid"`, `"CheckIn.EventId.Invalid"`, `"CheckIn.CheckedInByUserId.Invalid"`). The event id is required for every scope (`:19`), which is what lets the attendance rollup bucket any row by conference. The recorder is whoever wrote the row: an organizer for a scan or manual check-in, the attendee for a self-recorded visit (`:27`).
  - `EnsureTargetMatchesScope` (`:44-71`) runs the session check first (`:50-58`) and returns it when it fails (`:60-61`), otherwise runs the sponsor check (`:62-70`), so the caller gets the first specific failure rather than a merged pair.
  - `EnsureTargetPresence` (`:75-95`) is the private rule stated once. `isOwningScope` decides the direction: the owning scope requires the id and treats `null` or `default` as missing (`:85-90`), and every other scope forbids it outright (`:92-94`). The comment above it (`:73-74`) records why one method serves both targets: both are `int` aliases, so the parameter is typed `int?`.
  - `EnsureScopeIsDefined` (`:101-102`) delegates to `CommonInvariants.EnsureEnumIsDefined` with the code `"CheckIn.Scope.Invalid"`, which matters because a scope can arrive from a deserialized request rather than from C# code.
- **Why it's built this way**: pushing the shape rule into the domain rather than into each use case means the three write paths (organizer scan, sponsor visit, room check-in) cannot drift apart, and the separate error codes make a failure legible at the API boundary without a message-parse.
- **Where it's used**: composed with `Result.Combine` inside [`CheckIn.Create`](#checkin) (`CheckIn.cs:98-103`); that factory is the only caller.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `EnsureTargetPresence` treats a supplied-but-`default` id as missing only for the owning scope (`:87`); a non-owning scope rejects any non-null value, `default` included (`:92`).
