### ErasedUser

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.ErasedUsers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/ErasedUsers/ErasedUser.cs:20` · Level 6 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root that records one erased account in the Engagement database: the erased user's id and when Identity erased it (`ErasedUser.cs:23`, `:26`). It holds no personal data, only the fact of erasure, so write handlers can ask "has this account been erased?" without reaching across a service boundary.
- **Depends on**: [`AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype) (bound to `ErasedUserIdentifierType`, `:20`), `UserIdentifierType`, `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault` (`:43-44`) and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: only `System.DateTimeOffset`.
- **Concept introduced, a tombstone that closes the erasure gap.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` assesses whether erasure actually holds. An access token outlives the account it was issued for, and the per-feature erasure handlers only reach rows that exist when they run, so a question, vote, bookmark, badge, room check-in or sponsor visit written afterwards would carry an erased user id that no erasure revisits. The `ErasedUser` row is the answer: the erasure writes it once (`UserDeletedSessionQuestionsHandler.cs:101-108`, a no-op when a row for that user already exists) and every Engagement write handler keyed to the caller checks it through [`ErasedUserGuard`](#eraseduserguard) (`ErasedUserGuard.cs:26-43`), which refuses with a `Forbidden` error coded `Engagement.AccountErased` (`ErasedUserGuard.cs:18`). `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` is the other half: Identity owns the account, so Engagement keeps its own scalar copy of the id rather than a cross-database reference ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `UserId` (`:23`) and `ErasedOn` (`:26`): `private set` scalars; `ErasedOn` is the time Identity erased the account, taken from the `UserDeleted` event, not the time Engagement processed it (`:39`).
  - Two constructors, an EF-only parameterless one (`:29`) and a private assigning one (`:31-35`). Construction always runs through the factory.
  - `Create(userId, erasedOn)` (`:41-49`): validates the id with `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault` under the code `Engagement.ErasedUser.UserIdInvalid` (`:43-44`), re-wraps a failure as `Result.Failure<ErasedUser>` (`:45-46`), and otherwise builds the entity with `Id = default` (`:48`) so the database generates the key. No domain event is raised: nothing downstream subscribes to an erasure record being written.
- **Why it's built this way**: the persistence side pins uniqueness, one row per erased account, with a unique index on `UserId` (`ErasedUserConfiguration.cs:29-30`, [`ErasedUserConfiguration`](#eraseduserconfiguration)), so a redelivered `UserDeleted` event cannot create a second record. The identifier alias follows the module convention ([ADR-085](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/085-identifier-type-aliases-revisited.html)).
- **Where it's used**: created by `UserDeletedSessionQuestionsHandler` (`UserDeletedSessionQuestionsHandler.cs:108`); read by [`ErasedUserGuard`](#eraseduserguard); persisted by [`ErasedUserConfiguration`](#eraseduserconfiguration) and the `AddErasedUsers` migration (`20261020142915_AddErasedUsers.cs`); mapped into the Engagement database through the shared per-engine [`SQLServerDbContext`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#sqlserverdbcontext), since `ErasedUserConfiguration` derives from `EntityTypeConfigurationSQLServer<ErasedUser, ErasedUserIdentifierType>` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/ErasedUsers/ErasedUserConfiguration.cs:15-16`). Unit-tested by [`ErasedUserTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: which handlers run the guard is spread across the write handlers and is not enumerated here; the class comment on `ErasedUserGuard` (`:7-14`) lists the write kinds it covers. The `L207` marker in those comments is a backlog reference whose text is not in this source.

### PointsController

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Controllers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/PointsController.cs:37` · Level 6 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the REST surface for the points game: the caller's own ledger, the public leaderboard, joining or leaving that leaderboard, and the organizer rollup.
- **Depends on**: [`ApiControllerBase`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#apicontrollerbase), four handlers over [`ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult) / [`IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) (`PointsController.cs:38-41`), the queries [`GetMyPointsQuery`](#getmypointsquery), [`GetLeaderboardQuery`](#getleaderboardquery) and [`GetPointsOverviewQuery`](#getpointsoverviewquery), the request [`SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest`](#setleaderboardparticipationrequest), the contracts [`MyPointsDTO`](#mypointsdto), [`LeaderboardEntryDTO`](#leaderboardentrydto) and [`PointsOverviewDTO`](#pointsoverviewdto), plus [`EngagementFeatures`](#engagementfeatures), [`EngagementPermissions`](#engagementpermissions), [`HasPermissionAttribute`](group-08-auth.md#haspermissionattribute), [`RefuseMachineClientsAttribute`](group-08-auth.md#refusemachineclientsattribute) and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: ASP.NET Core MVC, `Asp.Versioning`, `[FeatureGate]`, and `[Range]` from `System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations`.
- **Concept introduced, the surface with no ownership argument.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses how ownership is enforced per endpoint. Contrast this controller with [`BookmarksController`](#bookmarkscontroller), which has to bind a body field, a query argument and a stored row to the caller in three different ways. Here the class comment (`:25-28`) states the design instead: nothing on this surface takes a user id. The three attendee endpoints resolve the caller from the token inside their handlers, so there is no argument a caller could change, and the one endpoint that reads across every attendee returns no attendee identity at all. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` is the other half: the leaderboard serves only the display-name snapshot an attendee published at opt-in (`:71-74`), so rendering the board makes no call into Identity and exposes nothing an attendee did not choose to publish, and the organizer overview carries activity, points and timestamps only (`:118-119`). `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` covers the paging arguments: `pageNumber`/`pageSize` (`:55-56`) and `recentCount` (`:127`) are `[Range]`-validated and select how much comes back, never whose data it is (`:46-48`).
- **Walkthrough** (endpoints in file order)
  - `GetMyPointsAsync` (`:54`), `GET me`: dispatches [`GetMyPointsQuery`](#getmypointsquery) with the paging pair defaulting to page 1 of 20 (`:55-56`, `:60`), returning the running total, the caller's leaderboard status and a page of ledger entries.
  - `GetLeaderboardAsync` (`:79`), `GET leaderboard`: dispatches a parameterless [`GetLeaderboardQuery`](#getleaderboardquery) (`:83`). The board length is fixed by configuration (`Points:LeaderboardSize`), not by the caller (`:73-74`).
  - `SetLeaderboardParticipationAsync` (`:104`), `PUT me/leaderboard-participation`: the one write. The request carries only a boolean because the published display name is taken from the caller's token server-side and never from the body (`:94-95`), and it answers 204 (`:101`, `:112`).
  - `GetPointsOverviewAsync` (`:126`), `GET overview`: the only endpoint with a permission, `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.PointsViewOverview)]` (`:122`).
  - The whole controller is behind `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.Points)]` (`:34`) with a bare `[Authorize]` (`:35`) as the floor, and `[RefuseMachineClients]` (`:36`) keeps a client-credentials caller off an attendee surface ([ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)).
- **Why it's built this way**: designing the routes so no endpoint accepts an identity is a cheaper guarantee than checking one. There is no filter to forget and no claim comparison to invert, which is the failure mode the ownership checks on [`BookmarksController`](#bookmarkscontroller) exist to prevent. See [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html) for the points design and [ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html) for the ownership axis this surface sidesteps.
- **Where it's used**: mounted at `/points` by `[Route("[controller]")]` (`:32`) behind the Gateway; consumed by [`MyPoints`](#mypoints) and [`OrganizerPointsOverview`](#organizerpointsoverview) through [`IPointsUIService`](#ipointsuiservice). Covered by [`PointsControllerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), and checked for the machine-client attribute by `MachineClientParticipationTests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `Points:LeaderboardSize` and the per-activity point values are configuration, read by the handlers rather than by this controller. Note also that the one write here carries no `[Idempotent]`, unlike the four POSTs on [`CheckInsController`](#checkinscontroller): setting participation is a PUT of an absolute value, so a replay lands on the same state without help.

- **Concept introduced, a long write answered as a queued run.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` assesses whether the contract tells a client what happened. One route, `POST roster`, has two outcomes by design: a dry run answers 200 with the counts, and a commit answers 202 Accepted with the queued run (`:61-62`), because a whole roster is applied in batches by a background run whose progress `GET roster/import` reports (`:42-45`). A second commit while the event's run is active answers 409 (`:44-45`, `:66`). `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` is the reason for the split: the request returns as soon as the run is queued instead of holding a connection open for the whole apply, and the body is capped twice, by `[RequestSizeLimit(TicketRosterLimits.MaxRequestBytes)]` (`:59`) on the request and by `TicketRosterLimits.MaxFileBytes` on the file buffer (`:77-78`).

  - `IsBlank` (`:141-143`): true when every header and every field is white space.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class comment (`:24-30`) places this controller as a sibling of [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller) under the same `/tickets` prefix (`[Route("Tickets")]`, `:32`) with the same posture: authenticated (`:35`), `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.TicketsManage)]` on every action (`:60`, `:125`), and behind `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.Tickets)]` (`:34`), so with the flag off every route answers 404 ([ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html)).

Covered by [`TicketRosterImportControllerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup); the upload helper it calls is covered by [`FormFileCsvUploadTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).

- **Concept introduced, two audiences on one surface.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether each endpoint carries the weakest authorization that is still correct. Seven of the nine actions are organizer actions with `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.TicketsManage)]` (`:65`, `:94`, `:170`, `:193`, `:217`, `:243`, `:294`); the attendee pair, `claim` and `mine`, carries none, because both take the attendee from the token rather than the request (`:114`, `:148-149`; BR-269 in the class comment, `:32-33`). The claim endpoint adds enumeration resistance: an unknown barcode, a ticket linked to another account and a voided ticket all answer the same 404, so the endpoint does not confirm which barcodes exist, and each signed-in account has an attempt budget that answers 429 when spent (`:115-118`, `:136`). The comment records why there is no per-address limit: attendees at the venue share one address, and server-rendered calls share the UI host's (`:118-119`).
- **Concept, privacy by aggregation.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`: the two insights reads are aggregate only (BR-278). The roster report carries no name, email address or account id and withholds a count of 1 or 2 in the email-domain mix (`:186-188`); the engagement report withholds every count of 1 or 2 on the server (`:209-211`). The CSV export writes a withheld count as "fewer than 3" and never the number behind it (`:233-237`).
- **Concept, idempotency for an accurate answer.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: the three POSTs carry `[Idempotent]` (`:64`, `:93`, `:130`), and the remarks argue it differently from the check-in surface. A second `invites` or `link-existing` execution would be harmless but would report 0 sent or 0 linked, so the replay exists to keep the organizer's answer the one the first execution gave (`:58-62`, `:87-91`); a repeated claim already answers 200 with the same ticket (`:126-127`) ([ADR-017](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/017-request-idempotency.html)).
- **Walkthrough** (endpoints in file order)
  - `SendInvitesAsync` (`:70`), `POST invites` (BR-270): one invite per eligible order email, up to a per-run cap, and a re-run sends only to tickets not yet invited or linked (`:52-54`).
  - `LinkExistingAccountsAsync` (`:99`), `POST link-existing?eventId=` (BR-277, UC-55): links roster tickets to accounts that already exist with a confirmed address; when the Identity lookup is unavailable nothing is linked and the run fails (`:81-83`).
  - `ClaimAsync` (`:137`), `POST claim` (BR-273): links a ticket to the caller by barcode, answering 200 again for a ticket already linked to the caller (`:112-121`). A 409 comes only from the idempotency filter, for a duplicate of a claim still in flight (`:120`).
  - `GetMineAsync` (`:155`), `GET mine` (UC-51): dispatches a parameterless [`GetMyTicketsQuery`](#getmyticketsquery-getticketrosterimportquery-getticketrostersummaryquery) (`:158`).
  - `GetSummaryAsync` (`:173`), `GET summary?eventId=` (UC-52): the adoption funnel of tickets, invited, linked, voided and pending-invite counts.
  - `GetRosterInsightsAsync` (`:196`) and `GetEngagementInsightsAsync` (`:220`), `GET insights/roster` and `GET insights/engagement` (UC-56): the A1 to A6 and B1 to B4 reports. A failed Conference lookup degrades the engagement report and is flagged in it rather than failing the request (`:211-212`).
  - `ExportInsightsAsync` (`:247`), `GET insights/export?eventId=&report=`: rejects an undefined [`TicketInsightsReport`](#ticketinsightsreport) with `Ticket.Insights.UnknownReport` (`:252-259`), reuses whichever insights handler owns the report (`:263-280`), renders it through [`TicketInsightsCsv`](#ticketinsightscsv) and returns `File(...)` with a UTF-8 byte-order mark, the `text/csv` content type and a file name built from report, event and generation time (`:282-285`). The dedicated route follows [ADR-078](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/078-csv-export-endpoint.html) (`:235-236`).
  - `DeleteRosterAsync` (`:298`), `DELETE roster?eventId=` (BR-274): deletes the whole roster after the event and answers 204, including for an event with no roster (`:288-289`, `:308`).
- **Why it's built this way**: every action except the export is a pure dispatch followed by `HandleFailure(result.Errors)` or the success result, so the rules (invite caps, the claim attempt budget, the withheld-count threshold) live in handlers that are unit testable without HTTP. The whole surface sits behind `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.Tickets)]` (`:39`), so with the flag off every route answers 404 ([ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html)), with `[Authorize]` (`:40`) as the floor and `[RefuseMachineClients]` (`:41`) refusing a client-credentials caller ([ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)).
- **Where it's used**: mounted at `/tickets` by `[Route("[controller]")]` (`:37`) and fronted by the YARP Gateway; the attendee side is consumed by [`MyTicketsPanel`](#myticketspanel) and the organizer side by the ticket pages, through [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice). Covered by [`TicketsControllerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the invite cap, the claim attempt budget and the withheld-count threshold are enforced in the handlers and settings, not in this file. Which UI component calls which endpoint is inferred from the type map rather than traced call by call.

### AttendeeBadge

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Badges` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Badges/AttendeeBadge.cs:18` · Level 7 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root holding an attendee's badge credential, the opaque value encoded into their QR badge and the only thing an organizer's scan carries.
- **Depends on**: [`AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype) (the base, `:18`), [`AttendeeBadgeInvariants`](#attendeebadgeinvariants) (`:42`), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), and [`IdValueGeneratedAttribute`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#idvaluegeneratedattribute) (`:17`), which tells the persistence layer the database assigns the id. Externals: `System.Guid`.
- **Concept introduced, the opaque bearer credential.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses how a credential is issued, verified and revoked. The design decision is written in the class comment (`:7-11`): the credential is server-verified on every scan, so it needs no signature and no expiry of its own, and revoking a leaked badge is a `Regenerate` away. The most instructive line in the file is the private helper comment (`:65-67`): `Guid.NewGuid()` is chosen over `Guid.CreateVersion7()` precisely because a v7 value embeds its creation timestamp and orders monotonically, which is the property a guessable bearer value must not have. That is a case where the newer API is the wrong one, and the file says so rather than leaving the next reader to "modernize" it. `[Rubric §4, DDD]` covers the aggregate shape: private setters, a private EF constructor, a static factory returning [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result)`<T>`, and a named mutator instead of a public property setter.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Two properties: `UserId` (`:21`), one badge per user, and `Credential` (`:24`), the `Guid` encoded into the QR.
  - The parameterless private constructor (`:27`) exists for EF Core materialization; the private assigning constructor (`:29-33`) is what the factory uses.
  - `Create(userId)` (`:40`) validates through [`AttendeeBadgeInvariants`](#attendeebadgeinvariants) (`:42`), returns the failure unchanged when it fails (`:43-44`), then builds the badge with a fresh credential and `Id = default` (`:46-49`) so the store assigns the key. It raises no domain event, and the class comment (`:12-15`) explains that too: a badge existing says nothing a downstream module needs to react to, because the interesting fact is the check-in, which [`CheckIn`](#checkin) publishes.
  - `Regenerate()` (`:59-63`) replaces the credential in place and returns success, invalidating every previously issued copy: a printout left on a table, a screenshot shared in a chat (`:54-57`).
  - `NewCredential()` (`:68`) is the one place a credential is minted.
- **Why it's built this way**: the badge is deliberately the thinnest possible aggregate, because everything expensive (who may scan, whether the event is running, whether this is a duplicate) belongs to the check-in write path rather than to the credential. Keeping the credential opaque and server-verified is the decision recorded in [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html), which also fixes the encoded form the scanner reads.
- **Where it's used**: minted on first use by [`GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler`](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/UseCases/GetOrCreateMyBadge/GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler.cs:49`) behind [`CheckInsController`](#checkinscontroller)'s `my-badge` endpoint; read back by [`CheckInAttendeeHandler`](#checkinattendeehandler), which first extracts the credential from the scanned payload through [`BadgePayload`](#badgepayload) (`.../CheckInAttendee/CheckInAttendeeHandler.cs:43`) and then resolves it to an attendee (`:50`). Persisted by `AttendeeBadgeConfiguration` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/CheckIns/AttendeeBadgeConfiguration.cs:15`), which puts a unique index on both the owner and the credential (`:31`, `:35`), and exposed as a `DbSet` on the module context (`.../Persistence/DbContexts/ModuleApplicationDbContext.cs:30`). It deliberately gets no `INavigationPopulator` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:87-89`) because it has no navigation. Covered by [`AttendeeBadgeTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `Regenerate()` has no production call site today. The only callers in the repository are the domain tests (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Tests/Badges/AttendeeBadgeTests.cs:54`, `:67`, `:77`): the revocation path exists on the model but no endpoint or handler invokes it.

### MyTicketProjection

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.DTOs` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/DTOs/MyTicketProjection.cs:12` · Level 7 · class (static, internal)

- **What it is**: the one projection of a linked [`Ticket`](#ticket) to [`MyTicketDTO`](#myticketdto), shared by the my-tickets query (run as SQL) and the claim response (run in memory), so both answer the same shape (`MyTicketProjection.cs:7-11`).
- **Depends on**: [`Ticket`](#ticket) and [`MyTicketDTO`](#myticketdto). Externals: `System.Linq.Expressions`.
- **Concept**: one expression, two execution sites. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]`: rather than a mapper method plus a hand-copied `Select`, the projection is held as an `Expression<Func<Ticket, MyTicketDTO>>` (`:15`), which EF Core can translate into the query and which the in-memory path compiles, so the two outputs cannot drift. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]`: the query path selects only the nine DTO columns instead of loading the entity.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `Selector` (`:15-26`) copies the ticket id, event id, source event and ticket type names, the attendee's first and last name and the status (`:17-23`), and unwraps `LinkMethod` and `LinkedOn` with `!.Value` (`:24-25`). That is safe only because the projection is applied to linked tickets, which always carry both (`:10`).
  - `ToDTO` (`:34`) compiles the selector on every call. The comment (`:28-31`) justifies it: it serves the claim response only, one ticket per request, so caching the delegate would buy nothing measurable.
- **Where it's used**: [`GetMyTicketsHandler`](#getmyticketshandler) passes `MyTicketProjection.Selector` to its query (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetMyTickets/GetMyTicketsHandler.cs:36`), and [`ClaimTicketHandler`](#claimtickethandler) calls `ToDTO` for both of its success paths (`.../Tickets/UseCases/ClaimTicket/ClaimTicketHandler.cs:90`, `:105`). Both feed [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: applied to an unlinked ticket, the `!.Value` unwraps would throw in memory; nothing in this class enforces the linked precondition, the callers do.

### CheckInsController

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API.Controllers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/CheckInsController.cs:42` · Level 8 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the REST surface for QR badge check-in. Six endpoints covering the attendee's own badge, the organizer scan and its manual fallback, the two attendee self-recorded scan surfaces (sponsor booth, room), and the organizer attendance rollup.
- **Depends on**: [`ApiControllerBase`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#apicontrollerbase) (for `HandleFailure`), seven injected handlers over [`ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult) and [`IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#iqueryhandlerin-tquery-tresult) (`CheckInsController.cs:43-49`), the request and result contracts [`CheckInAttendeeRequest`](#checkinattendeerequest), [`ManualCheckInRequest`](#manualcheckinrequest), [`SponsorVisitRequest`](#sponsorvisitrequest), [`RoomCheckInRequest`](#roomcheckinrequest), [`CheckInResultDTO`](#checkinresultdto), [`SponsorVisitResultDTO`](#sponsorvisitresultdto), [`RoomCheckInResultDTO`](#roomcheckinresultdto), [`MyBadgeDTO`](#mybadgedto), [`AttendanceStatsDTO`](#attendancestatsdto), the use-case types [`GetMyBadgeQuery`](#getmybadgequery), [`GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand`](#getorcreatemybadgecommand) and [`GetAttendanceStatsQuery`](#getattendancestatsquery), plus [`IdempotentAttribute`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#idempotentattribute), [`RefuseMachineClientsAttribute`](group-08-auth.md#refusemachineclientsattribute), [`EngagementFeatures`](#engagementfeatures), [`EngagementPermissions`](#engagementpermissions), [`ErrorType`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype) and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: ASP.NET Core MVC, `Asp.Versioning`, and `Microsoft.FeatureManagement.Mvc`'s `[FeatureGate]`.
- **Concept introduced, the authorization ladder on one controller.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether each endpoint carries the weakest authorization that is still correct. This controller has three rungs, and reading them top to bottom is the fastest way to understand the whole check-in feature. The class-level `[Authorize]` (`:40`) is the floor: authenticated, no policy, no role, with `[RefuseMachineClients]` (`:41`) keeping client-credentials callers off it entirely ([ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)). Three endpoints add `[HasPermission(EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage)]` (`:105`, `:129`, `:213`), which is the organizer rung. The remaining three deliberately stay at the floor, and the doc comments say why: `my-badge` (`:52-53`) and the two self-recorded scans (`:147-149`, `:178-179`) take the attendee from the token and never from the request, so there is no ownership argument a caller could tamper with and therefore no ownership check to get wrong. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` covers the other decision worth studying: a repeat scan answers 200 with an `AlreadyCheckedIn` flag rather than 409 (`:93-96`, `:181-182`), because at a door a second scan is a normal event, not a client error, and the organizer needs to see whose badge it is either way. The room endpoint extends the same rule to points: being checked in to another session in the same time slot, or session points being switched off (`Points:SessionCheckIn` at 0), still answers 200 with the check-in recorded, reporting the difference through `EarnsPoints` false and `PointsPaused` true rather than through an error status (`:183-186`). `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` covers feature gating: the whole controller is behind `EngagementFeatures.CheckIn` (`:39`) and the two self-service endpoints add their own gates (`:160`, `:195`), so a disabled surface answers 404 rather than 403 ([ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html)).
- **Concept introduced, idempotency layered onto an already-repeatable endpoint.** Every one of the four POSTs carries `[Idempotent]` (`:104`, `:128`, `:159`, `:194`), the framework's replay cache ([ADR-017](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/017-request-idempotency.html), [`IdempotentAttribute`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#idempotentattribute)). The doc comments are careful about why that is safe rather than merely convenient, and they are worth reading as a checklist: the endpoint's response must not drift within the retry window. For the scan and manual paths the argument is that a repeat already answers the same 200 (`:99-101`, `:125`), so a replayed response says exactly what a re-executed one would; for sponsor visits it is `AlreadyVisited` (`:155-156`); for room check-in the comment adds the load-bearing extra clause, that the session is resolved server-side (`:189-191`), so nothing in the response depends on a value that could change mid-retry. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` is what this buys: a conference-day network that is dropping responses stops costing a second database round trip per retry.
- **Walkthrough** (endpoints in file order)
  - `GetMyBadgeAsync` (`:64`), `GET my-badge`: reads first, mints only when needed. It dispatches [`GetMyBadgeQuery`](#getmybadgequery) (`:67-69`) and returns the existing badge on success (`:71-74`). Only a `NotFound` failure falls through to [`GetOrCreateMyBadgeCommand`](#getorcreatemybadgecommand) (`:76`, `:82-88`), and not for a read-only "View as" session: `User.IsViewAs()` (`:77`) sends that caller the query's 404, which the badge page renders as its "no badge yet" state, because every command is refused for a View-as session (`:55-58`). The action declares that 404 alongside 200 and 403 (`:61-63`).
  - `CheckInAsync` (`:110`), `POST`: the organizer scan path, dispatching [`CheckInAttendeeRequest`](#checkinattendeerequest) to [`CheckInAttendeeHandler`](#checkinattendeehandler). Declares 400, 403 and 404 alongside the 200 (`:106-109`).
  - `ManualCheckInAsync` (`:134`), `POST manual`: the fallback for a dead phone, a head with no camera, or an attendee found by name search (`:121-123`), same permission and same outcome shape.
  - `RecordSponsorVisitAsync` (`:164`), `POST sponsor-visits`: attendee self-service behind `EngagementFeatures.SponsorVisits` (`:160`). The response carries the sponsor name so the landing page needs one round trip (`:151-152`).
  - `RecordRoomCheckInAsync` (`:199`), `POST room-visits`: attendee self-service behind `EngagementFeatures.RoomCheckIn` (`:195`). The session is never client supplied; the server resolves it from the room plus the configured grace window and answers 404 `CheckIns.NoCurrentSession` when nothing is running there (`:179-181`). A 200 can carry `EarnsPoints` false for a second session in the same time slot, and `PointsPaused` true when `Points:SessionCheckIn` is 0 (`:183-186`).
  - `GetAttendanceStatsAsync` (`:216`), `GET stats?eventId=`: the organizer rollup, with the event id `[FromQuery, Required]` (`:217`) and no paging arguments.
  - Every action after `my-badge` is the same three lines: dispatch the handler, then `HandleFailure(result.Errors)` or `Ok(result.Value)`. The read-then-mint branch on `my-badge` is the only control flow in the file, and no business rule lives here.
- **Why it's built this way**: the class comment (`:26-35`) records the scoping fact that explains the whole surface: the conference runs door and arrival check-in through TicketLeap (`:31-33`), so the Event scope here is not a door process. Session check-in is the working path, and Event scope stays available for a future info-desk or points-activation use. Keeping the endpoints thin keeps the decisions (idempotency of the business rule, session resolution, badge verification, points eligibility) in handlers that are unit testable without HTTP ([ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html)). Splitting `my-badge` into a query plus a conditional command is what lets a read-only View-as session see an attendee's badge without the write being attempted.
- **Where it's used**: mounted at `/checkins` by `[Route("[controller]")]` (`:37`) and fronted by the YARP Gateway. Its clients are the organizer scanning UI and the two attendee landing pages, [`RoomCheckIn`](#roomcheckin) and [`SponsorVisit`](#sponsorvisit), through [`ICheckInUIService`](#icheckinuiservice). Covered by [`CheckInsControllerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: which features are switched on in a given environment is configuration. The permission-to-role mapping behind `EngagementPermissions.CheckInManage` is resolved by the auth layer, not here, and the idempotency key header and retention window are the framework filter's, not this controller's. How `EarnsPoints` and `PointsPaused` are computed lives in the handler and result DTO, not in this controller. `User.IsViewAs()` is an extension imported from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Auth`; its claim test is not restated here.

- **Concept introduced, identity read from claims on every action, not from the request.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether ownership travels through a value a caller could tamper with. All three actions resolve `currentUserService.UserId` first and answer `Error.Forbidden("LivePolls.Forbidden", "Access denied.")` when it is absent (`:55-59`, `:84-88`, `:114-118`); no action takes a user id as a parameter. `GetResultsAsync` (`:80-97`) adds a second identity read for the scope check the handler performs: `GetCallerSpeakerId()` (`:130-134`) reads the speaker claim by its shared constant `ClaimNames.SpeakerId` (`:132`) rather than trusting a caller-supplied speaker id, and `IsCallerOrganizer()` (`:137`) reads the role directly with `currentUserService.IsInRole(RoleNames.Organizer)`. The doc comment on `GetResultsAsync` (`:71-75`) states the resulting behavior: a Draft poll, or a poll on an unpublished event, is visible only to the BR-236 rights holders and answers 404 to everyone else, so walking sequential poll ids reveals neither content nor existence. The class also carries `[RefuseMachineClients]` (`:36`), so a client-credentials caller never reaches the vote path ([ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)).
- **Concept, idempotency on an explicit-value write.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`: `CastVoteAsync` (`:109-127`) carries `[Idempotent]` (`:105`). The doc comment (`:101-102`) gives the same argument [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller)'s participation write relies on: the request names the target option explicitly (set my vote to X, not toggle), so a conference-day retry over flaky wifi replays onto the same state rather than double-toggling.
- **Walkthrough** (endpoints in file order)
  - `GetOpenPollsAsync` (`:50`), `GET open?eventId=&sessionId=`: both filters are optional query arguments (`:51-52`); dispatches [`GetOpenPollsQuery`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#getopenpollsquery) with the caller's id (`:61-63`), returning every open poll's tallies plus the caller's own vote for each.
  - `GetResultsAsync` (`:80`), `GET {id}/results`: dispatches [`GetPollResultsQuery`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#getpollresultsquery)`(id, userId.Value, GetCallerSpeakerId(), IsCallerOrganizer())` (`:90-92`), the scope-aware read described above.
  - `CastVoteAsync` (`:109`), `POST {id}/votes`: dispatches [`CastVoteCommand`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#castvotecommand)`(id, request.OptionId, userId.Value)` (`:120-122`), returning the updated tallies on success.
  - All three follow the same two-line shape once the identity check passes: dispatch the handler, then `HandleFailure(result.Errors)` or `Ok(result.Value)`.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping every identity read inline and claims-only means there is no argument on any of the three routes that a caller could substitute to see or vote as someone else, the same shape [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller) uses for its own no-ownership-argument endpoints. The scope logic behind Draft/unpublished visibility stays in the query handler rather than in this controller, so the 404 masking is enforced in one place regardless of caller.
- **Where it's used**: mounted at `/livepolls` by its route attribute and fronted by the YARP Gateway; its clients are the live-poll attendee and speaker surfaces. Covered by [`LivePollVotingControllerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup), and its constructor width is one of the subjects of `ConstructorDependencyCountTests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: which polls exist and how an organizer opens or closes one is out of scope for this controller; it only reads and votes. The permission-to-role mapping behind the Organizer check is resolved by the auth layer, not here.

Externals: `DateTimeOffset`.
- **Concept introduced, one aggregate for a family of shapes.** `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]` assesses aggregate boundaries. The tempting alternative is three aggregates (session check-in, sponsor visit, room check-in), and the class comment (`:10-15`) argues against it from the behavior: the row, the idempotency rule and the attendance query are the same shape for each, only the required target differs, and self-recorded rows stay distinguishable by `CheckedInByUserId`. The cost of that choice is that "which target is legal for which scope" becomes an invariant instead of a type, which is exactly what [`CheckInInvariants`](#checkininvariants)`.EnsureTargetMatchesScope` exists for.
- **Concept, an integration event raised from inside the aggregate.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS and Event-Driven]` assesses where an announcement is produced. `AddDomainEvent` is called inside the factory (`:112-119`), not by a handler, and the payload is [`AttendeeCheckedIn`](#attendeecheckedin), which derives from [`BaseIntegrationEvent`](group-04-events-outbox.md#baseintegrationevent) rather than from a plain domain event. Because the aggregate collects it before `SaveChangesAsync` runs, the outbox captures the announcement in the same transaction as the row ([ADR-003](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/003-outbox-dual-dispatch.html)): the check-in and its cross-module event either both land or neither does.
- **Concept, the audit marker on an attendance assertion.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy and Data Governance]` covers the [`IAuditedEntity`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#iauditedentity) marker, whose reason is written out (`:21-25`): a check-in is an attendance assertion about a named person that feeds the points economy, so a disputed or revoked row needs a record of what it looked like before ([ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html)). This is the same marker [`PointsEntry`](#pointsentry) carries, for the same reason on the other side of the earn path.

  - Seven private-set properties: `UserId` (`:31`), `Scope` (`:34`), `EventId` (`:37`, always set), the nullable `SessionId` (`:40`) and `SponsorId` (`:43`), `CheckedInByUserId` (`:49`) and `CheckedInOn` (`:52`). The two nullable targets plus the scope are the polymorphic part; everything else is present on every row.
  - The parameterless private constructor (`:55`) is EF's; the assigning private constructor (`:57-73`) is the factory's.
  - `Create` (`:89-122`) takes the scope explicitly and the sponsor id last with a default (`:96`), which the doc comment (`:87`) justifies: the scan and manual paths can never carry one, so they stay unchanged as sponsor visits were added.
  - Validation is one `Result.Combine` of five invariants (`:98-103`), so a caller gets every violated rule at once rather than the first; a failure returns the errors unchanged (`:104-105`).
  - Construction sets `Id = default` (`:107-110`) so the store assigns the key, matching the `[IdValueGenerated]` attribute on the class.
  - `AddDomainEvent(new AttendeeCheckedIn(...))` (`:112-119`) projects the aggregate onto the wire contract, converting the enum scope to its stable string with `CheckInScopeNames.ToName` (`:114`) and passing the nullable session and sponsor ids straight through.

- **Why it's built this way**: the factory doc comment (`:75-80`) states the guarantee the whole points path leans on: because the event is added before the save, a persisted check-in has always published exactly one event, and because the handler's duplicate short-circuit never reaches this method, a repeat scan publishes none. The second scoping fact is in the class comment (`:16-20`): the conference runs door and arrival check-in through TicketLeap, so the Event scope is not a door process and session check-in is the working path ([ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html)).
- **Where it's used**: created through [`CheckInProcessor`](#checkinprocessor) on behalf of [`CheckInAttendeeHandler`](#checkinattendeehandler) and [`ManualCheckInHandler`](#manualcheckinhandler) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/Services/CheckInProcessor.cs:72`, after the duplicate short-circuit at `:59-68`), and directly by [`RecordSponsorVisitHandler`](#recordsponsorvisithandler) (`.../CheckIns/UseCases/RecordSponsorVisit/RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:97`, scope `Sponsor`) and [`RecordRoomCheckInHandler`](#recordroomcheckinhandler) (`.../CheckIns/UseCases/RecordRoomCheckIn/RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:99`, scope `Session` with the attendee as their own recorder); read by [`GetAttendanceStatsHandler`](#getattendancestatshandler) (`.../CheckIns/UseCases/GetAttendanceStats/GetAttendanceStatsHandler.cs:25-35`) and exported by [`UserEngagementExportService`](#userengagementexportservice) (`.../Exports/UserEngagementExportService.cs:51-59`). Externals: ASP.NET Core MVC, `Asp.Versioning`, `[FeatureGate]`, `ClaimTypes` and `CultureInfo` for the `Created` location.
- **Concept introduced, three ways to enforce one ownership rule.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses row-level authorization, and this controller is the reference example in the module because the same rule ("a non-organizer may only touch their own bookmarks") is enforced three different ways, each matched to where the owner identity actually travels ([ADR-033](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/033-resource-ownership-authorization.html)).
  1. On the three GETs the owner arrives as a `userId` **query argument**, so the shared `[ServiceFilter(typeof(OwnerOrAdminFilter))]` (`:91`, `:121`, `:147`) compares it to the caller's user-identifier claim, with Organizer bypassing. The ADC vocabulary for that filter is configured in the Engagement module registration, not here (`:87-89`).
  2. On POST the owner arrives in the **request body**, which no query-argument filter can see, so the check is inline (`:65-77`) and the comment records the consequence of omitting it (`:68-69`): any authenticated user could create bookmarks owned by another user by supplying a foreign `UserId`.
  3. On DELETE the owner is not in the request at all, it is a property of the stored row, so the check is a database probe run through the shared [`OwnershipHelper`](group-08-auth.md#ownershiphelper)`.ValidateOwnershipAsync` (`:175-184`), with the same owner claim (`ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier`, `:177`) and bypass role (`RoleNames.Organizer`, `:178`) the filter uses (`:173-174`).
  The DELETE also teaches a second decision: per the comment (`:171-174`) a non-owner gets 404 rather than 403, so the response cannot be used to learn that a given bookmark id exists, while an unresolvable user claim gets 403 without the lookup running. Contrast the whole picture with [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller), which avoids all three mechanisms by never accepting a user id.
- **Concept, the change feed for offline clients.** `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]`: `GET changes` serves one keyset page of a user's bookmark changes since a point in time, live bookmarks with their DTO and deleted ones as tombstones, oldest change first, so an offline client can bring its copy of the schedule up to date (`:109-111`, [ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)). The page is an opaque cursor plus a size clamped to `MaxChangesPageSize` = 500 (`:46`, `:135`), and the feed is scoped to the named user by an [`InlineSpecification<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-03-querying-specifications.md#inlinespecificationtentity-tidentifiertype) on `UserId` (`:136`).
- **Walkthrough** (members in file order)
  - The class carries `[FeatureGate(EngagementFeatures.SessionBookmarks)]` (`:34`), a bare `[Authorize]` (`:35`) and `[RefuseMachineClients]` (`:36`, [ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)), and is mounted at `/bookmarks` (`[Route("[controller]")]`, `:32`). `MaxChangesPageSize` (`:46`) is the framework's default list ceiling.
  - `CreateAsync` (`:61`): the one endpoint with `[Idempotent]` (`:57`). The doc comment states the safety argument (`:52-54`): the request names the (user, session) pair explicitly and a duplicate already answers 409, so replaying a retried star is what the attendee meant rather than a second row or a spurious conflict ([ADR-017](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/017-request-idempotency.html)). The action then runs the inline body-vs-claim check for non-organizers, failing with `Error.Forbidden("Bookmarks.Forbidden", ...)` when the caller id is missing or does not match (`:70-77`), dispatches (`:79`), and unwraps the outcome with `TryGetValue` (`:81`): a failure goes to `HandleFailure`, and a success answers 201 with the unwrapped DTO and a relative location built culture-invariantly from its `Id` (`:83`), so the action never dereferences a nullable `Value`.
  - `GetUserBookmarksAsync` (`:93`): `userId` is `[FromQuery, Required]`, `eventId` is an optional filter, and paging defaults to page 1 of 10 (`:94-97`); returns a [`PagedCollectionResult<T>`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#pagedcollectionresultt).
  - `GetChangesAsync` (`:125`): `userId` required, `since` and `cursor` optional, `pageSize` defaulting to 100 (`:126-129`); calls `bookmarkQueryService.GetChangesSinceAsync` directly rather than a handler (`:132-137`) and answers a [`KeysetCollectionResult<T>`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#keysetcollectionresultt) of [`EntityChange<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#entitychangetentitydto-tidentifiertype) (`:139-141`).
  - `GetBookmarkedSessionIdsAsync` (`:149`): returns an `IReadOnlyDictionary<SessionIdentifierType, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>` (`:148-149`), which is the shape a session list needs to render bookmark toggles without one call per row.
  - `DeleteAsync` (`:167`): runs `OwnershipHelper.ValidateOwnershipAsync` with an `ExistsAsync` probe for a row with this id and this owner (`:175-184`), tagging a failure with the controller and entity names (`:182-183`) and returning it through `HandleFailure` (`:185-186`). Only then does it dispatch the generic [`DeleteEntityCommand<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#deleteentitycommandtentity-tidentifiertype) (`:188-190`), which soft-deletes, and answer 204 (`:194`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the mixed enforcement is deliberate rather than inconsistent. A shared action filter can only read what is on the request line, so the body and the stored-row cases cannot use it, and pushing the DELETE check into the handler would either duplicate it across every future mutation or force the generic delete command to learn about ownership. The stored-row probe now goes through the framework's [`OwnershipHelper`](group-08-auth.md#ownershiphelper), so the 403-versus-404 split is decided in one shared place rather than re-written inline per controller.
- **Where it's used**: mounted at `/bookmarks` and routed to the Engagement service by the Gateway; consumed by the Conference session-list and personal-schedule surfaces. Note that the writes here are also what trigger [`UserSessionBookmarkCacheEvictionHandler`](#usersessionbookmarkcacheevictionhandler): the aggregate raises [`UserSessionBookmarkChanged`](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) on every path this controller reaches, so a star or an un-star broadcasts an output-cache eviction to Conference. Covered by [`BookmarksControllerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the `OwnerOrAdminFilter` configuration (the claim name, the `userId` argument name, and the Organizer bypass role) is set during module registration and is not visible in this file. The exact 403 and 404 errors on DELETE are produced inside `OwnershipHelper`, not here. The business-rule numbers in the comments (UC-11, BR-42) are the controller's own claim; the authoritative statements live in the ADC specifications guide.

### PointsEntry

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/PointsEntry.cs:31` · Level 7 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root recording one points award, and the whole of the points ledger. An attendee's total is never a stored number: it is the sum of their entries.
- **Depends on**: [`AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype) (bound to `PointsEntryIdentifierType`), [`IAuditedEntity`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#iauditedentity), [`PointsEntryInvariants`](#pointsentryinvariants), the [`PointsEntryChanged`](#pointsentrychanged) domain event, [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) and [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys), [`DomainEntityState`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate), [`IdValueGeneratedAttribute`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#idvaluegeneratedattribute), and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result).
- **Concept introduced, the append-only ledger.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` assesses whether the schema states the intended semantics rather than relying on convention. This type has a factory and **no mutators at all**: every property has a `private set` and nothing inside the class ever writes one after construction (`PointsEntry.cs:33-46`). A total is therefore always derivable and never a number somebody edited (`:11-13`). `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]`: immutability is the model's statement that an award is a historical fact, not a mutable balance.
- **Concept introduced, the value snapshot.** `Points` stores the configured award as it stood at award time (`:39-40`), resolved by the caller before it reaches the factory (`:72`). `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` and `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`: retuning the economy mid-conference changes what the next award is worth and never rewrites history (`:14-17`). The alternative (storing only the activity and multiplying by today's configured value at read time) would silently restate every past award every time an operator changed a setting.
- **Concept introduced, idempotency and anti-farming in one index.** `[Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]` and `[Rubric §11, Security]` both apply. The unique index on `(UserId, ActivityType, SubjectKey)` ([`PointsEntryConfiguration`](#pointsentryconfiguration), `PointsEntryConfiguration.cs:46-48`) is the real rule behind both properties (`:18-22`): a replayed award collides with the row it already wrote, and N questions asked in one session collapse onto one subject key (`session:{id}`, `PointsSubjectKeys.cs:24-25`) so they award exactly once. Neither guarantee is implemented by counting in application code. [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) adds a pre-check for the ordinary duplicate (`PointsAwarder.cs:66-73`) and reads the index violation from a concurrent race as already-awarded rather than as a failure (`PointsAwarder.cs:85-91`, via [`IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector)).
- **Concept, the audit marker on a ledger.** `[Rubric §13, Observability and Operability]` assesses whether operationally load-bearing writes leave a trail. The class implements [`IAuditedEntity`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#iauditedentity) (`:31`) for a stated reason (`:23-28`): the ledger decides a prize-bearing leaderboard, so the append-only rule is worth being able to prove rather than merely assert. With the trail ([ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html)), an insert that was never followed by an update is visible in the data, and the one write that does move a total (a soft-delete or erasure of an entry) is recorded with it.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `[IdValueGenerated]` (`:30`): database-generated id, so the factory writes `Id = default` (`:93`).
  - Five `private set` properties: `UserId` (`:34`, a cross-database scalar), `ActivityType` (`:37`), `Points` (`:40`), `SubjectKey` (`:43`, defaulted to `string.Empty` so the EF constructor never leaves it null), `OccurredOnUtc` (`:46`, supplied by the caller's `TimeProvider` rather than read from a clock here).
  - Two constructors: EF-only parameterless (`:49`) and the private assigning one (`:51-63`).
  - `Create(userId, activityType, points, subjectKey, occurredOnUtc)` (`:76-104`): `Result.Combine` over all four invariants (`:83-87`), failure re-wrapped as `Result.Failure<PointsEntry>` (`:88-89`), the entity built with `Id = default` (`:91-94`), then `PointsEntryChanged(DomainEntityState.Added, id, userId, activityType, points)` raised (`:96-101`). There is no `Update`, no `Adjust`, and no `Delete` override: correcting an award means writing the compensating history, not editing the row.
- **Why it's built this way**: the contract is deliberately conference-agnostic. Neither this entity nor [`IPointsAwarder`](#ipointsawarder) names an event, a session, or a check-in: an award is a user, an activity, an opaque subject key, and a timestamp (`IPointsAwarder.cs:10-17`). `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`: that is what would make lifting the ledger into MMCA.Common a move rather than a rewrite, leaving only the thin award adapters behind in ADC. The scan surfaces that feed it are described in [ADR-072](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/072-qr-badge-check-in-and-points.html).
- **Where it's used**: written only by [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) (`PointsAwarder.cs:75`, the single write path into the ledger); read by [`GetMyPointsHandler`](#getmypointshandler) (`GetMyPointsHandler.cs:54`), [`GetPointsOverviewHandler`](#getpointsoverviewhandler) (`GetPointsOverviewHandler.cs:39`) and [`GetLeaderboardHandler`](#getleaderboardhandler) (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:54`), all projecting to [`PointsEntryDTO`](#pointsentrydto) rather than returning the aggregate; exported by [`UserEngagementExportService`](#userengagementexportservice); persisted per [`PointsEntryConfiguration`](#pointsentryconfiguration), which adds a `UserId`-leading index so the "my points" read is a seek (`PointsEntryConfiguration.cs:51-52`). Unit-tested by [`PointsEntryTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/LeaderboardOptIn.cs:19` · Level 6 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root recording that one attendee agreed to publish their score on the points leaderboard. Opting out soft-deletes the row, so "the board" is exactly the set of active opt-ins and nothing else (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:9-11`). It carries two pieces of state: the attendee's id and the display name they chose to publish.
- **Depends on**: [`AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype) (bound to `LeaderboardOptInIdentifierType`), [`LeaderboardOptInInvariants`](#leaderboardoptininvariants), the [`LeaderboardOptInChanged`](#leaderboardoptinchanged) domain event, [`DomainEntityState`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate), [`IdValueGeneratedAttribute`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#idvaluegeneratedattribute), and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result). Externals: only `System.StringComparison`.
- **Concept introduced, the published-name snapshot.** `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]` assesses whether a read can be served without reaching across a service boundary. `DisplayName` is not a lookup key into Identity: it is the name the attendee explicitly published at opt-in, stored here verbatim (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:12-16`). That single choice is what lets [`GetLeaderboardHandler`](#getleaderboardhandler) project the whole board out of the Engagement database (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:39-43`) with no gRPC call into Identity, and it also bounds the exposure: the board can only ever leak the name the attendee chose to put on it. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy and Data Governance]` is the other half, taught below on `EraseDisplayName`.
- **Concept, opt-in as a row rather than a flag.** `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]` assesses whether the model states the rule rather than encoding it in a boolean somewhere. Participation is a first-class aggregate with its own lifecycle (join, leave, rejoin), which means leaving is auditable (`CreatedOn/By` and `LastModifiedOn/By` come from the auditable base) and rejoining is a state transition on the same row rather than a new record.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `[IdValueGenerated]` (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:18`): the id is database-generated, so the factory writes `Id = default` and SQL Server's `IDENTITY` fills it (see [`IdValueGeneratedAttribute`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#idvaluegeneratedattribute)).
  - `DisplayNameMaxLength = 100` (`:22`) and `ErasedDisplayName = "Deleted Account"` (`:29`): two constants that the rest of the system reads rather than restates. The EF configuration binds the column length to the first ([`LeaderboardOptInConfiguration`](#leaderboardoptinconfiguration), `LeaderboardOptInConfiguration.cs:28-30`) and [`LeaderboardOptInInvariants`](#leaderboardoptininvariants) validates against it (`LeaderboardOptInInvariants.cs:23`). The second matches the placeholder the Identity aggregate anonymizes to, so an erased account reads the same wherever a row survives (`:24-28`).
  - `UserId` (`:32`) and `DisplayName` (`:35`): `private set` scalars. `UserId` is a cross-database reference, never a navigation ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)).
  - `IsDisplayNameErased` (`:42`): a computed `bool` comparing `DisplayName` to `ErasedDisplayName` with `StringComparison.Ordinal`. It exists so a redelivered erasure can recognise that there is nothing left to write (`:37-41`).
  - Two constructors, an EF-only parameterless one (`:45`) and a private assigning one (`:47-51`). Construction always runs through the factory.
  - `Create(userId, displayName)` (`:60-78`): `Result.Combine` over both invariants (`:64-66`), errors re-wrapped as `Result.Failure<LeaderboardOptIn>` on failure (`:67-68`), the entity built with `Id = default` (`:70-73`), then `LeaderboardOptInChanged(DomainEntityState.Added, ...)` raised (`:75`).
  - `Reactivate(displayName)` (`:87-102`): validates the name first (`:89-91`), calls the inherited `Undelete()` (`:93`), and only on success overwrites `DisplayName` and raises the same `Added` event (`:97-98`). Rejoining therefore republishes the attendee's current name, not the one they had the first time (`:80-83`, BR-135).
  - `Delete()` (`:109-117`): overrides the base soft-delete, calls `base.Delete()` (`:111`) and raises `LeaderboardOptInChanged(DomainEntityState.Deleted, ...)` on success (`:114`). This is "left the board", not "erased".
  - `EraseDisplayName()` (`:130`): a one-line, irreversible overwrite of `DisplayName` with `ErasedDisplayName`. `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy and Data Governance]` assesses whether erasure is modelled distinctly from deletion. The remarks (`:119-129`) state why the two are deliberately separate methods: taking an entry off the board and erasing the name it carried are different promises, and only the second is irreversible. The row itself survives (anonymize in place, [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)), so the scalar `UserId` reference and the audit trail stay intact, and the operation is idempotent because a redelivered erasure rewrites the same placeholder.
- **Why it's built this way**: the unique index on `UserId` is filtered on the soft-delete flag ([`LeaderboardOptInConfiguration`](#leaderboardoptinconfiguration), `LeaderboardOptInConfiguration.cs:33-35`), so an attendee can hold at most one active opt-in while their history survives ([ADR-095](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/095-soft-delete-unique-indexes.html)). That index is precisely what makes `Reactivate` necessary rather than optional: without it a rejoin would insert a second row and collide, which is the reasoning recorded at the call site (`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler.cs:78-80`).
- **Where it's used**: reactivated and created by [`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler`](#setleaderboardparticipationhandler) (`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler.cs:108` and `:92` respectively); read by [`GetLeaderboardHandler`](#getleaderboardhandler) (`GetLeaderboardHandler.cs:39-43`, ordering tie-break on `DisplayName` at `:71`); soft-deleted and erased by [`UserDeletedPointsHandler`](#userdeletedpointshandler) (`UserDeletedPointsHandler.cs:64-83`); persisted per [`LeaderboardOptInConfiguration`](#leaderboardoptinconfiguration). Unit-tested by [`LeaderboardOptInTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the erasure comment cites `PRIVACY.md` section 11 (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:121`); that document lives in the ADC repo's own docs, not in this file, so the citation cannot be verified from the source under this type.

### LeaderboardOptInInvariants

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/LeaderboardOptInInvariants.cs:9` · Level 6 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the two-rule invariant helper for [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin): the opt-in must name a real attendee, and the published name must be present and fit the column.
- **Depends on**: [`CommonInvariants`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants) (`LeaderboardOptInInvariants.cs:1`), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), the `UserIdentifierType` alias (solution-wide `global using`, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)), and the `LeaderboardOptIn.DisplayNameMaxLength` constant.
- **Concept introduced, the static invariant class.** `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]` assesses whether business rules live in the model rather than leaking into handlers or the database schema alone. Every aggregate in this module pairs with a static class whose methods each return a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), so a factory can compose them with `Result.Combine` and report every violation at once instead of failing on the first. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]`: one method, one rule, one reason to change. The idiom is the same one the framework value objects use in [Group 02](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md); the three siblings in this unit ([`CheckInInvariants`](#checkininvariants), [`PointsEntryInvariants`](#pointsentryinvariants) and [`UserSessionBookmarkInvariants`](#usersessionbookmarkinvariants)) are the same shape with different rules.
- **Walkthrough**: two expression-bodied methods, both taking a `source` string that the caller passes as its own method name so a failure carries its origin without a stack trace.
  - `EnsureUserIdIsValid(userId, source)` (`:15-16`): delegates to `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault` with code `"LeaderboardOptIn.UserId.Invalid"` and message `"User ID must be provided."`. A `default` id (zero or empty, whichever the alias resolves to) fails.
  - `EnsureDisplayNameIsValid(displayName, source)` (`:22-29`): fails when the name is null, empty, whitespace, or longer than `LeaderboardOptIn.DisplayNameMaxLength`, returning `Error.Invariant` with code `"LeaderboardOptIn.DisplayName.Invalid"` and an interpolated message that reads the constant rather than hardcoding 100 (`:26`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the length rule is stated once as a constant on the aggregate and consumed in three places (this check, the EF column at `LeaderboardOptInConfiguration.cs:28-30`, and the error message), so widening the column cannot silently disagree with the domain rule. Validating the name in the domain rather than only at the API boundary matters because [`LeaderboardOptIn.Reactivate`](#leaderboardoptin) also writes it (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:89`), and that path never passes through a request validator.
- **Where it's used**: called by [`LeaderboardOptIn.Create`](#leaderboardoptin) (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:64-66`) and by `Reactivate` (`LeaderboardOptIn.cs:89`).

### PointsEntryInvariants

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.Points` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Points/PointsEntryInvariants.cs:10` · Level 6 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the four-rule invariant helper for [`PointsEntry`](#pointsentry). It is the widest invariant class on the points side of the module, because a ledger row has four things that can be wrong: the attendee, the activity, the amount, and the subject the award is scoped to.
- **Depends on**: [`CommonInvariants`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) and [`PointsSubjectKeys`](#pointssubjectkeys) from `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared` (`PointsEntryInvariants.cs:1`), and the `UserIdentifierType` alias. No BCL externals of its own: every rule delegates to a `CommonInvariants` helper.
- **Concept**: the static invariant class is taught on [`LeaderboardOptInInvariants`](#leaderboardoptininvariants). What is worth teaching here is the boundary between a **rule** and a **kill switch**. `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]`: a zero-point award is rejected outright here (`:26-27`), because turning an earn rule off is the awarder's job, not the ledger's. A rule configured to 0 short-circuits inside [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) before any entity is built (`PointsAwarder.cs:45-50`), so a zero reaching this factory can only be a caller bug, which is exactly what the doc comment states (`:19-22`).
- **Walkthrough**: four expression-bodied methods, each a one-call delegation to a shared `CommonInvariants` helper (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Invariants/CommonInvariants.cs`) with this aggregate's own error code and message.
  - `EnsureUserIdIsValid(userId, source)` (`:16-17`): `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault`, code `"PointsEntry.UserId.Invalid"`.
  - `EnsurePointsArePositive(points, source)` (`:26-27`): `CommonInvariants.EnsureIntIsPositive`, which fails any value `<= 0` with an `Error.Invariant` (`CommonInvariants.cs:94-98`), code `"PointsEntry.Points.Invalid"`.
  - `EnsureSubjectKeyIsValid(subjectKey, source)` (`:36-44`): `CommonInvariants.EnsureStringLengthIsWithin(subjectKey, 1, PointsSubjectKeys.MaxLength, ...)`, which rejects null, empty, whitespace, or longer than `PointsSubjectKeys.MaxLength` (64, `PointsSubjectKeys.cs:13`; helper at `CommonInvariants.cs:219-223`), with code `"PointsEntry.SubjectKey.Invalid"` and a message that reads the constant (`:42`). The comment (`:29-32`) explains why this is more than cosmetic: the key is part of the unique index, so a truncated or blank key would break idempotency rather than merely look wrong.
  - `EnsureActivityTypeIsDefined(activityType, source)` (`:50-51`): `CommonInvariants.EnsureEnumIsDefined`, an `Enum.IsDefined` check behind a `struct, Enum` constraint (`CommonInvariants.cs:177-182`), code `"PointsEntry.ActivityType.Invalid"`. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices and Code Quality]`: [`PointsActivityType`](#pointsactivitytype) deliberately starts at 1 and reserves 0 for "no activity" (`PointsActivityType.cs:11-15`), so this one check turns a defaulted field or an unset payload into a validation failure instead of a silently mis-attributed award.
- **Why it's built this way**: three of the four rules exist to protect the ledger's unique index on `(UserId, ActivityType, SubjectKey)` ([`PointsEntryConfiguration`](#pointsentryconfiguration), `PointsEntryConfiguration.cs:46-48`). Idempotency and anti-farming both rest on that index, and an index cannot defend itself against a blank or truncated component, so the domain does.
- **Where it's used**: called by [`PointsEntry.Create`](#pointsentry) (`PointsEntry.cs:83-87`), combined through `Result.Combine`. Unit-tested by [`PointsEntryInvariantsTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).

### TicketRosterUpload

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.Tickets` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Tickets/TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:26` · Level 6 · class (partial, `IDisposable`)

- **What it is**: the file-upload half of the organizer's Ticket Roster page: a child component that takes a TicketLeap CSV export, dry-runs it so the organizer sees what would change, then commits the same bytes as a background import run and follows that run's progress until it ends (UC-48, `TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:95`, `:171-174`). It writes no status of its own: every outcome is handed back to the host page through a callback.
- **Depends on**: [`ITicketUIService`](#iticketuiservice) (injected, `:45`), [`TicketRosterLimits`](#ticketrosterlimits), [`TicketRosterImportErrorCodes`](#ticketrosterimporterrorcodes), [`TicketRosterImportResultDTO`](#ticketrosterimportresultdto), [`TicketRosterImportRunDTO`](#ticketrosterimportrundto) and [`TicketRosterImportStatus`](#ticketrosterimportstatus), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), and the `EventIdentifierType` alias. Externals: Blazor `InputFileChangeEventArgs`/`IBrowserFile`, MudBlazor `Severity`, `IStringLocalizer<TicketRosterUpload>` (`TicketRosterUpload.razor:2`).
- **Concept introduced, dry run then commit over one buffered read.** `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation and UX Safety]` assesses whether a destructive or bulk action can be previewed and is guarded against double submission. A browser file stream cannot be read twice, so the picked file is copied into a `byte[]` once (`:117-123`) and held as `_pendingContent` between the dry run and the commit (`:70-74`); the dry run posts it through `DryRunRosterAsync` (`:125`) and the commit posts the identical bytes through `StartRosterImportAsync` (`:186`). The commit button is therefore guaranteed to apply exactly the file the organizer reviewed. `IsClosed` (`:87`) closes the picker and the commit while the host is busy, this component is busy, or a run is active.
- **Concept, a server-owned run polled from the client.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience and Business Continuity]` assesses whether long work survives a disconnect. The commit answers a queued run at once and the server applies it in the background (`:172-174`), so the run's state lives on the server: `OnInitializedAsync` (`:155-169`) asks for the event's latest run and, if one is still active, resumes tracking it, so a reloaded page on any replica picks the progress back up (`:151-153`). `TrackImportAsync` (`:211-240`) polls every `PollInterval` (2 seconds by default, `internal` so bUnit can shrink it, `:82-83`). A failed poll keeps the last progress on screen and polls again rather than declaring the run failed (`:227-231`), and a generation counter (`_trackGeneration`, `:80`, bumped at `:213`, checked at `:222`) ends a superseded track when a resumed or retried run starts a new one.
- **Concept, refusals worded by error code.** `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` assesses whether user-facing text follows the selected language. `FailureResourceKeys` (`:35-43`) maps the API's machine-readable codes (for example `"Ticket.Roster.MissingColumn"` and `TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.AlreadyRunning`) to resource keys, so the wording comes from this component's resources rather than from the server's English message. `DescribeKnownFailure` (`:294-306`) adds a detail argument where one exists: the file cap for `Error.FileRequired`, the server message for `Error.MissingColumn`, and the CSV line carried in `Error.Target` for `Error.Malformed` (`:300-304`). An unmapped code falls back to wording by error type (`DescribeByErrorType`, `:309-324`: forbidden, not found, validation or invariant, else generic).
- **Walkthrough**
  - Parameters (`:47-59`): `EventId` (`[EditorRequired]`), `Disabled`, `OnStatus` (an `EventCallback<(string Message, Severity Severity)>`) and `OnImported`. `ReportAsync` (`:277`) is the single exit for every message.
  - `LifetimeToken` (`:66`): reads the token through the `LifetimeToken()` extension on the component's `CancellationTokenSource`, so a handler that resumes after disposal sees a cancelled token rather than an `ObjectDisposedException` (`:63-65`).
  - `OnFileSelectedAsync` (`:96-149`): discards any previous dry run, refuses a file over `TicketRosterLimits.MaxFileBytes` before uploading (`:107-112`, worded in whole megabytes via `MaxFileMegabytes`, `:93`), buffers and dry-runs it, and maps an `IOException` from the browser stream to `Error.FileUnreadable` (`:140-144`).
  - `CommitImportAsync` (`:176-204`): posts the held bytes, clears `_runFailure`, and starts tracking the returned run (`:193-194`). It is also the Retry action of a failed run (`:174`).
  - `FinishImportAsync` (`:243-267`): on `TicketRosterImportStatus.Succeeded` it drops the held file, reports the added, updated, unchanged, voided and reinstated counts (`:249`), appends the linked-existing-accounts count when it is above zero (BR-277, `:250-254`), and raises `OnImported` so the host reloads its funnel (`:257`). Otherwise `_runFailure` is set to the abandoned or the generic failed wording (`:261-263`).
  - `Dispose(bool)` (`:330-344`): cancels before disposing the token source, the idiom shared by every page in this folder.
- **Why it's built this way**: the import itself can take longer than a request should, so the server runs it out of band and the client only ever reads its state. Keeping the run on the server (not in this component's memory) is what makes reload-and-resume possible, and keeping the bytes in the component between preview and commit is what makes the preview honest. Checking the size client-side as well as in the API (`:107`) spares the organizer an upload that would be refused anyway.
- **Where it's used**: hosted by [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster-1) (`TicketRoster.razor:104`, re-keyed through `_uploadKey` and disabled while the page is busy). The server side of the dry run and the commit is [`ImportTicketRosterHandler`](#importticketrosterhandler) and [`StartTicketRosterImportHandler`](#startticketrosterimporthandler) behind [`TicketRosterImportController`](#ticketrosterimportcontroller). Tested by `TicketRosterUploadImportRunTests`, `TicketRosterFailureWordingTests` and `TicketRosterTests` in `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Tests` ([test rollup](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: which handler serves the dry-run post versus the commit post is inferred from the handler names in the type map, not read from the controller here.

### UserSessionBookmarkInvariants

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmarkInvariants.cs:9` · Level 6 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the static invariant helper for [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark). Two rules, both guarding that the aggregate's cross-module foreign keys are actually set before a bookmark can be constructed.
- **Depends on**: [`CommonInvariants`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#commoninvariants) (`UserSessionBookmarkInvariants.cs:1`), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), and the `UserIdentifierType` / `SessionIdentifierType` aliases (solution-wide `global using`, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)).
- **Concept**: the static invariant class is taught on [`LeaderboardOptInInvariants`](#leaderboardoptininvariants). This is the minimal instance of it: no lengths, no enums, just the two identifiers. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]`: each method has exactly one reason to change.
- **Walkthrough**: two one-line methods.
  - `EnsureUserIdIsValid(userId, source)` (`:11-12`): forwards to `CommonInvariants.EnsureIdIsNotDefault` with code `"UserSessionBookmark.UserId.Invalid"` and message `"User ID must be provided."`.
  - `EnsureSessionIdIsValid(sessionId, source)` (`:14-15`): the same shape for `SessionId`, code `"UserSessionBookmark.SessionId.Invalid"`.
  - Both take the `source` string the caller fills with its own method name, so a failure carries the originating call site.
- **Why it's built this way**: enforcing "a bookmark must reference a real user and a real session" in the domain, not only through a database `NOT NULL`, means an invalid bookmark can never be materialized. Because `SessionId` and `UserId` point at rows in other services' databases (database-per-service, [ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)), there is no cross-database foreign key to lean on, so the not-default check is the domain's own front line.
- **Where it's used**: called by [`UserSessionBookmark.Create`](#usersessionbookmark) (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:44-46`), combined through `Result.Combine`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: unlike its siblings in this unit, this class carries no XML doc comments on its members (`UserSessionBookmarkInvariants.cs:11-15`); the intent has to be read off the error codes.
