### Columns

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure.Tickets.TicketLeap` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Tickets/TicketLeap/TicketLeapRosterParser.cs:147` · Level 7 · class (private sealed, nested in `TicketLeapRosterParser`)

- **What it is**: the resolved column index of every header [`TicketLeapRosterParser`](#ticketleaprosterparser) reads, computed once per file so each row is read by index rather than by header lookup (`TicketLeapRosterParser.cs:146`).
- **Depends on**: [`CsvTable`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#csvtable) (`FindColumn`), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), and the parser's header constants.
- **Concept**: a header whitelist split into required and optional columns. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices and Code Quality]`: the three columns the import cannot work without are `required int` (`:149-153`): the ticket ID (the upsert key), the barcode (the claim key) and the event name (the void scope), as the comment states (`:169-170`). The other seven are `int?` (`:155-167`), so a missing optional column reads as blank rather than failing the file.
- **Walkthrough**: `Resolve(table)` (`:171-205`) looks up the three required headers (`:173-175`), collects every one that is missing (`:177-182`), and fails with one `Error.Validation` naming all of them under code `"Ticket.Roster.MissingColumn"` (`:184-190`), so an organizer who uploads the wrong export learns every missing header at once. On success it builds the instance with the required indexes plus a `FindColumn` for each optional header (`:192-204`).
- **Where it's used**: only by `TicketLeapRosterParser.Parse` (`:75`) and `ReadEntry` (`:118-138`). The `"Ticket.Roster.MissingColumn"` code is the one [`TicketRosterUpload`](#ticketrosterupload) words with the server's message as a detail argument (`TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:39`, `:298`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the name `Columns` is not unique in the workspace; the usage sites the inventory lists for it (list-page grids in MMCA.Common and Conference) belong to other members named `Columns`, not to this nested class.

### NewestRosterTicketSpecification

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.Specifications` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Specifications/NewestRosterTicketSpecification.cs:12` · Level 7 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: a one-row query over an event's roster that returns the most recently created ticket, or the most recently changed one, depending on a constructor flag.
- **Depends on**: [`QuerySpecification<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-03-querying-specifications.md#queryspecificationtentity-tidentifiertype) bound to [`Ticket`](#ticket) and `TicketIdentifierType`, and the `EventIdentifierType` alias. Externals: `System.Linq.Expressions`.
- **Concept**: the specification pattern is taught in [Group 03](group-03-querying-specifications.md). This one shows the "top 1 by ordering" shape: an ordering plus `ApplyPaging(0, 1)` (`NewestRosterTicketSpecification.cs:31`) instead of a `Max` aggregate, so the caller can project the single row to whichever timestamp it wants.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `_eventId` (`:14`), captured by the constructor and read by `Criteria` (`:35`): `ticket.EventId == _eventId`.
  - Constructor `(eventId, byLastChange)` (`:19-32`): `byLastChange` orders descending by `LastModifiedOn ?? CreatedOn` (`:24`), otherwise descending by `CreatedOn` (`:28`); either way the page is one row (`:31`).
- **Where it's used**: twice in [`GetRosterInsightsHandler`](#getrosterinsightshandler) (`GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:312-319`), once per flag, each projected to a nullable `DateTime`, to fill the roster-health "last added" and "last changed" timestamps on [`RosterHealthDTO`](#rosterhealthdto) that [`TicketInsights`](#ticketinsights) renders.

### TicketLeapRosterParser

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure.Tickets.TicketLeap` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/Tickets/TicketLeap/TicketLeapRosterParser.cs:28` · Level 7 · class (internal sealed)

- **What it is**: the TicketLeap implementation of [`ITicketRosterParser`](#iticketrosterparser): it turns the bytes of a TicketLeap attendee-export CSV into the application-layer `TicketRoster` record (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/TicketRoster.cs:11`: one source event name plus a list of [`TicketRosterEntry`](#ticketrosterentry)), or into the first reason the file cannot be imported.
- **Depends on**: [`ITicketRosterParser`](#iticketrosterparser), [`CsvReader`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#csvreader), [`CsvTable`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#csvtable) and [`CsvRow`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#csvrow) from MMCA.Common, [`TicketInvariants`](#ticketinvariants), [`Ticket`](#ticket) (`NormalizeEmail`), [`TicketRosterEntry`](#ticketrosterentry), the nested [`Columns`](#columns), and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). Externals: `System.Globalization.CultureInfo`.
- **Concept introduced, the vendor format behind an application port.** `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` assesses whether the application layer depends on abstractions rather than on a vendor's details. The application side knows only `ITicketRosterParser` and the neutral roster record; every TicketLeap header name (`TicketLeapRosterParser.cs:31-58`) and every TicketLeap quirk (buyer-name and buyer-email fallbacks) lives here, in Infrastructure, behind `internal`. Supporting a second ticketing vendor would be a second parser registration, not a change to the import handlers.
- **Concept, refuse the whole file at the first bad row.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`: an import that applies part of a file is hard to reason about, so `Parse` (`:73-116`) returns a failure for the first invalid, duplicated or inconsistent row instead of skipping it, and each row failure names the CSV line (`RowFailure`, `:140-144`, message `"Line {n}: ..."`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - Header constants (`:31-58`): ten `internal const string` names, from `"Ticket ID"` and `"Barcode"` to `"(Order) Email Address"` and its fallback `"Buyer Email"`.
  - `ParseAsync(content, cancellationToken)` (`:61-71`): wraps the bytes in a read-only `MemoryStream`, reads the table through `CsvReader.ReadTableAsync` (`:66`), and either parses it or passes the CSV reader's own errors through (`:67-69`).
  - `Parse(table)` (`:73-116`): resolves [`Columns`](#columns) (`:75-77`), then per row records the event name, builds the entry, and checks `TicketInvariants.EnsureEntryIsValid` (`:89-91`, code `"Ticket.Roster.InvalidRow"`), a duplicate ticket ID (`:93-94`) and a duplicate barcode (`:96-97`) with ordinal `HashSet`s (`:79-81`). After the loop the file must carry exactly one non-blank event name (`:102-109`, code `"Ticket.Roster.EventName"`, the message counting the names found), and that name must pass `TicketInvariants.EnsureSourceEventNameIsValid` (`:112`).
  - `ReadEntry(row, map)` (`:118-138`): trims every cell; uses the buyer's name only when both attendee name cells are blank (`:120-122`); prefers the order-form email and falls back to the buyer email (`:124-125`); stores a well-formed address lowercased via `Ticket.NormalizeEmail` and passes a malformed one through unchanged so the invariant refuses the row by line rather than silently dropping the address (`:127-129`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the event name is the void scope of an import (the comment at `:169-170`), so a file mixing two events, or rows without one, is refused rather than guessed at. Duplicate ticket IDs and barcodes are caught here, before anything is written, because the ticket ID is the upsert key and the barcode is the claim key.
- **Where it's used**: registered as the singleton `ITicketRosterParser` (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:31`, `TryAddSingleton`); consumed by the roster import path ([`ImportTicketRosterHandler`](#importticketrosterhandler) and [`TicketRosterStaging`](#ticketrosterstaging)). Unit-tested by `TicketLeapRosterParserTests` ([test rollup](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the record it returns is also named `TicketRoster`; this group's `ticketroster` anchor belongs to the Blazor page [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster), so the record is cited by path, not linked. Which import classes call `ParseAsync` is taken from the inventory's usage list, not re-read here.

### UserSessionBookmark

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/UserSessionBookmark.cs:16` · Level 7 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the aggregate root of the session-bookmark feature, one row per user's saved session (a personal-schedule entry). It holds two scalar foreign keys, `UserId` and `SessionId`, and nothing else: its whole behavior is a create/reactivate/delete lifecycle expressed through a single domain event.
- **Depends on**: [`AuditableAggregateRootEntity<TIdentifierType>`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#auditableaggregaterootentitytidentifiertype) (bound to `UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType`), [`UserSessionBookmarkInvariants`](#usersessionbookmarkinvariants), the [`UserSessionBookmarkChanged`](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) domain event, [`DomainEntityState`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate), [`IdValueGeneratedAttribute`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#idvaluegeneratedattribute), and [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result).
- **Concept introduced, one domain event with a state enum (BR-60).** `[Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design]` and `[Rubric §6, CQRS and Event-Driven]` assess whether aggregates own their invariants and announce state changes as events. This aggregate is the module's clearest example of the deliberate "one event, many states" choice: rather than separate `BookmarkCreated` and `BookmarkDeleted` types, every lifecycle transition raises a single [`UserSessionBookmarkChanged`](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) carrying a [`DomainEntityState`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate) discriminator (`Added` or `Deleted`), documented in the class remarks (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:12-13`). Downstream consumers subscribe to one signal and branch on the enum. That is the framework-wide taxonomy decision recorded in [ADR-083](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/083-crud-lifecycle-event-taxonomy.html); [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin) follows the same pattern.
- **Concept, the reactivation lifecycle (BR-135).** Re-bookmarking a previously removed session must revive the soft-deleted row rather than insert a second one. The database half of that rule is [`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration`](#usersessionbookmarkconfiguration)'s soft-delete-filtered unique index (`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration.cs:31-33`, the convention behind it taught on [`SoftDeleteUniqueIndexConvention`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#softdeleteuniqueindexconvention) and decided in [ADR-095](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/095-soft-delete-unique-indexes.html)); the decision half is [`BookmarkManagementDomainService`](#bookmarkmanagementdomainservice).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `[IdValueGenerated]` (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:15`): marks the id as database-generated, so the factory leaves `Id = default` and SQL Server's `IDENTITY` fills it.
  - `UserId` / `SessionId` (`:19`, `:22`): `private set` scalar FKs. They are not navigations: the referenced rows live in the Identity and Conference databases (database-per-service, [ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)), so a navigation would cross a service boundary.
  - Two constructors, an EF-only parameterless one (`:25`) and a private `(userId, sessionId)` one (`:27-31`). Neither is callable from outside: construction runs through the factory.
  - `Create(userId, sessionId)` (`:40-60`): combines both invariants via `Result.Combine` (`:44-46`); on failure re-wraps the errors as `Result.Failure<UserSessionBookmark>` (`:47-48`); on success builds the entity with `Id = default` (`:50-53`) and raises `UserSessionBookmarkChanged(DomainEntityState.Added, ...)` (`:57`). The comment above that call (`:55-56`) is the one subtle line in the file: the id is still 0 at this point because the `IDENTITY` value is assigned by the `INSERT`, and the event captures it by value, so consumers correlate on the user and the session rather than on the bookmark's own id.
  - `Reactivate()` (`:68-76`): calls the inherited `Undelete()` (`:70`) and, only if that succeeds, re-raises the same `Added` event (`:73`). The row keeps its identity and audit trail. Note the contrast with [`LeaderboardOptIn.Reactivate`](#leaderboardoptin), which takes a display name and refreshes it: a bookmark carries no snapshot to refresh, so this overload takes no arguments.
  - `Delete()` (`:83-91`): overrides the base soft-delete, calls `base.Delete()` first (`:85`) and, on success, raises `UserSessionBookmarkChanged(DomainEntityState.Deleted, ...)` (`:88`).
- **Why it's built this way**: reactivation over delete-then-insert preserves referential continuity and the audit trail, consistent with the soft-delete-everywhere policy ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)). Funnelling create and reactivate through the same `Added` event means consumers see one uniform "this bookmark is now active" signal regardless of whether the row is new or revived.
- **Where it's used**: created and reactivated by [`BookmarkManagementDomainService`](#bookmarkmanagementdomainservice); counted by [`BookmarkCountService`](#bookmarkcountservice); mapped by [`UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper`](#usersessionbookmarkdtomapper); persisted per [`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration`](#usersessionbookmarkconfiguration); the aggregate type parameter for the CRUD surface on [`BookmarksController`](#bookmarkscontroller). Unit-tested by [`UserSessionBookmarkTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).

### BookmarkManagementDomainService

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain.UserSessionBookmarks` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/UserSessionBookmarks/BookmarkManagementDomainService.cs:11` · Level 8 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the create-or-reactivate lifecycle for session bookmarks (BR-135, `BookmarkManagementDomainService.cs:5`), collapsed to a `static` class with a single `static` method rather than an injectable, interface-backed service. Given a possibly null previously soft-deleted bookmark plus the acting user and session, `CreateOrReactivate` returns the active bookmark: either the reactivated old row or a brand-new one.
- **Depends on**: [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), and the `UserIdentifierType` / `SessionIdentifierType` aliases (solution-wide `global using`, see [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to)). No EF, no repository, no `CancellationToken`, and, being `static`, no DI registration.
- **Concept, soft-delete meets a filtered unique index.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` assesses deliberate schema semantics. [`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration`](#usersessionbookmarkconfiguration) declares a unique index on `(UserId, SessionId)` filtered to the soft-delete flag (`UserSessionBookmarkConfiguration.cs:31-33`), so a second active row for the same pair is impossible, but a soft-deleted row still occupies that pair's history. That is exactly why you cannot blindly `Create` on a re-bookmark: you must flip the existing row back to active. This method is the domain half of that dance and the index is the database half, applied automatically by [`SoftDeleteUniqueIndexConvention`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#softdeleteuniqueindexconvention) ([ADR-095](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/095-soft-delete-unique-indexes.html)). The same pairing appears one aggregate over on [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin), where the reactivate branch lives in the handler instead.
- **Walkthrough** (`:76-91`): `CreateOrReactivate(existingDeletedBookmark?, userId, sessionId)` returns `Result<UserSessionBookmark>` (`:76`). If `existingDeletedBookmark is not null` (`:81`): call `existingDeletedBookmark.Reactivate()` (`:83`), which on the aggregate calls the inherited `Undelete()` and re-raises `UserSessionBookmarkChanged(DomainEntityState.Added, ...)` (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:68-76`). If reactivation fails, its errors are propagated as `Result.Failure<UserSessionBookmark>(reactivateResult.Errors)` (`:84-85`); otherwise the revived entity is returned via `Result.Success(...)` (`:87`). If `null`: delegate to the factory `UserSessionBookmark.Create(userId, sessionId)` (`:90`), which validates invariants and raises the same `Added` event (`UserSessionBookmark.cs:40-60`).
- **Why it's built this way**: reactivation (not delete-then-insert) preserves the row's identity, its audit trail (`CreatedOn/By`), and any scalar references that point at it, consistent with the soft-delete-everywhere policy ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)). Both branches funnel through the same `Added` domain event so downstream consumers see one uniform "bookmark is now active" signal (BR-60, a single [`UserSessionBookmarkChanged`](#usersessionbookmarkchanged) carrying [`DomainEntityState`](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#domainentitystate) rather than separate Created/Changed events, [ADR-083](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/083-crud-lifecycle-event-taxonomy.html)). The type used to be a `sealed class BookmarkManagementDomainService : IBookmarkManagementDomainService` with an implicit constructor; the interface has since been removed and the class made `static`, since a state-free decision needs no instance and nothing else ever implemented the contract.
- **Where it's used**: [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler) calls the static method directly after querying for a soft-deleted match, `BookmarkManagementDomainService.CreateOrReactivate(deletedBookmark, command.UserId, command.SessionId)` (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:64`), and only adds the returned entity to the repository when there was no prior row to revive (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:68-71`). A concurrent insert that gets past the pre-check surfaces as a unique-index violation the handler catches via `uniqueConstraintViolationDetector.IsUniqueConstraintViolation(exception)` and translates back into the same `UserSessionBookmark.Duplicate` conflict error (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:77-89`).

### ClaimTicketHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.UseCases.ClaimTicket` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/ClaimTicket/ClaimTicketHandler.cs:32` · Level 9 · class (sealed partial, primary constructor)

- **What it is**: the command handler that links an imported [`Ticket`](#ticket) to the calling attendee when they type the barcode printed on it, answering the linked ticket as a [`MyTicketDTO`](#myticketdto).
- **Depends on**: [`ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult) over [`ClaimTicketRequest`](#claimticketrequest), [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [`ICurrentUserService`](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice), [`ICacheService`](group-09-caching.md#icacheservice), [`TicketSettings`](#ticketsettings) through `IOptions<T>`, [`ErasedUserGuard`](#eraseduserguard), [`MyTicketProjection`](#myticketprojection), [`TicketLinkMethod`](#ticketlinkmethod), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). Externals: `TimeProvider`, `ILogger<T>` with `[LoggerMessage]` source generation.
- **Concept introduced, one answer for every unclaimable barcode.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether an endpoint leaks what it guards. A barcode is a bearer secret, so the handler gives the same `404` (`NotClaimableCode = "Ticket.NotFound"`, `ClaimTicketHandler.cs:41`, built by `NotClaimable()` at `:111-115`) for an unknown barcode (`:86-87`) and for a ticket that exists but is linked to someone else or is no longer live: `LinkTo`'s `Conflict` errors are rewritten to the same not-found answer (`:94-99`), because telling them apart would confirm the barcode exists (`:92-93`).
- **Concept, a per-user attempt budget counted before the lookup.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` again: guessing barcodes is bounded by a counter in the distributed cache, keyed per user (`tickets:claim-attempts:{userId}`, `:108-109`) and incremented through `ICacheService.IncrementAsync` with a sliding window (`:64-67`). The defaults are 10 attempts per 60 minutes (`TicketSettings.cs:24`, `:27`). Every attempt counts, successful or not, so the budget cannot itself be read as a signal, and the comment records the known gap: concurrent attempts can undercount, which loosens the budget but never tightens it (`:60-62`). Over budget the handler logs a warning and answers `Error.TooManyRequests` with code `"Ticket.ClaimAttemptsExceeded"` (`:68-76`).
- **Walkthrough** (`HandleAsync`, `:44-106`)
  - Caller from the token: `RequireUserId("Ticket.Forbidden")` (`:50`), then `ErasedUserGuard.EnsureNotErasedAsync` (`:56`) so an erased account cannot claim ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)).
  - Budget check (`:64-76`), then a tracked lookup by `(EventId, trimmed Barcode)` through the write repository (`:78-84`).
  - Already linked to the caller: answer the ticket again without writing (`:89-90`), so a repeated claim is idempotent.
  - Otherwise `ticket.LinkTo(userId, TicketLinkMethod.Barcode, timeProvider.GetUtcNow())` (`:94`); non-conflict errors pass through unchanged (`:97-99`); on success save, log at information level (`:102-103`) and project with `MyTicketProjection.ToDTO` (`:105`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the claim is the fallback path for a ticket the organizer's import could not link by email, so it is reachable by any signed-in attendee and must resist enumeration without a separate lockout table; a cache counter plus a uniform not-found answer is the smallest mechanism that does both.
- **Where it's used**: injected into [`TicketsController`](#ticketscontroller) (`TicketsController.cs:44`) behind `POST tickets/claim` (`:129-146`, marked `[Idempotent]`, see [`IdempotentAttribute`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#idempotentattribute)); called from the UI by [`MyTicketsPanel`](#myticketspanel). Request shape checked first by [`ClaimTicketRequestValidator`](#claimticketrequestvalidator). Unit-tested by `ClaimTicketHandlerTests` ([test rollup](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: that the claim is the fallback for tickets not linked by email is drawn from the sibling types' names and comments ([`ExistingAccountLinker`](#existingaccountlinker), the "left for barcode" count on [`TicketRoster`](#ticketroster)), not from this file.

Externals: MudBlazor `BreadcrumbItem`, `CultureInfo`.

Each group owns an [`InsightLoadState<T>`](#insightloadstatet) (`:54-55`); `LoadReportsAsync` starts both with `Task.WhenAll` so each renders the moment its own answer arrives (`:151-153`). `Begin()` returns a generation (`:164`, `:184`) and a result is applied only if it is still current (`:168`, `:188`), so switching events quickly never lets a slow answer for the previous event land on screen. - **Concept**: confirm what cannot be undone, and only that. `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation and UX Safety]` assesses whether irreversible actions are guarded proportionately. `SendInvitesAsync` asks for confirmation through `Dialogs.ConfirmAsync` with `destructive: false` (`TicketRoster.Invites.razor.cs:24-29`): sending email cannot be undone, but it removes nothing (`:23`). `LinkExistingAccountsAsync` asks nothing, because it sends nothing, links only by the BR-272 rules, and a re-run links nothing new (`:64-68`).

  - `SendInvitesAsync` (`:16-62`): returns unless an event is selected and the summary reports pending invites (`:18`); after confirmation posts `SendInvitesAsync(eventId, dryRun: false, ...)` (`:38`), words the sent and tickets-covered counts, appends the remaining count when the server's per-run cap left some for the next run (`:45-49`), and reloads the summary without the loading state (`:52`).

Tested by `TicketRosterTests` and `TicketRosterFailureWordingTests` ([test rollup](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).

The name is shared with the application-layer `TicketRoster` record (`MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/TicketRoster.cs:11`) that [`TicketLeapRosterParser`](#ticketleaprosterparser) produces; the inventory's usage list for this type mixes both.

### UserDeletedBadgeHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.CheckIns.IntegrationEventHandlers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/CheckIns/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedBadgeHandler.cs:22` · Level 8 · class (public sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the erasure handler for attendee badges. When Identity deletes an account, this soft-deletes that user's [`AttendeeBadge`](#attendeebadge) rows in the Engagement database. The check-in records themselves are kept; only the badge, which carries a per-user credential, goes (class doc, `:10-13`).
- **Depends on**: [`ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent) closed over Identity's [`UserDeleted`](group-24-identity-module.md#userdeleted) integration event (`:25`, imported from `MMCA.ADC.Identity.Shared.Users.IntegrationEvents` at `:4`), [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:34`), the [`IRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#irepositorytentity-tidentifiertype) it obtains for [`AttendeeBadge`](#attendeebadge) (`:35`) and that aggregate's `Delete()` (`:46`). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, `ILogger<T>` and the source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` (`:61-62`, which is why the class is `partial`).
- **Concept, cross-database erasure by event.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`. Under database-per-service ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)) the Identity-side erasure cannot reach a row in the Engagement database, so the deletion travels as an event and the owning service carries it out (`:11-13`). It is one of several `UserDeleted` handlers in this module; the Engagement host registers a single consumer for the type, and that consumer runs every handler for it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:193-196`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:29`). The retained check-in history follows the commitment the class doc cites (PRIVACY.md section 1.2), which lives in ADC's private docs rather than this repo.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleScopedAsync(integrationEvent, services, cancellationToken)` (`:28-59`) is the override; the base has opened the per-delivery scope and passes its provider. The body takes the user id (`:33`), resolves the scoped unit of work (`:34`) and the badge repository (`:35`).
  - The read (`:37-41`) filters `badge.UserId == userId && !badge.IsDeleted` and asks for tracked entities (`asTracking: true`, `:40`) because mutations follow. It does not bypass the soft-delete query filter: only active badges are candidates.
  - The loop (`:43-50`) calls `badge.Delete()` per row and counts only the successes (`:46-49`); a failed `Delete()` result is skipped without a log.
  - When nothing was deleted the method returns without saving (`:52-55`); otherwise it saves once for the batch (`:57`) and logs the count at `Information` through `LogErased` (`:58`, `:61-62`).
- **Why it's built this way**: idempotence is a requirement, because at-least-once delivery makes redelivery normal (`:15-16`). Reading active rows only means a second delivery finds nothing and writes nothing. Exceptions are deliberately not caught (`:16-17`), so a failed erasure propagates to the base and the broker retries it rather than acking it away. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`.
- **Where it's used**: registered by the Application convention scan (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`) and driven by the `UserDeleted` consumer registered at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:29` (passed to `AddBrokerMessaging` at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:224`). Sibling erasure handlers: [`UserDeletedBookmarksHandler`](#userdeletedbookmarkshandler) and [`UserDeletedPointsHandler`](#userdeletedpointshandler). Covered by [`UserDeletedBadgeHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/CheckIns/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedBadgeHandlerTests.cs`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the deletion is a soft delete through the aggregate's `Delete()`, so the row stays in the table flagged deleted; whether anything later purges it is not determinable from this file.

### UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.UserSessionBookmarks.DTOs` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/DTOs/UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper.cs:12` · Level 8 · class (sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the Mapperly-generated mapper that projects a [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark) aggregate to its wire-facing [`UserSessionBookmarkDTO`](#usersessionbookmarkdto).
- **Depends on**: [`IEntityDTOMapper<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#ientitydtomappertentity-tentitydto-tidentifiertype) (closed over the bookmark triple, `UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapper.cs:13`), [`UserSessionBookmark`](#usersessionbookmark), [`UserSessionBookmarkDTO`](#usersessionbookmarkdto). Externals: `Riok.Mapperly.Abstractions` (the `[Mapper]` source generator).
- **Concept, compile-time DTO mapping with Mapperly ([ADR-001](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/001-manual-dto-mapping.html)).** `[Rubric §2, Design Patterns]` and `[Rubric §15, Best Practices and Code Quality]` assess mapping that is explicit and allocation-cheap rather than reflection based. The `[Mapper]` attribute (`:11`) makes Mapperly generate the body of the `partial` method at compile time, so there is no runtime reflection and a shape mismatch is a build error rather than a silent null (the framework-wide manual-mapping versus Mapperly rationale is taught in [Group 12](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md)).
- **Walkthrough** (`:12-24`): the class implements the shared [`IEntityDTOMapper`](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#ientitydtomappertentity-tentitydto-tidentifiertype) contract. `MapToDTO(entity)` (`:16`) is declared `partial` and Mapperly writes the property-by-property copy. `MapToDTOs(collection)` (`:19-23`) is hand-written: it guards null with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` and returns `[.. entityCollection.Select(MapToDTO)]`, a collection-expression materialization.
- **Why it's built this way**: a source-generated single-item map plus a tiny hand-written collection wrapper keeps the hot path reflection-free while still satisfying the batch signature the query pipeline expects. `sealed partial` is mandatory: `partial` lets the generator supply the method body, `sealed` keeps the type closed.
- **Where it's used**: auto-registered by the module's convention scan and injected directly by [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler) (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:22`, used at `:90`) and [`GetUserBookmarksHandler`](#getuserbookmarkshandler) (`GetUserBookmarksHandler.cs:21`, used at `:72`); also resolved by the generic [`EntityQueryService<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>`](group-03-querying-specifications.md#entityqueryservicetentity-tentitydto-tidentifiertype) registered for bookmarks (`DependencyInjection.cs:41`) behind [`BookmarksController`](#bookmarkscontroller). Unit-tested by [`UserSessionBookmarkDTOMapperTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).

### ErasedUserGuard

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.ErasedUsers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/ErasedUsers/ErasedUserGuard.cs:15` · Level 8 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: the one-call refusal of a write from an account that has been erased. Every Engagement write handler that a still-valid token could reach calls `EnsureNotErasedAsync` first and gets back a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result): success for a live account, an `Error.Forbidden` for an erased one. A second member, `GetErasedUserIdsAsync`, is the batch form for a write that acts for many accounts at once.
- **Depends on**: [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (parameter, `:26-30`, `:54-57`), the [`ErasedUser`](#eraseduser) tombstone read through the unit of work's read repository (`:32`, `:62`, the batch read typed as [`IEntityQuerier<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ientityqueriertentity-tidentifiertype)), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). The user key is the module's `UserIdentifierType` alias.
- **Concept, erasure is checked at write time, not by token revocation.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`. Erasure (see [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)) removes the user's rows, but a deleted account's token can stay valid for a while. Without a gate, a late request could re-create rows for an account that no longer exists. The guard asks the tombstone table whether the user was erased and refuses the write if so.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `AccountErasedCode` (`:18`): the constant `"Engagement.AccountErased"`, the error code callers and tests can match on.
  - `EnsureNotErasedAsync(unitOfWork, userId, source, cancellationToken)` (`:26-43`): obtains the read-side repository for `ErasedUser` (`:32`, typed as `IEntityReader`, so no tracking and no write surface), runs `ExistsAsync(erased => erased.UserId == userId)` (`:33-35`), then returns `Error.Forbidden` with `AccountErasedCode`, the message "This account has been deleted." and the caller-supplied `source` for attribution (`:37-41`), or `Result.Success()` (`:42`).
  - `GetErasedUserIdsAsync(unitOfWork, userIds, cancellationToken)` (`:54-69`): the batch form (doc `:45-53`, which names its use: linking an event's roster to existing accounts, BR-277). An empty input returns an empty set without touching the database (`:59-60`); otherwise one `GetProjectedAsync` projects `UserId` from the tombstones whose id is in `userIds` (`:62-66`) and returns the erased subset as an `IReadOnlySet<UserIdentifierType>` (`:68`). It returns data rather than a `Result` because the caller decides per account what to skip, rather than refusing the whole write.
- **Why it's built this way**: a static helper rather than a decorator or a service, because the check needs the handler's own unit of work (one scope, one connection) and the `source` string so the error names the handler that refused. `Forbidden` rather than `NotFound` tells the client the request was understood and denied. The sibling handler [`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler`](#setleaderboardparticipationhandler) applies the same message and `Forbidden` type to its own erased-opt-in case under code `Points.AccountErased`.
- **Where it's used**: `EnsureNotErasedAsync` is called from [`CreateBookmarkHandler`](#createbookmarkhandler) (`CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:32`), [`GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler`](#getorcreatemybadgehandler) (`GetOrCreateMyBadgeHandler.cs:40`), [`ManualCheckInHandler`](#manualcheckinhandler) (`ManualCheckInHandler.cs:44`), [`RecordRoomCheckInHandler`](#recordroomcheckinhandler) (`RecordRoomCheckInHandler.cs:67`), [`RecordSponsorVisitHandler`](#recordsponsorvisithandler) (`RecordSponsorVisitHandler.cs:58`), [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) (`PointsAwarder.cs:57`), [`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler`](#setleaderboardparticipationhandler) (`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler.cs:71`), [`TicketLinker`](#ticketlinker) (`TicketLinker.cs:56`), [`ClaimTicketHandler`](#claimtickethandler) (`ClaimTicketHandler.cs:56`), plus the `CastVoteHandler` (`:36`), `SubmitQuestionHandler` (`:66`) and `ToggleUpvoteHandler` (`:33`) use cases. `GetErasedUserIdsAsync` has one caller, [`ExistingAccountLinker`](#existingaccountlinker) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/ExistingAccountLinker.cs:75`). All sites are under `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the guard is `internal`, so it is unreachable from the API or UI projects, and each handler must remember to call it; no fitness test enforcing that is visible in this unit's source.

### UserDeletedTicketHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.IntegrationEventHandlers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedTicketHandler.cs:28` · Level 8 · class (public sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the erasure handler for roster tickets. When Identity deletes an account, every [`Ticket`](#ticket) linked to that account has its holder fields anonymized and its link cleared (class doc, `:10-15`, BR-274), the same anonymize-then-unlink shape as the speaker erasure.
- **Depends on**: [`ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent) closed over Identity's [`UserDeleted`](group-24-identity-module.md#userdeleted) integration event (`:31`, imported at `:4`), [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) (`:40`), the [`IRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#irepositorytentity-tidentifiertype) it obtains for [`Ticket`](#ticket) (`:41`), and that aggregate's `Anonymize()` and `Unlink()` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Domain/Tickets/Ticket.cs:337`, `:314`). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, `ILogger<T>` and the source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` (`:67-68`, which is why the class is `partial`).
- **Concept, erasure that must reach soft-deleted rows too.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`. Under database-per-service ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html)) the ticket rows live in the Engagement database, so the owning service performs the erasure on receipt of the event, as the sibling [`UserDeletedBadgeHandler`](#userdeletedbadgehandler) does. Unlike that sibling, this read bypasses the soft-delete filter (`ignoreQueryFilters: true`, `:47`): deleting a roster after the event only soft-deletes its tickets, and a deleted row must not keep naming the erased person either (`:13-15`). Anonymization follows [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html) (`:12`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleScopedAsync(integrationEvent, services, cancellationToken)` (`:34-65`): takes the user id (`:39`), resolves the unit of work and the ticket repository (`:40-41`), then reads every ticket with `LinkedUserId == userId`, tracked and with query filters ignored (`:43-48`).
  - The loop (`:51-58`) calls `ticket.Anonymize()` first, then `ticket.Unlink()`, counting a ticket only when `Unlink` reports it changed something (`:55-57`). The comment (`:53-54`) explains the order: the holder fields must not survive a ticket this erasure touched, and `Anonymize` only assigns placeholders, so its `Result` is not inspected.
  - Zero unlinks returns without a save (`:60-61`); otherwise one `SaveChangesAsync` covers both changes for the batch (`:63`) and `LogErased` records the count at `Information` (`:64`, `:67-68`).
- **Why it's built this way**: both changes land in one pass and one save because the link is the only way to find the tickets: an unlink committed without the anonymization would hide them from every later delivery (`:17-18`). Reading linked rows only makes a redelivered event find nothing and write nothing, and exceptions propagate so a failed erasure is retried rather than acked away (`:21-23`). `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`.
- **Where it's used**: registered by the Application convention scan (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`) and driven by the single `UserDeleted` consumer that [`EngagementBrokerConsumers`](#engagementbrokerconsumers) registers (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:29`), which runs every erasure handler for the type (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:193-196`). Covered by [`UserDeletedTicketHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/Tickets/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserDeletedTicketHandlerTests.cs`) and exercised from `ProcessTicketRosterImportHandlerTests`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: a ticket whose `Unlink` reports no change is anonymized in memory but not counted, and if no ticket in the batch unlinks, nothing is saved, so that anonymization is dropped. Whether that combination (a linked ticket that `Unlink` declines) can occur is not determinable from this file.

### SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Points.UseCases.SetLeaderboardParticipation` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Points/UseCases/SetLeaderboardParticipation/SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler.cs:33` · Level 9 · class (public sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the command handler behind "put me on the leaderboard" and "take me off". One boolean in, a [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) out, with all the interesting work in how it resolves the published name and how it reconciles with a soft-deleted prior opt-in.
- **Depends on**: [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork), [`ICurrentUserService`](group-08-auth.md#icurrentuserservice) and its [`CurrentUserServiceExtensions`](group-06-validation.md#currentuserserviceextensions)`.RequireUserId` member (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Extensions/CurrentUserServiceExtensions.cs:35`), [`IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector), [`IConcurrencyConflictDetector`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iconcurrencyconflictdetector), [`LeaderboardOptIn`](#leaderboardoptin), [`SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest`](#setleaderboardparticipationrequest), [`ErasedUserGuard`](#eraseduserguard) (`using MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.ErasedUsers`, `:3`), and the framework contracts [`ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>`](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md#icommandhandlerin-tcommand-tresult), [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [`Error`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error). Externals: `System.Security.Claims`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` and its `[LoggerMessage]` source generator (which is why the class is `partial`, `:241-245`).
- **Concept, server-side identity for a public surface.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether trust decisions read from the token rather than the request body. [`SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest`](#setleaderboardparticipationrequest) carries a single `bool Participate` and nothing else; the display name comes from the caller's claims (`:76`, `:199-230`). The class doc (`:17-20`) states the threat directly: a name in the body would let any caller publish a name they do not own, on a surface whose whole purpose is showing names to other people.
- **Concept, create-or-reactivate against a filtered unique index.** `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`, `[Rubric §4, DDD]`. Because the unique index declared in [`LeaderboardOptInConfiguration`](#leaderboardoptinconfiguration) is filtered on the soft-delete flag, a soft-deleted opt-in still occupies the `UserId` slot for a filtered read but not for the constraint. `JoinAsync` therefore reads through `FindIncludingDeletedAsync`, which returns the active and the deleted matches as a tuple (`:83-86`), and the comment (`:80-82`) states the consequence of not doing so: every rejoin would insert a fresh row and collide with the index. State transitions stay in the aggregate (`deleted.Reactivate(displayName)` at `:108`, `LeaderboardOptIn.Create(...)` at `:114`), each returning a `Result` the handler propagates; the create result is unwrapped with `TryGetValue(out var optIn)` (`:115`) rather than a null-forgiving `.Value!`.
- **Concept, an erased account cannot join, two layers deep.** `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]`. Account erasure leaves a deleted account's token valid for a while, so the join path refuses that caller twice. First, before anything else, `JoinAsync` calls [`ErasedUserGuard`](#eraseduserguard)`.EnsureNotErasedAsync(unitOfWork, userId, nameof(SetLeaderboardParticipationHandler), ...)` and returns its failure as-is (`:71-74`); the comment (`:68-70`) explains why only the join is guarded: leaving is the erasure's own direction. This closes the case of an erased account with no opt-in row at all, which would otherwise insert a fresh one carrying the token's display name. Second, the reactivate path keeps its own check: erasure ([`UserDeletedPointsHandler`](#userdeletedpointshandler)) leaves an existing row soft-deleted with an erasure marker in place of the name, so before reactivating, `JoinAsync` checks `deleted.IsDisplayNameErased` and returns `Error.Forbidden` with code `Points.AccountErased` instead of bringing the row back under a fresh public name (`:100-106`); the comment (`:97-99`) draws the line against an ordinary opt-out, which keeps its real name and still rejoins.
- **Concept, classifying both lost join races through injected detectors.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]`, `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`. The save is wrapped in a `try` whose exception filter is `when (IsLostJoinRace(exception))` (`:125`), and `IsLostJoinRace` (`:144-146`) is an OR of two injected abstractions. [`IUniqueConstraintViolationDetector`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iuniqueconstraintviolationdetector) covers the insert path: two first-time joins collide on the unique index on `UserId`. [`IConcurrencyConflictDetector`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iconcurrencyconflictdetector) covers the reactivate path: a rejoin after an opt-out has both requests updating the same soft-deleted row, and the loser fails the concurrency check rather than the index (comment `:127-131`). Both are abstractions rather than inline message matches, so the provider-specific knowledge of what each failure looks like lives once in the infrastructure layer (for the duplicate-key case, [`SqlServerUniqueConstraintViolationDetector`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#sqlserveruniqueconstraintviolationdetector)) and this handler stays provider-agnostic. [`PointsAwarder`](#pointsawarder) leans on the unique-constraint collaborator too (`PointsAwarder.cs:85`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleAsync(command, cancellationToken)` (`:41-57`): null-guards the command (`:45`), calls `currentUserService.RequireUserId("Points.Forbidden")` and returns its failure when there is no caller (`:47-49`), resolves the typed repository (`:52`), then dispatches on `command.Participate` to `JoinAsync` or `LeaveAsync` (`:54-56`).
  - `JoinAsync` (`:63-136`): refuse an erased account through [`ErasedUserGuard`](#eraseduserguard) (`:71-74`); resolve the name and bail on failure, unwrapping it with `TryGetValue(out var displayName)` (`:76-78`); read both the active and the soft-deleted opt-ins for the user, tracked (`:83-86`); if any is active, return success **without writing** (`:90-91`), because re-publishing the name on every call would let a name change ride in on a no-op request (`:88-89`); otherwise, for a soft-deleted row, refuse an erased one with `Points.AccountErased` (`:100-106`) and reactivate any other (`:108-110`), or create the first one (`:112-119`); then save inside the race-filtered `try` (`:121-133`), which converts either lost join race (insert or reactivate) into the same success the already-on-board path returns, logging at `Debug` (`:132`). The comment (`:127-131`) frames it as intent satisfaction: being on the board is what was asked for.
  - `IsLostJoinRace(exception)` (`:144-146`): a private predicate, `IsUniqueConstraintViolation(exception) || IsConcurrencyConflict(exception)`, so the exception filter on the `catch` stays one readable call.
  - `LeaveAsync` (`:152-181`): note the parameter type, [`IEntityQuerier<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#ientityqueriertentity-tidentifiertype) rather than the full [`IRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#irepositorytentity-tidentifiertype) (`:153`), because this branch only reads and then mutates the aggregate it already holds. A filtered, tracked read (`:157-160`), success without writing when there is nothing active (`:161-162`), otherwise `active.Delete()` (`:164`) and save inside a `try` (`:168-178`) whose filter is `concurrencyConflictDetector.IsConcurrencyConflict(exception)` only (`:172`): a concurrent opt-out soft-deleted the same row first, this save lost the rowversion check, and being off the board is what was asked for, so it logs at `Debug` through `LogConcurrentLeave` (`:177`, `:244-245`) and succeeds. No erasure guard runs here, by design (`:68-70`). Soft-delete, not erasure, which is what leaves the row available for the next reactivate. Unlike `JoinAsync`, the filter has no unique-index half, since leaving never inserts.
  - `ResolveDisplayName(user)` (`:199-230`): tries `ClaimTypes.Name`, then the raw `name`, then `unique_name` (`:201-203`), because inbound claim mapping is not uniform across the hosts that serve this module (`:187-190`). An empty result is an `Error.Validation("Points.DisplayNameUnavailable", ...)` (`:206-213`) rather than a placeholder, since "Attendee" or an email fragment would be meaningless or would leak something the attendee never chose to publish (`:192-194`). Over-long names are cut at `LeaderboardOptIn.DisplayNameMaxLength` (`:215-229`), backing off one index when the cut would split a surrogate pair (`:223-227`); the comment (`:220-222`) names the visible symptom it prevents, a `U+FFFD` in the public leaderboard response.
  - `FindClaimValue(user, claimType)` (`:238-239`): a null-tolerant one-liner over `ClaimsPrincipal`.
- **Why it's built this way**: every branch that finds the world already in the requested state returns `Result.Success()` without writing, so the command is idempotent from the client's point of view and safe to retry. `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`. Note what the handler does not do: it carries no transactional marker, so the [CQRS decorator pipeline](group-05-cqrs-pipeline.md) opens no transaction around it, which is consistent with each branch performing at most one save. Both branches now absorb their lost race as success, so a retry or a double-tap never surfaces a conflict to the user.
- **Where it's used**: injected into [`PointsController`](#pointscontroller) as `ICommandHandler<SetLeaderboardParticipationRequest, Result>` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/PointsController.cs:40`, action at `:103-104`); reached from the UI through [`PointsService`](#pointsservice)`.SetLeaderboardParticipationAsync` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Points/PointsService.cs:58`) off the [`MyPoints`](#mypoints) page (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Points/MyPoints.razor.cs:139`). Covered by [`SetLeaderboardParticipationHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the display-name cap is applied by truncation, not rejection, so a caller with a very long token name silently publishes a shortened one; nothing surfaces that to the user. Whether the resulting name is unique on the board is not enforced anywhere: the unique index is on `UserId`, not on `DisplayName`, so two attendees with the same token name appear identically.

### LiveEventListener

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Components` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Components/LiveEventListener.razor.cs:26` · Level 10 · class (public partial component)

- **What it is**: the module's invisible layout component. It renders no markup; on the first render, and again on every authentication-state change, it decides the circuit's membership in the event-wide live channel: a signed-in user joins while the current event is inside its live window (so a poll opening reaches the attendee on whatever page they happen to be on), a signed-out user releases what was held. When the shell opens before the window, it arms a timer and joins when the window opens. The `.razor` half is only a comment wrapped in `CascadingAuthenticationState` / `AuthorizeView` / `Authorized` (`LiveEventListener.razor:4-10`); all the behavior lives in the code-behind, which does its own authentication check rather than relying on that wrapper.
- **Depends on**: [`ILiveEventUIService`](group-22-engagement-module.md#iliveeventuiservice), the [`LiveEventLookup`](group-22-engagement-module.md#liveeventlookup) its `GetCurrentEventAsync` returns (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/ILiveEventUIService.cs:14`) and the [`LiveEventContext`](group-22-engagement-module.md#liveeventcontext) inside it, [`NotificationHubService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#notificationhubservice) (injected as the concrete sealed class, there is no interface in front of it), [`IToastService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#itoastservice) and [`ToastSeverity`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#toastseverity), [`LivePollChannel`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollchannel) and [`LivePollOpenedPayload`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollopenedpayload) from `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared`, [`IBatteryStatusService`](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#ibatterystatusservice) and [`IAccessibilityAnnouncer`](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#iaccessibilityannouncer) from `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Capabilities`, and [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths). Externals: Blazor's `NavigationManager`, `AuthenticationStateProvider` (injected at `:42` for the auth-change subscription) and the cascading `Task<AuthenticationState>`, `IStringLocalizer<LiveEventListener>` (injected in the markup, `LiveEventListener.razor:2`), `System.Text.Json`, `TimeProvider` (injected at `:41` for the live-window clock and the window timer), and the `[LoggerMessage]` source generator (`:358-359`).
- **Concept, the ambient listener that must never throw.** `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether a non-essential capability degrades instead of taking the user's session down with it. This component is contributed as a layout component and so is live on every page, and the shell's `ErrorBoundary` wraps only the page body, which the class remarks state directly (`:19-25`): an exception escaping its render lifecycle tears down the Blazor circuit and forces a full page reload wherever the user happens to be. Every evaluation (the first render and each auth change) therefore runs through `EvaluateGuardedAsync`, guarded end to end: `OperationCanceledException` is swallowed as the expected disposal signal (`:126-129`), and everything else is logged and absorbed behind an inline `CA1031` suppression whose justification is written into the pragma itself (`:130`). Every join that runs outside an evaluation (the energy-saver toast action and the live-window timer tick) goes through `JoinChannelGuardedAsync`, which repeats the same two catches. The remarks add that the guard stays even though the live-event read already turns transport, timeout and resilience-pipeline faults into a failed lookup (`:22-24`).
- **Concept, a join that follows the auth state inside one shell.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]`. The shell persists across an in-circuit sign-in on MAUI and WebAssembly (comment `:59-60`), so evaluating only on the first render would leave a user who signs in later without the channel. The component subscribes to `AuthenticationStateChanged` on the first render (`:75-76`) and re-evaluates on each change. A monotonically bumped `_evaluation` counter (`:63-66`, `:108`) makes an older evaluation stand down when a newer one started while it was awaiting (`:111-116`, `:154`), so a stale signed-out pass cannot release the join a newer sign-in made.
- **Concept, two concurrent holders of one channel.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses how a shared per-circuit resource is owned when more than one component holds it at once. This listener joins `LivePollChannel.ForEvent(liveEvent.EventId)` (`:163`, `:173`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/LivePolls/LivePollChannel.cs:24-25`), and the Happening Now page joins the identical key for the same event. Membership therefore cannot be a set: it is reference-counted per key inside [`NotificationHubService`](group-15-common-ui-framework.md#notificationhubservice) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Notifications/NotificationHubService.cs:25-28`, `:186-189`, `:217-219`), so navigating away from Happening Now releases one join and leaves this listener still receiving events on `event:{id}`. The flip side is that this listener must never leave a channel it did not join, or it would drop the other holder's reference: `_joinedChannelKey` (`:50-52`) records the join actually taken, kept distinct from `_channelKey`, which is also set while only the window timer is armed or the energy-saver opt-in is pending.
- **Concept, capability-aware live UX.** `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]` and `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]`. Every user-visible string is a resource key resolved through the injected localizer (`LiveEventListener.razor:2`, [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)), and each poll-opened toast is mirrored to the platform's assistive channel through [`IAccessibilityAnnouncer`](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#iaccessibilityannouncer) (`:328`) so a screen-reader user gets the same event a sighted user sees.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `PayloadJsonOptions` (`:28`): a static `JsonSerializerOptions.Web`, so payloads are read with the same web (camelCase) conventions the publisher serialized them with.
  - `MaxWindowTimerStep` (`:32`): a static one-day `TimeSpan`. The comment (`:30-31`) gives the reason: a timer delay above about 49.7 days (`uint.MaxValue - 1` ms) throws, and the next published event can be months away, so the wait runs in steps of at most one day.
  - Nine `[Inject]` properties (`:34-42`): the live-event service, the hub service, the toast service, `NavigationManager`, the battery-status and accessibility-announcer capabilities, the typed logger, `TimeProvider`, and `AuthenticationStateProvider`. The `[CascadingParameter] Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthState` (`:44-45`) is nullable because the component can be rendered outside a `CascadingAuthenticationState`.
  - The mutable state: `_subscription` and `_channelKey` (`:47-48`), `_joinedChannelKey` (`:52`), `_windowTimer` and `_disposed` (`:56-57`), `_authSubscribed` (`:61`) and `_evaluation` (`:66`). The timer is armed when the shell opens before the live window, a tab or MAUI shell left open from the evening before (comment `:54-55`), so the join happens when the window opens instead of never.
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync(firstRender)` (`:68-79`): a non-`async` method. Past the first render it returns `Task.CompletedTask` (`:70-73`); on the first it subscribes to `AuthStateProvider.AuthenticationStateChanged` and sets `_authSubscribed` (`:75-76`), then returns `EvaluateGuardedAsync(AuthState)` when a cascading auth state exists (`:78`).
  - `OnAuthenticationStateChanged(authStateTask)` (`:84-85`) and `ReevaluateAsync(authStateTask)` (`:87-97`): the event-handler signature discards the task explicitly rather than using `async void` (comment `:81-83`, VSTHRD100); `ReevaluateAsync` marshals onto the renderer with `InvokeAsync(() => EvaluateGuardedAsync(authStateTask))` (`:91`) and swallows only `ObjectDisposedException`, the renderer torn down between the event and the dispatch (`:93-96`).
  - `EvaluateGuardedAsync(authStateTask)` (`:104-138`): bumps `_evaluation` and awaits the state (`:108-109`), stands down if a newer evaluation started meanwhile (`:113-116`), calls `ReleaseAsync` for an unauthenticated principal (`:118-122`), and otherwise awaits `EvaluateSignedInAsync(evaluation)` (`:124`). The two catches follow (`:126-137`); the catch-all logs through `LogLiveChannelSetupFailed` and stays silent in the UI, since this component renders nothing and has no place to show a message (`:134-136`).
  - `EvaluateSignedInAsync(evaluation)` (`:146-175`): a no-op once disposed or once a `_channelKey` is held (`:148-151`), because a token refresh also raises the auth event (doc `:141-142`). It reads `(await LiveEventService.GetCurrentEventAsync()).LiveEvent` (`:153`) and stands down on no event, on disposal, or on a newer evaluation (`:154-157`). It then reads "now" once from the injected `TimeProvider` (`:159`) and branches three ways. Before `liveEvent.LiveWindowStartUtc` it sets `_channelKey` and calls `ArmLiveWindowTimer` instead of joining (`:160-166`); after the window (per `IsLiveAt`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveEventContext.cs:22-23` for the half-open window it tests) it returns (`:168-171`); inside it, it sets `_channelKey` (`:173`) and awaits `TryJoinAsync(JoinChannelAsync)` (`:174`), the unguarded join, since it already runs inside the evaluation guard. Reading the clock through the injected `TimeProvider` rather than `DateTime.UtcNow` lets a test pin "now": the resilience tests register `TimeProvider.System` (`LiveEventListenerResilienceTests.cs:49`), and `LiveEventListenerTests` drives the window from a controlled clock (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Tests/Components/LiveEventListenerTests.cs:68`, `:100`).
  - `TryJoinAsync(join)` (`:182-200`): the energy-saver check shared by the evaluation and the window timer. When `Battery.IsEnergySaverOn` (`:187`), the auto-join is skipped and an `Info` toast offers a "join anyway" action whose callback is `JoinChannelGuardedAsync` (`:191-195`), returning `Task.CompletedTask` (`:196`). The inline comment (`:184-186`) is explicit that only the lossy live channel is deferred and the core notification connection is untouched ([ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html) Wave 3). Otherwise it returns the supplied `join()` (`:199`): unguarded from the evaluation path, guarded from the timer (`:181`).
  - `ArmLiveWindowTimer(liveEvent, utcNow)` (`:206-215`): computes the time until the window starts (`:208`), disposes any previous timer (`:209`), and creates a one-shot `TimeProvider.CreateTimer` whose due time is the smaller of that gap and `MaxWindowTimerStep`, with an infinite period (`:210-214`). The callback marshals onto the renderer with `InvokeAsync(() => OnLiveWindowTimerAsync(liveEvent))` (`:211`).
  - `OnLiveWindowTimerAsync(liveEvent)` (`:221-236`): does nothing once `_disposed` is set or `_channelKey` has been cleared, which covers a tick queued before a sign-out released the channel (`:223-226`, comment `:217-220`); re-reads the clock and re-arms when the tick was a capped step that still lands before the window (`:228-233`); otherwise joins through `TryJoinAsync(JoinChannelGuardedAsync)` when the window is live, and joins nothing when it has already closed (`:235`).
  - `JoinChannelGuardedAsync()` (`:242-258`): the same two catches again, because the toast action and the timer tick fire outside the evaluation and inherit none of its guarding (doc `:238-241`, `:189-190`). `IToastService.ShowAction` documents the same rule from the other side: exceptions are the caller's to handle (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/Interfaces/IToastService.cs:96-101`).
  - `JoinChannelAsync()` (`:260-276`): a non-`async` method returning `Task`. A guard first (`_disposed || _channelKey is null || _subscription is not null`, returning `Task.CompletedTask`, `:265-268`), so a toast-triggered join after an auto-join cannot double-subscribe and a join that resumes after disposal takes nothing nobody would release (`:262-264`). Then `HubService.OnChannelEvent(_channelKey, HandleChannelEventAsync)` (`:270`), `_joinedChannelKey` recorded before the hub call because the hub counts the reference synchronously (`:272-274`), and `HubService.JoinChannelAsync(_channelKey)` returned directly, un-awaited (`:275`), so the caller's `await` observes the hub join and no extra state machine is allocated. Subscribing does not join the server-side group, and joining does not register a handler, so both calls are required.
  - `ReleaseAsync()` (`:284-302`): shared by disposal and a sign-out (doc `:278-283`). It disposes the window timer (`:286-290`), disposes the subscription and clears `_channelKey` (`:292-294`), and calls `HubService.LeaveChannelAsync` only when `_joinedChannelKey` is set, clearing it first (`:296-301`).
  - `HandleChannelEventAsync(eventName, payloadJson)` (`:304-342`): filters to `LivePollChannel.PollOpened` (the literal `poll.opened`, `LivePollChannel.cs:14`) with an ordinal comparison (`:306-309`), deserializes a [`LivePollOpenedPayload`](group-23-engagement-live-layer.md#livepollopenedpayload) and returns silently on a `JsonException` or a null result (`:311-324`), announces the poll with the question text (`:328`), then marshals back to the renderer with `InvokeAsync` to raise the toast (`:332-341`). That call passes `ToastSeverity.Info` and `requireInteraction: true` (`:340-341`), so the toast is pinned open rather than expiring on the host timer, and it carries an action that navigates to [`EngagementRoutePaths`](#engagementroutepaths)`.HappeningNow`, that is `/happening-now` (`:337`, `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementRoutePaths.cs:11`).
  - `DisposeAsync()` (`:345-356`): sets `_disposed` first (`:347`), so a tick already queued on the renderer finds the flag and joins nothing; unsubscribes from `AuthenticationStateChanged` when subscribed (`:348-352`); awaits `ReleaseAsync()` (`:354`); and calls `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)` (`:355`).
  - `LogLiveChannelSetupFailed` (`:358-359`): a source-generated `Error`-level log whose message states the degraded outcome ("the live channel stays dormant for this session"). `[Rubric §13, Observability]`.
- **Why it's built this way**: the live layer is best-effort by design, so every failure on this path degrades to "no live channel" rather than surfacing to the user, and the authoritative data is always one page load away. The energy-saver deferral and the screen-reader announcement are the two device-capability touch points, both reached through interfaces whose web fallbacks are no-ops, so the same component runs unchanged on Blazor Server, WebAssembly, and the MAUI hybrid head.
- **Where it's used**: contributed by [`EngagementUIModule`](#engagementuimodule) as its single `LayoutComponentTypes` entry (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementUIModule.cs:45`) and rendered by the shared `MainLayout` on every page; regression-tested by [`LiveEventListenerResilienceTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Tests/Components/LiveEventListenerResilienceTests.cs`, for example the energy-saver and failing-join cases at `:128`, `:154`), with the live window and the auth-state behavior pinned by `LiveEventListenerTests`: a render sixty days before the window that must arm without throwing (`LiveEventListenerTests.cs:100`), a later in-shell sign-in that joins (`:135`), a sign-out that releases (`:151`), a stale signed-out evaluation that must not release a newer join (`:167`), and disposal cases that must leave another holder's channel joined or never join afterwards (`:191`, `:207`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the battery state is read only at the moment of a join attempt (`:187`, on an evaluation or on the window-timer tick), and the component never subscribes to an energy-saver-changed notification, so turning energy saver off later does not auto-join; the toast action is the only way in for that session. Once a `_channelKey` is held, a later signed-in evaluation is a no-op (`:148-151`), so an event rescheduled after the timer was armed is not picked up until the next sign-in cycle or page load. The leave call in `ReleaseAsync` carries no try/catch of its own: on disposal it relies on the hub service handling its own failures, and on a sign-out a throw lands in the evaluation guard. The localizer `L` is declared only in the markup (`LiveEventListener.razor:2`), so it is invisible in the code-behind despite being used throughout it.

### UserEmailVerifiedTicketLinkHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.IntegrationEventHandlers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserEmailVerifiedTicketLinkHandler.cs:22` · Level 10 · class (public sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the handler that links an account's roster tickets once the account proves control of its email address (BR-272): a confirmed email, an attached external login with a verified address, or a redeemed sign-in link (class doc, `:10-12`). It is a thin adapter from Identity's event to the shared linking rules in [`TicketLinker`](#ticketlinker).
- **Depends on**: [`ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent) closed over Identity's [`UserEmailVerified`](group-24-identity-module.md#useremailverified) integration event (`:25`, imported at `:4`), [`TicketLinker`](#ticketlinker)`.LinkVerifiedEmailAsync` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/TicketLinker.cs:43`), and the scoped [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) and `TimeProvider` it passes in (`:34-35`). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, `ILogger<T>` and the source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` (`:48-49`, which is why the class is `partial`).
- **Concept, cross-module linking by event, with the rules in one place.** `[Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven]`, `[Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]`. Identity owns the account and Engagement owns the roster, so the link is made by the Engagement side on receipt of an event rather than by a call across the module boundary. Both link handlers delegate to the same `TicketLinker` method, so the matching rules live once and are idempotent: a repeated proof links nothing more (`:17`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleScopedAsync(integrationEvent, services, cancellationToken)` (`:28-46`): calls `TicketLinker.LinkVerifiedEmailAsync` with the scoped unit of work, `TimeProvider`, the event's `UserId` and `Email`, and `firstName: null, lastName: null` (`:33-40`), because this event carries no account name. A positive count is logged at `Information` through `LogLinked` (`:42-45`, `:48-49`).
- **Why it's built this way**: without a name, the BR-272 name match cannot run, so the address's ticket is linked only when it holds exactly one for the event; a multi-ticket order waits for a barcode claim (BR-273) unless [`UserRegisteredTicketLinkHandler`](#userregisteredticketlinkhandler) already matched it by name (`:14-17`). Exceptions are not caught, so the base and the broker retry a failed link.
- **Where it's used**: registered by the Application convention scan (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`) and driven by the `UserEmailVerified` consumer that [`EngagementBrokerConsumers`](#engagementbrokerconsumers) registers (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:31`; mapping comment at `MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:199`). Covered by [`TicketLinkHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/Tickets/IntegrationEventHandlers/TicketLinkHandlerTests.cs`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the matching rules themselves (one ticket per address per event, the erased-account refusal) are in `TicketLinker`, not here; this file only shows that a zero count is silent.

### UserRegisteredTicketLinkHandler

> MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application · `MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tickets.IntegrationEventHandlers` · `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserRegisteredTicketLinkHandler.cs:25` · Level 10 · class (public sealed partial)

- **What it is**: the handler that links a new account's roster tickets when its address is already proven at registration (BR-272): an account an invite created, or one created from an external login whose provider vouched for the address (class doc, `:10-12`). The sibling of [`UserEmailVerifiedTicketLinkHandler`](#useremailverifiedticketlinkhandler), and the one that can match by name.
- **Depends on**: [`ScopedIntegrationEventHandlerBase<TIntegrationEvent>`](group-04-events-outbox.md#scopedintegrationeventhandlerbasetintegrationevent) closed over Identity's [`UserRegistered`](group-24-identity-module.md#userregistered) integration event (`:28`, imported at `:4`), [`TicketLinker`](#ticketlinker)`.LinkVerifiedEmailAsync` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/Services/TicketLinker.cs:43`), and the scoped [`IUnitOfWork`](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#iunitofwork) and `TimeProvider` it passes in (`:40-41`). Externals: `IServiceScopeFactory`, `ILogger<T>` and the source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` (`:54-55`).
- **Concept, a typed address proves nothing.** `[Rubric §11, Security]`. The event's `EmailVerified` flag is the gate (`:36-37`), exactly as for the Conference speaker auto-link (BR-207): an address typed into a registration form proves nothing, so a local password registration links nothing here until [`UserEmailVerified`](group-24-identity-module.md#useremailverified) arrives and the sibling handler runs (`:13-15`). Linking on an unproven address would hand someone else's ticket to whoever typed it.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `HandleScopedAsync(integrationEvent, services, cancellationToken)` (`:31-52`): returns at once when `EmailVerified` is false (`:36-37`); otherwise calls `TicketLinker.LinkVerifiedEmailAsync` with the scoped unit of work, `TimeProvider`, the event's `UserId`, `Email`, `FirstName` and `LastName` (`:39-46`), and logs a positive count at `Information` (`:48-51`, `:54-55`).
- **Why it's built this way**: this is the one event that carries the account name, so it is where a multi-ticket order is matched by name (`:17-18`). An invite-created account raises both events; the shared rules are idempotent, so the second delivery links nothing more (`:18-20`).
- **Where it's used**: registered by the Application convention scan (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:94`) and driven by the `UserRegistered` consumer that [`EngagementBrokerConsumers`](#engagementbrokerconsumers) registers (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/EngagementBrokerConsumers.cs:30`); Conference consumes the same event on its own queue (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Service/Program.cs:197-198`). Covered by [`TicketLinkHandlerTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application.Tests/Tickets/IntegrationEventHandlers/TicketLinkHandlerTests.cs`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: how the name match resolves ties within an order is `TicketLinker`'s concern and is not visible in this file.
